senses.meaningEn: used before a singular noun when you mention something for the first time or it is not a particular one

examples.en: I need a pen. Do you have one?
She has a dog and two cats.
examples.ko: 그녀는 개 한 마리와 고양이 두 마리를 키워.

senses.note: 셀 수 있는 단수 명사 앞에는 a/an 을 반드시 붙임: I'm a student. (not 'I'm student'). 자음 소리 앞 a, 모음 소리 앞 an(an hour, a university).

senses.meaningEn: used to say how much of something there is for each unit of time or amount

examples.en: Apples are two dollars a kilo.
I go to the gym three times a week.
examples.ko: 나는 일주일에 세 번 헬스장에 가.

senses.note: once a day, twice a month, 60 km an hour. 이때 a = per(격식).

senses.meaningKo: 입이 가벼운 사람, 비밀을 못 지키는 입
senses.meaningEn: someone who talks too much and cannot keep secrets

examples.en: Don't tell Jake. He has a big mouth.
Sorry, I have a big mouth. I told everyone.
examples.ko: 미안, 내가 입이 싸서 다 말해 버렸어.

senses.note: have a big mouth = 입이 가볍다. 실제 "큰 입" 이 아님. 비난하는 느낌이 있어 당사자 앞에서는 조심. 유사: can't keep a secret.

senses.meaningEn: a person who loves reading and reads a lot

examples.en: She's a real bookworm. She reads every night.
examples.ko: 그녀는 진짜 책벌레야. 매일 밤 책을 읽어.

examples.en: I was a bookworm when I was a kid.

senses.note: 한국어 '책벌레' 와 거의 그대로 대응함. 대체로 긍정적이거나 애정 어린 표현. 공부벌레는 nerd / grind 등 다른 단어.

senses.meaningEn: a person who is not brave and is afraid to do something

examples.en: Don't be a chicken. Just jump in the pool!
examples.ko: 겁쟁이처럼 굴지 마. 그냥 수영장에 뛰어들어!

examples.en: He's such a chicken when it comes to spiders.

senses.note: 친구 사이의 장난스러운 놀림. 형용사로도 씀: Are you chicken?(겁먹었어?). chicken out = 겁먹고 그만두다. 음식 '닭고기' 는 셀 수 없는 chicken(I ate chicken), 겁쟁이는 a chicken.

senses.meaningEn: a person who copies what someone else does, says, or wears

examples.en: Stop being a copycat and draw your own picture.
examples.ko: 따라 그리지 말고 네 그림을 그려.

examples.en: You bought the same shoes? Copycat!

senses.note: 아이들이 서로 놀릴 때 흔히 씀. 어른 사이에선 다소 유치한 느낌. 범죄 뉴스의 copycat crime 은 '모방 범죄'.

senses.meaningKo: 소파에 누워 TV 만 보는 게으른 사람
senses.meaningEn: a person who spends a lot of time sitting on the sofa watching TV and doing little exercise

examples.en: Don't be a couch potato. Let's go for a walk.
My brother is a total couch potato on weekends.
examples.ko: 우리 형은 주말마다 완전히 소파에 눌어붙어 있어.

senses.note: couch(소파) 위에 감자처럼 가만히 있다는 비유. 장난스러운 핀잔으로 쓰며 심한 욕은 아님. 복수 couch potatoes.

senses.meaningKo: (셀 수 있는 명사) 몇 개의, 조금의
senses.meaningEn: a small number of people or things

examples.en: I have a few questions for you.
We stayed there for a few days.

senses.note: 셀 수 있는 복수 명사 앞(a few friends, a few minutes). 셀 수 없는 명사에는 a little. a 없는 few 는 "거의 없다"는 부정적 뜻: Few people came.(온 사람이 거의 없었다).

senses.meaningEn: a small number of the things or people already mentioned

examples.en: Do you want some cookies? Just a few, please.
examples.ko: 쿠키 좀 먹을래? 몇 개만 주세요.

examples.en: Most people left, but a few stayed.

senses.note: quite a few = 꽤 많은(헷갈리기 쉬움!): Quite a few people came. = 사람이 꽤 많이 왔다.

senses.meaningEn: slightly; to a small degree

examples.en: I'm a little tired today.
Can you speak a little more slowly?

senses.note: 형용사·부사·비교급 앞에서 "조금": a little cold, a little better. 구어에서는 a bit 과 바꿔 쓸 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: a small amount of something that cannot be counted

examples.en: Add a little salt to the soup.
I speak a little Korean.
examples.ko: 저는 한국어를 조금 할 수 있어요.

senses.note: 셀 수 없는 명사(salt, water, time, money)에 a little, 셀 수 있는 명사에는 a few. a 없이 little 만 쓰면 "거의 없다"는 부정적 뜻: I have little time.(시간이 거의 없어).

senses.meaningEn: many years in the past

examples.en: My grandparents moved here a long time ago.
examples.ko: 우리 할아버지 할머니는 오래전에 여기로 이사 오셨어.

examples.en: A long time ago, there was a king who had three sons.
examples.ko: 옛날에 아들 셋을 둔 왕이 있었습니다.

senses.note: ago 는 과거시제와 씀(not 'have moved ... ago'). 이야기 시작은 A long time ago, ... 또는 Once upon a time. '얼마 전에' 는 a little while ago / not long ago.

senses.meaningEn: very much or very often

examples.en: Thanks a lot for your help!
I travel a lot for work.
examples.ko: 나는 일 때문에 출장을 많이 다녀.

senses.note: 동사 뒤에서 부사처럼: like it a lot, talk a lot. "alot" 으로 붙여 쓰는 건 틀림. very much 보다 구어적.

senses.meaningEn: a large number or amount of something

examples.en: There were a lot of people at the market.
I don't have a lot of time today.

senses.note: a lot of 는 셀 수 있는 명사·없는 명사 모두에 씀(many/much 구분 불필요). lots of 는 더 캐주얼. 비교급 강조도 가능: a lot bigger(훨씬 큰).

senses.meaningKo: 저녁형 인간, 밤늦게까지 깨어 있는 사람
senses.meaningEn: a person who likes to stay up late at night

examples.en: I'm a night owl. I work best after midnight.
examples.ko: 나는 저녁형 인간이야. 자정 넘어서 제일 잘 돼.

examples.en: Night owls often skip breakfast.
examples.ko: 밤늦게 자는 사람들은 아침을 자주 건너뛰어.

senses.note: 올빼미(owl)가 밤에 활동하는 데서 온 말. an early bird 와 짝으로 익히면 좋음. 나쁜 뜻은 없고 생활 패턴을 말할 때 쓴다.

senses.meaningEn: to tell someone angrily and honestly what you think of their behavior

examples.en: I'm going to give him a piece of my mind.
She gave the rude driver a piece of her mind.

senses.note: give + 사람 + a piece of one's mind. 화난 상태에서 하는 말. peace of mind(마음의 평화) 와 발음이 같으니 혼동 주의.

senses.meaningEn: a strong liking for sweet foods

examples.en: I have a sweet tooth. I can't say no to cake.
examples.ko: 난 단것을 좋아해서 케이크를 못 참아.

examples.en: Does your son have a sweet tooth?

senses.note: 항상 have a sweet tooth 로 쓰며, 단수 tooth(복수 teeth 아님). 사람 자체를 가리키지 않고 '입맛' 을 가리키므로 'He is a sweet tooth' 는 틀림.

senses.meaningEn: having the skill, time, or chance to do something

examples.en: I wasn't able to sleep last night.
Will you be able to come tomorrow?

senses.note: 항상 be able to + 동사 로 씀. can 과 뜻이 같지만, 미래(will be able to)·완료(have been able to)처럼 can 을 쓸 수 없는 자리에서 사용. 명사 ability.

senses.meaningEn: clever or skilled at doing things

examples.en: She is a very able student.
He's one of the ablest players on the team.
examples.ko: 그는 팀에서 가장 능력 있는 선수 중 하나야.

senses.note: 명사 앞에서 an able student / worker 로 쓰면 '능력 있는'. 약간 격식 있는 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: on the subject of something

examples.en: Tell me about your trip.
What is this book about?

senses.note: talk/think/know/worry about. How about ~? / What about ~? = ~는 어때?(제안·의견 묻기).

senses.meaningEn: a little more or less than a number; approximately

examples.en: It takes about ten minutes to walk there.
The shirt costs about twenty dollars.

senses.note: about = around(구어). 격식은 approximately. about 뒤에 숫자가 오면 거의 항상 '대략' 의 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: going to do something very soon

examples.en: I was about to call you!
Hurry, the movie is about to start.

senses.note: be about to + 동사 = 바로 직전. be going to 보다 훨씬 가까운 미래.

senses.meaningEn: in a higher position than something

examples.en: There's a clock above the door.
We live in the apartment above the bakery.

senses.note: above = 단순히 더 높은 위치, over = 바로 위를 덮거나 가로지르는 느낌. 접촉하면 on.

senses.meaningEn: more than a number, level, or temperature

examples.en: It's five degrees above zero today.
Her test score was above average.

senses.note: above zero(영상), below zero(영하), above average(평균 이상). 나이·가격은 보통 over 를 더 많이 씀.

senses.meaningEn: higher up, or earlier in a piece of writing

examples.en: Look at the picture above.
Read the text above and answer the questions.

senses.note: 교과서·문서에서 the picture above / see above / as mentioned above(위에서 말한 것처럼).

senses.meaningEn: not in the place where you are expected to be, such as school or work

examples.en: Two students are absent today.
Why were you absent from class yesterday?

senses.note: be absent from + 장소/수업. 결석 = absence(명사). 출석 부를 때 교사가 Who's absent? 라고 물음. 'miss class' 도 같은 뜻으로 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to say yes to an offer, gift, or invitation

examples.en: She accepted the job offer right away.
Thank you, I'd love to accept your invitation.

senses.note: receive 는 단순히 '받다', accept 는 '동의해서 받아들이다'. except(제외하고)과 발음이 비슷하니 주의.

senses.meaningEn: to allow a type of payment

examples.en: Do you accept credit cards?
Sorry, we only accept cash here.

senses.note: 가게에서 가장 유용한 문장: Do you accept cards? = Can I pay by card?

senses.meaningEn: from one side of something to the other

examples.en: Be careful when you walk across the street.
We swam across the small lake.

senses.note: go across = cross. through 는 '안을 통과', across 는 '표면을 가로질러'(across the river, through the tunnel).

senses.meaningEn: on the opposite side of something

examples.en: The bank is across from the post office.
She sat across the table from me.

senses.note: '맞은편'은 across from + 장소. 미국 구어에서는 across the street 로도 많이 말함.

senses.meaningEn: to behave in a particular way

examples.en: Stop acting like a baby.
He acted strangely at dinner last night.
examples.ko: 그는 어젯밤 저녁 식사 때 이상하게 행동했어.

senses.note: act like + 명사 / act + 형용사(act cool, act surprised). 한국어 "액트"처럼 공연만 떠올리지 말 것.

senses.meaningEn: to perform a part in a play or film

examples.en: She acts in a small theater downtown.
My brother wants to act in movies.
examples.ko: 내 남동생은 영화에서 연기하고 싶어 해.

senses.meaningEn: one of the main parts of a play, or a short performance

examples.en: The play has three acts.
The magic act was my favorite part.

senses.meaningEn: a person who acts in movies, TV shows, or plays

examples.en: He is my favorite actor.
examples.ko: 그 사람은 내가 제일 좋아하는 배우야.

examples.en: The actors practiced the scene many times.
examples.ko: 배우들이 그 장면을 여러 번 연습했어.

senses.note: 요즘은 남녀 모두 actor 로 부르는 경우가 많음. voice actor(성우), movie star(영화 스타).

senses.meaningEn: a woman who acts in movies, TV shows, or plays

examples.en: The actress won a big award last night.
examples.ko: 그 여배우가 어젯밤 큰 상을 받았어.

examples.en: My favorite actress is in this drama.
examples.ko: 내가 제일 좋아하는 여배우가 이 드라마에 나와.

senses.note: 여전히 많이 쓰지만, 뉴스나 시상식에서는 여성도 actor 로 부르는 흐름이 늘고 있음.

senses.meaningEn: to put something together with something else

examples.en: Add a little salt to the soup.
Can I add one more thing to my order?

senses.note: add A to B = B 에 A 를 더하다. 요리 레시피에 가장 자주 나오는 동사.

senses.meaningEn: to put numbers together to get a total

examples.en: Add five and three, and you get eight.
Let's add up the bill.

senses.note: add up = 합계를 내다. 'plus' 로 읽음: five plus three. 명사 addition = 덧셈, 추가.

senses.meaningEn: the number, street, and town where a person lives

examples.en: What's your home address?
Write your name and address on the box.

senses.note: e-mail address = 이메일 주소. 미국식은 흔히 두 번째 음절에 강세(/əˈdres/)도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: a person who is fully grown, not a child

examples.en: Tickets cost ten dollars for adults.
Children must be with an adult at all times.
examples.ko: 어린이는 항상 어른과 함께 있어야 합니다.

senses.note: 어린이와 대화할 때는 grown-up 을 더 자주 씀. 미국식 발음은 /əˈdʌlt/ 또는 /ˈædʌlt/ 둘 다 가능.

senses.meaningEn: for or about grown-up people

examples.en: This is an adult class, so no kids are allowed.
examples.ko: 성인 수업이라서 아이들은 들어올 수 없어.

examples.en: My adult daughter still calls me every day.
examples.ko: 다 큰 딸이 아직도 매일 전화해.

senses.note: adult content/movie 는 '성인용(19금)'이라는 뜻이 되니 주의.

senses.meaningEn: feeling fear

examples.en: My little sister is afraid of dogs.
Don't be afraid. I'm right here.
examples.ko: 겁내지 마. 내가 바로 여기 있잖아.

senses.note: afraid 는 명사 앞에 못 씀(an afraid child ✗ → a scared/frightened child). be afraid of + 명사, be afraid to + 동사.

senses.meaningEn: used to politely tell someone something disappointing

examples.en: I'm afraid we're closed on Sundays.
I'm afraid I can't come tomorrow.
examples.ko: 안타깝지만 내일은 못 갈 것 같아.

senses.note: 실제로 무섭다는 뜻이 아니라 나쁜 소식을 부드럽게 전하는 공손 표현. I'm afraid so(안타깝지만 그래요) / I'm afraid not(안타깝지만 아니에요).

senses.meaningEn: later than a time or event

examples.en: Let's play soccer after school.
I'll do my homework after dinner.

senses.note: after + 명사/동명사(after eating). 시간 표현: ten after six(미국식, 6시 10분). day after day(날마다), one after another(차례로).

senses.meaningEn: later than the time when something happens

examples.en: Call me after you get home.
After we ate, we went for a walk.
examples.ko: 우리는 밥을 먹은 후에 산책을 갔어.

senses.note: after 절도 미래라도 현재형(after you get home). 한국어 '~하고 나서'에 해당. 문장 전체를 '~ later' 로 바꿀 수 없으니 주의: '3일 후' 는 three days later.

senses.meaningEn: following or chasing someone

examples.en: The dog ran after the ball.
Close the door after you.

senses.note: look after = 돌보다, run after = 쫓다, named after = ~의 이름을 따서 짓다. 이런 구동사에서는 '시간'이 아니라 '뒤따름'의 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: in the end, especially when it is different from what was expected

examples.en: It didn't rain after all, so we went out.
examples.ko: 결국 비가 안 와서 우리는 밖에 나갔어.

examples.en: She decided to come to the party after all.

senses.note: '안 올 줄 알았는데 결국 왔다' 처럼 예상이 뒤집힐 때 문장 끝에 붙임. finally(마침내, 오래 기다리다가)와는 다름.

senses.meaningEn: used to add a reason that explains or excuses something

examples.en: Don't be too hard on him. After all, he's only five.
examples.ko: 너무 나무라지 마. 어차피 다섯 살밖에 안 됐잖아.

examples.en: Let's take a break. After all, we've worked all day.

senses.note: 문장 앞에 쓰면 '생각해 보면 당연하잖아' 라는 이유 제시. '결국' 의 뜻과 자리(문장 끝/앞)로 구별됨. '모든 것이 끝난 후에' 로 직역하면 안 됨.

senses.meaningEn: a polite way to let someone go through a door or do something before you

examples.en: After you. Oh, thank you.
Please, after you. I'm not in a hurry.

senses.note: 문 앞, 엘리베이터, 줄 서기, 음식 덜기 등에서 양보할 때. '당신 뒤에(제가 갈게요)' 라는 뜻. 답은 Thank you / No, after you(아뇨, 먼저 가세요). Go ahead 가 더 캐주얼.

senses.meaningEn: the part of the day between noon and evening

examples.en: I usually take a short nap in the afternoon.
examples.ko: 나는 보통 오후에 잠깐 낮잠을 자.

examples.en: Good afternoon, everyone. Please sit down.

senses.note: in the afternoon(오후에), this afternoon(오늘 오후에, 전치사 없음). Good afternoon 은 정오부터 저녁 전까지의 인사. 오후 3시는 three in the afternoon 또는 3 p.m.

senses.meaningEn: one more time; another time

examples.en: Could you say that again, please?
It's raining again today.

senses.note: 보통 문장 끝에 옴. once again = 다시 한번(약간 격식), again and again = 계속 반복해서. 상대 이름을 못 들었을 때: Sorry, what was your name again?

senses.meaningEn: many times, repeatedly

examples.en: I've told you again and again to close the door.
The baby watched the same video again and again.
examples.ko: 아기는 똑같은 영상을 계속 반복해서 봤어.

senses.note: over and over 와 거의 같음. 불평·잔소리 문장(I've told you again and again...) 에 특히 잘 어울림.

senses.meaningEn: how old a person or thing is

examples.en: What age is your daughter?
We're the same age.

senses.note: 나이를 물을 때는 How old are you? 가 가장 자연스러움. at the age of 10 = 열 살 때. 한국 나이와 만 나이 차이에 주의.

senses.meaningEn: a period of history

examples.en: We live in the age of the internet.
People in the Stone Age used simple tools.
examples.ko: 석기 시대 사람들은 단순한 도구를 썼어.

senses.note: the Ice Age(빙하기), the digital age(디지털 시대).

senses.meaningEn: to become older

examples.en: My grandmother has aged a lot this year.
Some people age faster than others.

senses.note: aging(미) / ageing(영) = 노화. age well = 잘 나이 들다 (사람·와인·치즈 모두).

senses.meaningEn: before now; used after a length of time

examples.en: I moved here two years ago.
She left just a few minutes ago.
examples.ko: 그녀는 몇 분 전에 막 나갔어.

senses.note: 항상 '기간 + ago' 순서(ten minutes ago). 과거형과만 쓰고 현재완료(have done)와 함께 쓰지 않는다. long ago = 오래 전에. before 는 과거 어느 시점 기준이고, ago 는 지금 기준이라는 차이가 핵심.

senses.meaningEn: to have the same opinion as someone

examples.en: I agree with you about the movie.
examples.ko: 그 영화에 대해서는 나도 네 말에 동의해.

examples.en: Do you agree that the test was hard?

senses.note: 사람에게는 agree with, 의견·계획에는 agree with / agree that. 'I'm agree' 는 틀린 표현 — 그냥 I agree.

senses.meaningEn: to say yes to a plan or request

examples.en: Mom agreed to let me stay up late.
examples.ko: 엄마가 늦게까지 안 자도 된다고 허락해 주셨어.

examples.en: We all agreed on pizza for dinner.

senses.note: agree to + 동사(하기로 하다), agree on + 명사(~로 합의하다).

senses.meaningEn: to have the same opinion as someone

examples.en: I agree with you. The movie was too long.
examples.ko: 네 말에 동의해. 영화가 너무 길었어.

examples.en: My mom doesn't agree with my plan.

senses.note: agree with + 사람/의견. agree to + 제안(수락하다), agree on + 주제(합의하다) 와 구별. 'I'm agree' 는 틀림 — agree 는 동사라서 I agree.

senses.meaningEn: (of food or weather) to be good for your health and not make you sick

examples.en: Spicy food doesn't agree with me.
examples.ko: 매운 음식은 내 몸에 안 맞아.

examples.en: The hot weather doesn't agree with my dad.
examples.ko: 더운 날씨는 아버지 몸에 안 맞아.

senses.note: 거의 항상 부정문(doesn't agree with me)으로 써서 '먹으면 탈이 난다'는 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: the mixture of gases around the earth that we breathe

examples.en: Let's open the window and get some fresh air.
examples.ko: 창문 열고 신선한 공기 좀 마시자.

examples.en: The air is very clean in the mountains.

senses.note: 불가산. fresh air = 맑은 공기, air conditioner = 에어컨, air pollution = 대기 오염.

senses.meaningEn: the space above the ground, or travel by plane

examples.en: He threw the ball high into the air.
We sent the package by air.

senses.note: in the air = 공중에, by air = 비행기로, airport = 공항, airline = 항공사.

senses.meaningEn: a machine that makes the air in a room cooler

examples.en: Please turn on the air conditioner.
The air conditioner is too loud at night.

senses.note: 줄여서 AC(미) 또는 air con(영). 한국식 '에어컨'은 그대로 말하면 안 통함. air conditioning = 냉방(시설).

senses.meaningEn: a vehicle with wings and an engine that flies through the air

examples.en: I have never been on an airplane.
examples.ko: 나 비행기 한 번도 안 타 봤어.

examples.en: The airplane landed safely in the rain.

senses.note: 미국식은 airplane, 영국식은 aeroplane. 일상 대화에선 짧게 plane 을 훨씬 많이 씀. 비행기로 = by plane/by air.

senses.meaningEn: a place where planes take off and land, with buildings for passengers

examples.en: We have to be at the airport by six.
My dad picked me up at the airport.

senses.note: 공항에 '가다/도착하다'는 go to / get to the airport, 공항에 '있다'는 at the airport. 공항 출국장은 departures, 입국장은 arrivals.

senses.meaningEn: living, not dead

examples.en: The fish is still alive.
My grandmother is 90 and still alive.

senses.note: alive 는 명사 앞에 못 씀(an alive fish ✗ → a live /laɪv/ fish, a living fish). be/stay/keep + alive 형태로 씀.

senses.meaningEn: full of energy and life

examples.en: I feel so alive after a morning run.
examples.ko: 아침에 달리고 나면 정말 살아 있는 기분이야.

examples.en: The city comes alive at night.

senses.note: feel alive(살아 있음을 느끼다), come alive(활기를 띠다) 콜로케이션.

senses.meaningEn: the whole number or amount of something

examples.en: All the cookies are gone.
I worked all day yesterday.

senses.note: all + 복수/불가산 명사. all day, all night, all week = 하루/밤/일주일 내내. every 는 단수와 씀.

senses.meaningEn: everyone or everything

examples.en: All of us went to the party.
That's all I need.

senses.note: That's all(그게 다예요)은 주문·대화를 마칠 때 유용. all of + 대명사(all of us). "all right" = 괜찮아, 좋아.

senses.meaningEn: completely or entirely

examples.en: My shoes got all wet in the rain.
I was all alone at home.

senses.note: 구어에서 강조로 자주 씀: all wet, all alone, all gone. not at all = 전혀.

senses.meaningEn: for the whole day, from morning until night

examples.en: It rained all day long yesterday.
The kids played outside all day long.

senses.note: all day 만 써도 되지만 long 을 붙이면 "정말 하루 내내" 하고 강조하는 느낌. 같은 식으로 all night long, all week long, all year long.

senses.meaningKo: 귀 기울여 듣고 있다, 어서 말해 봐
senses.meaningEn: listening carefully and ready to hear what someone is going to say

examples.en: Tell me what happened. I'm all ears.
examples.ko: 무슨 일인지 말해 봐. 다 듣고 있어.

examples.en: The kids were all ears during the story.
examples.ko: 아이들은 이야기 내내 귀를 쫑긋 세우고 들었어.

senses.note: 항상 be all ears. 상대가 "할 말이 있어" 라고 하면 "I'm all ears." 로 받는다. all eyes 는 "주목하고 보다".

senses.meaningEn: safe, well, or not hurt

examples.en: Are you all right? You look tired.
Don't worry, the kids are all right.

senses.meaningEn: used to agree to something or say yes

examples.en: All right, let's meet at six.
All right, I will call you later.

senses.note: "alright" 로 붙여 쓰기도 하지만 격식 글에서는 all right 두 단어가 표준.

senses.meaningEn: acceptable but not very good

examples.en: The pizza was all right, not great.
The movie was all right, I guess.

senses.note: 음식·영화 평가로 쓰면 "아주 좋다"가 아니라 "그냥 그렇다"에 가까움. 칭찬으로 들리지 않을 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: very often or continuously

examples.en: My little brother asks questions all the time.
We used to play together all the time.

senses.note: always 보다 '너무 자주' 라는 감정(불평·놀람) 이 섞이기 쉬움. 문장 끝에 놓음(always 는 동사 앞). It happens all the time. = 흔한 일이야.

senses.meaningEn: during the whole of a particular period

examples.en: He knew the answer all the time and said nothing.
examples.ko: 그는 내내 답을 알면서 아무 말도 안 했어.

examples.en: I was looking for my glasses, and they were on my head all the time.
examples.ko: 안경을 찾고 있었는데 줄곧 내 머리 위에 있었어.

senses.note: '어떤 일이 벌어지는 동안 내내' 라는 뜻. the whole time 으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: to let someone do something

examples.en: My parents don't allow me to stay out late.
examples.ko: 부모님은 내가 늦게까지 밖에 있는 걸 허락하지 않아.

examples.en: Are we allowed to take photos here?

senses.note: allow + 사람 + to 동사. let 은 to 없이(let me go). 안내문의 not allowed = 금지.

senses.meaningEn: to make sure you have enough time or money for something

examples.en: Allow thirty minutes to get to the airport.
Allow extra time for traffic.
examples.ko: 교통 체증 생각해서 시간을 넉넉히 잡아.

senses.note: allow + 시간/돈 = 여유를 두다. 여행 안내문에 자주 나옴.

senses.meaningEn: nearly but not completely

examples.en: Dinner is almost ready.
It's almost ten o'clock. Let's go to bed.

senses.note: almost all(거의 모두), almost never(거의 ~않다), almost every day. 'almost people'(X) → almost all people / most people.

senses.meaningEn: without other people

examples.en: I live alone in a small apartment.
Do you want to be alone for a while?

senses.note: alone 은 명사 앞에 못 씀(an alone man ✗ → a lonely man). alone 은 단순히 "혼자", lonely 는 "외로운"(감정). 혼자 있어도 외롭지 않을 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: used to tell someone not to touch or bother someone or something

examples.en: Leave me alone, I'm busy.
Please leave the dog alone while it eats.

senses.note: Leave me alone 은 꽤 강한 표현. 부드럽게는 I need some time alone 이 좋음.

senses.meaningEn: moving in a line next to something long, like a road or river

examples.en: We walked along the beach at sunset.
examples.ko: 우리는 해 질 때 해변을 따라 걸었어.

examples.en: There are many shops along this street.

senses.note: 길·강·해변처럼 '긴 것'과 함께 씀. 길 안내: Go along this road and turn left.

senses.meaningEn: together with someone, or going with them

examples.en: Can I come along to the party?
Bring your sister along next time.

senses.note: come along(같이 가다), bring ... along(데려오다, 가져오다), get along(사이가 좋다).

senses.meaningEn: the set of letters used to write a language, in a fixed order

examples.en: Can you say the alphabet backwards?
The Korean alphabet is called Hangul.

senses.note: alphabet 은 '글자 전체 체계'를 뜻함. 글자 하나는 letter. 'A, B, C 외워'는 learn the alphabet. 영어 글자 한 개를 alphabet 이라고 하면 틀림. 순서대로 = in alphabetical order.

senses.meaningEn: before now or before the expected time

examples.en: I have already finished my homework.
Is it ten o'clock already?

senses.note: 주로 긍정문·놀람을 나타내는 의문문에 씀. 부정문·일반 의문문에서는 yet 을 씀(Have you eaten yet?). 미국식은 과거형과도 자주 씀: I already ate.

senses.meaningEn: fine, safe, or acceptable

examples.en: Are you alright? That was a bad fall.
The movie was alright, nothing special.
examples.ko: 영화는 그냥 그랬어, 특별한 건 없었어.

senses.note: all right(두 단어)의 비격식 표기. 격식 있는 글에서는 all right 로 쓰는 것이 안전. 뜻과 쓰임은 okay 와 거의 같음.

senses.meaningEn: used to agree or to start saying something

examples.en: Alright, let's get started.
Alright, I'll do it your way.

senses.note: Alright 은 영국에서 인사(Alright? = 잘 지내?)로도 씀. 미국에서는 okay 가 더 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: in addition; too

examples.en: She speaks English and also a little Korean.
examples.ko: 그녀는 영어를 하고 한국어도 조금 해.

examples.en: I also want some ice cream.

senses.note: 위치: 일반동사 앞, be 동사 뒤(I also like / I am also tired). too 는 문장 끝, also 는 문장 중간. 부정문에서는 either 사용.

senses.meaningEn: every time; at all times

examples.en: I always drink coffee in the morning.
She is always late for class.

senses.note: 위치: 일반동사 앞(always drink), be 동사 뒤(is always). 빈도 순서: always > usually > often > sometimes > rarely > never. 부정은 not always(항상 ~인 것은 아니다).

senses.meaningEn: used with -ing to show that something happens too often or is a habit

examples.en: You're always losing your keys!
He's always helping other people.

senses.note: be always + -ing 는 짜증(불평) 또는 애정 섞인 칭찬의 느낌. 단순 현재(always loses)보다 감정이 실린다.

senses.meaningEn: a large place with rides and games where people go to have fun

examples.en: We're going to the amusement park this weekend.
The amusement park opens at ten in the morning.

senses.note: 놀이기구는 ride (go on a ride), 롤러코스터는 roller coaster. theme park 는 특정 주제(디즈니 등)로 꾸민 놀이공원. 한국식 '테마파크'도 통함.

senses.meaningEn: the form of 'a' used before a word that begins with a vowel sound

examples.en: Can I have an orange juice, please?
She waited for an hour at the airport.

senses.note: 철자가 아니라 소리 기준: an hour(h 묵음), an umbrella, 하지만 a university(/juː/), a European trip. 한국인이 자주 틀리는 포인트.

senses.meaningEn: a person who gets up early in the morning or arrives early

examples.en: My dad is an early bird. He's up at five.
I'm not an early bird. I hate mornings.
examples.ko: 나는 아침형 인간이 아니야. 아침이 싫어.

senses.note: 속담 The early bird catches the worm(일찍 일어나는 새가 벌레를 잡는다)에서 옴. 쇼핑·공연에서 early bird price/discount 는 '조기 예약 할인'.

senses.meaningEn: belonging to a time thousands of years ago

examples.en: We learned about ancient Egypt in class today.
examples.ko: 오늘 수업에서 고대 이집트에 대해 배웠어.

examples.en: These ancient coins are over two thousand years old.

senses.note: ancient Greece, ancient Rome 처럼 문명 이름 앞에 자주 붙음. 발음은 '에인션트'(앤시언트 아님).

senses.meaningEn: very old, often said as a joke

examples.en: My phone is ancient. It barely works.
examples.ko: 내 폰 완전 골동품이야. 겨우 돌아가.

examples.en: That ancient car still runs somehow.
examples.ko: 그 고물 차가 어떻게 아직 달리네.

senses.note: 물건이 너무 낡았다고 과장할 때 쓰는 농담 표현.

senses.meaningEn: used to join two words, phrases, or sentences together

examples.en: I like coffee and cake.
We watched a movie and went home.

senses.note: 셋 이상 나열할 때는 마지막 것 앞에만 and: apples, bananas, and milk. 구어에서는 /ən/ 으로 약하게 발음(bread 'n' butter).

senses.meaningEn: used to say that one thing happens after or because of another

examples.en: Press this button and the door opens.
Work hard and you'll pass the test.

senses.note: 명령문 + and + 결과 = '~하면 ~된다'. 반대 결과는 or(Hurry up, or you'll be late).

senses.meaningEn: the strong feeling you have when someone has done something bad or unfair

examples.en: He shouted in anger and left the room.
examples.ko: 그는 화가 나서 소리치고 방을 나갔어.

examples.en: Take a deep breath to control your anger.

senses.note: 형용사는 angry. in anger(화가 나서), control your anger(화를 다스리다). 불가산 명사라 an anger 라고 하지 않음.

senses.meaningEn: feeling strong displeasure because of something bad or unfair

examples.en: Mom was angry because I came home late.
Please don't be angry with me.

senses.note: angry with/at + 사람, angry about + 일. get angry(화가 나다). 미국 구어에서는 mad 를 더 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: a living thing that can move and eat, such as a dog, bird, or fish

examples.en: What's your favorite animal?
We saw lots of animals at the zoo today.

senses.note: pet 은 '집에서 키우는 동물', wild animal 은 '야생 동물'. 사람을 animal 이라고 하면 '짐승 같다'는 욕이 되니 주의.

senses.meaningEn: relating to or coming from animals

examples.en: He doesn't eat any animal products.
examples.ko: 그는 동물성 식품을 전혀 안 먹어.

examples.en: We're learning about animal homes in science class.
examples.ko: 과학 시간에 동물의 집에 대해 배우고 있어.

senses.note: animal products(동물성 식품), animal rights(동물 권리), animal lover(동물을 사랑하는 사람).

senses.meaningEn: the joint between your foot and your leg

examples.en: I twisted my ankle on the stairs.
Her ankle is swollen, so she can't walk well.
examples.ko: 발목이 부어서 그녀는 잘 못 걸어.

senses.note: 발목을 삐다 = twist / sprain my ankle. 손목은 wrist.

senses.meaningEn: one more person or thing of the same kind

examples.en: Can I have another cup of coffee?
Let's wait another ten minutes.

senses.note: another 는 an + other 이므로 단수 명사와만 씀(another people ✗). 단, another ten minutes 처럼 숫자 묶음 앞에는 가능.

senses.meaningEn: a different one

examples.en: That's another story.
Let's try another restaurant tonight.
examples.ko: 오늘 밤엔 다른 식당에 가 보자.

senses.note: "하나 더"와 "다른 것" 두 뜻이 있어서 문맥으로 구분. one another = 서로.

senses.meaningEn: what you say or write when someone asks a question

examples.en: What's the answer to number three?
I don't know the answer, sorry.

senses.note: the answer to the question(전치사 to). 정답 = the right/correct answer, 오답 = the wrong answer.

senses.meaningEn: to say or write something as a reply, or to pick up the phone

examples.en: Please answer the question in English.
Nobody answered the phone when I called.
examples.ko: 내가 전화했을 때 아무도 안 받았어.

senses.note: answer the question(to 없이, answer to ✗). answer the phone/door = 전화를 받다/문을 열어 주다.

senses.meaningEn: to pick up the phone when it rings and speak

examples.en: Can you answer the phone? I'm cooking.
examples.ko: 전화 좀 받아 줄래? 나 요리 중이야.

examples.en: Nobody answered the phone at the office.

senses.note: 한국어 '전화를 받다'를 receive the phone 이라고 하면 틀림. answer the phone / pick up (the phone). 구어로 Can you get that?(전화·문 등 받아 줄래?). 반대는 hang up(전화를 끊다).

senses.meaningEn: a very small insect that lives in large groups

examples.en: There are ants all over the kitchen floor!
An ant can carry food bigger than itself.
examples.ko: 개미는 자기보다 큰 먹이도 옮길 수 있어.

senses.note: aunt(이모/고모)와 미국식 발음이 같음(/ænt/). 문맥으로 구별.

senses.meaningEn: used in questions and negatives to mean some

examples.en: Do you have any questions?
I don't have any money right now.

senses.note: not ... any = no. I don't have any money = I have no money. 긍정문에는 some.

senses.meaningEn: it does not matter which one

examples.en: Call me any time you need help.
Any color is fine with me.

senses.note: 긍정문의 any 는 "아무 ~든지". anytime, anyone, anything 도 같은 뜻. 한국어 "아무"와 닮음.

senses.meaningEn: used in questions and negative sentences to mean any person

examples.en: Is anybody home?
I don't know anybody in this city.
examples.ko: 이 도시에는 아는 사람이 아무도 없어.

senses.note: anyone 과 같은 뜻, 조금 더 구어적.

senses.meaningEn: used in positive sentences to mean any person at all

examples.en: Anybody can join the club.
Ask anybody; they all know her.

senses.meaningEn: used in questions and negative sentences to mean any person

examples.en: Does anyone know the answer?
I didn't see anyone at the park.

senses.note: 부정문에서 '아무도 ~않다'는 not ... anyone 또는 no one: I saw no one. = I didn't see anyone. 둘 다 부정(didn't + no one)은 틀림.

senses.meaningEn: used in positive sentences to mean any person at all

examples.en: Anyone can learn to swim.
Anyone who wants to come is welcome.

senses.meaningEn: any thing; used in questions and negative sentences

examples.en: Do you need anything from the store?
I didn't eat anything for breakfast.

senses.note: 의문·부정문의 something. not ... anything = nothing: I didn't eat anything = I ate nothing. 식당에서 Anything else?(더 필요하신 건요?).

senses.meaningEn: it does not matter what; every kind of thing

examples.en: I'm so hungry. I'll eat anything.
You can ask me anything.

senses.note: 긍정문에서 쓰면 '뭐든 상관없다'는 뜻. 메뉴 고르기 귀찮을 때: Anything is fine.

senses.meaningEn: in, at, or to any place; used in questions and negatives

examples.en: I can't find my glasses anywhere.
Did you go anywhere fun this weekend?
examples.ko: 이번 주말에 어디 재미있는 데 갔어?

senses.note: 의문·부정문의 somewhere. 부정문에서 '어디에도 없다'는 not ... anywhere = nowhere. 긍정문에서 쓰면 '어디든지': You can sit anywhere.

senses.meaningKo: 아파트(한 가구가 사는 집), 공동 주택의 한 집
senses.meaningEn: a set of rooms for living in, inside a larger building

examples.en: I rent a one-bedroom apartment downtown.
examples.ko: 시내에 방 하나짜리 아파트를 빌려 살아.

examples.en: Her apartment is on the fifth floor.

senses.note: 영어 apartment 는 '건물'이 아니라 '한 집(호)'. 건물 전체는 apartment building. 영국식은 flat.

senses.meaningEn: to say that you are sorry for something you did

examples.en: I apologize for being late this morning.
He apologized for breaking my cup.
examples.ko: 그는 내 컵을 깨뜨린 것에 대해 사과했어.

senses.note: apologize for + 잘못(명사/동명사), apologize to + 사람: I apologized to her for the mistake. 'I'm sorry for ~' 보다 조금 더 격식 있음. 영국식 철자는 apologise.

senses.meaningEn: a round fruit with red or green skin and white inside

examples.en: I packed an apple for your lunch.
These apples are sweet and crunchy.

senses.note: 모음으로 시작하므로 an apple. apple pie(사과 파이), apple juice. 속담 An apple a day keeps the doctor away = 하루 사과 하나면 의사가 필요 없다.

senses.meaningEn: the fourth month of the year

examples.en: It rains a lot in April.
Her baby is due in early April.

senses.note: April Fools' Day(4월 1일, 만우절). April showers bring May flowers 라는 속담이 유명. 줄임말 Apr.

senses.meaningEn: to speak angrily to someone because you disagree with them

examples.en: My parents argued about money again last night.
examples.ko: 어젯밤에 부모님이 또 돈 문제로 다투셨어.

examples.en: Stop arguing and help me clean up.

senses.note: argue with 사람 about/over 주제. 명사는 argument(have an argument = 말다툼하다). fight 보다 말로만 하는 다툼.

senses.meaningEn: to give reasons why you think something is true or right

examples.en: She argued that homework should be shorter.
examples.ko: 그녀는 숙제가 더 짧아져야 한다고 주장했어.

examples.en: You can't argue with the facts.

senses.note: argue that + 문장. 'You can't argue with that.' = 그 말엔 반박할 수 없네(동의 표현).

senses.meaningEn: one of the two long parts of your body from your shoulders to your hands

examples.en: I broke my arm playing soccer.
She was carrying a baby in her arms.

senses.note: 한국어 '팔'에는 손이 포함되기도 하지만 arm 은 어깨~손목까지. arm in arm = 팔짱을 끼고. 팔꿈치 = elbow, 손목 = wrist.

senses.meaningEn: on every side of something, or in a circle

examples.en: We sat around the table and talked.
She put a scarf around her neck.

senses.note: 영국식은 round 도 같은 뜻. '동네를 돌아다니다'는 walk around the neighborhood.

senses.meaningEn: about; a little more or less than a number

examples.en: I'll be there around seven.
The ticket costs around ten dollars.

senses.note: 시간·숫자 앞에서 '~쯤'. around seven = about seven. 격식 글에서는 approximately.

senses.meaningEn: here and there, or nearby

examples.en: Let's look around the shop first.
Is there a bank around here?

senses.note: around here(이 근처), look around(둘러보다), turn around(뒤돌다).

senses.meaningEn: to get to the place you are going to

examples.en: What time does the train arrive?
We arrived in Tokyo late at night.

senses.note: 도시·국가처럼 넓은 곳은 arrive in, 역·공항·집 같은 지점은 arrive at. 'arrive to' 는 틀림. 구어에서는 get to 를 더 많이 씀(get to the airport). 명사 arrival(도착).

senses.meaningEn: the school subject where you draw, paint, and make things

examples.en: We painted flowers in art class today.
Art is my favorite class of the week.
examples.ko: 미술은 이번 주 중 가장 좋아하는 수업이야.

senses.note: art class = 미술 수업. 미술 선생님 = art teacher. 셀 수 없는 명사.

senses.meaningEn: paintings, drawings, and other beautiful things people make

examples.en: She loves modern art.
There's a lot of art on the walls.
examples.ko: 벽에 미술 작품이 많이 걸려 있어.

senses.note: art museum/gallery = 미술관. 예술가는 artist. the arts(복수) = 예술 전반(음악·연극 포함).

senses.meaningEn: a person who makes art, especially paintings or drawings

examples.en: The artist painted a picture of the sea.
My sister is an artist and sells her drawings.

senses.note: artist 는 그림뿐 아니라 조각·사진 등 예술 전반. 그림만 그리는 사람은 painter.

senses.meaningEn: a singer or musician who records songs

examples.en: Who is your favorite K-pop artist?
The artist sang three new songs at the show.
examples.ko: 그 아티스트는 공연에서 신곡 세 곡을 불렀어.

senses.note: 음악 앱의 Artist 항목처럼 '가수·음악인'의 뜻. 한국어 '아티스트'와 거의 같은 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: used to compare two things that are the same in some way

examples.en: She is as tall as her mother.
Come as soon as you can.

senses.note: as + 형용사/부사 + as. 부정은 not as ~ as(= less than). as soon as possible = 가능한 한 빨리(ASAP).

senses.meaningEn: used to say what job or role someone or something has

examples.en: She works as a nurse.
We used the box as a table.

senses.note: work as + 직업. like 는 '~처럼(비슷하게)', as 는 '실제로 ~로서': He works as a teacher(진짜 교사) vs He talks like a teacher.

senses.meaningEn: while something is happening, or because

examples.en: I saw her as I was leaving.
As it was late, we went home.

senses.note: '~하면서' 는 while 과 비슷, '~때문에' 는 because 보다 약하고 약간 격식. 초급에서는 as ~ as, work as 두 가지를 먼저 익히면 충분.

senses.meaningEn: as quickly as you can

examples.en: Please call me back as soon as possible.
examples.ko: 가능한 한 빨리 다시 전화 주세요.

examples.en: We need to leave as soon as possible.
examples.ko: 우리 가능한 한 빨리 출발해야 해.

senses.note: 줄여서 ASAP(에이에스에이피 / 에이샙) 로 쓰며 이메일·메시지에서 매우 흔함. 다만 ASAP 은 재촉하는 느낌이 있어 고객에게는 at your earliest convenience 가 더 부드러움.

senses.meaningEn: too; also

examples.en: I'd like a coffee and a cookie as well.
Can my sister come as well?

senses.note: 문장 맨 끝에 놓음(too 와 위치 같음). also 는 보통 동사 앞. 부정문에서는 쓰지 않고 either 를 씀: I don't like it either. as well as = ~뿐 아니라 ~도.

senses.meaningEn: to say something to someone in order to get an answer

examples.en: Can I ask you a question?
She asked me where I live.

senses.note: ask someone something (ask to someone ✗). 질문하다 = ask a question (question 만 동사로 쓰면 '심문하다' 느낌).

senses.meaningEn: to tell someone you want them to do or give something

examples.en: I asked him to help me with my homework.
Just ask for help if you need it.

senses.note: ask for + 원하는 것(ask for water), ask someone to + 동사(부탁). ask about = ~에 대해 묻다.

senses.meaningEn: to invite someone to go somewhere

examples.en: He asked me to his birthday party.
Why don't you ask her out?
examples.ko: 그녀에게 데이트 신청해 보는 게 어때?

senses.note: ask someone out = 데이트를 신청하다. ask someone over = 집에 초대하다.

senses.meaningEn: to say something in order to get information or an answer

examples.en: Can I ask a question about the homework?
examples.ko: 숙제에 대해 질문 하나 해도 돼요?

examples.en: The students asked a lot of questions.

senses.note: '질문하다'는 ask a question(question 만 동사로 쓰면 '의심하다'). ask + 사람 + a question: Let me ask you a question. 'ask to him' 은 틀림, ask him.

senses.meaningEn: to say that you want someone to give you something

examples.en: Let's ask for the check.
She asked for a glass of water.
examples.ko: 그녀는 물 한 잔을 달라고 했어.

senses.note: ask + 사람 + 질문(ask him a question), ask for + 물건(ask for help). '도움을 요청하다'는 ask for help, ask help ✗.

senses.meaningEn: to say that you want to speak to a particular person

examples.en: Someone called and asked for you.
Go to the front desk and ask for Mr. Lee.
examples.ko: 안내 데스크에 가서 이 선생님을 찾으세요.

senses.note: 전화나 방문에서 특정인을 찾을 때. You asked for it.(네가 자초한 거야) 라는 관용 표현도 있음.

senses.meaningEn: sleeping

examples.en: The baby is asleep. Please be quiet.
examples.ko: 아기가 자고 있어. 조용히 해 줘.

examples.en: I fell asleep on the bus again.

senses.note: asleep 은 명사 앞에 못 씀(an asleep baby ✗ → a sleeping baby). fall asleep = 잠들다(동작), be asleep = 자고 있다(상태). sleep 은 동사.

senses.meaningEn: (of an arm or leg) having no feeling because of pressure

examples.en: My leg is asleep from sitting too long.
examples.ko: 너무 오래 앉아 있어서 다리가 저려.

examples.en: My arm fell asleep while I was reading.

senses.note: 한국어 "다리가 저리다"를 영어로는 "다리가 잠들었다"고 표현. numb 도 같은 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: used to say exactly where someone or something is

examples.en: Let's meet at the bus stop.
She's at work right now.

senses.note: 한 지점으로 보는 장소: at home, at school, at work, at the door. 공간 '안' 을 강조하면 in. at the station(만나는 지점) vs in the station(건물 안).

senses.meaningEn: used before a time of day

examples.en: The class starts at nine.
I usually go to bed at midnight.

senses.note: at 9:00, at noon, at night, at the weekend(영국). 요일은 on, 월은 in. 'at the morning' 은 틀림 → in the morning.

senses.meaningEn: used to show who or what an action is directed toward

examples.en: Why are you looking at me?
He smiled at the baby.

senses.note: look at, smile at, laugh at(비웃다), shout at(화내며 소리치다). shout to 는 단순히 멀리서 부르는 것.

senses.meaningEn: used after adjectives like good or bad to say what skill you mean

examples.en: She's really good at math.
I'm bad at remembering names.
examples.ko: 나는 이름 기억하는 걸 잘 못해.

senses.note: good/bad/great/terrible at + 명사/동명사. 'good in English' 보다 good at English 가 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: in the beginning, before something changed

examples.en: At first, I didn't like the city.
examples.ko: 처음엔 그 도시가 마음에 안 들었어.

examples.en: At first it was hard, but now it is easy.

senses.note: 뒤에 but / later / now 가 따라와 "나중엔 달라졌다"는 뜻을 품음. 순서 나열의 "첫째로"는 first 또는 firstly 를 쓰고 at first 는 쓰지 않음.

senses.meaningEn: in the house or place where you live

examples.en: Is your mom at home right now?
I stayed at home all weekend.

senses.note: '집에' 라는 뜻으로 at home 에는 the 를 붙이지 않음(not 'at the home'). 미국 구어에서는 stay home, be home 처럼 at 을 빼기도 함.

senses.meaningKo: (feel at home) 편안한, 내 집 같은
senses.meaningEn: feeling relaxed and comfortable in a place or with people

examples.en: Please sit down and make yourself at home.
I feel at home in this city now.
examples.ko: 이제 이 도시가 내 집처럼 편해.

senses.note: 손님에게 쓰는 Make yourself at home. 은 '편하게 계세요' 라는 환영 인사. feel at home with + 사람/것 = ~이 익숙하고 편하다.

senses.meaningEn: finally, after a long wait or a lot of effort

examples.en: At last, the bus is here!
We found a parking spot at last.

senses.note: 오래 기다리거나 애쓴 끝에 이루어졌다는 안도감이 담김. 단순한 순서의 "마지막으로"는 finally/lastly 를 쓰고 at last 는 쓰지 않음.

senses.meaningEn: not less than a number or amount

examples.en: It costs at least fifty dollars.
You should sleep at least seven hours.

senses.note: 숫자 앞에서 "최소". 반대는 at most(최대). 발음은 /ət ˈliːst/, least 를 last 와 헷갈리지 않도록 주의.

senses.meaningEn: used to mention a good point in a bad situation

examples.en: It rained, but at least we had umbrellas.
At least you tried. Good job.

senses.note: 나쁜 상황에서 위안이 되는 점을 꺼낼 때. "Well, at least..."로 시작하는 말이 많음.

senses.meaningEn: during the night

examples.en: I can't sleep well at night.
The city is beautiful at night.

senses.note: 하루 시간대 중 night 만 at 을 씀: in the morning / in the afternoon / in the evening / at night / at noon / at midnight. 특정한 밤은 on Friday night, 늦은 밤은 late at night.

senses.meaningEn: at twelve o'clock in the middle of the day

examples.en: Let's have lunch at noon.
The meeting starts at noon sharp.

senses.note: noon = 12 p.m.(낮), midnight = 12 a.m.(밤). 둘 다 at 을 씀: at noon, at midnight. '정오쯤' 은 around noon. 영국에서는 midday 도 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: in the school building, usually for lessons

examples.en: The kids are at school until three.
I learned this song at school.

senses.note: '학교에서 공부 중' 이라는 뜻이면 at school(the 없음). at the school 은 건물 자체를 가리킴(There's a fire at the school.). 영국식 in school 과 미국식 in school 은 '재학 중' 의 뜻.

headword: at the end of the day

senses.meaningEn: used to say what is most important after everything has been considered

examples.en: At the end of the day, family is what matters.
At the end of the day, it's your choice.

senses.note: 실제 '하루가 끝날 때' 가 아니라 '모든 걸 따져 보면 결론은' 이라는 뜻. 의견을 마무리할 때 자주 씀. 너무 자주 쓰면 말버릇처럼 들릴 수 있음.

senses.meaningKo: (글자 그대로) 하루가 끝날 때, 퇴근 무렵에
senses.meaningEn: at the time when the day's work or activities finish

examples.en: I'm always tired at the end of the day.
examples.ko: 하루가 끝날 때쯤이면 난 늘 피곤해.

examples.en: We clean the kitchen at the end of the day.
examples.ko: 우리는 하루 마감할 때 주방을 청소해.

senses.note: 문맥에 따라 글자 그대로의 뜻으로도 쓰임. 뒤에 tired, clean up, go home 같은 말이 오면 글자 그대로의 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: now; at this present time

examples.en: I'm busy at the moment. Can I call you back?
examples.ko: 지금 좀 바빠. 다시 전화해도 돼?

examples.en: We don't have any milk at the moment.

senses.note: 보통 현재형·현재진행형과 함께 쓰며, '지금은 이렇지만 바뀔 수 있다' 는 뉘앙스. 문장 끝이나 앞에 둠. 한 단어 momentarily 와는 다른 표현.

senses.meaningEn: used politely to say that someone or something is not available right now

examples.en: Mr. Kim is not in the office at the moment.
examples.ko: 김 선생님은 지금 사무실에 안 계십니다.

examples.en: That item is sold out at the moment.

senses.note: '지금은 안 됩니다' 를 부드럽게 말할 때 자주 붙임. for the moment(당분간은)와 구별.

senses.meaningEn: happening together, at one moment

examples.en: We both laughed at the same time.
Don't talk and eat at the same time.

senses.meaningEn: used to add a point that seems the opposite of what you just said

examples.en: I'm happy, but at the same time I'm nervous.
It's expensive. At the same time, it lasts long.
examples.ko: 비싸긴 해. 그래도 한편으론 오래 쓰잖아.

senses.note: 앞 내용과 반대되는 점을 덧붙일 때. 시간의 "동시에"와 구분할 것. 보통 but at the same time 형태.

senses.meaningEn: at the place where you have a job, or busy doing your job

examples.en: Dad is still at work. He'll be late.
I can't talk now. I'm at work.
examples.ko: 지금 통화 못 해. 일하는 중이야.

senses.note: the 를 붙이지 않음. '회사에 있다' 는 at work 또는 at the office. 한국어 '회사' 를 그대로 at company 라고 하면 틀림.

senses.meaningEn: to try to hurt someone or something using violence

examples.en: A big dog attacked the little boy.
The soldiers attacked the town at night.

senses.note: attack 뒤에 전치사 없이 바로 목적어. 말로 공격(비난)할 때도 쓴다.

senses.meaningEn: a sudden short period of illness

examples.en: He had a heart attack last year.
She gets asthma attacks when it is cold.

senses.note: heart attack(심장마비), panic attack(공황 발작). have/get an attack.

senses.meaningEn: the eighth month of the year

examples.en: We always go to the beach in August.
The new school year begins in late August.

senses.note: 강세는 첫 음절(AU-gust). 형용사 august(/ɔːˈɡʌst/, 위엄 있는)는 강세가 달라 전혀 다른 단어. 줄임말 Aug.

senses.meaningEn: the sister of your mother or father, or the wife of your uncle

examples.en: My aunt lives in Busan with her two kids.
examples.ko: 우리 이모는 아이 둘과 부산에 사셔.

examples.en: Aunt Mary is coming for dinner tonight.
examples.ko: 메리 고모가 오늘 저녁 식사하러 오셔.

senses.note: 이모·고모·숙모 모두 aunt 하나로 표현. 이름과 함께 쓸 때 Aunt Mary 처럼 대문자. 발음은 ant 와 같게 /ænt/ 가 미국식.

senses.meaningEn: the season between summer and winter

examples.en: Autumn is the best time to visit Korea.
examples.ko: 가을은 한국을 여행하기 가장 좋은 때야.

examples.en: The autumn leaves were beautiful.

senses.note: 영국식에서 주로 쓰고, 미국식은 fall 이 더 흔하다. 끝의 n 은 발음하지 않는다(/ˈɔːtəm/). 형용사형 autumnal 은 격식 있는 표현.

senses.meaningEn: not sleeping

examples.en: Are you still awake? It's midnight.
The coffee kept me awake all night.
examples.ko: 커피 때문에 밤새 잠을 못 잤어.

senses.note: stay awake(깨어 있다), keep someone awake(잠 못 자게 하다), wide awake(완전히 깬). 명사 앞에는 못 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to stop sleeping or to make someone stop sleeping

examples.en: I awoke to the sound of rain.
She awoke early on her birthday.

senses.note: 동사 awake 는 문어적. 일상 대화에서는 wake up 을 씀(I woke up at seven). awake-awoke-awoken.

senses.meaningEn: to or at a distance from a place or person

examples.en: Go away! I'm busy right now.
The school is two blocks away from here.
examples.ko: 학교는 여기서 두 블록 떨어져 있어.

senses.note: 거리 표현: ten minutes away(10분 거리), far away(멀리). run away(도망가다), put away(치우다).

senses.meaningEn: not at home, at work, or at school because you went somewhere

examples.en: I'll be away next week on vacation.
examples.ko: 다음 주에는 휴가로 자리를 비울 거야.

examples.en: My parents are away for the weekend.
examples.ko: 부모님은 주말 동안 집에 안 계셔.

senses.note: be away = 멀리 가 있다(여행·출장). out 은 잠깐 외출, away 는 며칠 떠나 있을 때.

senses.meaningEn: very bad or unpleasant

examples.en: The food at that restaurant was awful.
What an awful day! Everything went wrong.

senses.note: terrible 과 거의 같은 세기. 냄새·맛·날씨에 특히 자주(an awful smell). 명사 awe(경외) 와 달리 awful 은 좋은 뜻이 없음.

senses.meaningEn: feeling very ill or very upset

examples.en: I feel awful. My head really hurts.
examples.ko: 몸이 몹시 안 좋아. 머리가 너무 아파.

examples.en: She felt awful about forgetting his birthday.
examples.ko: 그녀는 그의 생일을 잊어서 몹시 미안해했어.

senses.note: feel awful about + 일 = ~이 몹시 미안하다·마음에 걸린다. 부사 awfully 는 구어에서 '몹시'(awfully nice)로도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: a very young child who cannot walk or talk yet

examples.en: The baby is sleeping, so please be quiet.
examples.ko: 아기가 자고 있으니까 조용히 해 줘.

examples.en: My sister just had a baby girl.

senses.note: have a baby = 아기를 낳다. 아기를 가리킬 때 it 대신 he/she 를 쓰는 게 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: a name you call someone you love

examples.en: Good morning, baby. Did you sleep well?
Baby, I'll call you after work.

senses.note: 연인·배우자 사이의 애칭. 모르는 사람에게 쓰면 매우 무례함.

senses.meaningEn: made for babies, or very small and young

examples.en: We need to buy some baby clothes.
Look at the baby birds in the nest!
examples.ko: 둥지 안의 아기 새들 좀 봐!

senses.note: baby carrots(작은 당근), baby teeth(유치)처럼 작은 것에도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: the part of your body from your neck to the top of your legs, behind you

examples.en: My back hurts from sitting all day.
examples.ko: 하루 종일 앉아 있었더니 허리가 아파.

examples.en: Lie on your back and relax.

senses.note: 한국어 '허리'도 보통 back 이라고 함(lower back = 허리 아래쪽). waist 는 허리둘레 부위.

senses.meaningEn: to or at the place where someone or something was before

examples.en: I'll be back in five minutes.
When did you get back from Busan?

senses.note: come back(돌아오다), go back(돌아가다), get back(도착해 돌아오다), give back(돌려주다).

senses.meaningEn: the part of something that is farthest from the front

examples.en: Your name is on the back of the card.
Let's sit at the back of the bus.

senses.note: in the back of(안쪽 뒤), at the back of(뒤쪽에), behind(~의 뒤에)를 구분.

senses.meaningEn: going in one direction and then the opposite direction, many times

examples.en: The dog ran back and forth in the yard.
I go back and forth between Seoul and Busan for work.
examples.ko: 일 때문에 서울과 부산을 오가고 있어.

senses.note: 두 장소를 오가는 반복 이동. 영국식은 backwards and forwards. 비유적으로 '이야기가 오가다' 도 됨: We emailed back and forth. go back and forth on a decision = 결정을 두고 왔다 갔다(망설이다).

senses.meaningEn: a door at the back of a house or building

examples.en: Please use the back door; the front is locked.
The dog came in through the back door.

senses.note: 비유적으로 '뒷거래·편법'의 뜻도 있지만 초급에서는 실제 문으로만 쓰면 충분.

senses.meaningEn: to make a copy of computer files so you do not lose them

examples.en: Back up your photos before you change phones.
I back up my files every Friday.

senses.note: 명사는 backup(백업 파일). 한국어 '백업'과 같은 뜻. back up to the cloud(클라우드에 백업).

senses.meaningEn: to move backwards, especially in a car

examples.en: Back up a little. You're too close to the wall.
Everyone, please back up and give him some room.
examples.ko: 모두 뒤로 물러나서 공간을 좀 주세요.

senses.note: 운전할 때 '후진하다'는 미국에서 back up, 영국에서는 reverse 가 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: to support someone or say that what they said is true

examples.en: Thanks for backing me up at the meeting.
examples.ko: 회의에서 내 편 들어 줘서 고마워.

examples.en: Can you back up your story with photos?
examples.ko: 네 이야기를 사진으로 뒷받침할 수 있어?

senses.note: back someone up(사람을 지지하다), back up a claim(주장을 뒷받침하다). 교통 체증은 traffic is backed up.

senses.meaningEn: a bag that you carry on your back

examples.en: My backpack is so heavy today.
Put your lunch box in your backpack.

senses.note: 미국에서는 학생 책가방도 backpack. 한국식 '백(bag)' 하나로 말하면 무슨 가방인지 불분명.

senses.meaningEn: not good; unpleasant or of low quality

examples.en: I had a bad day at work.
The weather is getting worse.

senses.note: 비교급 worse, 최상급 worst. 'badder' 는 틀림. 'That's too bad.' 는 '아쉽다/안타깝다' 는 위로 표현.

senses.meaningEn: serious or harmful to your health

examples.en: I have a bad cold this week.
Too much sugar is bad for you.
examples.ko: 설탕을 너무 많이 먹으면 몸에 나빠.

senses.note: be bad for + 사람/건강. a bad headache, a bad back(허리가 안 좋음).

senses.meaningEn: no longer fresh and not safe to eat

examples.en: The fish smells bad. Don't eat it.
examples.ko: 그 생선 상한 냄새가 나. 먹지 마.

examples.en: The milk went bad in the heat.

senses.note: go bad = 상하다. smell/taste bad 처럼 감각동사 뒤에는 형용사 bad(badly 아님).

senses.meaningEn: feeling sorry or guilty about something

examples.en: I feel bad about forgetting your birthday.
Don't feel bad. It wasn't your fault.

senses.note: feel bad about + 명사/동명사. 'feel badly' 보다 'feel bad' 가 표준.

senses.meaningEn: in a way that is not good or skillful

examples.en: I play the piano very badly.
The team played badly in the second half.

senses.note: bad 는 형용사, badly 는 부사: play badly(O), play bad(X, 구어에선 쓰기도). 비교급 worse, 최상급 worst.

senses.meaningEn: very much or seriously

examples.en: He hurt his knee badly in the game.
I badly need a cup of coffee.

senses.note: badly hurt(심하게 다친), badly need/want(몹시 필요하다·원하다). 이때는 '나쁘게'가 아니라 '매우'의 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: a game in which players hit a small feathered object over a high net with light rackets

examples.en: We play badminton in the park every evening.
examples.ko: 우리는 매일 저녁 공원에서 배드민턴을 쳐.

examples.en: Badminton is easy to learn and fun.

senses.note: 발음 주의: '배드민턴'이 아니라 /ˈbædmɪntən/, 중간의 t 소리를 약하게. 셔틀콕은 shuttlecock 또는 birdie.

senses.meaningEn: a container made of cloth or leather that you carry things in

examples.en: I left my bag on the bus.
What's in your bag? It looks heavy.

senses.note: 가방 종류: backpack(배낭), handbag/purse(핸드백), shopping bag. 책가방은 school bag.

senses.meaningEn: a thin paper or plastic container for carrying things you buy

examples.en: Do you need a bag for that?
I bought a bag of chips.

senses.note: plastic bag(비닐봉지), paper bag(종이봉지). a bag of ~ = ~ 한 봉지. 계산대에서 "봉투 드릴까요?"는 Do you need a bag?

senses.meaningEn: a packet of thin fried potato slices

examples.en: I ate a whole bag of chips while watching TV.
examples.ko: TV 보면서 감자칩 한 봉지를 다 먹었어.

examples.en: Grab a bag of chips for the party.
examples.ko: 파티에 가져갈 감자칩 한 봉지 집어 와.

senses.note: 미국에서 chips 는 감자칩, 영국에서는 감자튀김(미국의 fries). 영국식으로는 a packet of crisps. a bag of 는 봉지에 든 것 전반에 쓴다: a bag of rice/candy/popcorn.

senses.meaningEn: to cook bread, cakes, or cookies in an oven

examples.en: I'm going to bake cookies this weekend.
My mom bakes bread every Sunday.

senses.note: 오븐에 굽는 것이 bake. 불판·그릴에 고기를 굽는 것은 grill, 팬에 굽는 것은 fry, 토스터는 toast. baked potato = 오븐에 구운 감자.

senses.meaningEn: a person who makes and sells bread and cakes

examples.en: The baker gets up at four every morning.
My mom is a great baker. Try her cookies!
examples.ko: 우리 엄마는 빵을 정말 잘 구워. 쿠키 먹어 봐!

senses.note: a great baker = 빵·과자를 잘 만드는 사람(직업 아니어도 됨). 빵집은 bakery, 빵 굽는 동작은 bake.

senses.meaningEn: a shop where bread and cakes are made or sold

examples.en: There's a new bakery next to the station.
I bought some fresh bread at the bakery.
examples.ko: 빵집에서 갓 나온 빵을 좀 샀어.

senses.note: bakery 는 가게, baker 는 빵 굽는 사람. 한국식 '제과점'의 케이크·쿠키도 bakery 에서 판다.

senses.meaningEn: a round object that you throw, kick, or hit in games

examples.en: Throw the ball to me!
The kids kicked the ball across the park.

senses.note: throw/catch/kick/hit a ball. 공 모양의 둥근 것에도 씀: a ball of rice(주먹밥), snowball(눈덩이).

senses.meaningEn: a big formal party where people dance

examples.en: Cinderella went to the ball in a beautiful dress.
examples.ko: 신데렐라는 예쁜 드레스를 입고 무도회에 갔어.

examples.en: The prince danced all night at the ball.

senses.note: 동화에 자주 나오는 뜻. have a ball(아주 즐거운 시간을 보내다) 이라는 구어 표현도 여기서 나옴.

senses.meaningEn: a small rubber bag that you fill with air to play with or use as a decoration

examples.en: Let's blow up some balloons for the party.
The red balloon flew up into the sky.

senses.note: blow up a balloon = 풍선을 불다, pop a balloon = 풍선을 터뜨리다. 열기구는 hot-air balloon.

senses.meaningEn: a long, curved fruit with a yellow skin

examples.en: I usually have a banana before I run.
examples.ko: 나는 보통 뛰기 전에 바나나를 하나 먹어.

examples.en: The bananas are still green.

senses.note: 발음은 [바나나]가 아니라 [버내너], 둘째 음절에 강세. 한 송이는 a bunch of bananas. go bananas = 미친 듯이 흥분하다(구어).

senses.meaningEn: a group of people who play music together

examples.en: My friends and I started a band last year.
The band played for two hours.

senses.note: rock band, school band, marching band(고적대). 밴드 멤버는 band member, 밴드를 만들다는 start/form a band. 클래식 오케스트라는 orchestra.

senses.meaningEn: a thin flat piece of material that goes around something

examples.en: She tied her hair back with a band.
Put a rubber band around the cards.

senses.note: rubber band(고무줄), hair band(머리띠/머리끈), wristband(손목 밴드). 상처용 밴드는 Band-Aid(상표명) 또는 bandage.

senses.meaningEn: a long piece of cloth you wrap around a hurt part of the body

examples.en: The nurse put a bandage on my arm.
examples.ko: 간호사가 내 팔에 붕대를 감아 줬어.

examples.en: Do you have a bandage? I cut my finger.

senses.note: 미국에서는 작은 일회용 밴드를 Band-Aid(상표명)라고 부르는 경우가 많다. 붕대를 감다 put on a bandage.

senses.meaningEn: to wrap a bandage around a part of the body

examples.en: She bandaged his knee carefully.
examples.ko: 그녀는 그의 무릎에 조심스럽게 붕대를 감았어.

examples.en: Let me bandage that cut for you.
examples.ko: 그 상처에 내가 붕대 감아 줄게.

senses.meaningEn: a place where you keep your money or borrow money

examples.en: I need to go to the bank today.
The bank closes at four o'clock.

senses.note: bank account(계좌), bank card(카드), online banking(인터넷 뱅킹). 현금인출기는 ATM.

senses.meaningEn: the land along the side of a river

examples.en: We had a picnic on the bank of the river.
The river bank was muddy after the rain.

senses.note: river bank 으로 자주 씀. 바다·호수의 '가'는 shore, 해변은 beach.

senses.meaningEn: to make the short, loud sound that a dog makes

examples.en: Why is the dog barking at night?
My dog barks at everyone who passes by.

senses.note: bark at + 대상. 명사로도 씀(a loud bark). 'His bark is worse than his bite' = 말은 험해도 실제로는 안 무섭다.

senses.meaningEn: the hard outside cover of a tree

examples.en: The bark of this tree is very rough.
Some animals eat tree bark in winter.

senses.note: 셀 수 없는 명사. 두 뜻은 전혀 다른 단어가 우연히 같은 모양이 된 것이니 문맥으로 구별.

senses.meaningEn: a game in which two teams of nine players hit a ball with a bat and run around four bases

examples.en: Let's go to a baseball game this weekend.
My dad taught me how to play baseball.

senses.note: 야구 경기는 baseball game(match 아님), 야구 방망이는 bat, 야구장은 ballpark / stadium. 야구공도 그냥 baseball 이라고 함.

senses.meaningEn: a container made of thin strips of wood or plastic, often with a handle

examples.en: She put the fruit in a basket.
Put your dirty clothes in the laundry basket.

senses.note: laundry basket(빨래 바구니), shopping basket(장바구니), picnic basket. 온라인 쇼핑의 장바구니는 미국에서 cart.

senses.meaningEn: the net in basketball, or a score made by throwing the ball through it

examples.en: He made the basket right before the end.
She shot the ball into the basket.

senses.note: make a basket = 골을 넣다. 농구는 basketball.

senses.meaningEn: a game in which two teams of five players try to throw a ball through a high hoop

examples.en: We play basketball at lunch every day.
She's tall, so she's great at basketball.
examples.ko: 그녀는 키가 커서 농구를 아주 잘해.

senses.note: shoot a basketball(슛하다), basketball court(농구 코트). 공 자체도 basketball. NBA 는 미국 프로 농구.

senses.meaningEn: washing your whole body while sitting in a tub of water

examples.en: I love a hot bath after a long day.
examples.ko: 긴 하루 끝에 뜨거운 물로 목욕하는 게 정말 좋아.

examples.en: Mom gave the baby a bath.

senses.note: 목욕하다 take a bath(미국) / have a bath(영국). 아기를 목욕시키다 give the baby a bath. 욕조 자체는 bathtub.

senses.meaningEn: a room in a house with a toilet, a sink, and a bath or shower

examples.en: I'll take a quick shower in the bathroom.
The bathroom is at the end of the hall.

senses.meaningEn: a room with a toilet in a public place, in American English

examples.en: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
Can I use your bathroom, please?

senses.note: 미국에서는 식당·학교 화장실도 bathroom 또는 restroom. toilet 은 변기 자체를 가리키는 느낌이 강해 미국에서는 피함.

senses.meaningEn: a long container that you fill with water and sit in to wash

examples.en: I filled the bathtub with warm water.
The kids love playing in the bathtub.
examples.ko: 아이들은 욕조에서 노는 걸 정말 좋아해.

senses.note: 줄여서 tub 라고도 함. take a bath = 목욕하다.

senses.meaningEn: used to say who or what someone or something is, or what they are like

examples.en: I am a student, and she is a nurse.
The soup was too hot.

senses.note: 주어에 따라 am/is/are, 과거 was/were 로 변함. 한국어는 '학생이다' 처럼 조사로 끝나지만 영어는 be 동사가 꼭 필요: I student (×) → I am a student.

senses.meaningEn: used to say where someone or something is

examples.en: Where are my shoes?
Mom is in the kitchen right now.

senses.note: 위치의 '있다'도 be 동사. '~이 있다(존재)'는 there is/are: There are two cats on the sofa. '가지고 있다'는 have 와 구분.

senses.meaningEn: used with -ing or past participle to make continuous and passive forms

examples.en: They are playing soccer in the park.
The window was broken by the wind.

senses.note: be + -ing(진행), be + p.p.(수동). 'I'm boring'(나는 지루한 사람이다)과 'I'm bored'(나는 지루하다)처럼 형용사 선택에 주의.

senses.meaningEn: said to warn someone to pay attention so they do not get hurt or make a mistake

examples.en: Be careful, the floor is wet.
Be careful with that knife.

senses.note: be careful with + 물건(조심해서 다뤄), be careful of + 위험(~를 조심해), be careful not to + 동사(~하지 않도록 조심해). 급박한 순간에는 짧은 Watch out! / Look out!

senses.meaningEn: to be very interested in and enjoy something

examples.en: My friends are into K-pop these days.
examples.ko: 내 친구들은 요즘 케이팝에 푹 빠져 있어.

examples.en: My brother is into video games.
examples.ko: 내 동생은 비디오 게임을 아주 좋아해.

senses.note: 구어체. What are you into? = 뭐 좋아해?(취미 묻기). 격식 글에서는 be interested in. 사람이 목적어면 '~에게 호감이 있다': I think she's into you.

senses.meaningEn: an area of sand or small stones next to the sea

examples.en: Let's go to the beach this weekend.
The kids played on the beach all day.

senses.note: '바다에 놀러 가다'는 go to the beach. on the beach(해변에서), at the beach(해변에 가 있는 상태) 둘 다 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: a seed from a plant that is cooked and eaten as food

examples.en: I added some beans to the rice.
Beans are a good source of protein.

senses.note: 주로 복수형 beans 로 씀. soybean = 대두, green beans = 껍질콩, coffee beans = 커피 원두.

senses.meaningEn: a large heavy wild animal with thick fur and sharp claws

examples.en: We saw a bear in the mountains last summer.
Bears sleep all winter long.

senses.note: teddy bear(곰 인형), polar bear(북극곰), panda bear(판다). 발음은 bare(벌거벗은)와 같음(/ber/). 맥주 beer /bɪr/ 와 구별.

senses.meaningEn: to accept or deal with something unpleasant

examples.en: I can't bear this hot weather anymore.
examples.ko: 이 더운 날씨 더는 못 참겠어.

examples.en: She bore the pain without crying.

senses.note: 주로 can't bear(참을 수 없다) 형태로 씀. 과거형 bore, 과거분사 borne. 비슷한 stand(can't stand)가 구어에서 더 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: hair that grows on a man's chin and cheeks

examples.en: My dad has a short gray beard.
examples.ko: 우리 아빠는 짧은 회색 턱수염이 있어.

examples.en: Are you growing a beard?

senses.note: 콧수염은 mustache. 수염을 기르다 = grow a beard, 수염을 깎다 = shave. 발음 /bɪrd/ (bird 와 비슷하지만 모음이 다름).

senses.meaningEn: very nice to look at

examples.en: What a beautiful dress!
Your garden is so beautiful in spring.

senses.note: pretty 보다 강한 칭찬. 사람·풍경·물건 모두 가능. 남성 외모에는 handsome, good-looking 을 더 많이 씀.

senses.meaningEn: very good or pleasant

examples.en: It's a beautiful day. Let's go outside.
That was a beautiful goal!

senses.note: 날씨·음악·경기 장면 등에 '훌륭하다'는 뜻으로 폭넓게 쓰임. 미국 구어로 Beautiful! 은 '좋아, 완벽해'라는 맞장구로도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: for the reason that

examples.en: I stayed home because I was sick.
We were late because the bus didn't come.

senses.note: Why? 에 대한 답은 Because ~ 로 시작. 뒤에는 주어+동사가 옴. 명사만 올 때는 because of: because of the rain.

senses.meaningEn: used before a noun to give the reason for something

examples.en: The game was canceled because of the rain.
I couldn't sleep because of the noise.

senses.note: because + 절(문장) / because of + 명사. 'because of it rained' 는 틀림.

senses.meaningEn: to start to be something or to change into a different state

examples.en: She became a doctor last year.
It's becoming very cold at night.

senses.note: become + 명사/형용사. 구어에서는 get 이 더 흔함: get cold, get married. 직업·신분이 '되다'는 become.

senses.meaningEn: a piece of furniture that you sleep on

examples.en: I go to bed around eleven every night.
Make your bed before you leave.

senses.note: go to bed(자러 가다), be in bed(누워 있다)는 관사 없이. make the bed = 이불·시트를 정리하다. 침대 '위에' 는 on the bed, 이불 속은 in bed.

senses.meaningEn: an area of ground in a garden where flowers or vegetables grow

examples.en: We planted roses in the flower bed.
The dog ran right through the vegetable bed.

senses.note: flower bed = 화단. 거의 항상 flower bed / vegetable bed 처럼 앞에 꾸밈말이 붙음.

senses.meaningEn: a room where you sleep

examples.en: My bedroom is upstairs on the left.
We're looking for a two-bedroom apartment.
examples.ko: 우리는 방 두 개짜리 아파트를 찾고 있어.

senses.note: 집 크기는 방 개수로 말함: a three-bedroom house = 방 세 개짜리 집.

senses.meaningEn: a yellow and black insect that makes honey and can sting

examples.en: Don't move, there's a bee on your arm.
Bees make honey from flowers.

senses.note: 벌에 쏘이다 = get stung by a bee. 'as busy as a bee' 는 '아주 바쁘다'. 꿀벌은 honeybee, 말벌은 wasp.

senses.meaningEn: the meat from a cow

examples.en: I don't eat beef, but I eat chicken.
examples.ko: 나는 소고기는 안 먹지만 닭고기는 먹어.

examples.en: This beef is really tender.

senses.note: 동물은 cow, 고기는 beef. 셀 수 없는 명사: a beef (×). ground beef(다진 소고기), beef stew(소고기 스튜). 한국 음식 설명 시 bulgogi 는 marinated beef.

senses.meaningEn: earlier than a time or event

examples.en: Wash your hands before dinner.
Please come back before ten o'clock.

senses.note: before + 명사/동명사(before eating). 순서를 말할 때 Korea comes before Japan on the list(순서상 앞). 반대는 after. 장소의 '앞'은 보통 in front of 를 쓴다.

senses.meaningEn: earlier than the time when something happens

examples.en: Brush your teeth before you go to bed.
Think before you speak.

senses.note: before 절은 미래라도 현재형을 쓴다(before you go, not before you will go).

senses.meaningEn: at an earlier time

examples.en: Have we met before?
I've never tried kimchi before.
examples.ko: 나는 전에 김치를 먹어 본 적이 없어.

senses.note: 문장 끝에 단독으로 쓰고 경험(현재완료)과 잘 어울린다. the day before = 그 전날.

senses.meaningEn: to start doing something, or to start happening

examples.en: Let's begin with page ten.
The class began five minutes ago.

senses.note: start 보다 약간 격식 있고 글말에서 더 자주 보임. begin with = ~부터 시작하다. 과거 began, 과거분사 begun 을 혼동하지 말 것. 명사는 beginning.

senses.meaningEn: at or toward the back of something

examples.en: The ball is behind the sofa.
Someone is standing behind you.

senses.note: behind + 명사. 'in back of' 도 미국 구어로 가능. 앞은 in front of(of 를 빼지 않도록 주의).

senses.meaningEn: in the place you have left, or further back than others

examples.en: Oh no, I left my phone behind!
Walk faster. You're falling behind.

senses.note: leave something behind = 깜빡 두고 오다. fall behind = 뒤처지다(걷기·공부·일 모두). stay behind = 남아 있다.

senses.meaningEn: late or slower than planned or than other people

examples.en: I'm behind in my homework this week.
The train is twenty minutes behind schedule.

senses.note: behind schedule(일정보다 늦음) vs ahead of schedule(일정보다 빠름). be behind in/with + 일.

senses.meaningEn: to think that something is true or that someone is telling the truth

examples.en: I don't believe him; he always lies.
examples.ko: 난 그 사람 말 안 믿어. 항상 거짓말하잖아.

examples.en: Can you believe it's already December?

senses.note: believe + 사람/말 = 그 말을 믿다. believe in = 존재나 가치를 믿다(believe in ghosts, believe in you). 'I can't believe it!' 은 놀람 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to think something is probably true, but not be sure

examples.en: I believe the store opens at ten.
She's at the library, I believe.

senses.note: think 보다 약간 조심스럽고 정중한 느낌. 문장 끝의 I believe 는 '아마 ~일 거예요'.

senses.meaningEn: to think that something exists or is real

examples.en: Do you believe in ghosts?
My little sister still believes in Santa Claus.

senses.note: believe + 사람/말 = (그 말이) 사실이라고 믿다(I believe you). believe in = 존재·가치를 믿다. 둘을 혼동하기 쉬움.

senses.meaningEn: to trust someone or feel sure that they can succeed

examples.en: I believe in you. You can do it!
examples.ko: 난 널 믿어. 넌 할 수 있어!

examples.en: Our coach really believes in the team.

senses.note: 격려할 때 아주 자주 쓰는 표현. believe in yourself = 자신을 믿어라.

senses.meaningEn: to be owned by someone

examples.en: Who does this umbrella belong to?
That bike belongs to my brother.

senses.note: belong to + 사람. 진행형으로 쓰지 않음. Does this belong to you? = 이거 당신 건가요?

senses.meaningEn: to be in the right or usual place

examples.en: Put the milk back where it belongs.
These books belong on the top shelf.
examples.ko: 이 책들은 맨 위 선반에 두는 거야.

senses.note: '소속감'을 말할 때도 씀: I feel like I belong here(여기가 내 자리 같아).

senses.meaningEn: to be owned by someone

examples.en: Does this umbrella belong to you?
That red car belongs to my neighbor.
examples.ko: 저 빨간 차는 우리 이웃 거야.

senses.note: 진행형으로 쓰지 않음: It belongs to me (not 'is belonging'). 뜻은 be mine/yours 와 같고 조금 더 격식 있음.

senses.meaningEn: to be a member of a group or organization

examples.en: I belong to the school soccer club.
examples.ko: 나는 학교 축구 동아리에 속해 있어.

examples.en: Which team do you belong to?

senses.note: belong 만 쓰면 '어울리다, 있을 자리에 있다': I feel like I belong here.

senses.meaningEn: in a lower position than something

examples.en: The cups are on the shelf below the plates.
We live two floors below you.
examples.ko: 우리는 너희 두 층 아래에 살아.

senses.note: under 는 바로 밑(닿거나 가려짐), below 는 더 낮은 위치 전반. 온도·숫자에는 below 를 씀: below zero(영하).

senses.meaningEn: lower on the same page or further down

examples.en: Please write your name below.
See the picture below for the answer.

senses.note: 문서에서 '아래 내용 참고'는 see below, '위 내용'은 see above.

senses.meaningEn: a band of leather or cloth worn around the waist

examples.en: These pants are loose, so I need a belt.
He wears a brown belt with brown shoes.
examples.ko: 그는 갈색 구두에 갈색 벨트를 매.

senses.note: 벨트를 '매다'는 wear/put on. 태권도 '검은 띠'는 black belt.

senses.meaningEn: a strap in a car or plane that holds you in your seat

examples.en: Please fasten your seat belt.
Is your belt on? We're leaving now.

senses.note: 보통 seat belt 또는 safety belt 로 말함. 매다 = fasten/buckle up, 풀다 = unfasten.

senses.meaningEn: a long seat for two or more people, usually outdoors

examples.en: An old man was sitting on a bench in the park.
examples.ko: 할아버지 한 분이 공원 벤치에 앉아 계셨어.

examples.en: Let's sit on that bench and rest a bit.

senses.note: 벤치에 '앉다'는 sit on a bench(in 아님). 스포츠에서 '벤치(후보 선수들)'도 같은 단어: He sat on the bench all game.

senses.meaningEn: to make something curved or not straight

examples.en: Bend your knees a little when you lift the box.
examples.ko: 상자를 들 때 무릎을 살짝 구부려.

examples.en: He bent the wire into a circle.

senses.note: bend your knees/elbows. 형용사 bent = 구부러진: a bent spoon.

senses.meaningEn: to move the top part of your body downward

examples.en: She bent down to tie her shoes.
examples.ko: 그녀는 몸을 숙여 신발 끈을 묶었어.

examples.en: I bent over to pick up the coin.

senses.note: bend down(아래로 숙이다) / bend over(허리를 굽히다). 허리 다친 사람: I can't bend.

senses.meaningEn: a curved part of a road or river

examples.en: There's a sharp bend in the road ahead.
examples.ko: 앞에 길이 급하게 굽은 곳이 있어.

examples.en: Slow down before the bend.

senses.meaningEn: the friend you like most and feel closest to

examples.en: Mina has been my best friend since middle school.
I'm going to the movies with my best friend.

senses.note: best friend 는 보통 한 명(또는 소수). 여럿 중 '친한 친구'는 close friend / good friend. 구어·문자에서 BFF(best friends forever) 라고도 함. '내 가장 친한 친구' 는 my best friend(my the best friend ✗).

senses.meaningEn: it is better to do something late than not do it at all

examples.en: Sorry I'm late. Well, better late than never!
examples.ko: 늦어서 미안. 뭐, 안 오는 것보다는 낫지!

examples.en: He finally called me back. Better late than never.
examples.ko: 드디어 답전화가 왔어. 늦었지만 안 한 것보단 낫지.

senses.note: 혼자 쓰는 한 문장 속담. 늦은 사람을 가볍게 용서할 때, 또는 늦게라도 시작하는 자신을 격려할 때 쓴다.

senses.meaningEn: in the space that separates two things or people

examples.en: The bank is between the café and the bookstore.
I sat between my parents.

senses.note: between A and B(둘). 셋 이상 사이에 '둘러싸여' 있으면 among. between 뒤에 and 를 써야 함('between A to B' 는 틀림).

senses.meaningEn: in the period or range that separates two times or amounts

examples.en: Call me between six and seven.
The tickets cost between 20 and 30 dollars.

senses.note: 기간·가격·나이 범위 모두 between A and B. Between you and me = 우리끼리 얘긴데(비밀).

senses.meaningEn: used to talk about a relationship, choice, or difference involving two things

examples.en: What's the difference between these two?
You have to choose between pizza and pasta.

senses.note: the difference between A and B, choose between A and B. 둘 다 '사이' 로 외우면 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: a vehicle with two wheels that you move by pushing pedals with your feet

examples.en: My son learned to ride a bicycle last summer.
examples.ko: 아들이 지난여름에 자전거 타는 법을 배웠어.

examples.en: I go to school by bicycle when it's sunny.

senses.note: 자전거를 '타다'는 ride a bicycle(drive 아님). 대화에서는 줄임말 bike 가 훨씬 흔하고 bicycle 은 약간 격식체·문어체. 자전거 도로는 bike lane.

senses.meaningEn: large in size

examples.en: They live in a big house near the park.
examples.ko: 그들은 공원 근처 큰 집에 살아.

examples.en: Can I get a bigger size, please?
examples.ko: 더 큰 사이즈로 주실 수 있어요?

senses.note: big 은 구어체, large 는 조금 더 격식·사이즈 표기(옷은 L = large). 비교급은 g 를 겹쳐 bigger.

senses.meaningEn: older (used about brothers and sisters)

examples.en: My big sister is in college.
He always listens to his big brother.
examples.ko: 그는 항상 형 말을 잘 들어.

senses.note: big brother/sister = 형·오빠·누나·언니(older). 반대는 little brother/sister. 구어체이며 격식은 older.

senses.meaningEn: important or serious

examples.en: Tomorrow is a big day for me.
It's not a big problem. We can fix it.
examples.ko: 큰 문제 아니야. 고칠 수 있어.

senses.note: a big decision(중대한 결정), a big fan of(~의 열렬한 팬), No big deal.(별일 아니야).

senses.meaningEn: a bicycle (the usual everyday word)

examples.en: I rode my bike to the park.
Can I borrow your bike for an hour?
examples.ko: 네 자전거 한 시간만 빌려도 돼?

senses.note: bicycle 의 일상 표현. ride a bike, go for a bike ride(자전거 타러 가다). 문맥에 따라 오토바이(motorbike)를 뜻할 수도 있음. 한국어 '바이크'는 주로 오토바이지만 영어 bike 는 기본적으로 자전거.

senses.meaningEn: to ride a bicycle somewhere

examples.en: We biked along the river all afternoon.
examples.ko: 우리는 오후 내내 강을 따라 자전거를 탔어.

examples.en: Do you bike to work?

senses.note: bike to work / bike around the lake. 같은 뜻으로 cycle 도 씀(영국에서 더 흔함). 자전거 타기(운동)는 biking / cycling.

senses.meaningEn: a piece of paper that shows how much you have to pay

examples.en: Can we have the bill, please?
I have to pay the electricity bill this week.
examples.ko: 이번 주에 전기 요금을 내야 해.

senses.note: 식당 계산서는 미국에서 check 를 더 자주 씀(Check, please!). 공과금은 bills: phone bill, gas bill. '계산은 내가 할게'는 I'll get the bill.

senses.meaningEn: a piece of paper money

examples.en: He paid with a twenty-dollar bill.
Can you change this bill into coins?
examples.ko: 이 지폐를 동전으로 바꿔 줄 수 있어?

senses.note: 미국식. 영국에서는 지폐를 note 라고 함. a ten-dollar bill 처럼 하이픈으로 연결.

senses.meaningEn: an animal with feathers and wings that usually can fly

examples.en: A bird is singing outside my window.
Those birds fly south in the winter.

senses.note: early bird = 아침형 인간. Birds fly, sing, build nests. 발음 주의: bird /bɜːrd/ 와 beard(수염) /bɪrd/ 를 구분.

senses.meaningEn: the day each year that is the same date as the day you were born

examples.en: Happy birthday! How old are you now?
My birthday is on March 3rd.

senses.note: birthday party(생일 파티), birthday cake(생일 케이크). 날짜는 on + 날짜, 월만 말할 땐 in March. 태어난 '날짜' 자체는 date of birth.

senses.meaningEn: to cut into food with your teeth

examples.en: Don't bite it. It's too hot.
She bit into the apple.
examples.ko: 그녀는 사과를 한 입 베어 물었어.

senses.note: bite into ~ = ~을 한 입 베어 물다. 과거 bit, 과거분사 bitten. 손톱 물어뜯는 것도 bite one's nails.

senses.meaningEn: when an animal or insect uses its teeth or mouth to hurt you

examples.en: Does your dog bite?
I got bitten by a mosquito last night.

senses.note: 벌레에 물린 자국은 a mosquito bite / bug bite. 벌에 '쏘이다'는 sting.

senses.meaningEn: a piece of food you bite off, or a small quick meal

examples.en: Can I have a bite of your sandwich?
examples.ko: 네 샌드위치 한 입 먹어도 돼?

examples.en: Let's grab a bite before the movie.
examples.ko: 영화 보기 전에 뭐 간단히 먹자.

senses.note: a bite of ~ = ~ 한 입. grab a bite (to eat) = 간단히 먹다. 아주 흔한 구어 표현.

senses.meaningEn: having a strong, sharp taste that is not sweet, like black coffee

examples.en: This coffee is too bitter for me.
The medicine tastes very bitter.
examples.ko: 그 약은 아주 쓴 맛이 나.

senses.meaningEn: angry and unhappy because of something unfair that happened

examples.en: He still feels bitter about losing the game.
examples.ko: 그는 경기에서 진 것에 대해 아직도 씁쓸해해.

examples.en: Don't be bitter. Just try again next time.
examples.ko: 억울해하지 마. 다음에 다시 해 보면 돼.

senses.note: bitter about ~ = ~에 대해 씁쓸해하다. 날씨가 '매섭게 추운' 것도 bitter cold.

senses.meaningEn: having the darkest color, like night

examples.en: I bought a black coat for winter.
Our cat is black with white paws.
examples.ko: 우리 고양이는 발만 하얀 검은 고양이야.

senses.note: black and white(흑백). 한국어 "블랙"처럼 멋스러운 이미지도 있지만 기본은 색 이름.

senses.meaningEn: coffee or tea served without milk or cream

examples.en: I take my coffee black, no sugar.
examples.ko: 저는 커피 블랙으로, 설탕 없이 마셔요.

examples.en: Two black coffees, please.

senses.note: 카페에서 "아메리카노"라고 말해도 통하지만, black coffee 는 우유 없는 커피 전반을 말함.

senses.meaningEn: the color black

examples.en: She usually dresses in black.
Does this shoe come in black?

senses.meaningEn: a dark board in a classroom that you write on with chalk

examples.en: The teacher wrote the date on the blackboard.
Can you read the blackboard from there?

senses.note: 미국에서는 chalkboard 도 흔히 씀. 흰 보드는 whiteboard.

senses.meaningEn: a thick, warm cover that you put on a bed or over your body

examples.en: It's cold. Can I have another blanket?
examples.ko: 추워. 담요 하나 더 줄 수 있어?

examples.en: She fell asleep under a warm blanket.

senses.note: 한국식 두꺼운 이불은 comforter(미) / duvet, 홑이불은 sheet. 담요를 '덮다'는 put a blanket over / get under a blanket.

senses.meaningEn: what you say to someone just after they sneeze

examples.en: Achoo! Bless you! Thanks.
Bless you! Are you getting a cold?

senses.note: God bless you 의 줄임. 재채기 소리를 들으면 모르는 사람에게도 거의 반사적으로 말하는 관습. 재채기한 사람은 Thank you / Thanks 로 답함. 한국에는 없는 관습이어서 안 하면 약간 무심해 보일 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: used to show that you are very grateful or touched by what someone did

examples.en: You carried my bags? Oh, bless you!
examples.ko: 제 짐을 들어 주셨어요? 아이고, 고마워요!

examples.en: Bless you for helping my mother.

senses.note: 어른(특히 나이 든 분)이 친절에 감동했을 때 자주 씀. 'Bless you' 또는 'Bless your heart' — 단, 미국 남부의 bless your heart 는 가끔 비꼬는 뜻이니 주의.

senses.meaningKo: 블록, 구획 (한 길에서 다음 길까지의 거리)
senses.meaningEn: the distance along a street from one corner to the next

examples.en: The bank is two blocks from here.
Walk one block and turn right.

senses.note: 미국 도시는 격자형이라 길 안내에 block 을 많이 씀. go straight for three blocks(세 블록 직진). 동네 산책은 walk around the block.

senses.meaningEn: a solid piece of something with flat sides, such as wood or stone

examples.en: The baby is playing with wooden blocks.
examples.ko: 아기가 나무 블록을 가지고 놀고 있어.

examples.en: Cut the cheese into small blocks.

senses.note: a block of ice/wood/cheese. 레고 블록처럼 쌓는 장난감은 building blocks.

senses.meaningEn: to stop something from moving through or past a place

examples.en: A big truck is blocking the road.
Please don't block the door.

senses.note: 길·시야·입구를 막을 때 block. SNS 에서 사람을 '차단하다'도 block someone. '길이 막히다(교통 체증)'는 block 이 아니라 The traffic is heavy / I got stuck in traffic.

senses.meaningEn: the red liquid that flows through your body

examples.en: There was some blood on his finger.
The nurse took some blood for a test.

senses.note: 발음 주의 /blʌd/ (블러드). 셀 수 없는 명사. blood test(혈액 검사), blood type(혈액형), blood pressure(혈압). 피가 나다 = bleed.

senses.meaningEn: when wind moves, or when wind moves something

examples.en: The wind is blowing hard today.
My hat blew off in the wind.

senses.note: 과거형 blew, 과거분사 blown. blow away = 날려 버리다, blow off = (바람에) 벗겨지다.

senses.meaningEn: to push air out of your mouth

examples.en: Blow out the candles and make a wish!
He blew on his hot soup to cool it.
examples.ko: 그는 뜨거운 국을 식히려고 후후 불었어.

senses.note: blow your nose = 코를 풀다. blow up a balloon = 풍선을 불다. blow up 은 "폭발하다" 뜻도 있음.

senses.meaningEn: if the wind blows something away, it carries it off

examples.en: The wind blew my hat away!
Hold the papers or they'll blow away.

senses.note: 자동사(날아가다)·타동사(날려 보내다) 둘 다 가능. 날씨 이야기에 자주.

senses.meaningEn: to impress or surprise someone very much

examples.en: Her singing really blew me away.
I was blown away by the view from the top.

senses.note: be blown away by = ~에 엄청 감동/놀람. 구어체 칭찬 표현으로 매우 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: to make a flame stop burning by blowing on it

examples.en: Make a wish and blow out the candles!
The wind blew the match out right away.
