senses.note: blow out the candles 는 생일 파티 필수 표현. 목적어는 중간·뒤 모두 가능.

senses.meaningEn: if a tire blows out, it bursts suddenly while driving

examples.en: Our tire blew out on the highway.
If a tire blows out, don't brake too hard.
examples.ko: 타이어가 터지면 브레이크를 너무 세게 밟지 마.

senses.note: 명사형 a blowout = 타이어 펑크(터짐). 조금 바람 빠진 건 a flat tire.

senses.meaningEn: to fill something with air

examples.en: Can you help me blow up the balloons?
I need to blow up my bike tires.

senses.note: '불어서 부풀리다' 라는 뜻. 격식은 inflate. 반대는 let the air out.

senses.meaningEn: to explode, or to destroy something with a bomb

examples.en: The old factory blew up in the night.
They blew up the bridge in the movie.

senses.meaningEn: to suddenly become very angry

examples.en: Dad blew up when he saw the broken window.
examples.ko: 아빠는 깨진 창문을 보고 버럭 화를 내셨어.

examples.en: Don't blow up at me, it wasn't my fault!
examples.ko: 나한테 화내지 마, 내 잘못 아니야!

senses.note: blow up at someone = ~에게 폭발하다. 사진 '확대하다' 도 blow up: blow up the photo.

senses.meaningEn: having the color of a clear sky or the sea

examples.en: The sky is so blue today.
He always wears a blue shirt to work.
examples.ko: 그는 회사에 항상 파란 셔츠를 입고 가.

senses.note: light blue(하늘색), dark blue / navy(짙은 파랑). 한국어 "푸르다"는 green 도 포함하지만 영어 blue 는 파란색만.

senses.meaningEn: feeling sad or unhappy

examples.en: I feel a little blue on rainy days.
Why are you so blue this morning?
examples.ko: 오늘 아침 왜 그렇게 기분이 가라앉았어?

senses.note: feel blue 로 자주 씀. 노래 장르 blues 도 이 뜻에서 왔음.

senses.meaningEn: the color blue

examples.en: Blue is my favorite color.
Do you have this bag in blue?

senses.note: 쇼핑할 때 in + 색: Do you have it in blue/black?

senses.meaningEn: a game played by moving pieces on a flat board, often with dice or cards

examples.en: We played board games all night.
What's your favorite board game?

senses.note: play a board game 으로 씀. 체스·모노폴리·젠가 등을 포함. 한국어처럼 '보드'만으로는 뜻이 통하지 않음.

senses.meaningEn: a small vehicle that travels on water

examples.en: We took a boat across the lake.
Can you row a boat?

senses.note: 작은 배는 boat, 큰 배는 ship. 배에 타다 = get on/in a boat, by boat(배로). 'We're in the same boat.' 는 '같은 처지야'라는 관용구.

senses.meaningEn: the whole physical form of a person or animal

examples.en: Exercise is good for your body.
My whole body hurts after the hike.

senses.note: body 는 머리까지 포함한 '몸 전체'. 몸매는 figure, 체형은 body type.

senses.meaningEn: a dead person

examples.en: Police found a body near the river.
The body was taken to the hospital.

senses.note: 뉴스·드라마에서 매우 자주 나오는 뜻. dead body 라고도 함.

senses.meaningEn: to heat a liquid until it bubbles, or to reach that point

examples.en: Boil some water for the tea.
The water is boiling. Turn off the stove.
examples.ko: 물이 끓고 있어. 가스 불 꺼.

senses.note: 물이 끓는 상태는 boiling. '끓는 물'은 boiling water, '끓인 물(식은 것 포함)'은 boiled water.

senses.meaningEn: to cook food in boiling water

examples.en: Boil the eggs for ten minutes.
I boiled some potatoes for dinner.

senses.note: boiled egg = 삶은 달걀. hard-boiled(완숙) / soft-boiled(반숙). 국처럼 오래 끓이는 것은 simmer / stew.

senses.meaningEn: one of the hard white parts inside your body that make up your skeleton

examples.en: The doctor said no bones are broken.
Milk helps make your bones strong.

senses.note: break a bone(뼈가 부러지다). 생선 가시도 fish bone.

senses.meaningEn: a hard part inside meat or fish that you do not eat

examples.en: Be careful, this fish has lots of bones.
Chicken on the bone tastes better.

senses.note: 뼈 없는 = boneless (boneless chicken).

senses.meaningEn: a set of printed pages with a cover that you read

examples.en: I'm reading a really good book right now.
examples.ko: 지금 정말 좋은 책을 읽고 있어.

examples.en: Please open your books to page ten.

senses.meaningEn: to arrange to have a seat, room, or table at a future time

examples.en: I booked a hotel room for two nights.
Should we book a table for dinner?

senses.note: book a flight / book a table / book a room. 영국·미국 모두 흔히 씀.

senses.meaningEn: a shop that sells books

examples.en: I bought this novel at the bookstore downtown.
Is there a bookstore near the station?

senses.note: 미국식은 bookstore, 영국식은 bookshop. 온라인 서점은 online bookstore.

senses.meaningEn: shoes that cover your foot and the lower part of your leg

examples.en: Wear your boots; it's snowing outside.
These boots are too tight.

senses.note: a pair of boots. rain boots(장화), hiking boots(등산화), snow boots. 영국에서 boot 는 자동차 트렁크라는 뜻도 있음.

senses.meaningEn: feeling tired and unhappy because something is not interesting

examples.en: I'm bored. Let's go outside.
The students got bored during the long lecture.

senses.note: 사람은 bored, 지루하게 만드는 것은 boring. I'm boring 은 '나는 재미없는 사람'이 되므로 주의. bored with/of + 명사, bored to death(지루해 죽겠다).

senses.meaningEn: not interesting; making you feel tired and uninterested

examples.en: The movie was so boring that I fell asleep.
Math class is boring for me.

senses.note: boring(지루하게 만드는) vs bored(지루함을 느끼는). I'm boring. = '나는 재미없는 사람' → '나 지루해' 는 I'm bored.

senses.meaningEn: to take and use something that belongs to someone else, and give it back later

examples.en: Can I borrow your pen for a minute?
examples.ko: 펜 좀 잠깐 빌릴 수 있을까?

examples.en: I borrowed three books from the library.

senses.note: 한국어 '빌리다'는 방향이 없지만 영어는 borrow(내가 받아 옴) / lend(내가 내줌)를 구분. 'Can I borrow ~?' 가 자연스러운 요청. borrow A from B.

senses.meaningEn: the person who is in charge of you at work

examples.en: My boss said I can leave early today.
examples.ko: 상사가 오늘은 일찍 가도 된다고 했어.

examples.en: Who is your boss at the new company?

senses.note: 직급과 상관없이 '나를 관리하는 윗사람'. 회사 대표는 CEO/owner. 'You're the boss.'(네 말대로 할게) 라는 관용 표현도 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: a very strong enemy at the end of a level in a video game

examples.en: I finally beat the last boss!
This boss is too hard. Help me!

senses.note: beat/defeat the boss(보스를 이기다). boss fight(보스전), final boss(최종 보스).

senses.meaningEn: the two people or things together

examples.en: Both my parents are teachers.
examples.ko: 우리 부모님은 두 분 다 선생님이셔.

examples.en: I like both of these shoes.
examples.ko: 이 신발 둘 다 마음에 들어.

senses.note: 둘일 때만 both, 셋 이상은 all. 항상 복수 동사. 부정은 neither(both ... not 은 피함).

senses.meaningKo: both A and B: A와 B 둘 다
senses.meaningEn: used with and to emphasize that two things are true

examples.en: She speaks both Korean and English.
examples.ko: 그녀는 한국어와 영어를 둘 다 해.

examples.en: The movie was both funny and sad.
examples.ko: 그 영화는 웃기기도 하고 슬프기도 했어.

senses.note: both A and B 는 A, B 의 형태를 맞출 것(명사-명사, 형용사-형용사).

senses.meaningEn: to annoy someone or make them feel a little upset

examples.en: Sorry to bother you, but is this seat taken?
The noise from upstairs really bothers me.

senses.note: 'Sorry to bother you' 는 말을 걸거나 부탁할 때의 정중한 시작. 'Does it bother you if ~?' = ~해도 괜찮아? 'Don't bother.' = 굳이 안 해도 돼.

senses.meaningEn: to make the effort to do something, usually used in negative sentences

examples.en: He didn't even bother to say goodbye.
Don't bother cooking; let's order in.

senses.note: 주로 부정문에서 not bother to + 동사 / not bother -ing = 번거로워서 안 하다. 'Why bother?' = 뭐 하러 그래?

senses.meaningEn: a container with a narrow neck, usually for liquids

examples.en: I always carry a water bottle with me.
Please put the empty bottles in the recycling bin.
examples.ko: 빈 병은 재활용 통에 넣어 주세요.

senses.meaningEn: the amount of liquid a bottle holds

examples.en: We shared a bottle of wine at dinner.
examples.ko: 우리는 저녁에 와인 한 병을 나눠 마셨어.

examples.en: Can you buy two bottles of milk?

senses.note: a bottle of water / wine / milk. 뚜껑은 bottle cap, 병따개는 bottle opener.

senses.meaningEn: water sold or kept in a bottle

examples.en: Can I get a bottle of water, please?
Bring a bottle of water to the gym.
examples.ko: 헬스장에 갈 때 물 한 병 가져가.

senses.note: a bottle of water = 병에 든 물 하나, bottled water = (수돗물이 아닌) 병에 든 물 자체. 두 병이면 two bottles of water(bottle 만 복수). 한국처럼 '물 하나'를 a water 라고도 구어에서 말하지만 격식에선 bottle of 를 붙인다.

senses.meaningEn: a deep round dish for food or liquid

examples.en: Put the soup in a big bowl.
I need a bowl for my cereal.

senses.meaningEn: the amount of food that a bowl holds

examples.en: I had a bowl of rice and some kimchi.
examples.ko: 밥 한 그릇에 김치 좀 먹었어.

examples.en: Would you like a bowl of soup?

senses.note: a bowl of rice / noodles / soup. 밥·국·면처럼 깊은 그릇에 담는 음식에 씀.

senses.meaningEn: a game in which you roll a heavy ball down a long lane to knock over pins

examples.en: Let's go bowling after dinner.
I'm terrible at bowling, but I love it.
examples.ko: 나 볼링 진짜 못 치는데 그래도 좋아해.

senses.note: go bowling(볼링 치러 가다). 볼링장은 bowling alley. 발음은 '볼링'보다 /boʊ/ 로 '보울링'에 가까움.

senses.meaningEn: a container with straight sides, often made of cardboard

examples.en: Put the books in this box.
I need a bigger box for these shoes.
examples.ko: 이 신발 넣을 더 큰 상자가 필요해.

senses.note: a box of ~ = ~ 한 상자 (a box of chocolates). cardboard box = 종이 상자, lunch box = 도시락통.

senses.meaningEn: a small square on a form or screen that you write in or tick

examples.en: Check the box if you agree.
Write your name in the box below.

senses.note: check the box(미) / tick the box(영) = 칸에 체크하다.

senses.meaningEn: breakfast cereal sold in a cardboard box

examples.en: We're out of cereal. Can you buy a box of cereal?
examples.ko: 시리얼이 다 떨어졌어. 시리얼 한 상자 사다 줄래?

examples.en: The kids finished a whole box of cereal in two days.
examples.ko: 아이들이 이틀 만에 시리얼 한 상자를 다 먹었어.

senses.note: a box of 는 상자 단위로 파는 것에 쓴다: a box of cereal/tissues/chocolates. 그릇에 담은 시리얼 한 그릇은 a bowl of cereal.

senses.meaningEn: a sport in which two people fight with their fists wearing big gloves

examples.en: He takes boxing classes to stay fit.
examples.ko: 그는 몸매 유지하려고 복싱 수업을 들어.

examples.en: We watched a boxing match on TV last night.

senses.note: boxing gloves(복싱 글러브), boxing ring(링), boxer(복싱 선수). 상자(box)와 철자가 같으니 문맥으로 구분.

senses.meaningEn: a male child or young man

examples.en: The boy is riding his bike to school.
examples.ko: 그 남자아이가 자전거를 타고 학교에 가고 있어.

examples.en: There are twelve boys in my class.
examples.ko: 우리 반에는 남자아이가 열두 명 있어.

senses.note: 성인 남성을 boy 라고 부르면 무례할 수 있음. 아들을 뜻할 때 my boy 도 가능.

senses.meaningEn: used to show you are surprised, happy, or tired

examples.en: Boy, it's hot today!
Oh boy, I forgot my keys again.

senses.note: Oh boy! 는 기쁠 때도, 곤란할 때도 씀. 미국 구어.

senses.meaningEn: a man or boy that someone is in a romantic relationship with

examples.en: Do you have a boyfriend?
Her boyfriend bought her flowers.

senses.note: 연인만 뜻함. 그냥 남자인 친구는 a male friend / a guy friend. 한국어 '남친'과 똑같이 연애 상대.

senses.meaningEn: the organ inside your head that controls your body and lets you think

examples.en: The brain needs a lot of sleep to work well.
examples.ko: 뇌가 잘 돌아가려면 잠을 충분히 자야 해.

examples.en: Fish is good for your brain.

senses.note: brain 은 신체 기관. '머리가 좋다'는 He is smart. 또는 He has a good brain. 구어로 Use your brain!(머리 좀 써!).

senses.meaningEn: a part of a tree that grows out from the trunk

examples.en: A bird is sitting on that branch.
examples.ko: 새 한 마리가 저 나뭇가지에 앉아 있어.

examples.en: The branch broke in the strong wind.

senses.note: 작은 잔가지는 twig, 나무 몸통은 trunk.

senses.meaningEn: a local office or shop that is part of a bigger company

examples.en: Is there a bank branch near here?
The store opened a new branch downtown.
examples.ko: 그 가게가 시내에 새 지점을 열었어.

senses.note: 본사는 head office / headquarters.

senses.meaningEn: not afraid of danger or difficult situations

examples.en: You were so brave at the dentist today!
It was brave of her to speak first.
examples.ko: 그녀가 먼저 말한 건 용감한 행동이었어.

senses.note: It was brave of + 사람 + to 동사 패턴. 명사는 bravery / courage. 아이를 칭찬할 때 매우 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: a basic food made from flour and water that is baked

examples.en: Can you buy some bread on your way home?
examples.ko: 집에 오는 길에 빵 좀 사 올 수 있어?

examples.en: I had bread and butter for breakfast.

senses.note: 셀 수 없는 명사: a bread (×) → a loaf of bread(한 덩이), a slice of bread(한 장), a piece of bread. 한국어 '빵'은 케이크·과자류까지 넓게 가리키지만 영어 bread 는 식빵·바게트 같은 식사용 빵만 뜻함.

senses.meaningEn: to separate into pieces, or damage something

examples.en: Be careful, don't break the glass.
These plates break very easily.

senses.meaningEn: to stop working

examples.en: My phone breaks every time I drop it.
examples.ko: 내 폰은 떨어뜨릴 때마다 고장 나.

examples.en: If you press too hard, it will break.
examples.ko: 너무 세게 누르면 고장 날 거야.

senses.note: 이미 고장 난 상태는 It's broken.

senses.meaningEn: a short rest from work or study

examples.en: Let's take a ten-minute break.
We have a lunch break at noon.

senses.note: take a break = 쉬다. coffee break, lunch break.

senses.meaningEn: used to wish someone good luck, especially before a performance

examples.en: Your concert is tonight? Break a leg!
Break a leg at your interview tomorrow.

senses.note: 글자 그대로 '다리를 부러뜨려라' 가 아님. 무대·공연 전 'good luck' 이 불운을 부른다는 미신에서 유래. 주로 공연·발표·면접 전에 씀.

senses.meaningEn: if a car or machine breaks down, it stops working

examples.en: Our car broke down on the way to the beach.
examples.ko: 바닷가 가는 길에 차가 고장 났어.

examples.en: The washing machine breaks down all the time.

senses.note: 움직이던 것이 멈추는 고장. be broken 은 '고장 난 상태'. 명사형 a breakdown.

senses.meaningEn: to start crying or lose control of your feelings

examples.en: She broke down when she heard the news.
examples.ko: 그 소식을 듣고 그녀는 무너져 울었어.

examples.en: He broke down in tears at the airport.

senses.note: break down in tears = 눈물을 쏟으며 무너지다. 몸이 아닌 마음의 '고장'.

senses.meaningEn: to divide something into smaller parts so it is easier to understand

examples.en: Let's break the problem down into small steps.
The teacher broke down the word into sounds.
examples.ko: 선생님은 그 단어를 소리별로 나눠 설명했어.

senses.note: break down A into B. 이 뜻에서는 목적어가 있음(타동사).

senses.meaningEn: to enter a building by force, usually to steal things

examples.en: Someone broke in while we were on vacation.
examples.ko: 우리가 휴가 간 사이에 누가 침입했어.

examples.en: Thieves broke in through the back window.

senses.note: 목적어 없이 break in, 목적어가 있으면 break into the house. 명사형 a break-in = 침입 사건.

senses.meaningEn: to interrupt someone when they are talking

examples.en: Sorry to break in, but we have to go.
examples.ko: 말 끊어서 미안한데, 우리 가야 해.

examples.en: She broke in with a question before I finished.
examples.ko: 내가 말을 끝내기 전에 그녀가 질문하며 끼어들었어.

senses.meaningEn: to wear new shoes until they become comfortable

examples.en: I need to break in these new shoes.
examples.ko: 이 새 신발 좀 길들여야 해.

examples.en: It took a week to break my boots in.

senses.note: 신발·야구 글러브·새 차 등을 '길들이다'. 목적어는 중간·뒤 모두 가능.

senses.meaningEn: if a fire, war, or illness breaks out, it starts suddenly

examples.en: A fire broke out in the kitchen last night.
Fights often break out after the game.

senses.note: 주어는 fire, war, fight, disease 처럼 나쁜 일. 명사형 an outbreak(발생, 유행).

senses.meaningEn: to escape from a place such as a prison

examples.en: Two men broke out of prison last week.
examples.ko: 지난주에 남자 두 명이 감옥에서 탈출했어.

examples.en: The dog broke out of the yard again.

senses.note: break out of + 장소. 명사형 a breakout.

senses.meaningEn: if your skin breaks out, spots suddenly appear on it

examples.en: My face breaks out when I eat chocolate.
He broke out in a rash after the medicine.

senses.note: break out in a rash / in a sweat(땀이 확 나다). 명사형 a breakout = 피부 트러블.

senses.meaningEn: to end a romantic relationship

examples.en: Did you hear? Tom and Amy broke up.
She broke up with her boyfriend last week.

senses.note: break up with someone = ~와 헤어지다. 명사형 a breakup. 부부 이혼은 보통 get divorced.

senses.meaningEn: to break into small pieces, or to make something do this

examples.en: Break up the chocolate and put it in the bowl.
The ice is starting to break up on the lake.

senses.note: 요리에서 break up the meat = 고기를 풀어 주다.

senses.meaningEn: if a meeting or school term breaks up, it ends and people leave

examples.en: The meeting broke up at around five.
When does school break up for the summer?

senses.note: school breaks up 은 영국식. 미국은 school lets out / gets out. 밴드 해체도 break up: The band broke up in 2010.

senses.meaningEn: the first meal of the day, eaten in the morning

examples.en: What did you have for breakfast?
I never skip breakfast.

senses.note: have breakfast(관사 없음). eat a breakfast 라고 하지 않음. for breakfast = 아침으로. skip breakfast = 아침을 거르다.

senses.meaningEn: to take air into your body and let it out again

examples.en: Breathe in slowly, then breathe out.
It's hard to breathe with this cold.

senses.note: 동사 breathe /briːð/ 와 명사 breath /breθ/ 를 구분. breathe in(들이쉬다), breathe out(내쉬다), take a deep breath(심호흡하다).

senses.meaningEn: a structure built over a river or road so people and cars can cross

examples.en: We walked across the bridge to the park.
The bridge over the Han River is beautiful at night.

senses.note: 다리를 '건너다'는 cross the bridge / go across the bridge. 신체의 다리(leg)와 헷갈리지 말 것 — bridge 는 건너는 구조물.

senses.meaningEn: full of light or shining strongly

examples.en: The sun is so bright today.
The screen is too bright. Can you turn it down?
examples.ko: 화면이 너무 밝아. 좀 낮춰 줄래?

senses.note: bright light, bright sunshine. 너무 밝아 눈부실 땐 The light is blinding me.

senses.meaningEn: strong and easy to see (used about colors)

examples.en: She loves bright colors like yellow and orange.
examples.ko: 그녀는 노랑·주황 같은 밝은 색을 좋아해.

examples.en: I'll take the bright red one, please.

senses.note: bright red/blue = 선명한 빨강/파랑. 옅은 색은 light blue, 어두운 색은 dark blue.

senses.meaningEn: intelligent and quick to learn

examples.en: He's a bright student who asks good questions.
examples.ko: 그는 좋은 질문을 하는 똑똑한 학생이야.

examples.en: That's a bright idea!

senses.note: a bright kid/student 처럼 아이·학생에게 자주 씀. 미래가 밝다는 a bright future. 밝은 성격은 cheerful 이 더 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: to carry or take something or someone to the place where the speaker is

examples.en: Did you bring your umbrella today?
Can I bring a friend to the party?

senses.note: bring 은 '말하는 사람 쪽으로' 가져오다, take 는 '다른 곳으로' 가져가다. 집에서 '학교에 가져가'는 take it to school, 학교에서 '내일 가져와'는 bring it tomorrow.

senses.meaningEn: to carry food or things to a person, especially in a restaurant

examples.en: Could you bring us some water, please?
The waiter brought the wrong dish.

senses.note: bring + 사람 + 물건 = ~에게 ...을 가져다주다. 식당에서 Could you bring me...? 는 정중한 요청 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to take someone or something with you when you go somewhere

examples.en: Feel free to bring along a friend.
Don't forget to bring your umbrella along.
examples.ko: 우산 챙겨 오는 거 잊지 마.

senses.note: bring + 사람/물건 + along 도 가능. along 은 '같이' 라는 느낌을 더해 주며, 그냥 bring 만 써도 뜻은 거의 같음.

senses.meaningEn: to return with something, or to return something to where it was

examples.en: Can you bring back some snacks from the store?
examples.ko: 가게에서 과자 좀 사 올 수 있어?

examples.en: I brought back a gift for you from Japan.
examples.ko: 일본에서 너 주려고 선물 사 왔어.

senses.note: bring back = 가서 가지고 '이쪽으로' 오다. 빌린 것을 돌려줄 때도(bring the book back) 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to make you remember something from the past

examples.en: This song brings back so many memories.
examples.ko: 이 노래 들으면 추억이 정말 많이 떠올라.

examples.en: Seeing my old school brought back my childhood.
examples.ko: 옛 학교를 보니 어린 시절이 떠올랐어.

senses.note: bring back memories 는 거의 고정 표현. 주어는 노래·사진·장소 같은 '계기'.

senses.meaningEn: to carry something from outside into a building

examples.en: Can you bring in the groceries from the car?
examples.ko: 차에서 장 본 것 좀 들여와 줄래?

examples.en: It's raining, bring the chairs in!

senses.note: bring in the laundry / the dog 처럼 집 안으로 들이는 모든 것에 쓸 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: to earn money, or to ask someone to join or help

examples.en: The food truck brings in about $500 a day.
We need to bring in a plumber to fix this.

senses.note: bring in money / customers = 벌어들이다, 끌어들이다. bring in an expert = 전문가를 부르다.

senses.meaningEn: to carry something out of a place so people can see or use it

examples.en: The waiter brought out our food very quickly.
Mom brought out a big birthday cake.
examples.ko: 엄마가 커다란 생일 케이크를 꺼내 오셨어.

senses.note: 주방·안쪽에서 손님 쪽으로 내오는 느낌. 서빙할 때 자주 듣는 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to produce a new product and start selling it

examples.en: They're bringing out a new phone this fall.
examples.ko: 그 회사가 이번 가을에 새 폰을 출시해.

examples.en: The band brought out a new album last month.
examples.ko: 그 밴드가 지난달에 새 앨범을 내놨어.

senses.note: come out(출시되다)의 타동사 짝: The phone came out. / They brought out the phone.

senses.meaningEn: to bring something or someone to the place where the speaker is, usually a home

examples.en: I'll bring over some food tonight.
She brought her new boyfriend over for dinner.
examples.ko: 그녀가 새 남자친구를 저녁 식사에 데려왔어.

senses.note: over 는 '이쪽(상대방 집)으로 건너와' 라는 느낌. 상대가 있는 곳으로 가는 거면 한국어로는 '가져가다' 로 번역되기도 함. come over = 놀러 오다.

senses.meaningEn: to care for a child until they are an adult

examples.en: She brought up three kids on her own.
I was brought up in a small town.

senses.note: be brought up in/by = ~에서/~에게 자랐다. 미국에서는 raise 가 더 흔하고, bring up 은 영국적 느낌이 조금 있음.

senses.meaningEn: to start talking about a subject

examples.en: Why did you bring up that story again?
Please don't bring up work at dinner.
examples.ko: 저녁 먹을 때 일 얘기는 꺼내지 말아 줘.

senses.note: bring up a topic / a question. 민감한 주제를 꺼낼 때 자주 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: a brush with a long handle that you use to sweep the floor

examples.en: Grab the broom and sweep the floor.
The broom is behind the kitchen door.

senses.note: 쓰레받기는 dustpan. 걸레질용 막대 걸레는 mop.

senses.meaningEn: a boy or man who has the same parents as you

examples.en: My brother plays soccer every Saturday.
Do you have any brothers or sisters?

senses.note: 형/오빠/남동생 구분 없음. older brother / younger (little) brother. big brother 도 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: having the color of chocolate, wood, or coffee

examples.en: She has long brown hair.
examples.ko: 그녀는 긴 갈색 머리를 하고 있어.

examples.en: The leaves turn brown in late fall.

senses.note: brown eyes(갈색 눈), brown rice(현미), brown sugar(흑설탕). 한국어 "브라운"과 같음.

senses.meaningEn: the color brown

examples.en: These boots come in brown or black.
Brown is a warm, natural color.

senses.meaningEn: to clean or make tidy using a brush

examples.en: Brush your teeth before bed.
She brushed her hair and left.

senses.note: brush my teeth(이를 닦다), brush my hair(머리를 빗다). wash my teeth 는 틀림.

senses.meaningEn: a tool with hairs or bristles used for cleaning, painting, or hair

examples.en: Where is my hair brush?
Use a soft brush to clean the shoes.

senses.note: 칫솔 toothbrush, 헤어브러시 hairbrush, 그림용 붓 paintbrush.

senses.meaningEn: to clean your teeth with a toothbrush

examples.en: Brush your teeth before you go to bed.
I brush my teeth twice a day.
examples.ko: 나는 하루에 두 번 이를 닦아.

senses.note: '양치하다'를 wash my teeth ✗ 로 쓰지 않음. 반드시 brush. 소유격을 주어에 맞춤(I brush my teeth). 치실은 floss, 칫솔은 toothbrush, 치약은 toothpaste.

senses.meaningEn: a round open container with a handle, used for carrying water

examples.en: Fill the bucket with water, please.
I need a bucket to wash the car.

senses.note: a bucket of water = 물 한 양동이. 치킨 "한 통"도 a bucket of chicken.

senses.meaningEn: to make something by putting parts together

examples.en: They are building a new school near my house.
examples.ko: 우리 집 근처에 새 학교를 짓고 있어.

examples.en: We built a sandcastle on the beach.

senses.note: build - built - built. build a house / a bridge / a model. 명사 building = 건물.

senses.meaningEn: to make something such as trust or a relationship grow over time

examples.en: It takes time to build trust with someone.
examples.ko: 누군가와 신뢰를 쌓는 데는 시간이 걸려.

examples.en: We built a good friendship over the years.
examples.ko: 우리는 여러 해에 걸쳐 좋은 우정을 쌓았어.

senses.note: build trust / build a relationship / build confidence(자신감을 키우다). 근육도 build muscle.

senses.meaningEn: a place with walls and a roof, such as a house, school, or office

examples.en: My office is in that tall building.
examples.ko: 내 사무실은 저 높은 건물에 있어.

examples.en: This is the oldest building in town.
examples.ko: 이게 이 동네에서 가장 오래된 건물이야.

senses.note: 동사 build(짓다)에서 나온 말. 아파트 '동'은 building 이라고 함(Building 3). 고층 건물은 tall building / skyscraper.

senses.meaningEn: to hit something by accident, usually not very hard

examples.en: I bumped my head on the car door.
She bumped into the table in the dark.

senses.note: bump into 사람 = 우연히 만나다(I bumped into an old friend). 같이 외우면 좋음.

senses.meaningEn: a round, raised area on your body or on a surface

examples.en: I have a bump on my head from the fall.
Slow down, there is a bump in the road.
examples.ko: 속도 줄여, 도로에 튀어나온 데가 있어.

senses.note: speed bump = 과속 방지턱. bumpy road = 울퉁불퉁한 길.

senses.meaningEn: to cook food too long so that it becomes black, or to be on fire

examples.en: Oh no, I burned the toast again!
The wood is burning nicely in the fireplace.

senses.note: 과거형은 burned(미국식)·burnt(영국식) 둘 다. 음식이 "탔다"는 It's burnt. 처럼 형용사로도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to hurt your skin with heat or fire

examples.en: I burned my hand on the hot pan.
Don't touch the stove or you'll burn yourself.
examples.ko: 가스레인지 만지지 마, 데일 수 있어.

senses.note: 햇볕에 타는 건 get sunburned / get a sunburn. 명사 burn = 화상(a bad burn).

senses.meaningEn: if a building burns down, it is destroyed by fire

examples.en: The old barn burned down last summer.
examples.ko: 오래된 헛간이 지난여름에 다 타 버렸어.

examples.en: Someone tried to burn down the school.

senses.note: burn down 은 건물·집처럼 '서 있는 것' 이 무너지듯 타는 것. 종이·음식이 타는 건 그냥 burn.

senses.meaningEn: if a fire or candle burns down, it gets smaller as it burns

examples.en: The campfire burned down to a few red coals.
examples.ko: 캠프파이어는 붉은 숯 몇 개만 남게 타 들어갔어.

examples.en: Let the candles burn down before you throw them away.

senses.meaningEn: if a fire or light burns out, it stops burning or working

examples.en: The candle burned out while we were talking.
examples.ko: 우리가 얘기하는 동안 초가 다 타서 꺼졌어.

examples.en: The kitchen light bulb has burned out again.

senses.note: 전구가 '나가다' = burn out (미국). 영국은 흔히 the bulb has gone.

senses.meaningEn: to become very tired and unable to work because you have worked too hard

examples.en: If you work every weekend, you'll burn out.
She burned out after two years in that job.
examples.ko: 그녀는 그 일을 2년 하고 완전히 지쳐 버렸어.

senses.note: 명사형 burnout(번아웃). be/feel burned out = 지친 상태. 한국어로도 '번아웃' 으로 그대로 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: a large road vehicle that carries many passengers along a fixed route

examples.en: I take the bus to school every day.
examples.ko: 나는 매일 버스 타고 학교에 가.

examples.en: Hurry up, or we'll miss the bus!
Which bus goes to the airport?

senses.note: 복수는 buses. 버스를 '타다'는 take the bus / get on the bus, '내리다'는 get off the bus. '버스로'는 by bus(관사 없음). 놓치다 = miss the bus, 잡다 = catch the bus.

senses.meaningEn: a place where a bus stops so people can get on or off

examples.en: I'll wait for you at the bus stop.
The bus stop is right in front of the bank.
examples.ko: 버스 정류장은 은행 바로 앞에 있어.

senses.note: 큰 버스 터미널은 bus station/terminal. 정류장 '앞/뒤'는 at the bus stop 으로 at 을 씀.

senses.meaningEn: a man who works in business, especially at a high level

examples.en: He is a successful businessman in Busan.
Two businessmen were talking on the train.
examples.ko: 기차에서 사업가 두 명이 이야기를 나누고 있었어.

senses.note: 여성은 businesswoman, 성 중립 표현은 businessperson. 복수는 businessmen(발음 거의 같음). 한국어 '비즈니스맨(회사원)'보다 '사업하는 사람'의 뜻이 강함.

senses.meaningEn: having a lot to do; not free

examples.en: Sorry, I'm busy right now. Can I call you back?
examples.ko: 미안, 지금 바빠. 다시 전화해도 될까?

examples.en: Are you busy this weekend?

senses.note: busy with + 명사(busy with work), busy + -ing(busy cooking). '바쁘다' 는 형용사라 be busy — I busy 처럼 be 를 빠뜨리는 실수 주의.

senses.meaningEn: full of people, cars, or activity

examples.en: The streets are busy on Friday nights.
This is the busiest station in the city.

senses.note: a busy road = 차가 많은 길. 전화에서 The line is busy = 통화 중.

senses.meaningEn: used to join two ideas when the second is different from or opposite to the first

examples.en: I want to go, but I'm too tired.
The food was cheap but really good.

senses.note: 문장 중간에 쓰고 앞에 쉼표를 찍는 게 기본. However 는 더 격식. 한국어 '그런데'를 매번 but 으로 옮기면 어색할 수 있음—화제 전환은 by the way, anyway.

senses.meaningEn: except for

examples.en: Everyone came but Tom.
I eat everything but mushrooms.

senses.note: everyone/nothing/all + but = 제외. nothing but = 오직(She drinks nothing but water).

senses.meaningEn: a person who cuts and sells meat

examples.en: The butcher cut the meat into thin slices.
examples.ko: 정육점 주인이 고기를 얇게 썰어 줬어.

examples.en: Ask the butcher for two pounds of beef.

senses.note: 가게 자체는 butcher's 또는 butcher shop. 미국에서는 마트의 meat counter 에서 사는 경우가 많아 butcher 를 볼 일이 적음.

senses.meaningEn: a soft yellow food made from cream that you spread on bread or cook with

examples.en: Can you pass me the butter, please?
Put some butter in the pan first.

senses.note: 셀 수 없는 명사: a stick of butter(한 덩이), a pat of butter(작은 조각). peanut butter(땅콩버터)도 자주 쓰임. 발음은 [버터]보다 [버러]에 가까움(미국식).

senses.meaningEn: to spread butter on something

examples.en: Butter the toast while it's still warm.
Do you want your bread buttered?

senses.note: butter up (someone) = 아부하다, 비위를 맞추다 (구어).

senses.meaningEn: a nervous, fluttering feeling in your stomach before something important

examples.en: I have butterflies in my stomach before the test.
examples.ko: 시험 앞두고 너무 긴장돼서 속이 울렁거려.

examples.en: She gets butterflies in her stomach every time she sees him.
examples.ko: 그녀는 그를 볼 때마다 가슴이 두근거려.

senses.note: 주어에 맞게 my/her/his 를 바꿈. 보통 get/have butterflies (in one's stomach). 시험·발표·첫 데이트 같은 "좋은 긴장"에 주로 씀.

senses.meaningEn: an insect with large, colorful wings that flies in the daytime

examples.en: A blue butterfly landed on my hand.
We saw lots of butterflies in the garden.

senses.note: 복수형은 butterflies. 'I have butterflies in my stomach' 은 긴장해서 속이 떨린다는 관용 표현. 수영 '접영'도 butterfly.

senses.meaningEn: a small round thing on clothes that you push through a hole to fasten them

examples.en: A button came off my shirt.
This coat has big black buttons.
examples.ko: 이 코트에는 큰 검은 단추가 달려 있어.

senses.meaningEn: a small part of a machine that you press to make it work

examples.en: Press the red button to start.
Which button turns on the TV?

senses.note: press/push a button = 버튼을 누르다. 화면 속 버튼도 button.

senses.meaningEn: to fasten clothes with buttons

examples.en: Button your coat; it's windy.
He buttoned his shirt to the top.

senses.note: button (up) = 채우다, unbutton = 풀다.

senses.meaningEn: to get something by paying money for it

examples.en: I bought some bread and eggs this morning.
examples.ko: 오늘 아침에 빵과 달걀을 좀 샀어.

examples.en: Where did you buy that jacket?

senses.note: buy A for B / buy B A = B에게 A를 사 주다(I bought her a book). 과거형 bought 발음 /bɔːt/. '사 오다'는 pick up 도 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to pay for food or a drink for someone else

examples.en: Let me buy you lunch today.
He bought everyone a drink after the game.
examples.ko: 경기 끝나고 그가 모두에게 한잔씩 샀어.

senses.note: '내가 살게'는 I'll buy. / It's on me. / My treat. 등으로 말함. 한국식 '밥 사 줘'는 Buy me lunch. 보다 Treat me to lunch. 가 부드러움.

senses.meaningEn: used to say how you travel or do something

examples.en: I go to work by subway.
Can I pay by card?

senses.note: by bus/train/car/plane(관사 없음). 걸어서는 on foot. by hand(손으로), by email(이메일로).

senses.meaningEn: next to or near something

examples.en: Sit by the window if you like.
There's a café by the river.

senses.note: by = next to 보다 조금 느슨한 '근처'. by the sea(바닷가에).

senses.meaningEn: not later than a particular time

examples.en: Please finish your homework by Friday.
I'll be home by seven.

senses.note: by = 늦어도 그때까지(완료 기한), until = 그때까지 계속(상태 지속). I'll stay until 7(7시까지 있다) vs I'll leave by 7(7시 전에 떠난다).

senses.meaningEn: used to say who did or made something

examples.en: This song is by my favorite singer.
examples.ko: 이 노래는 내가 제일 좋아하는 가수 거야.

examples.en: The window was broken by the wind.

senses.note: a book by Hemingway(헤밍웨이가 쓴). 수동태의 행위자: was made by. by myself = 혼자서.

senses.meaningEn: done with your hands, not by a machine

examples.en: I wash this sweater by hand.
She made all the cards by hand.

senses.note: wash / make / write / sew by hand. 형용사형은 handmade(손으로 만든). 관사 없이 by hand.

senses.meaningEn: from memory, so that you can say it without reading

examples.en: I know this song by heart.
Learn the poem by heart for Friday.

senses.note: know / learn / memorize ... by heart. "마음으로"가 아니라 "암기해서"라는 뜻. 관사 없이 by heart.

senses.meaningEn: used to add something new to the conversation that is not closely connected

examples.en: By the way, did you call your mom?
Nice bag, by the way. Where did you get it?

senses.note: 주제를 살짝 바꿀 때 문장 앞이나 끝에 붙임. 문자에서는 BTW 로 줄임. 격식 글에서는 incidentally 나 Also, ... 를 씀. 한국어 '그런데(but)' 처럼 반대 뜻은 없음.

senses.meaningEn: an informal way to say goodbye

examples.en: Bye! See you tomorrow.
Okay, I have to go now. Bye!
examples.ko: 그래, 이제 가야 해. 잘 있어!

senses.note: goodbye 의 줄임말. Bye-bye 는 아이에게 또는 아주 친근하게. 전화 끊을 때도 Bye. 한국어처럼 떠나는 사람·남는 사람 구분 없이 둘 다 bye.

senses.meaningEn: a large round vegetable with thick green or white leaves

examples.en: Kimchi is made from cabbage.
I had a cabbage salad for lunch.

senses.note: 배추는 napa cabbage 또는 Chinese cabbage 라고 구분해 말함.

senses.meaningEn: a small restaurant where you can buy coffee, drinks, and light meals

examples.en: Let's meet at the cafe on the corner.
I like studying at a quiet cafe.
examples.ko: 나는 조용한 카페에서 공부하는 게 좋아.

senses.note: café 로도 씀. 강세는 뒤(/kæˈfeɪ/). 미국에서는 coffee shop 도 흔히 씀. 영어 cafe 는 간단한 식사도 파는 곳.

senses.meaningEn: a restaurant in a school or office where you pick up your own food

examples.en: Let's eat lunch in the cafeteria.
The school cafeteria serves pizza on Fridays.

senses.note: cafe(카페)와 다름. 식판을 들고 음식을 받아 가는 셀프 식당. 미국 학교에서는 lunchroom 이라고도 함.

senses.meaningEn: a box made of bars or wire for keeping birds or animals in

examples.en: The bird got out of its cage.
Please don't put your hands in the cage.

senses.note: 햄스터·새 등 작은 동물용. 동물원의 큰 우리나 울타리는 enclosure 라고도 함.

senses.meaningEn: a sweet soft food made from flour, eggs, sugar, and butter, baked in an oven

examples.en: We're making a cake for her birthday.
examples.ko: 우리 그녀 생일 케이크를 만들 거야.

examples.en: Would you like a piece of cake?

senses.note: 케이크 한 조각은 a piece/slice of cake. a piece of cake = 아주 쉬운 일(관용구). 생일 케이크는 birthday cake.

senses.meaningEn: a chart or app that shows the days, weeks, and months of a year

examples.en: There's a calendar on the kitchen wall.
Let me check my calendar first.
examples.ko: 먼저 내 캘린더 좀 확인해 볼게.

senses.note: 요즘은 스마트폰 일정 앱도 calendar 라고 한다. put it on the calendar = 일정에 넣다. 철자 -dar(-der 아님)에 주의.

senses.meaningEn: to phone someone

examples.en: Call me when you get there.
I'll call you back in ten minutes.

senses.note: call back = 다시 전화하다. '전화하다'에 phone to 를 붙이지 않음.

senses.meaningEn: to say someone's name loudly, or to give a name

examples.en: Mom is calling you for dinner.
My friends call me Jay.

senses.note: What do you call this in English? = 이거 영어로 뭐라고 해?

senses.meaningEn: an act of talking to someone on the phone

examples.en: I got a call from my sister.
Sorry, I have to take this call.

senses.note: make a call = 전화를 걸다, take a call = 전화를 받다.

senses.meaningEn: to phone someone again, or phone someone who called you

examples.en: I'm busy now. Can I call you back later?
examples.ko: 지금 바빠. 나중에 다시 전화해도 될까?

examples.en: She didn't call me back.

senses.note: call 사람 back 순서(call back me ✗). 목적어 없이 "I'll call back later." 도 가능. 전화 응대: "Can he call you back?" = 다시 전화드리라고 할까요?

senses.meaningEn: to stop working for the rest of the day

examples.en: It's already seven. Let's call it a day.
examples.ko: 벌써 일곱 시네. 오늘은 여기까지 하자.

examples.en: I'm tired, so I'm going to call it a day.

senses.note: 밤에 끝낼 때는 call it a night 라고도 함. '그만두다(영구적)' 의 뜻으로도 확장: After 30 years, he decided to call it a day.

senses.meaningEn: to decide that a planned event will not happen

examples.en: They called off the game because of the rain.
We had to call off the party.

senses.note: call off = cancel 의 구어 표현. 대명사는 중간에(call it off). "called off due to rain" 은 자주 보이는 콜로케이션.

senses.meaningEn: to say something loudly so that people can hear you

examples.en: The teacher called out our names one by one.
examples.ko: 선생님이 우리 이름을 하나씩 크게 불렀어.

examples.en: I called out to him, but he didn't hear me.

senses.note: call out 이름/답 = 큰 소리로 부르다. call out to 사람 = 멀리 있는 사람을 부르다.

senses.meaningEn: to publicly say that someone has done something wrong

examples.en: She called him out for being rude.
If someone lies, call them out.

senses.note: call 사람 out on/for 잘못. SNS 에서 아주 흔한 표현. 뉘앙스가 꽤 직설적이니 격식 자리에서는 point out 을 쓰는 게 안전.

senses.meaningEn: to phone someone

examples.en: Call me up when you get home.
I called up my grandma last night.

senses.note: call up = call(미국 구어). 영국에서는 ring up. call 사람 up 순서로 많이 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to choose someone to join a national or higher team

examples.en: He was called up to the national team last week.
The coach called up two young players.
examples.ko: 감독이 어린 선수 두 명을 불러올렸어.

senses.note: 주로 수동태 be called up (to ~). 스포츠 뉴스에서 자주 보임. 군대 소집에도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: relaxed and not worried, angry, or excited

examples.en: Stay calm and tell me what happened.
She always stays calm in an emergency.

senses.note: l 은 소리 나지 않음 /kɑːm/. keep/stay calm = 침착함을 유지하다. Calm down! 은 좀 명령조로 들릴 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: (of weather or the sea) quiet, with no wind or big waves

examples.en: The sea was calm, so the boat trip was nice.
It was a calm, quiet morning.

senses.meaningEn: to become or make someone quiet and relaxed

examples.en: Calm down, everything is going to be okay.
It took a while to calm the baby.
examples.ko: 아기를 달래는 데 시간이 좀 걸렸어.

senses.note: calm down 은 자동사(진정하다)·타동사(진정시키다) 둘 다 가능. calm someone down = 누구를 달래다.

senses.meaningEn: to stop feeling angry, upset, or excited

examples.en: Calm down, everything is going to be fine.
It took him a while to calm down.
examples.ko: 그가 진정하는 데 시간이 좀 걸렸어.

senses.note: 화난 사람에게 Calm down 이라고 하면 오히려 더 화나게 할 수 있음(한국어 '진정해' 와 같음). 부드럽게는 Take a deep breath / It's okay.

senses.meaningEn: to make someone or something less upset or excited

examples.en: She calmed the baby down with a song.
Nothing could calm him down after the game.
examples.ko: 경기 후에 아무것도 그를 진정시킬 수 없었어.

senses.note: calm + 사람 + down 또는 calm down + 사람. 상황이 잠잠해질 때도: Things have calmed down at work.

senses.meaningEn: a large desert animal with a long neck and one or two humps on its back

examples.en: We rode camels in the desert in Egypt.
A camel can go many days without water.
examples.ko: 낙타는 물 없이 여러 날을 버틸 수 있어.

senses.note: 낙타의 등 혹은 hump. 강세는 첫 음절, 두 번째 음절은 약하게(/ˈkæml/). camel 은 '낙타색(연한 황갈색)'을 뜻하는 색 이름으로도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: a device for taking photos or videos

examples.en: Don't forget to bring your camera on the trip.
examples.ko: 여행 갈 때 카메라 잊지 말고 가져가.

examples.en: My phone camera takes great pictures.
examples.ko: 내 폰 카메라는 사진이 정말 잘 나와.

senses.note: take a picture/photo = 사진을 찍다. on camera = 카메라에 찍힌. Smile for the camera! = 카메라 보고 웃어!

senses.meaningEn: the activity of staying outdoors in a tent for a holiday

examples.en: We're going camping by the river this weekend.
Camping with kids is fun but a lot of work.
examples.ko: 아이들과 캠핑은 재밌지만 할 일이 많아.

senses.note: go camping(캠핑 가다). 캠핑장은 campsite / campground, 텐트를 치다는 set up a tent. 차박은 car camping.

senses.meaningEn: to be able to do something

examples.en: I can swim, but I can't dive.
examples.ko: 나는 수영은 할 수 있지만 다이빙은 못 해.

examples.en: Can you speak Korean?

senses.note: 조동사이므로 뒤에 동사 원형(can swim, can to swim ✗). 3인칭에도 s 를 붙이지 않음(He can ✓, He cans ✗). 부정은 can't / cannot(한 단어).

senses.meaningEn: to be allowed to do something

examples.en: You can sit anywhere you like.
Can I use your phone for a second?
examples.ko: 잠깐 네 전화 좀 써도 될까?

senses.note: 허락을 구할 때 Can I ~? 는 친근한 말투. 격식·공손은 Could I ~? / May I ~?.

senses.meaningEn: used to ask someone to do something for you

examples.en: Can I have a glass of water, please?
Can you help me with this bag?
examples.ko: 이 가방 좀 도와줄 수 있어요?

senses.note: 식당·가게에서 주문할 때 Can I have ~? 가 가장 흔한 표현. please 를 붙이면 충분히 공손함.

senses.meaningEn: a metal container for food or drink

examples.en: He opened a can of soda.
We need two cans of tuna for dinner.
examples.ko: 저녁에 참치 캔 두 개가 필요해.

senses.note: a can of + 내용물. 영국에서는 tin 도 씀. 조동사 can 과 철자가 같으니 문맥으로 구분.

senses.meaningEn: a sweet fizzy drink in a metal can

examples.en: He opened a can of soda and sat down.
examples.ko: 그는 탄산음료 한 캔을 따고 자리에 앉았어.

examples.en: How much is a can of soda from the machine?

senses.note: soda 는 미국 일반 표현이고, 지역에 따라 pop, coke(브랜드 상관없이)라고도 한다. 영국은 fizzy drink. 한국어 '사이다'는 영어로 lemon soda/Sprite; 영어 cider 는 사과 음료·사과주다.

senses.meaningEn: a stick of wax with a string inside that you burn for light

examples.en: We lit a candle when the lights went out.
She blew out the candles on her cake.
examples.ko: 그녀는 케이크 위의 초를 불어서 꺼뜨렸어.

senses.note: light a candle = 초를 켜다, blow out a candle = 초를 불어 끄다. 생일 케이크 초도 candles.

senses.meaningEn: a sweet food made from sugar or chocolate

examples.en: Don't eat too much candy before dinner.
examples.ko: 저녁 먹기 전에 사탕 너무 많이 먹지 마.

examples.en: The kids got lots of candy on Halloween.

senses.note: 미국식. 영국식은 sweets. 보통 셀 수 없는 명사로 쓰고, 한 개는 a piece of candy.

senses.meaningEn: a soft flat hat with a curved part at the front

examples.en: He always wears a baseball cap.
Put your cap on before we go outside.

senses.note: baseball cap, swimming cap(수영모). 테가 둥글게 있는 모자는 hat.

senses.meaningEn: a small lid that covers the top of a bottle, pen, or tube

examples.en: Put the cap back on the toothpaste.
I can't open the cap of this bottle.

senses.note: 돌려서 닫는 작은 뚜껑은 cap, 냄비·상자처럼 큰 뚜껑은 lid.

senses.meaningEn: a road vehicle with an engine and four wheels that carries a few people

examples.en: I usually go to work by car.
Can you drive me home in your car?
examples.ko: 네 차로 집까지 태워 줄 수 있어?

examples.en: We're getting a new car next month.
examples.ko: 우리 다음 달에 새 차 사.

senses.note: '차로 가다'는 by car(관사 없음) 또는 in my car / drive. 차에 '타다'는 get in the car, '내리다'는 get out of the car (버스·기차는 get on/off). 한국식 '카'는 안 통함.

senses.meaningEn: one of the separate sections of a train

examples.en: Our seats are in car number five.
The dining car is at the front of the train.

senses.note: 미국식 car, 영국식 carriage/coach. KTX 안내방송의 '5호차'가 car 5. 지하철 칸도 subway car.

senses.meaningEn: one of a set of small pieces of stiff paper used for playing games

examples.en: Do you want to play cards tonight?
Pick a card, any card.
examples.ko: 카드 한 장 골라 봐, 아무거나.

senses.note: play cards 는 복수형으로. 카드 한 벌은 a deck of cards. 보드게임의 카드도 같은 단어.

senses.meaningEn: a folded piece of stiff paper with a picture and a message that you send to someone

examples.en: I wrote a birthday card for my mom.
Thanks for the lovely card!

senses.note: birthday card, Christmas card, thank-you card. 편지와 달리 짧은 메시지만 적음.

senses.meaningEn: a small plastic card used to pay for things or to show who you are

examples.en: Can I pay by card?
I forgot my card at home.

senses.note: credit card(신용카드), debit card(체크카드), ID card(신분증). 미국에서 '체크카드'는 check card 가 아니라 debit card.

senses.meaningEn: to think that something is important and feel interested or worried about it

examples.en: I don't care what people think of me.
She really cares about her students.

senses.note: care about = 소중히 여기다, care for = 돌보다 또는 좋아하다. 'I don't care.' 는 '상관없어'인데 상황에 따라 무뚝뚝하게 들릴 수 있음 — 부드럽게는 'Either is fine.'. 'Who cares?' = 누가 신경 써?

senses.meaningEn: the act of looking after someone or something

examples.en: Take care! See you next week.
My grandmother needs care every day.

senses.note: take care of = 돌보다/처리하다. 헤어질 때 'Take care!' 는 '몸 조심해, 잘 가'. 'Handle with care.' = 취급 주의.

senses.meaningEn: to feel that someone or something is important to you

examples.en: I really care about you.
He cares about his friends a lot.

senses.note: care about = 마음을 쓰다(중요하게 생각). care for = 돌보다. 'I don't care.' = 상관없어/신경 안 써(약간 차갑게 들릴 수 있음).

senses.meaningEn: to think that something matters and be interested in it

examples.en: She doesn't care about money.
Young people care about the environment.

senses.note: What I care about is ~ = 내가 중요하게 생각하는 건 ~이다. 반대 표현 couldn't care less = 전혀 관심 없다.

senses.meaningEn: to look after someone who is sick, old, or very young

examples.en: She cares for her elderly father at home.
Nurses care for patients day and night.

senses.note: take care of 보다 약간 격식 있고 글말 느낌. 식물·피부 관리에도 care for your skin.

senses.meaningEn: to like or want something, used mostly in questions and negatives

examples.en: Would you care for some coffee?
I don't really care for spicy food.

senses.note: Would you care for ~? 는 Would you like ~? 의 정중한 버전. I don't care for ~ 는 '싫다'를 부드럽게 말하는 방식. '상관없다'의 I don't care 와 혼동 주의.

senses.meaningEn: giving attention to avoid mistakes or danger

examples.en: Be careful! The floor is wet.
She is always careful with money.

senses.note: Be careful! 은 '조심해!' 의 가장 기본 표현. careful with + 물건, careful of + 위험(careful of the dog). 부사 carefully.

senses.meaningEn: with care and attention, so you do not make a mistake or get hurt

examples.en: Please listen carefully to the teacher.
Drive carefully. The road is wet.

senses.note: listen/read/drive carefully 자주 결합. 명사 care, 형용사 careful. 'Be careful!'(조심해!)은 형용사.

senses.meaningEn: not giving enough attention, so you make mistakes

examples.en: I made a careless mistake on the test.
He's careless with his things and loses them.
examples.ko: 그는 물건을 함부로 다뤄서 자주 잃어버려.

senses.note: a careless mistake = 실수 중에서도 '부주의로 인한' 실수. careless 와 carefree(걱정 없는, 태평한) 는 다름.

senses.meaningEn: thick, soft material that covers a floor

examples.en: I spilled coffee on the carpet.
The bedroom has a soft gray carpet.
examples.ko: 침실에는 부드러운 회색 카펫이 깔려 있어.

senses.note: 바닥 전체를 덮는 것은 carpet, 일부만 깔린 작은 것은 rug. 카펫을 청소하다 = vacuum the carpet.

senses.meaningEn: a long orange vegetable that grows underground

examples.en: Rabbits love eating carrots.
examples.ko: 토끼는 당근 먹는 걸 아주 좋아해.

examples.en: Chop the carrots and put them in the soup.

senses.note: carrot and stick = 당근과 채찍(보상과 벌).

senses.meaningEn: to hold something and move it from one place to another

examples.en: Let me carry that heavy box for you.
examples.ko: 그 무거운 상자 내가 들어 줄게.

examples.en: She carried the baby up the stairs.

senses.note: carry 는 '들고 이동'하는 동작. 잠깐 들고 있는 건 hold. 과거형 carried(y→ied). carry 는 '가져오다'의 방향 의미가 없으므로 bring/take 와 다름.

senses.meaningEn: to have something with you, or (of a shop) to have goods for sale

examples.en: I always carry a small umbrella in my bag.
examples.ko: 항상 가방에 작은 우산을 넣고 다녀.

examples.en: Does this store carry phone cases?

senses.note: carry cash(현금을 지니다), carry an ID. 가게 점원에게 Do you carry...? = ~ 파나요? 테이크아웃 '캐리어'는 영어로 cup holder/tray.

senses.meaningEn: to continue doing something

examples.en: Sorry to interrupt. Please carry on.
She carried on talking as if nothing happened.
examples.ko: 그녀는 아무 일 없었다는 듯 계속 말했어.

senses.note: carry on + -ing / carry on with + 명사. 영국에서 특히 흔함(Keep calm and carry on). 미국은 go on / keep going 이 더 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: to take a bag with you onto a plane instead of checking it

examples.en: You can carry on one small bag.
examples.ko: 작은 가방 하나는 기내에 들고 탈 수 있어요.

examples.en: I'll carry this on so it doesn't get lost.
examples.ko: 잃어버리지 않게 이건 기내에 들고 탈게.

senses.note: 명사 carry-on = 기내 휴대 가방(a carry-on bag). 부치는 짐은 checked bag.

senses.meaningEn: to do and complete a task, plan, or promise

examples.en: The students carried out a simple science experiment.
He always carries out what he promises.

senses.note: carry out a plan / an experiment / a test / a promise. do 보다 격식 있고 '제대로 끝까지 한다' 는 느낌. 발음 주의: carry 는 /ˈkæri/.

senses.meaningEn: to buy food at a restaurant and take it away to eat somewhere else

examples.en: Is this for here or to carry out?
We carried out some pizza and ate at home.

senses.note: 미국에서 명사 carry-out / takeout = 포장 음식. 영국은 takeaway. 한국어 '테이크아웃' 과 같은 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: a large metal basket on wheels that you push around a store

examples.en: Can you grab a cart at the entrance?
Our cart was full of snacks and drinks.

senses.note: 미국식 shopping cart. 영국은 trolley. 온라인 쇼핑의 '장바구니'도 cart(add to cart).

senses.meaningEn: a small vehicle with wheels that is pushed or pulled

examples.en: He pulled the heavy cart up the hill.
examples.ko: 그는 무거운 수레를 언덕 위로 끌었어.

examples.en: We bought hot dogs from a food cart.
examples.ko: 우리는 길거리 음식 카트에서 핫도그를 샀어.

senses.note: luggage cart(공항 수하물 카트), food cart(길거리 음식 수레), golf cart(골프 카트).

senses.meaningEn: a film or TV program made with drawings, usually for children

examples.en: The kids are watching cartoons in the living room.
examples.ko: 아이들이 거실에서 만화 영화를 보고 있어.

examples.en: I loved this cartoon when I was little.
examples.ko: 어렸을 때 이 만화 영화 정말 좋아했어.

senses.note: TV 만화는 cartoon, 일본식 애니는 anime. 한국의 '만화책'은 cartoon 이 아니라 comic book.

senses.meaningEn: a funny drawing in a newspaper or magazine, often about the news

examples.en: There's a funny cartoon in today's newspaper.
examples.ko: 오늘 신문에 재미있는 만화가 하나 있어.

examples.en: He draws cartoons for a magazine.

senses.note: 신문의 시사 만화는 political cartoon / editorial cartoon. 그리는 사람은 cartoonist.

senses.meaningEn: money in the form of coins and bills, not cards

examples.en: Will you pay by cash or card?
I don't have any cash on me right now.

senses.note: 불가산 명사. pay in cash / pay cash = 현금으로 내다. 현금 인출기는 ATM 또는 cash machine. 한국의 '캐시(포인트)'와는 다름.

senses.meaningEn: a person whose job is to take money from customers in a store

examples.en: The cashier gave me the wrong change.
Please pay the cashier at the front.

senses.note: 강세가 뒤에 있음 /kæˈʃɪr/. 계산대는 cash register 또는 checkout. 셀프 계산대는 self-checkout.

senses.meaningEn: a large, strong building with thick walls, built long ago to protect people from attack

examples.en: There's an old castle on top of the hill.
The castle has high walls and a big gate.
examples.ko: 그 성은 높은 벽과 큰 문이 있어.

senses.note: t 는 묵음 → /ˈkæsəl/ '캐슬'. palace(궁전, 거주용)와 구분. 모래성은 sandcastle, 바운스 놀이기구는 bouncy castle.

senses.meaningEn: a small furry animal with whiskers and a long tail, often kept as a pet

examples.en: My cat sleeps on my bed every night.
examples.ko: 우리 고양이는 매일 밤 내 침대에서 자.

examples.en: Do you like cats or dogs more?
examples.ko: 고양이가 더 좋아, 개가 더 좋아?

senses.note: 새끼 고양이는 kitten. 고양이 소리 meow(야옹). 길고양이는 stray cat. cat person(고양이파) / dog person(개파).

senses.meaningEn: to take and hold something that is moving through the air

examples.en: Catch the ball with both hands!
He caught the keys I threw to him.

senses.note: '공놀이하다'는 play catch. 과거형 caught 발음은 /kɔːt/ — 'caught' 와 'cut' 을 구분할 것.

senses.meaningEn: to get on a bus, train, or plane before it leaves

examples.en: I have to catch the 8 o'clock bus.
We ran fast and caught the last train.
examples.ko: 우리는 빨리 달려서 마지막 열차를 탔어.

senses.note: catch the bus ↔ miss the bus(놓치다). 단순히 '버스로 가다'는 take the bus. catch 는 시간에 맞춰 '잡아 탄다'는 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: to get an illness from someone or something

examples.en: I think I caught a cold from my sister.
Wash your hands so you don't catch the flu.

senses.note: catch a cold / catch the flu 로 고정 표현처럼 쓰임. 한국어 '걸리다'를 hang 으로 옮기면 안 됨.

senses.meaningEn: to get on a bus in time before it leaves

examples.en: I have to catch a bus at eight.
We ran but we still caught the bus.

senses.note: catch 는 '놓치지 않고 시간 맞춰 탄다'는 느낌. 단순히 이동 수단으로 버스를 이용하면 take a bus. 반대는 miss the bus(버스를 놓치다). catch a train / catch a flight 도 같은 패턴.

senses.meaningEn: to become ill with a cold

examples.en: Wear a jacket or you'll catch a cold.
examples.ko: 재킷 입어, 안 그러면 감기 걸려.

examples.en: I caught a cold last week and I still have a cough.
examples.ko: 지난주에 감기에 걸렸는데 아직도 기침이 나.

senses.note: 감기에 '걸리다'는 catch 또는 get. 'take a cold' 는 틀린 표현. 이미 걸려 있는 상태는 have a cold(I have a cold = 감기 중). catch the flu / catch a virus 도 같은 패턴.

senses.meaningEn: to reach the same level or place as others after being behind

examples.en: I missed a week of class, so I need to catch up.
Run faster, or you won't catch up!
examples.ko: 더 빨리 뛰어, 안 그러면 못 따라잡아!

senses.note: catch up on + 밀린 일: catch up on sleep / homework / emails = 밀린 잠·숙제·메일을 해치우다.

senses.meaningEn: to talk with someone you haven't seen for a while and share news

examples.en: Let's grab coffee and catch up soon!
It was great to catch up with you yesterday.
examples.ko: 어제 오랜만에 얘기 나눠서 정말 좋았어.

senses.note: 오랜만에 만난 친구에게 자주 쓰는 표현. 명사 catch-up = 근황 수다(have a quick catch-up).

senses.meaningEn: to reach someone who is ahead of you by going faster

examples.en: Go ahead, I'll catch up with you later.
She ran fast and caught up with the bus.

senses.note: catch up with + 사람/대상. 실제로 달려 따라잡을 때도, 실력·수준을 따라잡을 때도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to meet or talk with someone and find out what they have been doing

examples.en: I caught up with an old friend over lunch.
examples.ko: 점심 먹으면서 옛 친구와 오랜만에 이야기했어.

examples.en: We should catch up with each other more often.
examples.ko: 우리 좀 더 자주 근황 나눠야 해.

senses.note: catch up 과 같은 뜻이고 상대를 밝힐 때 with 를 붙임.

senses.meaningEn: a large hole in the side of a hill or under the ground

examples.en: It's dark and cold inside the cave.
Bats live in this cave.

senses.note: 동굴 안으로 들어가다 = go into the cave. 동굴 탐험 = caving.

senses.meaningEn: the top inside surface of a room

examples.en: This room has a very high ceiling.
There's a small crack in the ceiling.

senses.note: roof(지붕)와 구분: 방 안에서 올려다보는 면이 ceiling. 철자 주의: cieling ✗.

senses.meaningEn: to do something special for a happy event or day

examples.en: How do you celebrate your birthday?
Let's go out and celebrate tonight!

senses.note: celebrate + 날/일(celebrate Christmas). 사람에게 '축하해'는 Congratulations! — celebrate you 라고 하지 않음.

senses.meaningEn: a small unit of money; there are 100 cents in a dollar

examples.en: The gum costs ninety-nine cents.
I found a few cents under the sofa.

senses.note: 기호 ¢. $1.50 은 one dollar fifty 또는 a dollar fifty 로 읽고 cents 는 보통 생략. percent(퍼센트)와 혼동 주의.

senses.meaningEn: a breakfast food made from grain, usually eaten with milk

examples.en: I usually have cereal for breakfast.
Pour some milk on your cereal.

senses.note: 셀 수 없는 명사. 종류를 말할 때만 cereals. serial(연속물)과 발음이 같음.

senses.meaningEn: a seat for one person, usually with a back and four legs

examples.en: Pull up a chair and join us.
We need two more chairs for the guests.
examples.ko: 손님용 의자가 두 개 더 필요해.

senses.note: 의자에 앉다 = sit on a chair, 안락의자처럼 푹 들어가는 의자는 sit in an armchair. 등받이 없는 의자는 stool, 긴 의자는 bench.

senses.meaningEn: a soft white stick used for writing on a blackboard

examples.en: We're out of chalk again.
The kids drew pictures with chalk on the sidewalk.

senses.note: 셀 수 없는 명사. '분필 한 개'는 a piece of chalk.

senses.meaningEn: a person or team that has won a competition, especially in sports

examples.en: He is the national chess champion.
Our school became the champions this year!

senses.note: world champion(세계 챔피언), become the champion(우승하다). 우승 대회는 championship. 발음 /ˈtʃæmpiən/ — '챔피온'이 아니라 '챔피언'.

senses.meaningEn: to make or become different

examples.en: Can we change the meeting to Friday?
You've changed a lot since high school.
examples.ko: 너 고등학교 때 이후로 많이 변했다.

senses.note: change one's mind = 마음을 바꾸다.

senses.meaningEn: to put on different clothes

examples.en: Give me five minutes to change.
I need to change into something warmer.

senses.note: change clothes / change into + 옷.

senses.meaningEn: to get off one bus or train and get on another

examples.en: Change trains at the next station.
Do I have to change buses to get there?

senses.note: change trains / change buses 처럼 복수형을 씀.

senses.meaningEn: coins, or the money you get back when you pay too much

examples.en: Here's your change. Have a nice day.
examples.ko: 거스름돈 여기 있습니다. 좋은 하루 보내세요.

examples.en: Do you have change for a twenty?

senses.note: Keep the change. = 잔돈은 가지세요.

senses.meaningEn: to fill a battery or device with electricity

examples.en: Let me charge up my phone before we go.
examples.ko: 가기 전에 휴대폰 충전 좀 할게.

examples.en: The car takes about an hour to charge up.
examples.ko: 그 차는 충전하는 데 한 시간쯤 걸려.

senses.note: charge 만 써도 되지만 up 을 붙이면 '끝까지, 완전히'라는 느낌. 충전기는 charger, 완충은 fully charged.

senses.meaningEn: to make someone excited and full of energy

examples.en: The music charged up the whole crowd.
I'm all charged up for the game tonight!
examples.ko: 오늘 밤 경기 때문에 완전히 들떠 있어!

senses.note: 형용사처럼 charged up(흥분한, 신난) 으로 자주 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: to run after someone or something to catch them

examples.en: The dog chased the cat up a tree.
examples.ko: 개가 고양이를 쫓아서 나무 위로 몰았어.

examples.en: The police chased the thief down the street.

senses.note: chase after 사람/사물 도 가능. 명사 a car chase(자동차 추격전).

senses.meaningEn: to try hard to get something you want

examples.en: She moved to Seoul to chase her dream.
Stop chasing money and enjoy your life.

senses.note: chase your dreams = 꿈을 좇다. follow your dreams 와 비슷.

senses.meaningEn: to talk with someone in a friendly, relaxed way

examples.en: We chatted for an hour over coffee.
examples.ko: 우리는 커피 마시면서 한 시간 동안 수다를 떨었어.

examples.en: Let's chat later, I'm busy now.

senses.note: chat with/to + 사람. 가볍고 편한 대화. 명사도 됨: have a chat = 잠깐 얘기하다. 과거형은 t 를 겹쳐 chatted.

senses.meaningEn: to exchange written messages with someone online

examples.en: I was chatting with my friend online.
You can chat with support on the website.

senses.note: 명사: a group chat = 단체 채팅방, a chat room. 한국어 '채팅'과 거의 같음.

senses.meaningEn: costing little money

examples.en: These shoes were really cheap, only ten dollars.
examples.ko: 이 신발 정말 싸게 샀어, 10달러밖에 안 했어.

examples.en: Is there a cheap hotel near the station?

senses.note: cheap 은 '싸구려·질이 안 좋은' 느낌이 섞일 수 있음. 칭찬으로 말할 때는 inexpensive, affordable, a good price 가 안전.

senses.meaningEn: not willing to spend money

examples.en: Don't be so cheap. Buy her a nice gift.
examples.ko: 그렇게 짜게 굴지 마. 좋은 선물 하나 사 줘.

examples.en: My brother is too cheap to eat out.
examples.ko: 우리 형은 너무 짜서 외식을 안 해.

senses.note: 사람에게 쓰면 부정적인 뜻. 비슷한 말 stingy. 돈을 신중하게 쓰는 좋은 의미는 careful with money.

senses.meaningEn: to act dishonestly to win or get an advantage, such as in a test or game

examples.en: He cheated on the math test.
Don't cheat; just play the game fairly.

senses.note: cheat on a test(시험 부정행위), cheat at cards(카드 게임 속임수). 사람을 속여 돈을 빼앗으면 cheat someone out of money.

senses.meaningEn: to secretly have a relationship with someone else while you have a partner

examples.en: She found out he was cheating on her.
examples.ko: 그녀는 그가 바람피우고 있다는 걸 알게 됐어.

examples.en: I would never cheat on you.
examples.ko: 난 절대 너 두고 바람 안 피워.

senses.note: cheat on + 사람(배우자·연인). 시험 부정행위의 cheat on a test 와 형태가 같으니 문맥으로 구분.

senses.meaningEn: a person who cheats

examples.en: You looked at my cards. You're a cheat!
Nobody wants to play with a cheat.
examples.ko: 반칙하는 사람하고는 아무도 놀고 싶어 하지 않아.

senses.meaningEn: to look at something to make sure it is correct or okay

examples.en: Let me check my schedule first.
Did you check the door is locked?

senses.note: check in = (호텔·공항) 체크인하다, check out = 퇴실하다.

senses.meaningEn: a bill in a restaurant

examples.en: Can we get the check, please?
I'll pay the check tonight.

senses.note: 미국식은 check, 영국식은 bill.

senses.meaningEn: to arrive at a hotel or airport and tell them you are there

examples.en: We can check in at the hotel after two.
examples.ko: 호텔 체크인은 2시 이후에 할 수 있어.

examples.en: You should check in two hours before your flight.
examples.ko: 비행기 출발 두 시간 전에 수속해야 해.

senses.note: check in at + 장소, check in for + 비행편. 명사는 check-in(check-in counter). 짐을 부치다 = check (in) a bag.

senses.meaningEn: to contact someone to find out how they are or what is happening

examples.en: I just wanted to check in and see how you're doing.
examples.ko: 그냥 어떻게 지내나 안부 확인하려고 연락했어.

examples.en: Let's check in with each other tomorrow.

senses.note: check in with + 사람 = ~와 연락해 상황을 확인하다. 직장에서도 자주 쓰는 가벼운 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to pay your bill and leave a hotel

examples.en: What time do we have to check out?
We checked out at ten and left for the airport.

senses.note: 명사 checkout = 체크아웃(시간), 또는 마트의 계산대(checkout counter).

senses.meaningEn: to look at or try something because it seems interesting

examples.en: Check out this video, it's so funny!
examples.ko: 이 영상 한번 봐, 진짜 웃겨!

examples.en: Let's check out that new cafe this weekend.
examples.ko: 이번 주말에 그 새로 생긴 카페 한번 가 보자.

senses.note: Check it out! = 이것 봐! 구어에서 매우 흔함. 사람을 check out 하면 '훑어보다, 관심 있게 보다'는 뜻이 될 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: to borrow a book from a library

examples.en: I checked out three books from the library.
You can check out up to five books at a time.
examples.ko: 한 번에 책 다섯 권까지 대출할 수 있어요.

senses.note: 미국 도서관에서 '대출' 은 check out, 반납은 return.

senses.meaningEn: to make sure that someone is safe or well, or that something is okay

examples.en: I'll go check up on the kids.
My mom checks up on me every day.
examples.ko: 엄마가 매일 내가 잘 있는지 확인하셔.

senses.note: check on 과 거의 같음. 뉘앙스상 check up on 은 '감시하듯 확인하다' 느낌이 조금 더 강할 수 있음. 명사 checkup = 건강 검진(get a checkup).

senses.meaningEn: the soft part of your face below your eye, on either side of your nose

examples.en: The baby has soft, round cheeks.
She kissed her grandma on the cheek.

senses.note: kiss someone on the cheek = 볼에 뽀뽀하다. 추워서 볼이 빨개지다 = My cheeks are red from the cold.

senses.meaningEn: to shout happily to support a team or person

examples.en: The fans cheered when the team scored.
We cheered for our school at the game.

senses.note: cheer for + 팀/사람. cheer up = 기분이 나아지다/기운 내게 하다('Cheer up!' = 기운 내!). 'Cheers!' 는 건배 또는 영국식 '고마워·안녕'. 응원단은 cheerleader.

senses.meaningEn: to shout encouragement to someone in a race or game

examples.en: We cheered on our team from the stands.
Come to the race and cheer me on!

senses.note: 목적어가 대명사면 cheer me/him on 으로 가운데에. 한국어 '파이팅' 에 가까운 소리 응원. cheer up 은 '기운을 북돋다' 로 뜻이 다름.

senses.meaningEn: to start to feel happier

examples.en: Cheer up! It's not the end of the world.
examples.ko: 기운 내! 세상이 끝난 것도 아니잖아.

examples.en: He cheered up as soon as he saw the puppy.

senses.note: Cheer up! = 힘내!(슬픈 사람에게). 응원할 때의 '파이팅' 은 cheer up 이 아니라 Good luck! / You can do it! 임.

senses.meaningEn: to make someone feel happier

examples.en: I brought some cake to cheer you up.
examples.ko: 너 기분 좋아지라고 케이크 좀 사 왔어.

examples.en: A walk outside always cheers me up.

senses.note: cheer + 사람 + up. 공간을 밝게 할 때도: Flowers cheer up the room.

senses.meaningEn: a solid food made from milk, often yellow or white

examples.en: Would you like extra cheese on your pizza?
I had cheese and crackers as a snack.

senses.note: 보통 셀 수 없음: a cheese (×) → a slice of cheese, a piece of cheese. 종류를 말할 때만 cheeses. 사진 찍을 때 Say cheese! = 웃으세요!

senses.meaningEn: a professional cook, especially the main cook in a restaurant

examples.en: The chef at this restaurant is from Italy.
My brother wants to be a chef.
examples.ko: 내 동생은 요리사가 되고 싶어 해.

senses.note: chef 는 전문 요리사. 집에서 요리하는 사람은 cook. 발음은 /ʃef/ (셰프), '체프'가 아님.

senses.meaningEn: a small round red fruit with a hard seed in the middle

examples.en: Cherries are expensive in winter.
There's a cherry on top of the cake.
examples.ko: 케이크 위에 체리가 하나 올려져 있어.

senses.note: 복수형은 cherries. cherry blossom = 벚꽃.

senses.meaningEn: a board game for two players with sixteen pieces each, including a king and queen

examples.en: My grandfather taught me how to play chess.
examples.ko: 할아버지가 체스 두는 법을 가르쳐 주셨어.

examples.en: Do you want to play a game of chess?

senses.note: play chess(체스를 두다) — 관사 없음. 체스판은 chessboard, 체스 말은 chess piece. 셀 수 없는 명사라 a chess 는 틀림; a game of chess 로.

senses.meaningEn: the upper front part of your body between your neck and stomach

examples.en: I have a pain in my chest.
He hit his chest and coughed.

senses.note: 신체 부위로서의 '가슴'은 chest. 여성의 가슴은 breast, 마음·감정의 '가슴'은 heart.

senses.meaningEn: a large strong box for keeping things in

examples.en: Put the blankets in the chest.
The kids found a treasure chest in the game.

senses.note: chest of drawers = 서랍장. treasure chest = 보물 상자. 일반적인 작은 상자는 box.

senses.meaningEn: to crush food with your teeth before swallowing it

examples.en: Chew your food slowly.
This meat is hard to chew.

senses.note: chewing gum = 껌. '껌을 씹다'는 chew gum. chewy = 질긴, 쫄깃한(떡의 식감 설명에 유용).

senses.meaningEn: a baby chicken or other baby bird

examples.en: The yellow chicks followed their mother everywhere.
A chick just came out of the egg!

senses.note: chicken(닭/닭고기)과 혼동 주의. 속어로 젊은 여성을 chick 이라 부르는 것은 무례하게 들릴 수 있으니 쓰지 말 것.

senses.meaningEn: the meat of a chicken, eaten as food

examples.en: I'll have the chicken, please.
We ordered fried chicken for the party.

senses.note: 고기를 뜻할 때는 셀 수 없음: some chicken, a piece of chicken. 한국어 '치킨'은 보통 튀긴 닭이지만 영어 chicken 은 조리법과 관계없는 닭고기 전체.

senses.meaningEn: a bird that is kept on farms for its eggs and meat

examples.en: My grandmother keeps chickens in her yard.
The chickens laid six eggs this morning.
examples.ko: 오늘 아침에 닭들이 알을 여섯 개 낳았어.

senses.note: 동물을 뜻할 때는 셀 수 있음: a chicken, two chickens. 수컷은 rooster, 암컷은 hen, 새끼는 chick.

senses.meaningEn: a person who is afraid to do something

examples.en: Don't be such a chicken, just try it!
examples.ko: 그렇게 겁먹지 말고 그냥 한번 해 봐!

examples.en: He's too chicken to ask her out.
examples.ko: 그는 그녀한테 데이트 신청할 용기가 없어.

senses.note: 친구 사이에서 장난스럽게 쓰는 표현. too chicken to ~ = ~할 용기가 없다. chicken out = 겁먹고 포기하다.

senses.meaningEn: a young person who is not yet an adult

examples.en: Every child needs love and care.
Tickets are free for children under five.

senses.note: 복수형은 childs 가 아니라 children. 구어에서는 kid 를 더 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: someone's son or daughter, at any age

examples.en: She is an only child.
My children are all grown up now.

senses.note: 나이와 상관없이 부모 입장에서 '자식'을 뜻함. only child = 외동.

senses.meaningEn: the plural of child; young people who are not yet adults

examples.en: The children are playing in the yard.
How many children do you have?

senses.note: childs 는 틀린 표현. children 은 이미 복수이므로 childrens 라고 쓰지 않음. 소유격은 children's.

senses.meaningEn: young people as a group, for example as readers or students

examples.en: This book is written for children.
The museum has a special program for children.
examples.ko: 그 박물관에는 어린이 특별 프로그램이 있어.

senses.note: children's book(어린이 책), children's hospital(어린이 병원).

senses.meaningEn: to calm down and stop being angry or worried

examples.en: Chill out, it's just a small mistake.
Tell him to chill out before he says something bad.
examples.ko: 나쁜 말 하기 전에 그 사람 좀 진정시켜.

senses.note: 친구 사이 구어. 짧게 "Chill!" 이라고도 한다. 어른·상사에게는 calm down 이 더 안전.

senses.meaningEn: to relax and do nothing special

examples.en: Let's just chill out at home this weekend.
examples.ko: 이번 주말엔 그냥 집에서 느긋하게 쉬자.

examples.en: I'm chilling out with some music.

senses.note: relax 의 구어. 요즘은 out 없이 "Let's chill." 으로 더 많이 말함.

senses.meaningEn: the part of your face below your mouth

examples.en: He has a little cut on his chin.
Keep your chin up and smile for the photo.

senses.note: chin 은 턱 끝(아래턱 앞부분), 턱뼈 전체·턱관절은 jaw. Chin up! = 기운 내!

senses.meaningEn: a sweet brown food made from cocoa beans

examples.en: I love dark chocolate.
She gave me a box of chocolates.

senses.note: 재료로 말하면 셀 수 없음(some chocolate), 낱개는 a chocolate / a box of chocolates. hot chocolate = 코코아 음료. 발음은 2음절 /ˈtʃɔːklət/.

senses.meaningEn: to pick one thing or person from two or more

examples.en: Which color did you choose for the bag?
I chose the blue shirt, not the red one.
examples.ko: 빨간 거 말고 파란 셔츠를 골랐어.

senses.note: choose - chose - chosen. 명사는 choice. 가볍게 '고르다'는 pick 을 더 자주 씀. choose between A and B / choose from ~ 중에서 고르다.

senses.meaningEn: to decide to do something

examples.en: She chose to stay home this weekend.
examples.ko: 그녀는 이번 주말에 집에 있기로 했어.

examples.en: You can choose to walk or take the bus.

senses.note: choose to + 동사. '~하지 않기로 하다'는 choose not to.

senses.meaningEn: to cut food into small pieces with quick, heavy cuts

examples.en: Chop up some garlic for the sauce.
I chopped the vegetables up for the soup.

senses.note: chop 은 칼을 내려치듯 빠르게 자르는 동작. finely chopped = 잘게 다진.

senses.meaningEn: to cut wood or a large object into pieces with an axe or heavy knife

examples.en: Grandpa chopped up wood for the fire.
We chopped up the old table and burned it.
examples.ko: 우리는 낡은 탁자를 토막 내서 태웠어.

senses.meaningEn: a pair of thin sticks used for eating food, especially in Asia

examples.en: Can you eat with chopsticks?
Could we get some chopsticks, please?

senses.note: 항상 복수 chopsticks. '젓가락 한 쌍'은 a pair of chopsticks. 한 짝은 a chopstick.

senses.meaningEn: a building where Christians go to pray

examples.en: There's an old church in the middle of town.
The church has a tall white tower.
examples.ko: 그 교회에는 높고 하얀 탑이 있어.

senses.note: 복수형은 churches. 성당은 Catholic church 또는 cathedral(대성당).

senses.meaningEn: the religious service that Christians attend

examples.en: We go to church every Sunday morning.
examples.ko: 우리는 매주 일요일 아침에 교회에 가.

examples.en: Church starts at ten, so don't be late.

senses.note: '예배에 가다'라는 뜻일 때는 관사 없이 go to church(school, bed 처럼). 건물을 가리킬 때는 the church.

senses.meaningEn: a building where you go to watch movies, mainly in British English

examples.en: Do you want to go to the cinema tonight?
The cinema near my house has cheap tickets.
examples.ko: 우리 집 근처 영화관은 표가 싸.

senses.note: 영국·유럽에서 쓰는 말. 미국에서는 movie theater / theater. 미국인에게 cinema 라고 하면 조금 격식 있게 들릴 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: movies in general, as an art or a business

examples.en: She is studying cinema at university.
I love Korean cinema from the 2000s.

senses.note: 이 뜻에서는 셀 수 없는 명사. 영화 한 편은 a movie / a film.

senses.meaningEn: a perfectly round flat shape

examples.en: Draw a circle on the paper.
The kids sat in a circle on the floor.

senses.note: sit/stand in a circle(둥글게 앉다/서다). round 는 형용사(둥근), circle 은 명사(원).

senses.meaningEn: to draw a circle around something

examples.en: Circle the correct answer.
I circled the date on my calendar.
examples.ko: 달력에 그 날짜를 동그라미 쳐 뒀어.

senses.note: 시험 지시문에 자주 나옴: Circle the right word.

senses.meaningEn: a large and important town where many people live

examples.en: Seoul is a very big city.
I grew up in a small town, not a city.
examples.ko: 나는 도시가 아니라 작은 동네에서 자랐어.

senses.note: 복수형은 cities. 도심은 downtown 또는 the city center. 큰 도시 안에서도 '시내'를 the city 라고 부름(go into the city).

senses.meaningEn: to hit your hands together to show you liked something

examples.en: Everyone clapped after the little girl sang.
examples.ko: 어린 여자아이가 노래를 마치자 모두 박수를 쳤어.

examples.en: Clap your hands if you know the answer.

senses.note: clap (your hands). 과거형은 p 를 겹침(clapped). 명사로는 '박수' = applause 또는 a round of applause; 'Let's give him a big hand.' 도 '박수 쳐 주자'.

senses.meaningEn: a period of time when a teacher teaches a group of students

examples.en: I have an English class at nine.
Don't be late for class again.

senses.note: 수업에 가다는 go to class(관사 없음). in class = 수업 중에.

senses.meaningEn: a group of students who are taught together

examples.en: There are thirty students in my class.
examples.ko: 우리 반에는 학생이 서른 명 있어.

examples.en: She's the smartest girl in our class.
examples.ko: 그 애는 우리 반에서 가장 똑똑한 여자애야.

senses.note: classmate = 같은 반 친구. 한국의 '3학년 2반'은 class 2 처럼 표현.

senses.meaningEn: a person who is in the same class as you at school

examples.en: My classmate helped me with my homework.
We were classmates in high school.

senses.note: 친한 사이가 아니어도 같은 반이면 classmate. '동창'은 old classmate, 학교 전체 동기는 schoolmate.

senses.meaningEn: a room in a school where lessons happen

examples.en: Please be quiet in the classroom.
Our classroom is on the second floor.

senses.note: in the classroom = 교실 안에서. 한 단어로 붙여 씀(class room ✗).

senses.meaningEn: not dirty

examples.en: Your room looks really clean today.
examples.ko: 오늘 네 방 정말 깨끗해 보인다.

examples.en: Is this cup clean?

senses.note: clean clothes = 깨끗한(세탁한) 옷. clean water = 깨끗한 물.

senses.meaningEn: to remove dirt from something

examples.en: I clean my room every Sunday.
Can you help me clean the kitchen?

senses.note: clean up = 치우다, 정리하다 (Clean up your mess!). do the cleaning = 청소를 하다.

senses.meaningEn: to make a room tidy by removing dirt and putting things away

examples.en: Clean your room before you go out.
I cleaned the room, so it looks nice now.

senses.note: clean the house / clean the kitchen / clean the bathroom 모두 같은 패턴. '방 정리하다(물건 제자리에 두기)'는 tidy (up) the room, '청소기 돌리다'는 vacuum the room. 'clean up' 은 어질러진 것을 치울 때.

senses.meaningEn: to make a place clean and tidy, especially after a mess

examples.en: Can you help me clean up the kitchen?
We cleaned up after the party.

senses.note: clean(청소하다) + up(완전히). clean up after + 사람/행사 = ~ 뒤처리를 하다. 더러워진 것(mess)을 치울 때 가장 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: to wash yourself and make yourself look neat

examples.en: Go clean up before dinner.
examples.ko: 저녁 먹기 전에 가서 씻고 와.

examples.en: Give me a minute to clean up, I'm all sweaty.
examples.ko: 잠깐만, 땀을 많이 흘려서 좀 씻을게.

senses.note: get cleaned up 도 같은 뜻. 한국어 '씻고 와' 에 해당.

senses.meaningEn: to make a place empty by removing everything from it

examples.en: I need to clear out my closet this weekend.
examples.ko: 이번 주말에 옷장을 싹 정리해야 해.

examples.en: We cleared out the garage and found old photos.
examples.ko: 창고를 다 비우다가 옛 사진을 찾았어.

senses.note: clear up 은 '정리', clear out 은 안을 '비우기'. 쓸모없는 물건 처분의 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: to leave a place quickly

examples.en: The police told everyone to clear out.
Clear out, this is my room!

senses.note: 명령문으로 쓰면 꽤 무례함(꺼져!). 친한 사이나 급한 상황에서만.

senses.meaningEn: if the weather clears up, the clouds or rain go away

examples.en: I hope it clears up this afternoon.
The sky cleared up after the storm.

senses.note: 날씨 관련 가장 흔한 구동사 중 하나. 피부·감기가 '낫다' 도 clear up: My cold cleared up.

senses.meaningEn: to make a place tidy by putting things away

examples.en: Clear up your toys before dinner.
Who's going to clear up this mess?

senses.note: 미국은 clean up 이 더 흔함. clear up 은 영국에서 특히 자주.

senses.meaningEn: to explain something so that there is no more confusion

examples.en: Let me clear up one thing before we start.
examples.ko: 시작하기 전에 한 가지 확실히 해 둘게.

examples.en: I want to clear up this misunderstanding.

senses.note: clear up a misunderstanding / a question / a problem.

senses.meaningEn: a person who helps customers and sells things in a store

examples.en: The clerk helped me find the right size.
Ask the clerk if they have more in the back.
examples.ko: 뒤에 재고가 더 있는지 점원에게 물어봐.

senses.note: 미국식 발음 /klɜːrk/, 영국식은 /klɑːk/. sales clerk, store clerk 라고도 함. 호텔 프런트 직원은 front desk clerk.

senses.meaningEn: a person whose job is to keep records and do office work

examples.en: She works as a clerk at the city office.
The clerk asked me to fill out a form.

senses.note: bank clerk(은행 직원), office clerk(사무원). 미국에서는 cashier 와 clerk 를 섞어 쓰는 경우도 많음.

senses.meaningEn: quick to learn and understand things

examples.en: She's a clever student and learns fast.
My dog is clever. He opens doors by himself.
examples.ko: 우리 개는 영리해서 혼자 문을 열어.

senses.note: 영국식에서 흔하고 미국식은 smart 를 더 씀. 미국에서 clever 는 '재치 있는, 머리를 잘 쓴'의 느낌이 강함.

senses.meaningEn: showing a smart or unusual way of doing something

examples.en: What a clever idea!
That's a clever way to save money.

senses.note: too clever = 지나치게 머리를 쓰는(약간 부정적). Don't be too clever. = 너무 잘난 척하지 마.

senses.meaningEn: to press a button on a mouse or touch a link on a screen

examples.en: Click the blue button to start.
Don't click on links from strangers.
examples.ko: 모르는 사람이 보낸 링크는 누르지 마.

senses.note: click (on) + 대상. 더블 클릭은 double-click, 길게 누르기는 press and hold. 휴대폰 화면은 tap 을 더 많이 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to go up something using your hands and feet

examples.en: We climbed the mountain in four hours.
examples.ko: 우리는 네 시간 만에 산에 올랐어.

examples.en: The cat climbed up the tree quickly.

senses.note: climb 의 b 는 묵음 — /klaɪm/. climb a mountain(산을 오르다)에는 전치사가 없고, climb up/down(올라가다/내려가다)은 방향을 강조.

senses.meaningEn: to move up or into something, often slowly or with effort

examples.en: I climbed the stairs to the fifth floor.
Grandpa climbed into the car slowly.

senses.note: climb the stairs = go up the stairs. climb into/out of a car 는 몸을 움직여 타고 내리는 느낌. 명사 climbing(등산·클라이밍)도 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to move down from a high place using your hands and feet

examples.en: Be careful when you climb down the ladder.
The cat couldn't climb down from the tree.

senses.note: climb down a ladder / a tree / the stairs. 그냥 '내려가다'는 go down 이 더 흔하고, climb down 은 손발을 쓰는 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: to admit you were wrong and stop arguing or demanding something

examples.en: He finally climbed down and said sorry.
Neither side wanted to climb down in the argument.
examples.ko: 말다툼에서 양쪽 다 물러설 생각이 없었어.

senses.note: 주로 영국식. 미국에서는 back down 이 더 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: to move up something using your hands and feet

examples.en: The kids climbed up the big tree in the yard.
We climbed up the stairs to the roof.

senses.note: climb 만으로도 "오르다" 지만 up 을 붙이면 방향이 분명해짐. climb up a ladder / a hill / a mountain.

senses.meaningEn: a device on a wall or table that shows the time

examples.en: The clock on the wall is five minutes fast.
Look at the clock. We're going to be late!

senses.note: 손목시계는 watch, 벽·탁상시계는 clock. 알람시계 = alarm clock. '시계 방향'은 clockwise. 한국어 '시계'를 전부 clock 으로 옮기지 않도록 주의.

senses.meaningEn: to shut something such as a door, window, or book

examples.en: Please close the window, it's getting cold.
examples.ko: 창문 좀 닫아 줘, 추워지고 있어.

examples.en: Close your eyes and make a wish.

senses.note: 동사는 /kloʊz/(즈). close the door/window/book/eyes. shut 보다 부드럽고 정중한 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: to stop being open for business for the day or for good

examples.en: The store closes at nine on weekdays.
The bank is closed on Sundays.

senses.note: What time do you close? = 몇 시에 닫아요? 간판: CLOSED / OPEN. 폐업하다 = close down.

senses.meaningEn: near in distance or time

examples.en: The station is close to my house.
Is the hotel close to the beach?

senses.note: 형용사는 /kloʊs/(스) 로 발음이 다름. close to + 장소. 비슷하게 near 도 많이 씀.

senses.meaningEn: knowing someone very well and liking them a lot

examples.en: We've been close friends since high school.
I'm very close to my older sister.

senses.note: a close friend = 친한 친구, be close to 사람 = ~와 친하다. 발음 /kloʊs/.

senses.meaningEn: a small room or a space in a wall where you keep clothes or other things

examples.en: Hang your coat in the closet.
My closet is full, but I have nothing to wear.
examples.ko: 옷장은 꽉 찼는데 입을 게 없어.

senses.note: 미국식. 영국에서는 wardrobe. 서서 들어가는 큰 옷방은 walk-in closet. 가구형 옷장은 wardrobe.

senses.meaningEn: things such as shirts, pants, and dresses that you wear on your body

examples.en: I need to buy some new clothes for winter.
examples.ko: 겨울 옷을 몇 벌 새로 사야 해.

examples.en: Put your dirty clothes in the basket.

senses.note: 항상 복수형(a clothes 는 틀림). 한 점은 a piece of clothing, 셀 때는 some clothes. 발음은 close(닫다)와 같은 /kloʊz/. cloth 는 '천'.

senses.meaningEn: a white or gray shape in the sky made of tiny drops of water

examples.en: Look at that big white cloud!
Dark clouds mean rain is coming.

senses.note: 셀 수 있는 명사: a cloud, clouds. 비구름 = rain cloud. on cloud nine = 너무 행복해서 구름 위에 떠 있는 기분.

senses.meaningEn: a service that stores your files on the internet

examples.en: I save all my photos to the cloud.
Your files are backed up in the cloud.

senses.note: 항상 the cloud. in the cloud(클라우드에), cloud storage(클라우드 저장 공간).

senses.meaningEn: with many clouds in the sky

examples.en: It's cloudy, but I don't think it will rain.
examples.ko: 흐리긴 한데 비는 안 올 것 같아.

examples.en: The sky was cloudy all afternoon.

senses.note: 흐림 정도: partly cloudy(구름 조금) < cloudy(흐림) < overcast(잔뜩 흐림).

senses.meaningEn: not clear; hard to see through

examples.en: The water looks a little cloudy.
Don't drink it if the juice is cloudy.

senses.meaningEn: a group of people who meet regularly to share an interest or activity

examples.en: I'm in the art club at school.
Do you want to join our book club?
