senses.meaningEn: a plant like a small onion with a strong taste, used in cooking

examples.en: Korean food uses a lot of garlic.
Add some garlic to the pan.

senses.note: 셀 수 없는 명사. 마늘 한 쪽은 a clove of garlic.

senses.meaningEn: a place where you buy gas (fuel) for your car

examples.en: Let's stop at the next gas station.
The gas station also sells snacks and coffee.

senses.note: 미국식 gas station(gas = gasoline, 휘발유), 영국식 petrol station. '기름을 넣다'는 get gas / fill up the car. 가스(LPG·도시가스)와 혼동하지 말 것.

senses.meaningEn: a door in a fence or wall outside a building

examples.en: Please close the gate so the dog stays in.
examples.ko: 개가 나가지 않게 문 좀 닫아 줘.

examples.en: I'll wait for you at the school gate.

senses.note: 건물 안의 문은 door, 담장·울타리에 달린 바깥문은 gate. 한국의 '교문'은 school gate.

senses.meaningEn: the place in an airport where you get on your plane

examples.en: Our flight leaves from gate twelve.
Hurry, the gate closes in ten minutes!

senses.note: boarding gate 라고도 함. 공항 안내판의 Gate B7 처럼 알파벳과 숫자로 표시.

senses.meaningEn: to come together in one place, or to bring people or things together

examples.en: The whole family gathers for dinner on Sundays.
examples.ko: 일요일에는 온 가족이 모여 저녁을 먹어.

examples.en: Please gather your things before we leave.

senses.note: 사람이 '모이다'와 물건을 '모으다' 둘 다 가능. gather around = 둘러 모이다.

senses.meaningEn: to collect information or facts from different places

examples.en: We need to gather more information first.
I'm gathering ideas for my school project.

senses.note: gather information/data 는 자주 쓰는 짝. collect 보다 조금 더 격식 있는 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: kind, calm, and careful not to hurt anyone

examples.en: He is very gentle with children.
Please be gentle with the puppy.

senses.note: be gentle with + 사람/동물. 한국어 "젠틀하다"는 주로 남자의 예의 바름을 말하지만, 영어 gentle 은 "부드럽고 거칠지 않다"는 뜻. 예의 바름은 polite.

senses.meaningEn: not strong or violent

examples.en: A gentle wind was blowing from the sea.
Wash it in gentle, warm water.

senses.note: gentle breeze(살랑바람), gentle slope(완만한 경사), gentle voice(부드러운 목소리). gently(부사)도 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: a polite word for a man

examples.en: This gentleman is waiting for a table.
Ladies and gentlemen, welcome to the show!
examples.ko: 신사 숙녀 여러분, 공연에 오신 것을 환영합니다!

senses.note: 복수는 gentlemen. 안내 방송·공연에서 Ladies and gentlemen. 이름 모르는 남성을 가리킬 때 that man 보다 정중함.

senses.meaningEn: a man who is polite and treats people well

examples.en: He opened the door for me. What a gentleman!
examples.ko: 그가 문을 열어 줬어. 정말 신사야!

examples.en: Be a gentleman and help her with the bags.
examples.ko: 신사답게 그녀 가방 좀 들어 줘.

senses.meaningEn: to receive, obtain, or buy something

examples.en: Did you get my text message last night?
I need to get some milk on the way home.
examples.ko: 집에 가는 길에 우유 좀 사야 해.

senses.meaningEn: to arrive at a place

examples.en: What time do we get to the airport?
Call me when you get home, okay?

senses.note: get to + 장소. 단, get home / get there 는 to 없이 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to become or change to a certain state

examples.en: It gets cold here at night.
Don't get angry, I was just joking.

senses.note: get + 형용사: get tired, get hungry, get better. become 보다 훨씬 구어적.

senses.meaningEn: to understand something

examples.en: Sorry, I don't get it. Can you explain again?
examples.ko: 미안, 이해가 안 돼. 다시 설명해 줄래?

examples.en: Oh, now I get what you mean.

senses.meaningEn: to have your hair cut by a hairdresser or barber

examples.en: I need to get a haircut this weekend.
Did you get a haircut? It looks great.

senses.note: 한국어 '머리를 잘랐다'를 I cut my hair 라고 하면 '내가 직접 잘랐다'는 뜻. 미용실에서 자른 경우는 get a haircut / get my hair cut. 머리 자르는 가게는 hair salon(미용실), barbershop(남성 이발소).

senses.meaningEn: to find and start paid work

examples.en: She got a job at a bank last month.
It's hard to get a job without experience.
examples.ko: 경험 없이 일자리를 얻는 건 어려워.

senses.note: get a job = 취직하다(결과), look for a job = 구직하다(과정), have a job = 직업이 있다. '아르바이트를 구하다'는 get a part-time job. 'get a work' 는 틀림(work 는 셀 수 없음).

senses.meaningEn: to have a friendly relationship

examples.en: My brother and I get along really well.
examples.ko: 우리 형이랑 나는 사이가 정말 좋아.

examples.en: They don't get along at all these days.
examples.ko: 요즘 그 둘은 전혀 안 맞아.

senses.note: 사이가 "좋다/나쁘다" 를 well / badly 로 표현. 미국식에서 가장 흔한 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to manage or make progress in a situation

examples.en: How are you getting along in your new school?
We're getting along fine without a car.
examples.ko: 우리는 차 없이도 잘 지내고 있어.

senses.note: How are you getting along? = 어떻게 지내? / 잘 돼 가?

senses.meaningEn: to have a friendly relationship with someone

examples.en: Do you get along with your roommate?
I've always gotten along with my mother-in-law.

senses.note: get along with + 사람. 영국식은 get on with. 면접에서 "I get along well with everyone." 도 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: to travel or move from place to place

examples.en: It's easy to get around Seoul by subway.
My grandma gets around with a walking stick.

senses.note: 여행 회화 필수: How do you get around here? = 여기서는 뭘 타고 다녀요?

senses.meaningEn: if news gets around, many people hear it

examples.en: News gets around fast in a small town.
Word got around that they were getting married.

senses.note: "word gets around" 가 고정 표현. get around to -ing = 미뤄 둔 일을 드디어 하다.

senses.meaningEn: to go somewhere for a short holiday or rest

examples.en: We want to get away for the weekend.
examples.ko: 우리는 주말에 어디 좀 떠나고 싶어.

examples.en: I can't wait to get away from the city.

senses.note: a weekend getaway = 짧은 주말 여행. get away from it all = 복잡한 일상에서 벗어나다.

senses.meaningEn: to escape from a person or a place

examples.en: The cat got away before I could catch it.
Get away from the fire, kids!

senses.note: get away with = 나쁜 일을 하고도 벌을 안 받다. "He got away with it."

senses.meaningEn: to return to a place

examples.en: What time did you get back from your trip?
We got back home just before the rain started.

senses.note: get back home / to the office / from work. come back 보다 "힘들게 도착" 느낌이 약간 있음.

senses.meaningEn: to have something returned to you

examples.en: Did you get your money back for the broken phone?
I finally got my book back from Jenny.

senses.note: get + 물건 + back. 환불은 get a refund 또는 get your money back.

senses.meaningEn: to contact someone again later

examples.en: Can I get back to you tomorrow about the party?
examples.ko: 파티 얘기는 내일 다시 연락해도 될까?

examples.en: I'll get back to you after I check my schedule.

senses.note: get back to + 사람 = 나중에 답하다. 비즈니스에서도 아주 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: to recover from an illness or start to feel well again

examples.en: I hope you get better soon.
He got better after a few days of rest.

senses.note: 아픈 사람에게 하는 인사: Get better soon! / Get well soon! 둘 다 자주 쓴다. 완전히 나은 상태는 be better(I'm better now).

senses.meaningEn: to improve at something

examples.en: Your English is getting better every day.
Keep practicing and you'll get better at it.
examples.ko: 계속 연습하면 더 잘하게 될 거야.

senses.note: get better at + 명사/동명사: get better at cooking. 상황이 나아질 때도 씀: Things will get better(다 잘될 거야).

senses.meaningEn: to have just enough money or ability to live or manage

examples.en: We don't have much, but we get by.
How do you get by on such a small salary?

senses.note: get by on + 돈/자원. "I can get by in English." = 영어로 기본적인 의사소통은 돼.

senses.meaningEn: to move past someone or something in your way

examples.en: Excuse me, can I get by, please?
The hallway was so full I could barely get by.
examples.ko: 복도가 너무 꽉 차서 겨우 지나갔어.

senses.note: 좁은 곳을 지나갈 때: Can I get by? / Let me get by.

senses.meaningEn: to move to a lower place or position

examples.en: Get down from that tree right now!
Everybody get down, the ball is coming!

senses.note: get down on your knees = 무릎을 꿇다. 식탁에서 아이에게 "Can I get down?" = 이제 일어나도 돼요?

senses.meaningEn: to write something quickly before you forget it

examples.en: Did you get down the phone number?
Let me get this down before I forget.

senses.meaningEn: to make someone feel sad or tired

examples.en: This rainy weather really gets me down.
examples.ko: 이런 비 오는 날씨는 정말 기분을 가라앉혀.

examples.en: Don't let one bad grade get you down.

senses.note: get + 사람 + down. get down to (work) = 본격적으로 (일을) 시작하다.

senses.meaningEn: to put your clothes on

examples.en: Hurry up and get dressed, we're late!
I got dressed in five minutes this morning.

senses.note: wear 는 '입고 있는 상태', put on 은 '한 벌 입는 동작', get dressed 는 '옷 입기를 마치다'. get dressed up = 차려 입다.

senses.meaningEn: to arrive at your home

examples.en: What time do you usually get home?
Call me when you get home, okay?

senses.note: home 앞에 to 를 쓰지 않음: get home (not get to home). go home 은 "집에 가다"(이동), get home 은 "집에 도착하다".

senses.meaningEn: to go into a car or taxi

examples.en: Get in, I'll give you a ride.
She got in the taxi and closed the door.

senses.note: 승용차·택시는 get in / get out of. 버스·기차는 get on / get off.

senses.meaningEn: to arrive at home or at a place

examples.en: What time did you get in last night?
The train got in ten minutes late.

senses.meaningEn: to be accepted at a school or university

examples.en: She applied to that college and got in!
It's hard to get in without good grades.

senses.meaningEn: to not know where you are or how to go somewhere

examples.en: We got lost on the way to the hotel.
Take a map so you don't get lost.

senses.note: be lost(상태) vs get lost(길을 잃게 되다). "I'm lost." = 지금 길을 잃었어요.

senses.meaningEn: used to rudely tell someone to go away

examples.en: Get lost! I never want to see you again.
He told the kids to get lost.

senses.note: 매우 무례한 표현. 친한 사이 농담 외에는 쓰지 말 것.

senses.meaningEn: to become someone's husband or wife

examples.en: They got married last summer in Busan.
When are you going to get married?

senses.note: get married to + 사람(with 아님): She got married to a doctor. 결혼한 상태는 be married(I'm married = 기혼이야). 동사 marry 는 바로 목적어: marry him. 'marry with' 는 틀린 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to leave a bus, train, or plane

examples.en: We get off at the next stop.
She got off the train and looked around.

senses.meaningEn: to finish work and leave

examples.en: What time do you get off work today?
I get off at six on Fridays.

senses.note: get off (work) = 퇴근하다. leave work 보다 구어적.

senses.meaningEn: to move off something you are on or touching

examples.en: Get off the table, we eat there!
Get off the sofa and help me, please.

senses.note: Get off me! = 저리 가! / 손 떼!

senses.meaningEn: to go onto a bus, train, plane, or bike

examples.en: We got on the bus at the last stop.
Get on quickly, the train is leaving!

senses.note: 버스·기차·비행기·자전거는 get on / get off, 승용차·택시는 get in / get out of.

senses.meaningEn: to have a friendly relationship with someone

examples.en: Do you get on well with your sister?
My parents and I get on really well.

senses.note: 주로 영국식. 미국에서는 get along (with) 이 더 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: to continue doing something, especially work

examples.en: Stop talking and get on with your work.
Let's get on with the lesson, everyone.

senses.note: Get on with it! = 빨리빨리 해!

senses.meaningEn: to leave a car, a room, or a building

examples.en: We got out at the gas station to stretch.
examples.ko: 우리는 주유소에서 내려서 몸을 좀 풀었어.

examples.en: Get out of my room, please!

senses.note: 차에서 내리다 = get out (of the car). 버스·기차는 get off.

senses.meaningEn: to go to different places and enjoy yourself

examples.en: You should get out more and meet people.
examples.ko: 좀 더 밖에 나가서 사람들을 만나 봐.

examples.en: I haven't gotten out much this winter.
examples.ko: 이번 겨울엔 거의 외출을 못 했어.

senses.note: get out (of the house) = 집에만 있지 말고 나가다.

senses.meaningEn: if news gets out, people hear about it

examples.en: How did the secret get out so fast?
Don't let this get out, okay?
examples.ko: 이거 밖에 새어 나가게 하지 마, 알았지?

senses.meaningEn: to leave a car, a place, or a bed

examples.en: She got out of the car and waved.
I could barely get out of bed this morning.
examples.ko: 오늘 아침엔 침대에서 거의 못 일어났어.

senses.note: get out of bed / the car / the shower / the house.

senses.meaningEn: to avoid doing something you should do

examples.en: How can I get out of this meeting?
examples.ko: 이 회의 어떻게 빠질 수 있을까?

examples.en: He always gets out of washing the dishes.

senses.note: get out of + 명사/-ing. 핑계로 빠져나가는 뉘앙스.

senses.meaningEn: to become well again after an illness

examples.en: It took me a week to get over the cold.
Have you gotten over your flu yet?

senses.meaningEn: to stop feeling sad or upset about something

examples.en: She still hasn't gotten over the breakup.
I can't get over how big your dog is!
examples.ko: 네 개가 이렇게 큰 게 믿기지 않아!

senses.note: get over + 사람 = 그 사람을 잊다. "I can't get over ~" = 너무 놀라서 믿기지 않다(감탄). Get over it! = 그만 잊어!

senses.meaningEn: to prepare yourself for something, such as going out

examples.en: Give me ten minutes to get ready.
She got ready for work in a hurry.

senses.note: get ready for + 명사(get ready for school), get ready to + 동사(get ready to leave). 남을 준비시킬 때는 get the kids ready.

senses.meaningEn: used to tell someone that something is about to happen

examples.en: Get ready, the show starts in a minute.
Get ready for some good news!

senses.note: Ready, set, go! 는 달리기 출발 신호. Get ready for ~ 는 '~에 대비하라' 는 광고 문구로도 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: to relax or sleep for a while so you feel less tired

examples.en: You look tired. Go home and get some rest.
examples.ko: 피곤해 보여. 집에 가서 좀 쉬어.

examples.en: I got some rest after lunch and felt much better.
examples.ko: 점심 먹고 좀 쉬었더니 훨씬 좋아졌어.

senses.note: rest 는 셀 수 없는 명사라 some rest. 'get a rest' 보다 get some rest 가 훨씬 자주 쓰인다. 아픈 사람·피곤한 사람에게 하는 말로 Get some rest! 는 거의 인사처럼 쓴다.

senses.meaningEn: to finish or survive something difficult

examples.en: I have to get through three exams this week.
examples.ko: 이번 주에 시험 세 개를 치러야 해.

examples.en: Coffee helps me get through the long afternoon.
examples.ko: 커피 덕분에 긴 오후를 버틸 수 있어.

senses.note: get through the day / the week / the winter. "We'll get through this." = 우리 이겨낼 수 있어.

senses.meaningEn: to reach someone by phone

examples.en: I tried calling, but I couldn't get through.
Did you finally get through to the doctor?

senses.note: get through to + 사람. 통화 연결 외에 "이해시키다" 뜻도 있음: I can't get through to him.

senses.meaningEn: to arrive at a place

examples.en: How do I get to the train station?
We got to the airport two hours early.
examples.ko: 우리는 공항에 두 시간 일찍 도착했어.

senses.note: 길 묻기 기본 문장: How do I get to ~? arrive 보다 훨씬 구어적.

senses.meaningEn: to have the chance to do something

examples.en: I got to meet my favorite singer!
examples.ko: 내가 제일 좋아하는 가수를 만날 수 있었어!

examples.en: Do we get to choose our seats?

senses.note: get to + 동사 = 좋은 기회를 얻어서 하다. have to(의무) 와 반대 느낌.

senses.meaningKo: (get to 사람) 신경 쓰이게 하다, 괴롭히다
senses.meaningEn: to upset or annoy someone

examples.en: Don't let his words get to you.
examples.ko: 그 사람 말에 신경 쓰지 마.

examples.en: The heat is really getting to me today.
examples.ko: 오늘 더위가 정말 사람을 지치게 하네.

senses.note: get to + 사람 = (감정적으로) 영향을 주다. 주로 부정적.

senses.meaningEn: to meet with friends or family, usually for fun

examples.en: Let's get together for coffee this weekend.
My family gets together every Sunday for dinner.
examples.ko: 우리 가족은 매주 일요일 저녁에 모여.

senses.note: 명사 get-together = 소규모 모임. "a small get-together at my place".

senses.meaningEn: to collect things into one place

examples.en: Get your things together, we leave in five minutes.
I need to get my papers together for school.

senses.note: get yourself together = 마음을 가다듬다, 정신 차리다.

senses.meaningEn: to get out of bed

examples.en: What time do you usually get up?
I get up at six on weekdays.

senses.note: wake up 은 눈을 뜨는 것, get up 은 실제로 침대에서 나오는 것.

senses.meaningEn: to stand up after sitting or lying

examples.en: Everyone, please get up and stretch.
Don't get up, I'll get the door.
examples.ko: 일어나지 마, 내가 문 열어 줄게.

senses.meaningEn: very large, much bigger than usual

examples.en: We shared a giant pizza for dinner.
There's a giant teddy bear in the shop window.
examples.ko: 가게 진열창에 엄청 큰 곰 인형이 있어.

senses.note: 형용사 giant 는 명사 앞에만 씀(The pizza is giant 는 구어에서만). huge 와 비슷하지만 "보통보다 훨씬 큰 사이즈"의 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: a very large person in stories, or a very big and powerful company or person

examples.en: The giant in the story lived on a mountain.
examples.ko: 이야기 속 거인은 산 위에 살았어.

examples.en: Samsung is a giant in the phone market.

senses.note: 동화(Jack and the Beanstalk) 의 거인부터 tech giant(거대 IT 기업)까지 폭넓게 씀.

senses.meaningEn: something you give to someone on a special day or to say thank you

examples.en: I need to buy a birthday gift for my mom.
Thank you for the lovely gift!

senses.note: gift 와 present 는 거의 같은 뜻. gift 는 약간 더 격식 있고 가게·포장 관련(gift shop, gift card, gift wrap)에 많이 씀. 선물을 '주다'는 give, '받다'는 get/receive.

senses.meaningEn: a natural ability to do something well

examples.en: She has a real gift for languages.
Cooking is his gift.

senses.note: have a gift for + 분야. gifted = 재능 있는(gifted children).

senses.meaningEn: a tall African animal with a very long neck and long legs

examples.en: A giraffe is the tallest animal in the world.
examples.ko: 기린은 세계에서 가장 키가 큰 동물이야.

examples.en: The giraffe ate leaves from the top of the tree.

senses.note: 강세는 두 번째 음절(/dʒəˈræf/), '지래프'에 가깝게 발음. 복수형은 giraffes. 목이 길다 = has a long neck.

senses.meaningEn: a female child or young woman

examples.en: The little girl is holding a red balloon.
examples.ko: 그 여자아이가 빨간 풍선을 들고 있어.

examples.en: My daughter is a very smart girl.

senses.note: 성인 여성을 girl 이라고 부르는 건 무례할 수 있음. 직장에서는 woman 을 쓰는 게 안전.

senses.meaningEn: a woman's female friends, used in a friendly way

examples.en: I'm going out with the girls tonight.
examples.ko: 오늘 밤 여자 친구들이랑 놀러 나가.

examples.en: Hey girls, are you ready to go?

senses.note: the girls = 여자인 친구 무리. 여성끼리 서로 부를 때 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: a woman or girl that someone is in a romantic relationship with

examples.en: He's going to the movies with his girlfriend.
I met my girlfriend at work.

senses.note: 연인 관계일 때 씀. 여성이 자기 여자인 친구를 my girlfriend 라고 부르기도 하지만, 오해를 피하려면 a friend of mine 이 안전.

senses.meaningEn: to give something to someone for free because you no longer want it

examples.en: I gave away my old clothes to charity.
The store is giving away free samples today.
examples.ko: 그 가게가 오늘 무료 샘플을 나눠 주고 있어.

senses.note: 명사 giveaway = 무료 증정(품), 이벤트 선물. 중고로 '팔다' 는 sell, 그냥 '주다' 는 give away.

senses.meaningEn: to let someone know a secret, often without meaning to

examples.en: Don't give away the ending of the movie!
Her smile gave her away.

senses.note: give away a secret / the answer / the ending. 표정·행동이 주어가 되어 '~가 들통나게 했다' 로도 많이 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to return something to the person who owns it or gave it to you

examples.en: Can you give me back my pen?
I'll give the book back to you tomorrow.

senses.note: give + 사람 + back + 물건 / give + 물건 + back. 돈 환불은 give a refund 또는 get your money back.

senses.meaningEn: to help other people or your community because they helped you

examples.en: She volunteers to give back to her community.
examples.ko: 그녀는 지역 사회에 보답하려고 봉사 활동을 해.

examples.en: I want to give something back someday.

senses.note: give back (to + 공동체). 목적어 없이 쓰이는 경우가 많음. 기부·봉사 맥락.

senses.meaningEn: to finally agree to something after refusing for a while

examples.en: The kids begged for ice cream, and Dad gave in.
examples.ko: 아이들이 아이스크림 달라고 졸라서 아빠가 결국 들어줬어.

examples.en: Don't give in to him, he's just being lazy.
examples.ko: 그 애한테 지지 마, 그냥 게으른 거야.

senses.note: give in to + 사람/유혹 = ~에 못 이기다. give up(포기하다)은 스스로 그만두는 것, give in 은 상대·압력에 지는 것.

senses.meaningEn: to give a piece of work to a teacher or person in charge

examples.en: Have you given in your homework yet?
We have to give in our forms by Monday.

senses.note: 이 뜻은 영국에서 주로 쓰고, 미국은 hand in / turn in 이 더 흔함.

senses.meaningKo: 좀 도와줘, 손 좀 빌려 줘
senses.meaningEn: to help someone, especially with something physical

examples.en: Can you give me a hand with these bags?
He gave me a hand moving the sofa.

senses.note: give + 사람 + a hand (with 명사 / -ing). lend a hand 도 같은 뜻. "손 하나만 줘" 가 아니라 "도와줘". give a big hand 는 "큰 박수를 치다" 로 전혀 다른 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: to give something to each of several people

examples.en: They were giving out free water at the race.
examples.ko: 경기에서 무료로 물을 나눠 주고 있었어.

examples.en: The teacher gave out the new books.

senses.note: hand out 과 거의 같음. give out your phone number = 전화번호를 알려 주다(여러 사람에게).

senses.meaningEn: to stop working because of being too tired or old

examples.en: My legs gave out after the long hike.
examples.ko: 오래 걷고 나니 다리에 힘이 풀렸어.

examples.en: The old car finally gave out on the highway.
examples.ko: 그 낡은 차가 결국 고속도로에서 멈춰 버렸어.

senses.note: 주어가 몸(legs, voice)이나 기계. 목적어 없이 씀. 비축분이 다 떨어지다(the food gave out)는 뜻도 있음.

senses.meaningEn: to stop trying to do something

examples.en: Don't give up. You can do it!
examples.ko: 포기하지 마. 넌 할 수 있어!

examples.en: I almost wanted to give up on learning English.

senses.note: give up on + 사람/일 = ~을 포기하다, 단념하다.

senses.meaningEn: to stop doing or having something, especially a habit

examples.en: My dad is trying to give up smoking.
examples.ko: 우리 아버지는 담배를 끊으려고 노력 중이셔.

examples.en: I'm trying to give up sugar.

senses.note: give up + 동명사: give up smoking (O), give up to smoke (X).

senses.meaningEn: pleased and happy about something

examples.en: I'm glad you came to the party.
Glad to meet you!

senses.note: glad 는 명사 앞에 못 씀(a glad person ✗ → a happy person). be glad (that)..., be glad to + 동사. happy 보다 "다행이다, 반갑다"의 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: willing and happy to do something

examples.en: I'd be glad to help you move.
She's always glad to answer questions.
examples.ko: 그녀는 항상 기꺼이 질문에 답해 줘.

senses.note: I'd be glad to = 기꺼이 할게요(제안 수락). I'd be happy to 와 같은 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: a container made of glass that you drink cold drinks from

examples.en: Can I get a glass of water?
He dropped the glass and it broke.

senses.note: a glass of water / juice / wine. 찬 음료는 glass, 뜨거운 음료는 cup.

senses.meaningEn: a hard clear material used for windows and bottles

examples.en: The table is made of glass.
Careful, there's broken glass on the floor.

senses.note: 재료로 쓸 때는 셀 수 없는 명사(a glass 아님).

senses.meaningEn: two lenses in a frame that you wear to see better

examples.en: I can't read without my glasses.
Where did I put my glasses?

senses.note: 안경은 항상 복수 glasses. '안경 하나'는 a pair of glasses. sunglasses = 선글라스.

senses.meaningEn: an amount of milk served in a glass

examples.en: Drink a glass of milk before bed.
examples.ko: 자기 전에 우유 한 잔 마셔.

examples.en: He poured himself a tall glass of milk.
examples.ko: 그는 큰 유리잔에 우유를 가득 따랐어.

senses.note: 찬 음료(우유·물·주스·와인)는 glass, 뜨거운 음료(커피·차)는 cup 을 쓴다. 한국인이 자주 틀리는 것: a cup of milk 는 요리 계량(1컵)으로 들린다.

senses.meaningEn: two lenses in a frame that you wear to see better

examples.en: I can't read this without my glasses.
Where did I put my glasses?

senses.note: 항상 복수형. '안경 하나'는 a pair of glasses. 안경을 쓰다 wear glasses, 쓰고 있다 have glasses on. 단수 glass 는 '유리, 유리잔'.

senses.meaningEn: more than one glass for drinking

examples.en: Two glasses of water, please.
Put the glasses on the table.

senses.note: a glass of water = 물 한 잔. 문맥에 따라 '안경'인지 '잔들'인지 구분.

senses.meaningEn: a round model of the Earth that you can turn

examples.en: There's a globe on the teacher's desk.
Find Korea on the globe.

senses.note: 교실 안의 '둥근 지구 모형'을 가리킴.

senses.meaningEn: the world

examples.en: People all over the globe watched the game.
examples.ko: 전 세계 사람들이 그 경기를 봤어.

examples.en: The news traveled around the globe in minutes.
examples.ko: 그 소식은 몇 분 만에 전 세계로 퍼졌어.

senses.note: the globe = 세계(약간 격식). around the globe = around the world. 형용사 global(세계적인), 명사 globalization(세계화).

senses.meaningEn: pieces of clothing that cover your hands, with a separate part for each finger

examples.en: Wear gloves; your hands will get cold.
I lost one of my gloves on the bus.

senses.note: 보통 복수형, a pair of gloves. 한 짝은 a glove. 손가락이 나뉘지 않은 손모아장갑은 mittens. 장갑을 '끼다'도 영어로는 wear/put on.

senses.meaningEn: a sticky liquid used for joining things together

examples.en: Put some glue on the back of the picture.
Do you have a glue stick?

senses.note: 셀 수 없는 명사. 딱풀은 glue stick, 순간접착제는 super glue.

senses.meaningEn: to stick things together with glue

examples.en: Glue the two pieces together.
I glued the handle back on the cup.

senses.note: glue A to B / glue A and B together.

senses.meaningEn: to move or travel to a place

examples.en: I go to the gym after work.
Where are you going this weekend?

senses.note: go to school / go home(to 없음) / go shopping(동명사).

senses.meaningEn: to change to a worse state

examples.en: The milk will go bad if you leave it out.
My hair is going gray already.

senses.note: go bad / go wrong / go crazy 처럼 주로 나쁜 변화에 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to happen or progress in a certain way

examples.en: How did your interview go?
Everything is going well so far.

senses.note: How's it going? 은 '잘 지내?'라는 인사.

senses.meaningEn: to follow or chase someone or something

examples.en: The dog went after the ball.
Go after him and give him his phone!
examples.ko: 쫓아가서 그 사람 전화기 좀 줘!

senses.meaningEn: to try hard to get something you want, such as a job or a prize

examples.en: You should go after your dream job.
She's going after first place this year.

senses.note: go after a job / a goal / a prize. 비슷한 go for 보다 "적극적으로 뒤쫓는" 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: used to tell someone they can do what they asked

examples.en: "Can I sit here?" "Sure, go ahead."
Go ahead and start without me.

senses.note: 허락할 때 "Sure, go ahead." 가 가장 자연스러움. 전화에서 "Go ahead." = 말씀하세요. go ahead and + 동사 = 망설이지 말고 ~하다.

senses.meaningEn: to happen or start as planned

examples.en: The meeting will go ahead as planned.
We decided to go ahead with the party.

senses.note: go ahead with 계획. 명사 go-ahead: give the go-ahead = 승인하다(허가를 내리다).

senses.meaningEn: to go somewhere before other people

examples.en: You go ahead. I'll catch up.
She went ahead to find a table.

senses.note: "After you." 와 달리 go ahead 는 "먼저 가(출발해)". go ahead of 사람 = ~보다 앞서 가다.

senses.meaningEn: to continue happening or moving forward

examples.en: How is your new job going along?
Just go along this road and turn left.
examples.ko: 이 길을 따라 쭉 가다가 왼쪽으로 돌아.

senses.note: as we go along = 하면서, 가면서(계획 없이 진행). "We'll decide as we go along."

senses.meaningEn: to agree with a person or plan and do what they want

examples.en: I'll go along with whatever you decide.
He didn't want to, but he went along with it.

senses.note: 적극 찬성보다 "그냥 따라가 주는" 느낌. agree with 보다 소극적.

senses.meaningEn: to leave a place or a person

examples.en: Go away! I'm trying to study.
The dog finally went away.

senses.note: 명령문 "Go away!" 는 꽤 무례함. 정중하게는 "Could you give me a minute?" 등으로.

senses.meaningEn: to leave home for a trip or to live somewhere else

examples.en: We're going away for the weekend.
He went away to college last year.
examples.ko: 그는 작년에 대학 가느라 집을 떠났어.

senses.note: go away for the weekend/on vacation = 짧게 여행 가다. 영국식으로 특히 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: to stop existing or disappear

examples.en: The headache went away after I slept.
The problem won't just go away.
examples.ko: 그 문제는 그냥 사라지지 않을 거야.

senses.note: 증상·냄새·문제가 "없어지다". go away on its own = 저절로 사라지다.

senses.meaningEn: to return to a place you were before

examples.en: I have to go back to the office.
We went back to the same hotel.

senses.note: go back(화자가 떠나서 돌아가다) vs come back(화자 쪽으로 돌아오다). go back home = 집에 돌아가다.

senses.meaningEn: to start doing something again, or return to an earlier point

examples.en: Let's go back to page ten.
After lunch, we went back to work.
examples.ko: 점심 후에 우리는 다시 일을 시작했어.

senses.note: go back to sleep(다시 자다), go back to work(다시 일하다), go back to school(복학하다·개학하다).

senses.meaningEn: if time goes by, it passes

examples.en: Time goes by so fast when you're having fun.
examples.ko: 재밌을 때는 시간이 정말 빨리 가.

examples.en: Two years went by before I saw her again.

senses.note: as time goes by = 시간이 지나면서. in days gone by = 지난날에.

senses.meaningEn: to move past a place or person

examples.en: A big truck just went by our house.
examples.ko: 큰 트럭이 방금 우리 집 앞을 지나갔어.

examples.en: I go by the bakery every morning on my way to work.
examples.ko: 출근길에 매일 아침 그 빵집 앞을 지나가.

senses.note: stop by / drop by = 잠깐 들르다(들어감). go by 는 들어가지 않고 지나침.

senses.meaningEn: to move to a lower place

examples.en: I'll go down and get the mail.
We went down to the beach after lunch.

senses.note: 해가 지다 도 the sun goes down. 반대는 go up / come up.

senses.meaningEn: to become lower in price or amount

examples.en: Prices usually go down after the holidays.
The temperature went down to minus five.

senses.note: go down = fall/decrease 의 구어. 열이 내리다 도 My fever went down.

senses.meaningEn: to stop working, especially a computer system or website

examples.en: The website went down for an hour.
The internet goes down every time it rains.

senses.note: 한국어 "서버 다운" 과 같은 뜻. 반대는 be back up(복구되다). go down well = 반응이 좋다(중급).

senses.meaningEn: to choose something

examples.en: I think I'll go for the chicken salad.
Which color did you go for in the end?

senses.note: 식당에서 메뉴를 고를 때 "I'll go for ~" 가 아주 자연스러움.

senses.meaningKo: (go for a walk / run 등) ~하러 가다
senses.meaningEn: to go somewhere to do an activity such as walking or running

examples.en: Let's go for a walk after dinner.
He goes for a run every morning.
examples.ko: 그는 매일 아침 달리기를 하러 가.

senses.note: go for a walk / a run / a swim / a drink / a coffee. 명사와 묶어 외우기.

senses.meaningEn: to try to get or achieve something

examples.en: If you really want the job, go for it!
examples.ko: 그 일 정말 원하면 한번 도전해 봐!

examples.en: She's going for the gold medal this year.

senses.note: Go for it! = 해 봐! / 한번 질러 봐! 응원할 때 아주 흔한 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to walk somewhere for pleasure or exercise

examples.en: The weather is nice. Let's go for a walk.
I went for a walk along the river after dinner.

senses.note: go for a walk = take a walk(미국식). 개를 산책시키는 것은 walk the dog. 같은 패턴: go for a run, go for a swim, go for a drive, go for a drink.

senses.meaningEn: to return to the place where you live

examples.en: It's getting late. I should go home now.
He went home early because he felt tired.

senses.note: home 은 부사라 to 를 붙이지 않음(go to home ✗). 같은 식으로 come home, get home, arrive home. 단, '집에' 머무르는 것은 at home(stay at home / stay home 둘 다 가능).

senses.meaningEn: to enter a place

examples.en: It's cold. Let's go in.
She went in and closed the door.

senses.note: 화자가 밖에서 안으로 들어가는 것. 장소를 말하면 go into the room. come in 은 안에 있는 사람 시점.

senses.meaningEn: to fit inside something

examples.en: The key won't go in.
This box won't go in the car.

senses.note: "It won't go in." = 안 들어간다(크기·모양이 안 맞음). 설명이 "머리에 안 들어오다" 도 It doesn't go in.

senses.meaningEn: to make a sudden loud noise, or to explode

examples.en: My alarm went off at six this morning.
The fireworks went off over the river.

senses.note: 알람이 "울리다" 는 go off(go on ✗). 한국인이 가장 자주 헷갈리는 구동사 중 하나. 폭탄·총도 go off.

senses.meaningEn: to stop working or shining

examples.en: The lights went off suddenly.
The heater goes off at midnight.

senses.note: 꺼지다 go off / go out, 켜지다 go on / come on. 사람이 끄면 turn off.

senses.meaningEn: to become bad and not safe to eat

examples.en: This milk has gone off. It smells bad.
Don't eat that chicken; it's gone off.

senses.note: 영국식. 미국은 go bad / spoil. has gone off 처럼 완료형으로 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to leave a place, especially suddenly

examples.en: He went off without saying goodbye.
They went off to Jeju for the weekend.

senses.note: go off to 장소 = ~로 떠나다. go off with 사람/물건 = ~와 떠나다, ~를 가지고 가 버리다.

senses.meaningEn: to continue doing something

examples.en: Go on, I'm listening.
She went on talking for an hour.
examples.ko: 그녀는 한 시간 동안 계속 말했어.

senses.note: go on + -ing = 하던 일을 계속하다, go on to + 동사 = 이어서 다른 일을 하다. "Go on." 은 말을 재촉하는 "계속해 봐".

senses.meaningEn: to happen

examples.en: What's going on here?
Something strange is going on.

senses.note: "What's going on?" = 무슨 일이야? / 잘 지내?(인사). 거의 항상 진행형으로 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to start working or shining

examples.en: The lights go on at six.
The heater went on by itself.

senses.note: 자동으로 켜지다(go on / come on). 사람이 켜는 것은 turn on. 꺼지다는 go off / go out.

senses.meaningEn: to leave for a trip or activity

examples.en: We're going on a trip next month.
They went on a picnic by the river.

senses.note: go on a trip / vacation / picnic / date / diet. go to 는 장소, go on 은 활동 앞에.

senses.meaningEn: to travel to a place for a holiday, for work, or for fun

examples.en: We're going on a trip to Busan next week.
My family went on a trip to Japan last summer.
examples.ko: 우리 가족은 지난여름에 일본 여행을 갔어.

senses.note: trip 앞에는 on: go on a trip / go on a school trip / go on a business trip(출장). travel 은 동사로 바로 쓰임(travel to Japan). '여행 잘 다녀와'는 Have a nice trip!

senses.meaningEn: to leave your home to do something fun

examples.en: Let's go out for dinner tonight.
I went out with my friends last night.

senses.note: go out for a meal/a walk/a drink. 그냥 "밖에 나가다" 뿐 아니라 "놀러 나가다" 의 뉘앙스가 강함.

senses.meaningEn: to have a romantic relationship with someone

examples.en: They've been going out for two years.
Will you go out with me?

senses.note: go out with 사람 = 사귀다. 한 번의 데이트가 아니라 교제 관계. "Will you go out with me?" 는 고백 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to stop burning or shining

examples.en: The lights went out during the storm.
The fire went out while we were asleep.

senses.note: 스스로 꺼지는 것(go out). 사람이 끄는 것은 turn off / put out(불을 끄다).

senses.meaningEn: to have a romantic relationship with someone

examples.en: How long have you been going out with Mike?
She went out with him for two years.

senses.note: go out with = date. "We're going out." = 우리 사귀는 사이야. 반대는 break up with.

senses.meaningEn: to leave your home to do something fun with someone

examples.en: I'm going out with my friends tonight.
Do you want to go out with us for dinner?

senses.note: 친구와 쓰면 단순히 "놀러 나가다". 연애 뜻과 헷갈릴 땐 hang out with 를 쓰면 안전.

senses.meaningEn: to look at or examine something carefully, often again

examples.en: Let's go over the homework together.
Can you go over this list one more time?
examples.ko: 이 목록 한 번만 더 봐 줄 수 있어?

senses.note: review 의 구어 표현. go over the rules / the plan / the notes 처럼 자주 묶여 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: to go to someone's house or to a place nearby

examples.en: I went over to Tom's house after school.
Go over and say hello to your grandma.

senses.note: go over to + 사람/장소. 가까운 거리를 "건너가는" 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: to go to shops or stores to buy things

examples.en: I'm going shopping this afternoon. Want to come?
examples.ko: 오늘 오후에 쇼핑 갈 건데, 같이 갈래?

examples.en: We went shopping for new shoes on Saturday.
examples.ko: 토요일에 새 신발을 사러 쇼핑을 갔어.

senses.note: 활동은 go + -ing: go shopping, go swimming, go fishing. '~을 사러'는 go shopping for ~. 식료품 장보기는 do the shopping / go grocery shopping.

senses.meaningEn: to go to a pool, a beach, or a lake in order to swim

examples.en: Let's go swimming at the beach this weekend.
I went swimming with my friends after school.

senses.note: '수영하러 가다'를 go to swim 이라고 하면 어색함. go + -ing 패턴(go swimming / jogging / hiking / camping). 수영을 하는 행위 자체는 swim: I swim every morning.

senses.meaningEn: to experience something difficult or unpleasant

examples.en: She went through a hard time last year.
We all go through bad days sometimes.
examples.ko: 우리 모두 가끔은 안 좋은 날을 겪지.

senses.note: 보통 안 좋은 일(a hard time, a divorce, a lot)에 씀. "I know what you're going through." = 네 심정 이해해.

senses.meaningEn: to look at or read all of something carefully from beginning to end

examples.en: Let me go through my notes before the test.
examples.ko: 시험 전에 노트 한 번 다 훑어볼게.

examples.en: I went through my bag, but my keys weren't there.

senses.note: go over 는 "검토", go through 는 "전부 하나씩 살펴보기·뒤지기" 에 가까움.

senses.meaningEn: to pass from one side of a place to the other

examples.en: The train goes through a long tunnel.
You have to go through security at the airport.

senses.meaningEn: to get into bed in order to sleep

examples.en: I usually go to bed around eleven.
The kids went to bed early last night.

senses.note: bed 앞에 the 를 쓰지 않음(go to the bed ✗). go to bed 는 '잠자리에 들다', fall asleep 은 '잠이 들다', sleep 은 '자다'. 과거형 went to bed.

senses.meaningEn: to travel to school to attend classes

examples.en: I go to school by bus every morning.
examples.ko: 나는 매일 아침 버스로 학교에 가.

examples.en: She didn't go to school yesterday because she was sick.
examples.ko: 그녀는 어제 아파서 학교에 안 갔어.

senses.note: 학생으로서 다니는 학교는 the 없이 go to school(go to the school 은 건물에 가는 것). 같은 패턴: go to work, go to bed, go to church. '학교 다니다(재학)'도 go to school: Where do you go to school?

senses.meaningEn: to go to a cinema to watch a film

examples.en: Do you want to go to the movies tonight?
We went to the movies and then had dinner.
examples.ko: 우리는 영화를 보고 나서 저녁을 먹었어.

senses.note: 미국식 go to the movies(항상 the + 복수), 영국식 go to the cinema. '영화를 보다'는 watch a movie(집에서) / see a movie(영화관에서) 가 더 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: to travel to the place where you work in order to start your job

examples.en: I go to work at eight thirty every day.
My dad went to work early this morning.

senses.note: work 는 셀 수 없는 명사라 the 없음(go to the work ✗). '퇴근하다'는 get off work / leave work / finish work. '출근 중'은 on my way to work.

senses.meaningEn: to move to a higher place

examples.en: Go up the stairs and turn left.
We went up to the roof to see the view.

senses.note: go up the stairs / the hill / to the second floor. 반대는 go down, come down.

senses.meaningEn: to become higher in price or amount

examples.en: Bus fares went up again this year.
The price of eggs keeps going up.

senses.note: go up = rise/increase 의 구어. 가격·기온·월세·숫자에 모두 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to be built

examples.en: A new apartment building is going up near the station.
examples.ko: 역 근처에 새 아파트가 올라가고 있어.

examples.en: Lots of new houses went up last year.

senses.note: 건물이 "올라간다" 는 한국어 표현과 같음. 포스터·장식이 "걸리다" 도 go up(The posters went up yesterday.).

senses.meaningEn: a point scored in sports like soccer or hockey when the ball goes into the net

examples.en: Son scored two goals in the second half.
What a great goal!

senses.note: score a goal(골을 넣다). 골대 자체도 goal, 골키퍼는 goalkeeper. 농구·야구의 득점은 goal 이 아니라 points / runs.

senses.meaningEn: something you want to achieve in the future

examples.en: My goal is to speak English every day.
examples.ko: 내 목표는 매일 영어로 말하는 거야.

examples.en: Set a small goal and reach it first.
examples.ko: 작은 목표를 세우고 그걸 먼저 이뤄 봐.

senses.note: set a goal(목표를 세우다), reach/achieve a goal(목표를 이루다). 한국어 '골'은 스포츠 뜻만 있어 '목표' 뜻을 놓치기 쉬움.

senses.meaningEn: a farm animal with horns and a short tail, kept for its milk and meat

examples.en: The goat is eating my mom's flowers again.
examples.ko: 염소가 또 엄마 꽃을 먹고 있어.

examples.en: Goats can climb almost anywhere.
examples.ko: 염소는 거의 어디든 올라갈 수 있어.

senses.note: goat cheese(염소 치즈), goat milk(염소젖). 요즘 인터넷에서 GOAT 는 Greatest Of All Time(역대 최고)의 약자로 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: a valuable yellow metal used for jewelry and money

examples.en: This ring is made of real gold.
examples.ko: 이 반지는 진짜 금으로 만든 거야.

examples.en: The price of gold went up again.

senses.note: gold(금, 명사·금으로 된)와 golden(금빛의, 황금 같은)을 구분. a gold ring(금반지) vs golden hair(금발).

senses.meaningEn: having the color of gold, or made of gold

examples.en: She wore a gold necklace to the party.
The sunset turned the water gold.

senses.meaningEn: a gold medal, given to the winner of a competition

examples.en: Korea won gold in archery again.
She is going for gold at the Olympics.

senses.note: win gold / go for gold. silver, bronze 도 같은 방식으로 씀.

senses.meaningEn: a game in which you hit a small ball into holes on a large grass course with clubs

examples.en: My father plays golf every Sunday morning.
examples.ko: 아버지는 매주 일요일 아침에 골프를 치셔.

examples.en: Golf is a slow but relaxing sport.

senses.note: play golf(골프를 치다). 골프 클럽(채)은 golf club, 골프장은 golf course. 스크린 골프는 screen golf / golf simulator.

senses.meaningEn: of high quality or pleasant

examples.en: That was a really good movie.
This is the best pizza in town.
examples.ko: 여기가 이 동네에서 제일 맛있는 피자야.

senses.note: 비교급 better, 최상급 best 로 불규칙 변화. 'more good' 은 틀림.

senses.meaningEn: able to do something well

examples.en: She's good at math.
I'm not very good at cooking.

senses.note: be good at + 명사/동명사. 'good in math' 보다 'good at math' 가 자연스러움. 사람에게 잘해 준다는 be good to + 사람.

senses.meaningEn: well-behaved and kind

examples.en: Be a good boy and brush your teeth.
He's a good man who helps everyone.

senses.meaningEn: not spoiled and still safe to eat

examples.en: Is this milk still good?
The bread is good for two more days.
examples.ko: 그 빵은 이틀 더 먹을 수 있어.

senses.note: 상한 건 go bad(The milk went bad).

senses.meaningEn: used to praise someone for doing something well

examples.en: You finished all your homework? Good job!
Good job on the test, everyone.

senses.note: 미국식 칭찬 표현. 선생님·부모가 아이에게, 동료끼리 가볍게. good job on + 명사 로 무엇을 잘했는지 붙임. 윗사람에게 'Good job' 은 평가하는 느낌이 있어 어색할 수 있음(Thank you for your hard work 가 안전).

senses.meaningEn: said to wish someone success before something important

examples.en: Good luck on your test tomorrow!
Good luck with your new job.

senses.note: Good luck on/with + 명사. 한국어 "파이팅" 에 가장 가까운 표현. 응답은 Thanks! 또는 Thank you, I'll need it. 비꼬는 "Good luck with that." 은 "어디 잘해 봐" 라는 뜻이니 억양에 주의.

senses.meaningEn: what you say when you leave someone or they leave you

examples.en: Goodbye, and thank you for everything.
He waved goodbye from the train window.
examples.ko: 그는 기차 창문에서 손을 흔들어 인사했어.

senses.note: bye 보다 격식 있고 조금 무거운 느낌(오래 못 볼 때). 매일 보는 사이면 See you / Bye 가 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: the act of saying goodbye to someone

examples.en: We said our goodbyes at the airport.
It was a hard goodbye for both of us.

senses.note: say goodbye to + 사람. 명사로 쓰면 복수 goodbyes 가능.

senses.meaningEn: a letter or number that shows how good a student's work is

examples.en: I got a good grade in science.
She always gets the best grades in class.
examples.ko: 그 애는 항상 반에서 최고 성적을 받아.

senses.note: get/receive a grade. 영국식은 mark. 숫자 점수는 score, 등급(A, B, C)은 grade.

senses.meaningEn: a level of school in the US, numbered 1 to 12

examples.en: My little brother is in the third grade.
What grade are you in?

senses.note: 미국식. in the 3rd grade = 3학년. 영국식은 Year 3. 대학생의 학년은 year(first-year, sophomore 등).

senses.meaningEn: the father of your mother or father

examples.en: My grandfather is eighty years old.
Her grandfather taught her how to fish.

senses.note: 친/외 구분 없음. 격식적 표현이며 부를 때는 Grandpa.

senses.meaningEn: an informal word for grandmother

examples.en: Grandma, can you tell me a story?
We're having lunch at Grandma's house today.

senses.note: 직접 부를 때는 대문자 Grandma. 어린아이는 granny, nana 도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: the mother of your mother or father

examples.en: My grandmother lives with us.
I visit my grandmother every Sunday.

senses.note: 친할머니/외할머니 구분이 없음. 필요하면 my mom's mother 처럼 설명.

senses.meaningEn: an informal word for grandfather

examples.en: Grandpa likes to read the newspaper every morning.
examples.ko: 할아버지는 매일 아침 신문 읽는 걸 좋아하셔.

examples.en: I made a card for Grandpa's birthday.

senses.note: 직접 부를 때는 대문자 Grandpa. granddad, gramps 도 구어로 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: the parent of your mother or father

examples.en: My grandparents live in the countryside.
She was raised by her grandparents.

senses.note: 보통 복수 grandparents 로 씀. Grandparents' Day 도 있음.

senses.meaningEn: a small, round green or purple fruit that grows in bunches and is used to make wine

examples.en: I bought some grapes for the picnic.
These green grapes have no seeds.

senses.note: 한국어 '포도'는 송이 전체를 말하지만 영어 grape 는 알 하나. 그래서 보통 복수형 grapes, 한 송이는 a bunch of grapes. 건포도는 raisin, 포도주는 wine.

senses.meaningEn: a common plant with thin green leaves that covers the ground

examples.en: Please don't walk on the grass.
Dad cuts the grass every Saturday morning.

senses.note: 보통 불가산명사. '잔디 깎다'는 cut/mow the grass. 잔디밭 자체는 lawn 이라고도 함.

senses.meaningEn: having a color between black and white, like ash or clouds

examples.en: The sky is gray. It might rain.
My dad is going gray already.
examples.ko: 우리 아빠는 벌써 머리가 세고 있어.

senses.note: 미국식 gray, 영국식 grey 둘 다 맞음. gray hair(흰머리), gray day(흐린 날). 한국어 "흰머리"는 white 가 아니라 gray hair.

senses.meaningEn: the color gray

examples.en: Gray matches almost anything.
I will take the sweater in gray.

senses.meaningEn: very good; excellent

examples.en: You did a great job today.
Great, see you at seven then!

senses.note: 대화의 응답으로 Great! / Sounds great! = '좋아!'. 비꼬는 톤으로 Oh, great. 라고 하면 '참 잘됐네(짜증)'.

senses.meaningEn: very large or very important

examples.en: The Great Wall of China is very long.
She was a great leader in history.

senses.note: a great deal of(많은), great-grandmother(증조할머니) 처럼 '크다·한 세대 위' 의 뜻도 있음.

senses.meaningEn: feeling very healthy or happy

examples.en: I feel great after a good night's sleep.
examples.ko: 잘 자고 났더니 몸이 아주 좋아.

examples.en: How are you? — I'm great, thanks!

senses.note: How are you? 에 대한 답으로 I'm great. > I'm good. > I'm okay. 순으로 긍정 정도가 다름.

senses.meaningEn: having the color of grass or leaves

examples.en: The trees are green again in spring.
Wait for the green light before you cross.

senses.note: 한국어로 "파란불"이라고 해도 영어로는 green light. 신호등 색 번역에 주의.

senses.meaningEn: good for the environment

examples.en: Our school is trying to go green this year.
examples.ko: 우리 학교는 올해 친환경을 실천하려고 해.

examples.en: Riding a bike is a green way to travel.

senses.note: go green(친환경적으로 바꾸다), green energy(친환경 에너지).

senses.meaningEn: the color green

examples.en: Green is a calm, relaxing color.
This jacket also comes in green.

senses.meaningEn: to say hello to someone or welcome them when you meet

examples.en: The dog greets me at the door every day.
examples.ko: 강아지가 매일 문 앞에서 나를 반겨 줘.

examples.en: She greeted everyone with a big smile.

senses.note: greet 뒤에 바로 목적어(greet the guests). 'say hello to' 가 더 구어적. 명사는 greeting(인사, 인사말 — Season's Greetings).

senses.meaningEn: a number of people or things that are together or connected

examples.en: A group of kids was playing in the park.
examples.ko: 아이들 한 무리가 공원에서 놀고 있었어.

examples.en: Please work in groups of four.

senses.note: a group of + 복수명사. 수업에서는 '모둠'이 자연스러운 번역. group chat = 단체 채팅.

senses.meaningEn: a small number of musicians or singers who perform together

examples.en: My favorite group is playing in Seoul next month.
examples.ko: 내가 좋아하는 그룹이 다음 달 서울에서 공연해.

examples.en: The group has four singers.

senses.note: 록·재즈는 band, 아이돌·보컬 팀은 group 이 더 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: to put people or things together in groups

examples.en: Group the words by their first letter.
The teacher grouped us by age.

senses.meaningEn: to become bigger or taller over time

examples.en: Kids grow so fast these days.
My hair grows really quickly in summer.

senses.note: grow up = 어른이 되다, 자라다: I grew up in Busan. grow 만 쓰면 키·크기가 커진다는 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: to plant and take care of plants so they develop

examples.en: We grow tomatoes in our garden.
My grandpa grew rice for forty years.

senses.note: 동물·아이를 키우는 건 raise: raise kids / raise chickens. grow 는 식물·수염(grow a beard).

senses.meaningEn: to increase in size, number, or amount

examples.en: The city has grown a lot since I moved here.
examples.ko: 내가 이사 온 뒤로 도시가 많이 커졌어.

examples.en: Our class grew from ten to twenty students.
examples.ko: 우리 반은 열 명에서 스무 명으로 늘었어.

senses.meaningEn: to change from a child into an adult, or to spend your childhood somewhere

examples.en: I grew up in a small town near Busan.
examples.ko: 나는 부산 근처 작은 동네에서 자랐어.

examples.en: What do you want to be when you grow up?

senses.note: grow(식물·키가 자라다) 와 달리 grow up 은 사람이 '어른이 되다'. Where did you grow up? = 어디서 자랐어요? 과거형 grew up. grown-up(명사) = 어른.

senses.meaningKo: (Grow up!) 철 좀 들어, 어른답게 행동해
senses.meaningEn: used to tell someone to stop behaving like a child

examples.en: Oh, grow up! Stop fighting over the remote.
examples.ko: 아, 철 좀 들어! 리모컨 가지고 싸우지 마.

examples.en: He needs to grow up and take responsibility.
examples.ko: 그는 철이 들어서 책임을 져야 해.

senses.note: 짜증 섞인 표현. 친한 사이에서만.

senses.meaningEn: to give an answer when you are not sure it is right

examples.en: Guess how old I am.
I guessed the answer and got it right.

senses.note: I guess so. = 그런 것 같아(확신 없음, 미국 구어). Guess what! = 있잖아, 맞혀 봐!(놀라운 소식 꺼낼 때).

senses.meaningEn: an answer you give when you are not sure

examples.en: Take a guess. What's in the box?
examples.ko: 한번 맞혀 봐. 상자 안에 뭐가 있을까?

examples.en: That was a good guess!

senses.note: make a guess / take a guess = 추측해 보다. My guess is... = 내 짐작으로는...

senses.meaningEn: used before telling someone surprising or exciting news

examples.en: Guess what? I got the job!
Guess what I found under the bed.
examples.ko: 침대 밑에서 뭘 찾았는지 맞혀 봐.

senses.note: 상대가 진짜로 맞히길 바라는 게 아니라 관심을 끄는 말. 답은 What? 로 받아 주면 됨. 뒤에 절을 붙이면(guess what happened) 진짜 '맞혀 봐' 의 뜻도 됨. 가까운 사이에서 쓰는 캐주얼한 표현.

senses.meaningEn: a person who is invited to your home or to an event

examples.en: We have guests coming for dinner tonight.
examples.ko: 오늘 밤 저녁 식사에 손님들이 와.

examples.en: Please make our guest feel welcome.

senses.note: 가게 손님은 customer, 집·파티 손님은 guest. Be my guest. = 그러세요, 마음껏 하세요.

senses.meaningEn: a person who is staying at a hotel

examples.en: Breakfast is free for hotel guests.
Are you a guest at this hotel?

senses.meaningEn: a musical instrument with six strings that you play with your fingers

examples.en: He plays the guitar in a small band.
I want to learn the guitar this year.

senses.note: 강세는 뒤 — gui-TAR. electric guitar(일렉 기타), acoustic guitar(어쿠스틱 기타). 기타 연주자는 guitarist, '기타 치다'는 play the guitar.

senses.meaningEn: a room or building for doing exercise or sports

examples.en: I go to the gym three times a week.
examples.ko: 나는 일주일에 세 번 헬스장에 가.

examples.en: The basketball game is in the school gym.

senses.note: 한국어 '헬스'는 영어로 통하지 않음 → go to the gym / work out. gymnasium 의 줄임말.

senses.meaningEn: a sports class at school

examples.en: We have gym after lunch today.
examples.ko: 오늘 점심 후에 체육 수업 있어.

examples.en: I forgot my gym clothes again!

senses.note: 체육 수업은 gym 또는 P.E.(physical education). gym class = 체육 시간.

senses.meaningEn: the thin threads that grow on your head

examples.en: I need to get my hair cut.
She has long black hair.

senses.note: 머리 전체를 말할 때는 셀 수 없는 명사: hairs(×). 머리 자르러 가다 = get a haircut. 염색하다 = dye my hair.

senses.meaningEn: one thread of hair, or the hair on an animal's body

examples.en: There's a hair in my soup!
The dog's hair is all over the sofa.
examples.ko: 소파에 개 털이 잔뜩 묻어 있어.

senses.note: 한 가닥은 a hair / two hairs 로 셀 수 있음. 동물 털은 hair 또는 fur.

senses.meaningEn: a place where you pay to have your hair cut, colored, or styled

examples.en: I have an appointment at the hair salon at three.
This hair salon is always busy on Saturdays.

senses.note: 남성 전용 이발소는 barbershop. '머리를 자르다'는 get a haircut / get my hair cut 이라고 하고, cut my hair 라고 하면 스스로 자른다는 뜻이 됨.

senses.meaningEn: one of two equal parts of something

examples.en: Can I have half of your sandwich?
Cut the apple in half.

senses.note: l 은 발음하지 않는다(/hæf/). 복수형은 halves. half an hour = 30분, half past two = 2시 30분. half of + 명사 또는 half + 명사(half the class) 둘 다 가능.

senses.meaningEn: being one of two equal parts

examples.en: Kids pay half price on Tuesdays.
I only drank a half cup of coffee.
examples.ko: 나는 커피 반 잔밖에 안 마셨어.

senses.note: half price(반값), half day(반일), half-brother(이복/이부 형제).

senses.meaningEn: a round piece of cooked meat served in a bread bun

examples.en: I'll have a hamburger and a cola.
This place makes the best hamburgers in town.
examples.ko: 이 집 햄버거가 이 동네에서 최고야.

senses.note: 일상에서는 줄여서 burger 라고 더 많이 말함. ham(햄)과는 관계없고 독일 도시 Hamburg 에서 온 이름. 치즈가 들어가면 cheeseburger.

senses.meaningEn: beef that has been cut into very small pieces (US)

examples.en: Buy a pound of hamburger for the tacos.
examples.ko: 타코 만들 다진 소고기 1파운드 사 와.

examples.en: The hamburger is on sale this week.
examples.ko: 이번 주에 다진 소고기가 할인 중이야.

senses.note: 미국 마트에서 hamburger 또는 hamburger meat 는 '다진 소고기(ground beef)' 를 뜻함. 셀 수 없는 명사로 씀.

senses.meaningEn: the part of your body at the end of your arm

examples.en: Wash your hands before you eat.
Raise your hand if you have a question.

senses.note: shake hands = 악수하다, hold hands = 손을 잡다. by hand = 손으로 직접.

senses.meaningEn: to give something to someone with your hand

examples.en: Could you hand me the salt, please?
She handed him the keys and left.

senses.note: hand + 사람 + 물건 / hand + 물건 + to + 사람. hand in = 제출하다, hand out = 나눠 주다.

senses.meaningEn: help with doing something

examples.en: Can you give me a hand with these boxes?
Do you need a hand with the dishes?

senses.note: give someone a hand = 도와주다. give someone a big hand = 큰 박수를 보내다(공연·발표에서).

senses.meaningEn: to give a piece of work or a document to a teacher or person in charge

examples.en: Please hand in your homework by Friday.
I handed in my essay a day late.

senses.note: 미국 교실에서는 turn in 도 똑같이 흔함. 격식(온라인 제출 등)은 submit. hand in your notice = 사직서를 내다.

senses.meaningEn: holding each other's hand

examples.en: The couple walked hand in hand in the park.
examples.ko: 그 커플은 공원에서 손을 잡고 걸었어.

examples.en: The little girl walked hand in hand with her dad.
examples.ko: 어린 소녀가 아빠와 손을 잡고 걸었어.

senses.note: walk hand in hand 가 가장 흔한 조합. hold hands(손을 잡다) 와 함께 기억.

senses.meaningKo: (go hand in hand) 함께 가는, 밀접하게 관련된
senses.meaningEn: closely connected; happening or existing together

examples.en: Practice and progress go hand in hand.
Good sleep goes hand in hand with good health.
examples.ko: 잘 자는 것은 건강과 밀접하게 연결돼 있어.

senses.note: A and B go hand in hand / A goes hand in hand with B 형태로 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: to give something to each person in a group

examples.en: The teacher handed out the test papers.
Can you help me hand out these flyers?
examples.ko: 이 전단지 나눠 주는 것 좀 도와줄래?

senses.note: 명사 handout = 유인물, 배부 자료. pass out 도 같은 뜻이지만 pass out 은 '기절하다' 라는 뜻도 있으니 주의.

senses.meaningEn: to give something to someone, often because they ask for it or have a right to it

examples.en: Hand over the remote, it's my turn.
He handed over his passport to the officer.

senses.note: 그냥 give 보다 '내 손에서 상대 손으로 넘긴다' 는 느낌이 강함. 권한·책임을 넘기다(hand over the project)는 중급.

senses.meaningEn: a small bag, usually carried by women, for money and personal things

examples.en: She carries a small black handbag.
examples.ko: 그녀는 작은 검은색 핸드백을 들고 다녀.

examples.en: My handbag is too heavy today.

senses.note: 영국에서 일상어, 미국에서는 purse 가 더 흔하고 handbag 은 패션·매장 용어로 들림.

senses.meaningEn: to put something on a hook or line so that it does not touch the ground, or to be in that position

examples.en: Hang your coat on the hook by the door.
A big family photo hangs over the sofa.
examples.ko: 소파 위에 큰 가족사진이 걸려 있어.

senses.note: hang the laundry = 빨래를 널다. 과거형 hung. (사람을 교수형에 처하다 뜻일 때만 hanged.)

senses.meaningEn: to spend time relaxing with friends

examples.en: We hung out at the mall all afternoon.
Do you want to hang out this weekend?

senses.note: hang out (with 사람). '놀다'를 play 로 하면 어린아이 느낌. 성인은 hang out.

senses.meaningEn: to end a phone call

examples.en: Don't hang up, I'm not finished yet!
examples.ko: 끊지 마, 아직 얘기 안 끝났어!

examples.en: She hung up before I could answer.
examples.ko: 내가 대답하기도 전에 그녀가 전화를 끊었어.

senses.note: hang up (on 사람) = (~의) 전화를 끊어 버리다. 반대는 pick up(받다).

senses.meaningEn: to wait for a short time

examples.en: Hang on, I'll be right there.
Hang on a second, let me check my bag.

senses.note: Hang on. = Hold on. = Wait a second. 전화·대화 모두 가능.

senses.meaningEn: used to tell someone to keep trying and not give up in a hard situation

examples.en: Hang in there, the exam is almost over.
examples.ko: 조금만 더 버텨, 시험 거의 다 끝났어.

examples.en: I know it's hard, but hang in there.
examples.ko: 힘든 거 알아, 그래도 조금만 더 힘내.

senses.note: 힘든 상황을 견디는 사람에게 하는 응원. 안부 대답으로 "I'm hanging in there."(그냥 버티고 있어) 도 자주 씀. Good luck 과 달리 이미 어려움을 겪고 있을 때 사용.

senses.meaningEn: to wait for a short time

examples.en: Hang on, I'm almost ready.
Hang on a second. Let me find my keys.

senses.note: Hang on = Hold on = Wait a minute(구어). 전화에서 "Hang on, please." 도 OK. "Hang on, what did you say?" 처럼 "잠깐, 뭐라고?" 로도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to hold something tightly so you do not fall

examples.en: Hang on tight, the road is bumpy.
She hung on to my arm on the ice.
examples.ko: 그녀는 빙판 위에서 내 팔을 꽉 붙잡았어.

senses.note: hang on (to 물건). hang on tight 가 흔한 콜로케이션. 비유로 "버티다"(Hang on, we're almost there.) 로도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to spend relaxed time with friends

examples.en: Do you want to hang out this weekend?
I hung out with my friends after school.

senses.note: hang out with 사람. 어른이 "놀다" 는 play ✗ → hang out ✓. 명사 hangout = 자주 모이는 곳.

senses.meaningEn: to put wet clothes outside so they dry

examples.en: I hung out the laundry this morning.
Hang out the towels to dry.

senses.note: hang out the washing/laundry. 줄에 널 때 쓰고, 건조기는 dry. 걸어서 말리다는 hang ~ to dry.

senses.meaningEn: to end a phone call

examples.en: Don't hang up! I have one more question.
examples.ko: 끊지 마! 하나 더 물어볼 게 있어.

examples.en: She hung up on me.
examples.ko: 그녀가 내 전화를 뚝 끊어 버렸어.

senses.note: hang up on 사람 = 상대가 말하는 중에 끊다(무례). 반대는 pick up(받다). 끊다를 cut 으로 쓰면 ✗.

senses.meaningEn: to put something on a hook or hanger

examples.en: Hang up your coat by the door.
He hung up a picture in the living room.

senses.note: hang up 과 hang 둘 다 "걸다". hang(걸다) 의 과거는 hung, hang(교수형에 처하다) 의 과거는 hanged.

senses.meaningEn: to take place, especially without being planned

examples.en: What happened to your arm?
examples.ko: 팔 왜 그래? 무슨 일 있었어?

examples.en: Don't worry, accidents happen.
examples.ko: 걱정 마, 사고는 일어날 수 있는 거야.

senses.note: What happened? = 무슨 일이야? happen to 사람/물건 = ~에게 일이 생기다. 수동태 없음(was happened ✗).

senses.meaningEn: to do something by chance

examples.en: I happened to see Jake at the store.
Do you happen to know what time it is?

senses.note: Do you happen to know ...? 는 '혹시 ~ 아세요?' 라는 정중한 질문.

senses.meaningEn: used at the end of a fairy tale to say the characters were happy for the rest of their lives

examples.en: And they lived happily ever after.
They got married and lived happily ever after.

senses.note: 거의 항상 live(d) happily ever after 로 동화 마무리. 현실에서는 "그래서 결말이 좋았다" 를 가볍게 말할 때 씀.

senses.meaningEn: feeling or showing pleasure

examples.en: I'm so happy to see you again!
She looked happy with her new puppy.

senses.note: happy to + 동사(~해서 기쁘다), happy with/about + 명사(~에 만족하다). Happy birthday! 처럼 인사에도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: willing to do something, or satisfied with a plan

examples.en: I'm happy to help you move this weekend.
Are you happy with seven o'clock for dinner?

senses.note: I'd be happy to... 는 요청에 흔쾌히 응할 때 쓰는 공손한 표현. 상대 의견을 물을 때 Are you happy with...?

senses.meaningEn: difficult to do or understand

examples.en: The math test was really hard.
It's hard to wake up early in winter.

senses.meaningEn: firm and not easy to bend or break

examples.en: This bread is too hard to eat.
examples.ko: 이 빵은 너무 딱딱해서 못 먹겠어.

examples.en: I can't sleep on a hard bed.
examples.ko: 나는 딱딱한 침대에서는 잠을 못 자.

senses.meaningEn: with a lot of effort or force

examples.en: She works very hard every day.
It's raining really hard outside right now.
examples.ko: 지금 밖에 비가 정말 세게 와.

senses.note: hardly 는 '거의 ~않다'로 뜻이 전혀 다름. work hard (O), work hardly (X).

senses.meaningEn: a lot of effort put into doing something

examples.en: Her success came from years of hard work.
examples.ko: 그녀의 성공은 몇 년간의 노력에서 나온 거야.

examples.en: Learning a language is hard work, but it's fun.
examples.ko: 언어를 배우는 건 힘든 일이지만 재미있어.

senses.note: work 는 셀 수 없는 명사라 a hard work ✗. '힘든 일'과 '노력' 두 뜻을 모두 가짐. 사람을 칭찬할 때 Good job! / Great work! 가 자연스럽고, 노력 자체를 말할 때 hard work. 형용사형은 hard-working(부지런한).

senses.meaningEn: a piece of clothing you wear on your head

examples.en: Wear a hat; the sun is strong today.
He took off his hat when he came in.

senses.note: hat 은 모자 전반(특히 테 있는 모자). 야구모자는 cap. 모자를 '쓰다'는 wear/put on, '벗다'는 take off.

senses.meaningEn: to dislike someone or something very much

examples.en: I hate getting up early on Mondays.
examples.ko: 월요일에 일찍 일어나는 거 정말 싫어.

examples.en: Why do you hate him so much?

senses.note: hate + -ing / to. 상당히 강한 말이라 사람에게는 don't like 가 더 부드러움. 명사 hatred(증오)는 중급.

senses.meaningEn: used to say politely that you are sorry to do something

examples.en: I hate to say it, but you're wrong.
examples.ko: 이런 말 하긴 싫지만, 네가 틀렸어.

examples.en: I hate to bother you, but can I ask something?
examples.ko: 귀찮게 해서 미안하지만, 하나 물어봐도 될까요?

senses.note: I hate to say this / I hate to bother you 는 안 좋은 말을 꺼내기 전 완충 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to own or possess something

examples.en: I have two brothers and one sister.
examples.ko: 나는 남동생 둘에 여동생 하나 있어.

examples.en: Do you have a pen I can borrow?

senses.note: 소유의 have 는 진행형으로 쓰지 않음. I'm having a car (X).

senses.meaningEn: to eat or drink something

examples.en: What do you want to have for lunch?
I usually have coffee in the morning.

senses.note: have breakfast / have a drink. eat 보다 부드러운 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to experience or suffer from something

examples.en: I have a bad headache today.
I think I have a fever. I feel hot.
examples.ko: 열이 있는 것 같아. 몸이 뜨거워.

senses.note: have a cold / have a headache / have a problem.

senses.meaningEn: to have a friendly, informal talk with someone

examples.en: Let's have a chat over coffee sometime.
examples.ko: 언제 커피 마시면서 얘기 좀 하자.

examples.en: I had a nice chat with my neighbor this morning.
examples.ko: 오늘 아침에 이웃과 즐겁게 이야기를 나눴어.

senses.note: have a chat with + 사람, have a chat about + 주제. 진지한 대화는 have a talk / have a word. 온라인 메시지 '채팅'도 chat 이지만 여기서는 '수다' 의미.

senses.meaningEn: to be ill with a cold, with a runny nose, cough, or sore throat

examples.en: I have a bad cold, so I'll stay home today.
She has a cold and can't come to class.
examples.ko: 그녀는 감기에 걸려서 수업에 못 와.

senses.note: have a cold 는 '걸린 상태', catch a cold / get a cold 는 '걸리는 순간'. 관사 a 필수(have cold ✗). '감기 조심해'는 Don't catch a cold. '독감'은 have the flu(the 사용).

senses.meaningEn: to enjoy yourself

examples.en: Did you have a good time at the party?
Have a good time on your trip!

senses.note: 작별 인사로 Have a good time! / Have fun! 을 자주 씀. have a great time 은 더 강한 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to feel pain in your head

examples.en: I have a headache. Do you have any medicine?
He had a terrible headache after the long meeting.
examples.ko: 긴 회의 뒤에 그는 머리가 심하게 아팠어.

senses.note: '머리가 아프다'를 My head is sick ✗ 로 옮기지 않음. have a headache / My head hurts. 같은 패턴: have a stomachache(배), have a toothache(이), have a sore throat(목), have a fever(열).

senses.meaningEn: to look at something quickly to check or examine it

examples.en: Can I have a look at your new phone?
examples.ko: 네 새 폰 한번 봐도 돼?

examples.en: I had a look at the menu, but nothing looked good.
examples.ko: 메뉴를 봤는데 딱히 먹고 싶은 게 없었어.

senses.note: 뒤에 at 을 붙임: have a look at ~. 미국식은 take a look 이 더 흔함. 가게에서 '그냥 둘러볼게요'는 I'm just looking / just having a look.

senses.meaningEn: to organize a party, usually at your home, for friends or family

examples.en: We're having a party on Friday. Can you come?
examples.ko: 금요일에 파티 할 건데, 올 수 있어?

examples.en: They had a party for her birthday.

senses.note: '파티를 열다'를 open a party ✗ 로 쓰지 않음. 구어 have a party, 조금 더 격식은 hold a party, 재미있게는 throw a party. '파티에 가다'는 go to a party.

senses.meaningEn: to stop what you are doing and relax for a short time

examples.en: You look tired. Go and have a rest.
We had a rest under a tree after the long walk.
examples.ko: 오래 걷고 나서 나무 아래에서 잠시 쉬었어.

senses.note: have a rest 는 영국식에서 더 흔하고, 미국식은 take a break / get some rest 가 자연스러움. 몸이 아플 때 '푹 쉬어'는 Get some rest.

senses.meaningEn: to sit down; used politely to invite someone to sit

examples.en: Please have a seat. The doctor will be with you soon.
examples.ko: 앉으세요. 의사 선생님이 곧 오실 거예요.

examples.en: Have a seat anywhere you like.

senses.note: Sit down. 은 명령처럼 들릴 수 있어, 손님에게는 Please have a seat. / Take a seat. 이 훨씬 부드러움. 병원·사무실·면접 상황에서 매우 자주 들리는 말.

senses.meaningEn: to eat the first meal of the day in the morning

examples.en: I have breakfast at seven every morning.
Did you have breakfast yet? I made eggs.

senses.note: 식사 이름 앞에 a/the 를 붙이지 않음(have a breakfast ✗). 단, 형용사가 붙으면 have a big breakfast. eat breakfast 도 맞지만 have 가 더 부드럽고 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: to eat the main meal of the day, usually in the evening

examples.en: What time do you usually have dinner?
We had dinner with my parents on Sunday.

senses.note: dinner 는 하루 중 가장 큰 식사라 격식 있는 자리에도 씀. 가볍게 먹는 저녁은 supper(미국 일부 지역·영국). 외식은 go out for dinner / eat out.

senses.meaningEn: said to tell someone to enjoy themselves

examples.en: Have fun at the party tonight!
Have fun, and be careful.

senses.note: 떠나는 사람에게 하는 인사. Have a good time. 과 같음.

senses.meaningEn: to enjoy yourself doing something

examples.en: We had fun at the beach yesterday.
Are you having fun? Yes, a lot!

senses.note: fun 은 셀 수 없는 명사: have a fun (X) → have fun (O). "very fun" 보다 a lot of fun / so much fun 이 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: to eat the meal in the middle of the day

examples.en: Let's have lunch together tomorrow.
We had lunch at a small Italian restaurant.
examples.ko: 우리는 작은 이탈리안 식당에서 점심을 먹었어.

senses.note: '점심 먹었어?' = Have you had lunch? / Did you have lunch? 둘 다 자연스러움. '~와 점심을 먹다'는 have lunch with. 관사 없음(have a lunch ✗).

senses.meaningEn: a male person or animal that has already been mentioned, as the subject

examples.en: He is my older brother.
Where is Dad? He went to the store.

senses.note: 목적어는 him, 소유는 his. 한국어는 "그 사람"으로 성별을 안 가리지만 영어는 he/she 를 꼭 가름.

senses.meaningEn: the top part of your body with your eyes, ears, and brain

examples.en: I hit my head on the door.
My head hurts. Do you have any medicine?

senses.note: '머리카락'은 hair. 머리가 아프다 = I have a headache / My head hurts.

senses.meaningEn: the person in charge of a group or organization

examples.en: She is the head of the sales team.
The head of our school is Mr. Lee.

senses.note: head of the family(가장), head teacher(교장, 영국), head office(본사).

senses.meaningEn: to go in a particular direction

examples.en: Let's head home. It's getting late.
We're heading to the beach this weekend.

senses.note: head home / head to the station / head back(돌아가다). home 앞에는 to 를 쓰지 않음.

senses.meaningEn: to start going back to the place you came from

examples.en: It's getting dark. We should head back now.
I'm heading back to Seoul on Sunday.

senses.note: head back to + 장소. go back 보다 '출발해서 돌아가는 길에 오르다' 느낌. head home(집으로 가다) 도 함께 기억.

senses.meaningEn: to go in the direction of a place

examples.en: Let's head for the beach before it gets hot.
After work, I usually head for home right away.

senses.note: head for / head to / head toward 모두 OK. head 가 동사로 쓰이면 '향하다'. 'Where are you headed?'(어디 가?) 도 구어에서 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: to be likely to experience something bad soon

examples.en: If you keep skipping class, you're heading for trouble.
examples.ko: 수업을 계속 빼먹으면 큰일 날 거야.

examples.en: He's heading for a cold if he doesn't rest.

senses.note: be heading for trouble / disaster / a fall. 진행형으로 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: a pain in your head

examples.en: I have a terrible headache today.
Take this pill if your headache doesn't go away.
examples.ko: 두통이 안 가라앉으면 이 약을 먹어.

senses.note: 항상 have a headache(a 필수). 발음 /ˈhedeɪk/ — ache 는 '에이크'. 골치 아픈 일도 a headache 라고 함.

senses.meaningEn: a warning or piece of information given in advance so someone can be ready

examples.en: Heads up! The teacher is coming.
Just a heads up, the store closes at 8 tonight.
examples.ko: 참고로 말해 두는데, 가게가 오늘 8시에 닫아.

senses.note: "Heads up!" 하나로 "조심!, 날아온다!" 경고. a heads-up(명사) 는 "미리 알림": give someone a heads-up. 업무 메시지에서도 아주 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: the condition of your body and how well you are

examples.en: Smoking is bad for your health.
My grandmother is in good health for her age.

senses.note: 셀 수 없는 명사(a health 아님). in good/bad health, health problems, health insurance(건강 보험). 형용사는 healthy.

senses.meaningEn: strong and well; not sick

examples.en: The baby is happy and healthy.
I want to stay healthy, so I exercise every day.

senses.note: th 는 /θ/ 로 발음. stay healthy(건강을 유지하다), keep healthy.

senses.meaningEn: good for your health

examples.en: Vegetables are a healthy choice for dinner.
Try to eat a healthy breakfast every morning.
examples.ko: 매일 아침 건강에 좋은 아침밥을 먹으려고 해 봐.

senses.note: healthy food(건강에 좋은 음식), a healthy diet(건강한 식단), healthy habits.

senses.meaningEn: to notice a sound with your ears

examples.en: Did you hear that noise?
I can't hear you. Can you speak up?
examples.ko: 안 들려. 좀 크게 말해 줄래?

senses.note: hear 는 저절로 들리는 것, listen (to) 는 귀 기울여 듣는 것. 보통 can hear 로 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to be told some news or information

examples.en: I heard you got a new job!
Have you heard from Mina lately?

senses.note: hear from 사람 = ~에게서 연락을 받다, hear about/of = ~에 대해 듣다. I've never heard of it. = 처음 들어 봐.

senses.meaningEn: to get news or information about something

examples.en: Did you hear about the new cafe downtown?
examples.ko: 시내에 새로 생긴 카페 얘기 들었어?

examples.en: I heard about your exam. Congratulations!

senses.note: hear about = 소식·사건을 듣다. hear of = 이름·존재를 들어 본 적 있다(I've never heard of him). hear from = ~에게서 연락받다. 셋을 구별할 것.

senses.meaningEn: to get a letter, call, or message from someone

examples.en: I haven't heard from Mina since last month.
It was nice to hear from you!

senses.note: 편지·이메일 끝의 'I hope to hear from you soon.' = 답장 기다리겠습니다. 소식을 '듣다' 는 hear about.

senses.meaningEn: the organ in your chest that pumps blood around your body

examples.en: My heart was beating really fast.
Exercise is good for your heart.

senses.note: heart attack(심장 마비), heart rate(심박수).

senses.meaningEn: the center of your feelings and emotions

examples.en: She has a very kind heart.
He broke my heart when he left.
examples.ko: 그가 떠났을 때 내 마음이 찢어졌어.

senses.note: learn by heart(암기하다), from the bottom of my heart(진심으로). 하트 모양도 heart.

senses.meaningEn: to make food hot

examples.en: I'll heat up the leftovers for lunch.
Heat up the pan before you add the oil.
examples.ko: 기름 넣기 전에 팬을 먼저 달궈.

senses.note: warm up 보다 더 뜨겁게 하는 느낌. 전자레인지 = microwave 도 동사로 씀(microwave it).

senses.meaningEn: to become hot or hotter

examples.en: The car heats up fast in summer.
It's really heating up this afternoon.

senses.meaningEn: a machine that makes a room or water warm

examples.en: Can you turn on the heater? I'm cold.
The heater in my room is broken.

senses.note: water heater = 온수기. 건물 전체 난방은 heating 이라고 함 (The heating is on).

senses.meaningEn: weighing a lot and hard to lift or move

examples.en: This box is too heavy for me to carry.
examples.ko: 이 상자는 내가 들기엔 너무 무거워.

examples.en: How heavy is your suitcase?

senses.note: 무게가 무거우면 heavy, 가벼우면 light. 사람의 체중을 완곡하게 말할 때도 heavy 를 쓴다.

senses.meaningEn: great in amount or force

examples.en: We had heavy rain all day yesterday.
examples.ko: 어제는 하루 종일 비가 많이 왔어.

examples.en: I was late because of heavy traffic.

senses.note: heavy rain / heavy snow / heavy traffic. '비가 강하다'를 strong rain 이라고 하지 않는다.

senses.meaningEn: rain that falls in large amounts

examples.en: We had heavy rain all night.
The game was canceled because of heavy rain.

senses.note: 비가 '많이' 오는 건 heavy(strong rain ✗, big rain ✗). 동사로는 It's raining heavily / It's raining hard. 약한 비는 light rain. heavy snow / heavy traffic 도 같은 패턴.

senses.meaningEn: how tall someone or something is

examples.en: The nurse measured my height and weight.
We are about the same height.

senses.note: 발음은 [하이트]. weight 와 달리 ei 가 /aɪ/ 로 소리 난다. 키가 크다는 I have a big height 가 아니라 I'm tall.

senses.meaningEn: an aircraft with large spinning blades on top that can fly straight up and down

examples.en: A helicopter flew over our house.
They took the sick man to the hospital by helicopter.

senses.note: 구어에서는 chopper 라고도 함. 한국어 '헬기'처럼 줄여서 heli 라고 하는 경우는 드묾.

senses.meaningEn: used as a greeting when you meet or see someone

examples.en: Hello, nice to meet you.
She said hello to everyone in the room.
examples.ko: 그녀는 방 안의 모두에게 인사를 건넸어.

senses.note: hi 보다 조금 더 격식 있음. 아침·저녁 상관없이 하루 종일 쓸 수 있음. say hello to ~ = ~에게 인사하다/안부 전하다.

senses.meaningEn: used when you answer the phone

examples.en: Hello? Who's calling, please?
Hello, this is Mina speaking.

senses.note: 전화 받을 때 첫말. 영어로 자기를 밝힐 때는 I am 이 아니라 This is + 이름 (speaking).

senses.meaningEn: used to get someone's attention or check if anyone is there

examples.en: Hello? Is anybody home?
Hello, excuse me, you dropped your wallet.

senses.meaningEn: a hard hat that protects your head

examples.en: Always wear a helmet when you ride a bike.
examples.ko: 자전거 탈 때는 항상 헬멧을 써.

examples.en: The workers all wear yellow helmets.
examples.ko: 작업자들은 모두 노란 안전모를 쓰고 있어.

senses.note: wear a helmet(쓰다), put on a helmet(쓰는 동작). 건설 현장용은 hard hat 이라고도 함.

senses.meaningEn: to make it easier for someone to do something

examples.en: Can you help me carry these boxes?
examples.ko: 이 상자들 옮기는 것 좀 도와줄래?

examples.en: Thanks for helping me move last weekend.

senses.note: help + 사람 + (to) 동사원형: help me carry / help me to carry 둘 다 가능. help with + 명사: help with homework. can't help -ing = ~하지 않을 수 없다.

senses.meaningEn: the act of helping someone

examples.en: Do you need any help?
Thanks a lot for your help today.

senses.note: 셀 수 없는 명사: a help ✗ → some help. 가게 점원: Can I help you? / Help! = 도와주세요!(위급).

senses.meaningEn: to take food or drink for yourself without waiting to be served

examples.en: Help yourself to some cookies.
Please help yourselves to drinks in the fridge.
examples.ko: 냉장고에 있는 음료 편하게 꺼내 드세요.

senses.note: help yourself (to + 음식). 손님에게 음식을 권할 때 가장 흔한 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to help someone by doing part of their work or by giving them something they need

examples.en: I help out at my uncle's shop on weekends.
Thanks for helping out with the dishes.

senses.note: help 와 뜻은 같지만 help out 은 '바쁠 때 잠깐 거들어 준다'는 가벼운 느낌. help out with + 명사(일). help someone out = 사람을 도와주다.

senses.meaningEn: to give someone money or things they need when they are in a difficult situation

examples.en: My parents helped me out when I lost my job.
Can you help me out? I'm a little short.
examples.ko: 좀 도와줄 수 있어? 돈이 조금 모자라.

senses.note: I'm short(돈이 부족해) 뒤에 help me out 이 오면 보통 돈을 빌려 달라는 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: used to tell someone to take as much food or drink as they want

examples.en: Help yourself to some cookies.
There's juice in the fridge. Help yourself.

senses.note: help yourself to + 음식 으로 씀. 여럿에게는 Help yourselves. 집에 온 손님에게, 뷔페·파티에서 자주. '스스로를 도와라' 라는 뜻이 아님.

senses.meaningEn: used to say that someone may take or use something freely

examples.en: Can I use your pen? Sure, help yourself.
examples.ko: 펜 좀 써도 돼? 응, 편하게 써.

examples.en: Help yourself to any book on the shelf.

senses.note: 음식뿐 아니라 물건·공간에도 씀. 허락을 구하는 질문(Can I...?)에 Sure, help yourself 로 답하면 '그래, 알아서 써' 라는 편한 허락.

senses.meaningEn: an adult female chicken

examples.en: The hens lay eggs every morning.
My grandma keeps six hens in her yard.
examples.ko: 할머니는 마당에서 암탉 여섯 마리를 키우셔.

senses.note: 수탉은 rooster(미) / cock(영), 병아리는 chick, 통칭은 chicken. lay eggs = 알을 낳다. 영국에서 hen party 는 신부 측 결혼 전 파티.

senses.meaningEn: a female person or animal already mentioned, used as the object

examples.en: I met her at the library yesterday.
Tell her the meeting is at three.
examples.ko: 그녀에게 회의가 세 시라고 말해 줘.

senses.meaningEn: belonging to a female person or animal already mentioned

examples.en: Her house is near the station.
Mina left her umbrella in the car.

senses.note: 목적어(her)와 소유(her)가 같은 형태라 한국인이 he/him/his 와 짝 맞추다 헷갈림. 뒤에 명사가 오면 소유, 아니면 목적어. 소유대명사는 hers.

senses.meaningEn: in, at, or to this place

examples.en: Come here and sit down.
I've lived here for ten years.

senses.note: here 앞에는 to/in/at 을 붙이지 않음. 'come to here' 가 아니라 come here.

senses.meaningEn: used when you give or show something to someone

examples.en: Here is your change.
Here you are, one coffee.

senses.note: Here you are / Here you go / Here it is 는 물건을 건넬 때 쓰는 세트 표현. 전화를 받을 때 '전데요' 도 This is he/she, 영국에서는 Speaking 이라고 하지 here 는 안 씀.

senses.meaningEn: used to say that you are present or have arrived

examples.en: Here! I'm sitting in the back.
The bus is here. Let's go.

senses.note: 출석 부를 때 Here! 라고 대답. 교통수단이 도착했을 때 be here = 도착했다.

senses.meaningEn: in several different places, not in one place

examples.en: There were a few trees here and there.
We stopped here and there to take pictures.

senses.note: '곳곳에' 지만 '많이' 는 아님(조금씩 흩어져 있는 느낌). 어순은 항상 here and there(there and here 아님). everywhere 는 '어디에나·사방에'.

senses.meaningEn: used when you are about to start doing something

examples.en: Everyone ready? Here we go!
Okay, here we go. Press the button.

senses.note: 놀이기구 출발, 게임·발표 시작, 아이를 안아 올릴 때 등. 흥을 돋우는 느낌. Here we go again 은 '또 시작이네' 라는 짜증·체념의 뜻이 되므로 주의.

senses.meaningEn: used when you find or finish something you were looking for or doing

examples.en: Where's my key? Oh, here we go.
examples.ko: 내 열쇠 어디 있지? 아, 여기 있네.

examples.en: Here we go, your table is ready.

senses.note: 찾던 것을 찾거나, 준비가 끝났을 때. Here you go(건넬 때)와 혼동하지 않도록.

senses.meaningEn: used when you give or hand something to someone

examples.en: Can I see your ticket? Here you are.
examples.ko: 표 좀 보여 주시겠어요? 여기 있습니다.

examples.en: Here you are, one coffee and a muffin.

senses.note: 돈·거스름돈·물건을 건네는 순간 하는 말. Here you go 와 거의 같고 조금 더 정중함. Here it is 는 '(찾던 게) 여기 있네' 로 뉘앙스가 다름. '당신이 여기 있다' 로 해석하지 않도록.

senses.meaningEn: used to say that you have arrived at the place you were going to

examples.en: Here you are, the station is just there.
Here you are. That'll be twelve dollars.

senses.note: 택시 기사나 길을 안내하는 사람이 도착했을 때. Here we are 는 함께 도착한 경우(우리 다 왔다).

senses.meaningEn: a person who is admired for being very brave or doing something great

examples.en: The firefighters are real heroes.
My mom is my hero.

senses.note: 복수형은 heroes(e 추가). 여성형 heroine 도 있지만 요즘은 남녀 모두 hero. superhero(슈퍼히어로).

senses.meaningEn: the main character in a story or movie

examples.en: The hero of the story is a young boy.
In the end, the hero saves the town.

senses.note: 영화·소설의 주인공을 hero/heroine 으로 부름. 악당은 villain.

senses.meaningEn: a very informal way to say hello to someone you know

examples.en: Hey, what's up?
Hey guys, come sit with us.

senses.note: 친구·가까운 동료에게만. 모르는 사람이나 윗사람에게 Hey 는 무례할 수 있음 → Hello/Excuse me.

senses.meaningKo: (주의를 끌거나 놀랐을 때) 야, 저기, 어
senses.meaningEn: used to get attention or to show surprise or annoyance

examples.en: Hey, that's my seat!
Hey, look at this photo.

senses.note: Hey, wait! = 야, 잠깐! 처음 보는 사람 부를 때는 Hey 보다 Excuse me 가 공손함.

senses.meaningEn: an informal way to say hello

examples.en: Hi, how's it going?
Hi everyone, sorry I'm late.

senses.note: 친구·동료 사이, 이메일 첫 줄(Hi Tom,)에도 흔히 씀. 가게 점원이 손님에게도 Hi 라고 함. 격식 상황에서는 Hello/Good morning.

senses.meaningEn: used in say hi to to send a friendly message to someone

examples.en: Say hi to your mom for me.
I just wanted to say hi before I leave.

senses.note: say hi to + 사람 = 안부를 전하다. Tell your mom I said hi. 도 같은 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: to put something where no one can see or find it

examples.en: I hid the presents in the closet.
Where did you hide my phone?

senses.note: hide 물건 from 사람 = ~에게 숨기다. 감정 숨기기도 hide: hide your feelings.

senses.meaningEn: to go to a place where no one can see or find you

examples.en: The cat is hiding under the bed again.
examples.ko: 고양이가 또 침대 밑에 숨어 있어.

examples.en: Quick, hide behind the door!

senses.note: hide-and-seek = 숨바꼭질. 숨기다·숨다 모두 hide 한 단어로 표현(자동사·타동사 둘 다).

senses.meaningEn: a children's game in which one player looks for the others who are hiding

examples.en: The kids are playing hide-and-seek in the yard.
Let's play hide-and-seek! You count first.

senses.note: play hide-and-seek — 관사 없음. 숨는 사람은 hide, 찾는 사람은 seek(찾다). 찾는 사람 역할은 'it'(You're it!). 술래잡기는 tag.

senses.meaningEn: a long way above the ground, or having a great height

examples.en: The shelf is too high for me to reach.
