examples.ko: 선반이 너무 높아서 손이 안 닿아.

examples.en: That mountain is very high.

senses.note: 사람·나무·건물의 키는 tall(a tall man), 위치나 산·벽의 높이는 high. 'a high man' 은 틀림.

senses.meaningEn: greater than normal in amount, level, or price

examples.en: Prices are very high in this area.
He has a high fever today.

senses.note: high price(비싼 가격), high temperature, high speed. 가격이 '비싸다'는 expensive 와 함께 high 도 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: at or to a great height

examples.en: The bird flew high in the sky.
He can jump really high.
examples.ko: 그는 정말 높이 뛸 수 있어.

senses.note: 부사 high 는 '물리적으로 높이'. highly 는 '매우, 높이(평가)'(highly recommended).

senses.meaningEn: hitting your raised hand against someone else's to celebrate or say well done

examples.en: We scored! Give me a high five!
The coach gave every kid a high five.

senses.note: give (사람) a high five / high-five someone(동사). "High five!" 라고 외치며 손을 들어 올린다. 주먹을 맞대는 건 fist bump.

senses.meaningEn: the activity of taking long walks in the mountains or countryside

examples.en: We went hiking in the mountains last weekend.
Hiking is very popular with older Koreans.
examples.ko: 등산은 한국 어르신들에게 아주 인기 있어.

senses.note: 한국식 '등산'은 보통 hiking. mountain climbing 은 장비를 쓰는 본격 등반. 등산화는 hiking boots, 등산 코스는 hiking trail.

senses.meaningEn: an area of high land that is smaller than a mountain

examples.en: Our school is on top of a hill.
It's hard to ride a bike up this hill.

senses.note: up the hill(언덕 위로) / down the hill(언덕 아래로). 한국의 '동네 뒷산'은 보통 hill 로 말하면 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: a male person or animal already mentioned, used as the object

examples.en: I saw him at the bus stop.
Give him a call when you get home.
examples.ko: 집에 가면 그에게 전화 한번 해.

senses.note: he(주어) → him(목적어) → his(소유). "That's him!"(저 사람이야!)처럼 be 동사 뒤에서도 구어에선 him 을 씀.

senses.meaningEn: belonging to a male person or animal already mentioned

examples.en: He lost his wallet on the bus.
His office is on the third floor.

senses.note: he → him → his. she 의 소유 her 와 섞이기 쉬우니 짝으로 외울 것.

senses.meaningEn: the thing or things that belong to him

examples.en: This cup is mine and that one is his.
examples.ko: 이 컵은 내 거고 저건 그의 거야.

examples.en: My bike is red. His is blue.
examples.ko: 내 자전거는 빨간색이야. 그의 것은 파란색이고.

senses.note: 소유격(his + 명사)과 소유대명사(his 단독)가 같은 형태. her/hers, my/mine 과 비교.

senses.meaningEn: the study of things that happened in the past

examples.en: We have a history test tomorrow.
My favorite subject is history.

senses.note: 과목으로 쓸 때는 관사 없음. Korean history = 한국사, world history = 세계사. 형용사는 historical.

senses.meaningEn: all the things that happened in the past

examples.en: This building has a long history.
The museum tells the history of the city.
examples.ko: 이 박물관은 도시의 역사를 보여 줘.

senses.note: a long history = 오랜 역사. '이야기(story)'와 철자가 비슷하지만 다른 단어.

senses.meaningEn: to touch something or someone hard and quickly with your hand or an object

examples.en: She hit the ball over the fence.
Stop hitting your brother!

senses.note: hit-hit-hit 으로 변하지 않는 동사. hit the ball(공을 치다), hit a home run(홈런을 치다). '사람을 때리다' 는 hit 이지만 가볍게 '툭 치다'는 tap.

senses.meaningEn: to touch something with force by accident, often causing pain or damage

examples.en: I hit my head on the low door.
The car hit a tree but nobody was hurt.
examples.ko: 차가 나무에 부딪혔지만 아무도 안 다쳤어.

senses.note: hit my head on + 물체 = ~에 머리를 부딪히다. 한국어 '부딪히다'를 생각하면 hit 이 떠오르지 않을 수 있으니 기억해 둘 것.

senses.meaningEn: a song, movie, or thing that is very popular and successful

examples.en: That song was a big hit last summer.
examples.ko: 그 노래 지난 여름에 크게 히트했지.

examples.en: The new game is a hit with kids.

senses.note: a hit song/movie, be a hit with + 사람(~에게 인기다). 한국어의 '히트'와 거의 같은 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: to begin studying hard

examples.en: I have a test tomorrow, so I need to hit the books.
examples.ko: 내일 시험이라 공부 열심히 해야 해.

examples.en: Stop playing games and hit the books!

senses.note: 미국 구어. 시험 직전에 집중해서 공부할 때 많이 씀. 책을 '치다' 가 아니라 '본격적으로 시작하다' 의 hit(hit the road, hit the gym 과 같은 쓰임).

senses.meaningEn: to go to bed

examples.en: It's late. Time to hit the hay.
I hit the hay at nine last night.

senses.note: hay = 건초(옛날 침대 속재료). hit the sack 과 완전히 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있음. 미국 구어.

senses.meaningEn: to go to bed

examples.en: I'm so tired. I'm going to hit the sack.
We hit the sack early because of the trip.
examples.ko: 여행 때문에 우리는 일찍 잠자리에 들었어.

senses.note: sack = 옛날에 자루에 짚을 넣어 만든 침대. 친구·가족 사이의 구어. 격식은 go to bed.

senses.meaningEn: an activity you do for fun in your free time

examples.en: What are your hobbies? I like cooking.
Taking photos is my new hobby.

senses.note: 복수형 hobbies. 원어민은 What do you do for fun? / in your free time? 으로 묻는 경우가 더 자연스러움. '취미는 독서'는 My hobby is reading.

senses.meaningEn: to have something in your hand or arms

examples.en: Can you hold my bag for a second?
She held the baby gently in her arms.

senses.note: hold hands = 손을 잡다, hold on = 잠깐 기다려(구어). 들고 이동하는 건 carry, 그 자리에서 쥐고 있는 건 hold.

senses.meaningEn: to organize and have a meeting, party, or event

examples.en: We hold a team meeting every Monday morning.
examples.ko: 우리는 매주 월요일 아침에 팀 회의를 해.

examples.en: The party was held at my uncle's house.

senses.note: 수동태 be held 가 매우 자주 쓰임: The game will be held on Sunday.

senses.meaningEn: to wait on the phone without hanging up

examples.en: Please hold, I'll get the manager for you.
examples.ko: 잠시만 기다려 주세요, 매니저 연결해 드릴게요.

examples.en: Can you hold for a minute while I check?

senses.note: 전화에서 Hold on, please. / Can you hold? 로 쓰임. on hold = 대기 중.

senses.meaningEn: to stop yourself from showing a feeling

examples.en: She couldn't hold back her tears.
I tried to hold back a laugh.

senses.note: hold back tears/a laugh/anger. 참다 를 endure 로 쓰면 어색; 감정을 "안 보이게 누르다" 는 hold back.

senses.meaningEn: to stop someone or something from moving forward

examples.en: The police held back the crowd.
The wall holds back the water when it rains.
examples.ko: 비가 오면 그 벽이 물을 막아 줘.

senses.note: 물리적으로 "앞으로 못 가게 막다". hold 사람 back.

senses.meaningEn: to not do or say something, or to stop someone from making progress

examples.en: Don't hold back. Ask any question you want.
Fear is holding him back.

senses.note: "Don't hold back." = 주저하지 말고 다 해/말해. hold 사람 back = 사람의 성장·발전을 막다.

senses.meaningEn: to wait for a short time

examples.en: Hold on, I'll be right back.
Hold on a minute, please. I'll check.

senses.note: 전화에서 "Hold on, please." = "Please hold."(잠시만 기다려 주세요). hang on 보다 조금 더 중립적이라 손님에게도 OK.

senses.meaningEn: to hold something tightly so you do not fall

examples.en: Hold on tight. The roller coaster is starting.
He held on as the boat rocked.

senses.note: Hold on tight! 가 대표 표현. 무엇을 잡는지 말하려면 hold on to the rail.

senses.meaningEn: to keep going in a difficult situation

examples.en: Hold on. Help is on the way.
Just hold on a little longer; it's almost over.

senses.note: 위로·응원할 때. 노래 가사에서도 매우 흔함("Hold on!").

senses.meaningEn: to hold something tightly so you do not fall or lose it

examples.en: Hold on to the rail when the bus moves.
examples.ko: 버스가 움직일 때는 손잡이를 꽉 잡아.

examples.en: She held on to my hand in the crowd.
examples.ko: 그녀는 사람들 속에서 내 손을 꽉 잡았어.

senses.note: hold onto 로 붙여 쓰기도 함. hold on(붙잡다) 뒤에 잡는 대상을 말할 때 to 를 붙임.

senses.meaningEn: to keep something and not give it away or throw it out

examples.en: Hold on to your receipt in case you need a refund.
examples.ko: 환불이 필요할지 모르니 영수증 잘 보관해.

examples.en: I held on to my old photos for years.
examples.ko: 나는 옛 사진들을 몇 년 동안 간직했어.

senses.note: 물건뿐 아니라 hold on to a dream/hope(꿈·희망을 놓지 않다) 로도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to move your hand or something in your hand toward someone

examples.en: He held out his hand for a handshake.
She held out a cookie to the little boy.

senses.note: hold out one's hand 가 대표 콜로케이션. 받으라고 내미는 동작.

senses.meaningEn: to continue to be enough, or to keep going in a hard situation

examples.en: Will the food hold out until Sunday?
The hikers held out for two days in the snow.

senses.note: hold out for ~(더 좋은 조건을 기다리며 버티다), hold out hope(희망을 버리지 않다) 로 확장됨.

senses.meaningEn: to lift something up so people can see it

examples.en: Hold up your hand if you know the answer.
She held up the picture so everyone could see.
examples.ko: 그녀는 모두 볼 수 있게 그림을 들어 올렸어.

senses.note: hold up 손/물건 = 들어서 보여 주다. raise your hand 와 같은 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: to make someone or something late

examples.en: Sorry I'm late. I was held up in traffic.
examples.ko: 늦어서 미안. 차가 막혀서 발이 묶였어.

examples.en: The accident held up the buses for an hour.
examples.ko: 그 사고로 버스가 한 시간 지연됐어.

senses.note: 수동태 be held up (in traffic / at work) = 늦어지다. 명사 holdup = 지연. 구어 "Hold up!" = 잠깐!(= Hold on!).

senses.meaningEn: used to tell someone to wait and not act too quickly

examples.en: Hold your horses! I'm not ready yet.
Hold your horses, let's read the rules first.

senses.note: 말(horse)을 몰던 시절에서 온 표현. 흥분해서 서두르는 사람에게 장난스럽게. 윗사람에게는 Just a moment, please 가 안전. 항상 복수 horses.

senses.meaningEn: a special day when most people do not go to work or school

examples.en: Monday is a national holiday, so no school.
Chuseok is a big holiday in Korea.

senses.note: 미국식에서 holiday 는 '공휴일·명절' 하나하나를 뜻함. Happy holidays! = 연말(크리스마스~새해) 인사. public holiday = 공휴일.

senses.meaningEn: time off from work or school, often spent traveling (British English)

examples.en: We're going on holiday to Spain in July.
The kids are on holiday until September.

senses.note: 영국·호주에서는 holiday 가 미국의 vacation 역할. 미국인에게 I'm on holiday. 라고 하면 알아듣긴 하지만 영국식으로 들림.

senses.meaningEn: the place where you live, especially with your family

examples.en: There's no place like home.
I usually work from home on Fridays.

senses.note: house 는 건물, home 은 '사는 곳·가정'의 느낌. at home = 집에(서).

senses.meaningEn: to or at the place where you live

examples.en: I'm going home now. See you tomorrow!
examples.ko: 나 이제 집에 가. 내일 봐!

examples.en: What time did you get home last night?

senses.note: go home, come home, get home — 앞에 to 를 붙이지 않음(go to home ✗).

senses.meaningEn: the address of the place where you live

examples.en: Please write your home address and phone number here.
examples.ko: 여기에 집 주소와 전화번호를 적어 주세요.

examples.en: I'll send the package to your home address.

senses.note: 직장 주소는 work/office address, 이메일 주소는 email address. 영어 주소는 작은 단위에서 큰 단위 순(번지→도로→도시→우편번호→국가). address 의 강세는 미국식에서 명사 ADdress, 동사 adDRESS.

senses.meaningEn: the classroom and short daily meeting where students check in with their main teacher

examples.en: We have homeroom at eight every morning.
Ms. Lee is my homeroom teacher.

senses.note: homeroom teacher = 담임 선생님. 미국 중·고등학교 용어로, 한국의 '우리 반 교실/조회'에 가장 가까운 말.

senses.meaningEn: schoolwork that a student does at home

examples.en: Have you finished your homework yet?
We have a lot of math homework tonight.

senses.note: 셀 수 없는 명사: homeworks ✗, a homework ✗. '숙제 하나'는 a piece of homework 또는 an assignment. do homework(하다), hand in homework(제출하다).

senses.meaningEn: telling the truth and not cheating

examples.en: To be honest, I didn't like the movie.
Just be honest with me. What happened?
examples.ko: 나한테 솔직하게 말해 줘. 무슨 일이야?

senses.note: h 는 묵음 → an honest man. To be honest(솔직히 말하면) 은 구어에서 매우 흔한 문장 시작. honest with + 사람. 명사 honesty.

senses.meaningEn: a sweet, sticky, golden food made by bees

examples.en: I put honey in my tea instead of sugar.
examples.ko: 나는 차에 설탕 대신 꿀을 넣어.

examples.en: This honey is from my uncle's farm.
examples.ko: 이 꿀은 우리 삼촌 농장에서 온 거야.

senses.note: 셀 수 없는 명사: a jar of honey. 벌은 bee, 벌집은 honeycomb.

senses.meaningEn: a name you call someone you love, such as a partner or child

examples.en: Honey, I'm home!
Are you okay, honey? You look tired.

senses.note: 연인·배우자·아이에게 쓰는 다정한 호칭. 비슷한 말: sweetie, dear, babe. 가게 점원이 손님에게 쓰면 지역에 따라 친근하거나 무례하게 들릴 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: to jump on one foot, or to make small jumps like a rabbit or bird

examples.en: The rabbit hopped across the garden.
Can you hop on one foot ten times?
examples.ko: 한 발로 열 번 뛸 수 있어?

senses.note: hop(짧게 깡충) vs jump(일반적으로 뛰다) vs skip(가볍게 뛰며 가다). 과거형 hopped.

senses.meaningEn: to get on or off a vehicle quickly

examples.en: Hop in, I'll give you a ride.
We hopped on the bus just in time.

senses.note: Hop in! = (차에) 타! hop on/off a bus/train. 가볍고 친근한 말투.

senses.meaningEn: to want something to happen and think it is possible

examples.en: I hope you feel better soon.
We're hoping for good weather this weekend.

senses.note: hope (that) + 절 / hope to 동사 / hope for 명사. I hope so. / I hope not. 으로 짧게 대답. 가능성이 있는 일에는 hope, 거의 불가능한 일에는 wish.

senses.meaningEn: the feeling that something good may happen

examples.en: Don't give up hope.
There's still hope for our team.

senses.note: give up hope = 희망을 버리다, lose hope = 희망을 잃다.

senses.meaningEn: believing that something good will probably happen

examples.en: I'm hopeful that I'll pass the exam.
The doctor was hopeful about her recovery.

senses.note: hopeful about + 명사 / hopeful that + 문장. hopefully(부사) = 바라건대: Hopefully it won't rain.

senses.meaningEn: a large animal with four legs that people ride or use to pull things

examples.en: I rode a horse for the first time yesterday.
The horses are running across the field.

senses.note: ride a horse = 말을 타다. horse racing(경마), horseback riding(승마). 조랑말은 pony. 발음 주의: horse /hɔːrs/ 와 house /haʊs/ 구별.

senses.meaningEn: a large building where sick or injured people are treated and stay

examples.en: He is in the hospital after the accident.
examples.ko: 그는 사고 후 병원에 입원해 있어.

examples.en: My mom works at a hospital near our house.
examples.ko: 엄마는 우리 집 근처 병원에서 일하셔.

senses.note: 한국어 '병원 가다'는 가벼운 진료면 see a doctor / go to the doctor. hospital 은 입원·응급 등 큰 병원 느낌. 미국은 in the hospital, 영국은 in hospital.

senses.meaningEn: a bed in a hospital for a patient to lie in

examples.en: Grandma was lying in a hospital bed for a week.
examples.ko: 할머니는 일주일 동안 병원 침대에 누워 계셨어.

examples.en: The hospital bed goes up and down with a button.
examples.ko: 병원 침대는 버튼으로 올리고 내릴 수 있어.

senses.note: in a hospital bed = 입원해서 누워 있는 상태. 입원하다는 be in the hospital, 뉴스에서 '병상 수'는 hospital beds.

senses.meaningEn: having a high temperature

examples.en: Careful, the coffee is very hot.
I want to take a hot shower.

senses.note: 음식·물·사물이 뜨거울 때. 미지근한 것은 warm.

senses.meaningEn: having hot weather

examples.en: It's so hot today!
Summer in Korea is hot and humid.

senses.note: 날씨는 It's hot. 사람이 더울 때 I'm hot. 도 가능하지만 상황에 따라 '매력적이다'로 들릴 수 있어 I'm feeling hot. 또는 I'm so warm. 이 안전.

senses.meaningEn: having a strong burning taste from spices

examples.en: Is this sauce hot?
This kimchi is too hot for me.

senses.note: '뜨겁다'와 '맵다'가 모두 hot 이라 헷갈릴 수 있음. 명확히 하려면 spicy hot / temperature hot.

senses.meaningEn: a long, thin sausage served in a long piece of bread

examples.en: We ate hot dogs at the baseball game.
Do you want ketchup on your hot dog?

senses.note: 미국의 hot dog 는 긴 빵 사이에 소시지를 끼운 음식. 한국식 '핫도그'(막대에 꽂아 튀긴 것)는 영어로 corn dog 라고 함.

senses.meaningEn: a building where you pay to stay in a room when you travel

examples.en: We stayed at a small hotel near the beach.
examples.ko: 우리는 해변 근처 작은 호텔에 묵었어.

examples.en: Is breakfast included at this hotel?
examples.ko: 이 호텔은 아침 식사가 포함되어 있나요?

senses.note: 호텔에 '묵다'는 stay at a hotel (stay in 도 가능). 체크인/체크아웃은 check in / check out. 발음은 두 번째 음절 강세 /hoʊˈtel/, 첫음절에 두면 어색함.

senses.meaningEn: a period of sixty minutes

examples.en: The movie is about two hours long.
examples.ko: 그 영화는 두 시간 정도 돼.

examples.en: I waited for an hour at the bus stop.

senses.note: h 가 묵음이라 관사는 an hour. half an hour = 30분, an hour and a half = 1시간 30분. 한국인이 자주 틀리는 것: '2시간'은 two hours(복수 s 필수).

senses.meaningEn: the time when a shop or office is open or when people work

examples.en: What are your opening hours on Sunday?
I work long hours during the busy season.

senses.note: office hours(근무/상담 시간), opening hours(영업시간), rush hour(출퇴근 혼잡 시간), after hours(영업 종료 후).

senses.meaningEn: a building where people live, usually for one family

examples.en: We live in a small house near the park.
examples.ko: 우리는 공원 근처 작은 집에 살아.

examples.en: Their house has a big backyard.

senses.note: 복수형 houses 는 /ˈhaʊzɪz/ 로 발음. 아파트에 살면 house 가 아니라 apartment.

senses.meaningEn: the people who live in a house, or someone's place

examples.en: Come over to my house after school.
The whole house was asleep by ten.
examples.ko: 열 시쯤엔 집안 사람들이 모두 잠들었어.

senses.note: my house = 우리 집(에). 친구를 초대할 때 Come to my house / Come over 를 많이 씀.

senses.meaningEn: in what way or by what method

examples.en: How do you spell your name?
How did you get here so fast?

senses.note: How about ~? = ~는 어때?(제안). What about 과 거의 같음.

senses.meaningEn: used to ask about someone's health, feelings, or situation

examples.en: How are you doing today?
How was your trip?

senses.note: How are you? 에는 Good, thanks. And you? 처럼 짧게 답하면 됨. How do you do? 는 아주 격식 있는 첫인사로 요즘은 잘 안 씀.

senses.meaningEn: used before an adjective or adverb to ask about amount, size, or degree

examples.en: How much is this bag?
How long does it take to get there?

senses.note: how much(돈·양) / how many(개수) / how old(나이) / how far(거리) / how often(빈도). 셀 수 있는 명사엔 many, 없으면 much.

senses.meaningEn: used to ask why something happened

examples.en: How come you didn't call me?
You're not eating? How come?

senses.note: why 보다 캐주얼하고 놀람·궁금함이 섞임. 어순 주의: 뒤에 평서문 순서가 옴. How come you are late?(O) / How come are you late?(X). Why are you late? 와 비교.

senses.meaningEn: to put your arms around someone to show love or friendship

examples.en: She hugged her mom at the airport.
Come here and hug me!

senses.note: 명사도 됨: give someone a hug = 안아 주다. 과거형은 g 를 겹쳐 hugged.

senses.meaningEn: extremely large in size

examples.en: They live in a huge house by the lake.
examples.ko: 그들은 호숫가의 엄청 큰 집에 살아.

examples.en: Wow, that dog is huge!

senses.note: big 보다 훨씬 강한 말. 이미 "매우"의 뜻이 있어서 very huge 는 어색하고 really/absolutely huge 가 자연스러움. 발음 /hjuːdʒ/ — h 를 빼먹지 않도록.

senses.meaningEn: very great in amount or degree

examples.en: Thank you, that's a huge help.
The concert was a huge success.

senses.note: a huge fan(열렬한 팬), a huge difference(큰 차이), a huge mistake(큰 실수) 처럼 추상명사와도 잘 씀.

senses.meaningEn: a person, not an animal or a machine

examples.en: Dogs can hear sounds that humans can't.
examples.ko: 개는 사람이 못 듣는 소리를 들을 수 있어.

examples.en: Robots can't feel like humans do.

senses.note: human being 도 같은 뜻. 동물·기계와 대비할 때 쓰고, 일상에서 '사람'은 person/people.

senses.meaningEn: relating to people, or showing normal human weakness

examples.en: The human body needs water every day.
Everyone makes mistakes. I'm only human.

senses.note: I'm only human. = 나도 사람이라 완벽할 수 없다(변명·위로 표현). human rights(인권).

senses.meaningEn: the number 100

examples.en: This jacket costs a hundred dollars.
There were about two hundred people there.

senses.note: 앞에 a 나 one 이 꼭 붙음: a hundred / one hundred. 숫자 뒤에서는 복수 -s 를 붙이지 않음(two hundred, two hundreds ✗).

senses.meaningEn: a very large number of people or things

examples.en: I've told you hundreds of times!
Hundreds of people waited in line.

senses.note: hundreds of + 복수 명사 = 수백의. 정확한 수가 아니라 '아주 많다'는 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: wanting or needing to eat

examples.en: I'm so hungry. Let's get lunch.
Are you hungry? I can make some pasta.
examples.ko: 배고파? 내가 파스타 만들어 줄 수 있어.

senses.note: '배고프다'는 I'm hungry. I have hunger 라고 하지 않는다. 아주 배고플 때는 starving.

senses.meaningEn: wanting something very much

examples.en: The new players are hungry to win.
examples.ko: 새로 온 선수들은 이기고 싶어 안달이야.

examples.en: She is hungry for a new challenge.

senses.note: hungry for + 명사 / hungry to + 동사. 긍정적인 열의를 나타낼 때 쓴다.

senses.meaningEn: to move or do something quickly because there is not much time

examples.en: Hurry up, or we'll miss the train!
She hurried to the bus stop in the rain.
examples.ko: 그녀는 빗속에서 버스 정류장으로 서둘러 갔어.

senses.note: Hurry up! 이 가장 흔한 명령형. hurried / hurrying. 'No hurry.' / 'There's no rush.' = 천천히 해도 돼. 명사 hurry 는 in a hurry(바쁜, 급한).

senses.meaningEn: to do something more quickly

examples.en: Hurry up, or we'll miss the train!
Can you hurry up in the bathroom, please?

senses.note: 명령문 Hurry up! 이 가장 흔함. hurry 만 써도 같은 뜻(Hurry!). 급하다는 be in a hurry: I'm in a hurry. 재촉하는 말이라 윗사람에게는 주의.

senses.meaningEn: to feel pain in a part of your body

examples.en: My throat hurts when I swallow.
Does it hurt when I press here?

senses.note: 주어가 신체 부위: My head hurts. (I hurt 가 아님). 과거·과거분사도 hurt(불규칙).

senses.meaningEn: to injure yourself or someone else

examples.en: I hurt my hand while cooking.
Be careful or you'll hurt yourself.

senses.note: hurt + 신체 부위 = 다치다. 다친 상태는 be hurt / get hurt: Nobody got hurt.(아무도 안 다쳤어)

senses.meaningEn: to make someone feel sad or upset

examples.en: Your words really hurt me.
I didn't mean to hurt your feelings.
examples.ko: 네 마음 상하게 하려던 건 아니었어.

senses.note: hurt someone's feelings = 마음을 상하게 하다. 상처받은 상태 = be hurt.

senses.meaningEn: the man that a person is married to

examples.en: My husband cooks dinner on weekends.
Her husband works for a bank.

senses.note: 's' 는 /z/ 로 발음: /ˈhʌzbənd/. husband and wife = 부부. 격식 없는 자리에서는 my hubby 라고도 함.

senses.meaningEn: the word a speaker uses to talk about himself or herself as the subject

examples.en: I am a student from Korea.
I think we should leave now.

senses.note: 문장 어디에 있어도 항상 대문자 I. 목적어 자리에는 me(Call me, not Call I). "Tom and I"가 주어, "Tom and me"가 목적어.

senses.meaningEn: frozen water that is hard and cold

examples.en: Can I have some water with ice, please?
Do you want ice in your drink?

senses.note: 셀 수 없는 명사: an ice ✗ → an ice cube(얼음 한 개), some ice. 아이스 아메리카노 = an iced Americano(iced 에 -d 가 붙음). no ice = 얼음 빼고.

senses.meaningEn: a layer of frozen water on a road, lake, or ground

examples.en: Be careful, there's ice on the road.
I slipped on the ice and fell.

senses.note: black ice = 잘 안 보이는 도로 빙판. break the ice = 처음 만난 자리에서 어색함을 깨다.

senses.meaningEn: a sweet frozen food made from milk or cream

examples.en: Let's get some ice cream after lunch.
What's your favorite ice cream flavor?

senses.note: 두 단어로 띄어 씀. 셀 수 없는 명사라서 '하나'는 an ice cream cone / a scoop of ice cream.

senses.meaningEn: a thought or plan that you think of

examples.en: I have an idea. Let's go to the beach!
That's a great idea!

senses.note: have/get an idea = 생각이 떠오르다. Good idea! = 좋은 생각이야. 발음에 주의: 아이'디'어, 강세는 두 번째 음절.

senses.meaningEn: what you know or understand about something

examples.en: I have no idea what this means.
Do you have any idea where he is?

senses.note: I have no idea. = 전혀 모르겠어(I don't know 보다 강함). 'any idea' 는 의문문에서 '혹시 알아?'의 뉘앙스.

senses.meaningEn: used to say that something will happen only when another thing happens

examples.en: If it rains, we'll stay inside.
Call me if you need any help.

senses.note: if 절에는 미래라도 현재 시제: If it rains (not 'if it will rain'). 결과 절에 will 을 씀.

senses.meaningEn: used to talk about something that may or may not be true; whether

examples.en: I don't know if she's coming.
Can you check if the store is open?

senses.note: ask/know/wonder/check + if = ~인지. 이때 if 절 안은 의문문 어순이 아님: I don't know if she is coming (not 'is she').

senses.meaningEn: not healthy; suffering from a disease

examples.en: My grandfather is very ill in the hospital.
She felt ill and went home early.
examples.ko: 그녀는 몸이 안 좋아서 일찍 집에 갔어.

senses.note: sick 보다 조금 격식 있고 영국에서 더 흔함. 보통 be/feel 뒤에 쓰고 명사 앞에는 잘 안 씀(an ill man 보다 a sick man). 심각한 병에 seriously ill.

senses.meaningEn: to form a picture or idea of something in your mind

examples.en: Imagine a beach with white sand and blue water.
examples.ko: 하얀 모래와 파란 바다가 있는 해변을 상상해 봐.

examples.en: I can't imagine living without my phone.
examples.ko: 폰 없이 사는 건 상상도 못 하겠어.

senses.note: imagine + -ing (imagine living). to 부정사는 쓰지 않음. I can't imagine ... 은 매우 흔한 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to think that something is probably true

examples.en: I imagine she's very tired after the trip.
examples.ko: 여행 끝나고 많이 피곤할 것 같아.

examples.en: I imagine the store is closed now.
examples.ko: 지금은 가게가 닫혀 있을 것 같은데.

senses.note: I imagine ... = I suppose/guess ... 보다 살짝 부드러운 추측.

senses.meaningEn: having a big effect or value; mattering a lot

examples.en: I have an important meeting at ten.
It's important to drink enough water.

senses.note: It's important to + 동사 / It's important that... 패턴. '중요한 사람' = an important person(VIP). 강조는 very / really important.

senses.meaningEn: having great value to a particular person

examples.en: My family is the most important thing to me.
You're very important to me.

senses.note: important to + 사람 = '~에게 중요하다'. important for 는 '~에게 유익하다·필요하다'(Exercise is important for your health).

senses.meaningEn: inside a place, container, or area

examples.en: The keys are in my bag.
We live in a small town.

senses.note: 공간·도시·나라 안: in the kitchen, in Seoul, in Korea. 넓은 공간은 in, 지점은 at(at the bus stop), 표면 위는 on.

senses.meaningEn: during a month, year, or season; or after a period of time

examples.en: My birthday is in March.
I'll be back in ten minutes.

senses.note: in + 월/연도/계절/아침·저녁(in the morning). 요일·날짜는 on, 시각은 at. in ten minutes = 10분 후(이내가 아님).

senses.meaningEn: wearing something, or using a particular way or language

examples.en: The woman in the red dress is my aunt.
examples.ko: 빨간 드레스 입은 여자분이 우리 이모야.

examples.en: How do you say this in English?

senses.note: in English, in cash(현금으로), in a hurry(급히), in red(빨간색으로). 옷은 wear 대신 in 으로도 묘사 가능.

senses.meaningEn: into a place, or at home

examples.en: Come in and take off your coat.
Is your dad in?

senses.note: Come in! = 들어오세요. be in = 집·사무실에 있다, be out = 외출 중.

senses.meaningEn: needing to do something quickly because you do not have much time

examples.en: Sorry, I can't talk. I'm in a hurry.
examples.ko: 미안, 얘기 못 해. 지금 급해.

examples.en: She left in a hurry and forgot her phone.
examples.ko: 그녀는 서둘러 나가다가 휴대폰을 두고 갔어.

senses.note: be in a hurry (to do) = 급하다. 'There's no hurry.' / 'No hurry.' = 서두를 필요 없어. 부정문 I'm not in any hurry to ~ = ~할 생각이 별로 없다.

senses.meaningEn: very soon, after a short time

examples.en: Dinner is ready! — I'm coming in a minute.
The bus will be here in a minute.

senses.note: 실제 1분이 아니라 '곧' 이라는 뜻. in + 시간 = ~후에(in ten minutes = 10분 후에). 한국어 '10분 안에' 는 within ten minutes. Just a minute. / Wait a minute. = 잠깐만.

senses.meaningEn: very soon; in a very short time

examples.en: Hold on, I'll be back in a second.
The page will load in a second.

senses.note: in a minute 보다 조금 더 빠른 느낌이지만 거의 같게 쓰임. 구어에서는 in a sec 으로 줄임. Just a second. = 잠깐만요.

senses.meaningEn: used to say what is really true, often different from what people think

examples.en: He looks young, but in fact he is fifty.
examples.ko: 젊어 보이지만 사실 그는 쉰 살이야.

examples.en: I'm not tired. In fact, I feel great.

senses.note: 앞 말을 바로잡거나 더 강하게 덧붙일 때. actually 와 거의 같고, 글에서는 in fact 가 더 자연스러움. as a matter of fact 는 더 긴 같은 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: in a position that is further forward than something or someone

examples.en: Let's meet in front of the station.
A tall man sat in front of me.
examples.ko: 키 큰 남자가 내 앞에 앉았어.

senses.note: in front of 는 바깥쪽 앞. '건물의 앞부분(정면)' 은 the front of the building. before 는 위치보다 시간·순서에 주로 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: where other people can see or hear you

examples.en: Don't say that in front of the kids.
examples.ko: 아이들 앞에서 그런 말 하지 마.

examples.en: I was nervous speaking in front of the class.
examples.ko: 반 아이들 앞에서 말하는 게 떨렸어.

senses.note: '남들이 보는 자리에서' 라는 뜻. in front of everyone = 모두 앞에서.

senses.meaningEn: in trouble because you did something wrong

examples.en: He's in hot water for skipping class again.
examples.ko: 그는 또 수업을 빼먹어서 곤란하게 됐어.

examples.en: You'll be in hot water if Mom sees this mess.
examples.ko: 엄마가 이 난장판 보시면 너 혼날 거야.

senses.note: be/get in hot water (with 사람 / for 잘못). in trouble 과 같은 뜻의 구어. 실제 뜨거운 물과는 무관.

senses.meaningEn: used to say the same thing again in a simpler or clearer way

examples.en: He's not coming. In other words, he's busy.
examples.ko: 그는 안 온대. 다시 말해 바쁘다는 거지.

examples.en: In other words, you want more money?

senses.note: 앞 말을 쉽게 바꿔 말할 때 문장 앞에 쉼표와 함께. 상대의 숨은 뜻을 짚어 되물을 때 'In other words, no?'(그러니까 싫다는 거지?) 처럼도 씀. 글에서는 i.e. 와 비슷.

senses.meaningEn: during the part of the day between noon and evening

examples.en: We have music class in the afternoon.
Let's meet at three in the afternoon.

senses.note: 3 in the afternoon = 3 p.m. 특정 날의 오후는 on Sunday afternoon, '오늘 오후' 는 this afternoon(전치사 없음). early/late afternoon 으로 세분.

senses.meaningEn: finally, after everything else has happened or been considered

examples.en: In the end, we decided to stay home.
It was hard, but it worked out in the end.

senses.note: 많은 고민·일 끝의 "결국". at the end 는 "~의 끝에(장소·시간)": at the end of the street / at the end of May. 한국인이 둘을 자주 혼동함.

senses.meaningEn: during the part of the day between the end of afternoon and night

examples.en: My family eats together in the evening.
examples.ko: 우리 가족은 저녁에 함께 밥을 먹어.

examples.en: I like to read in the evening before bed.
examples.ko: 자기 전 저녁에 책 읽는 걸 좋아해.

senses.note: evening 은 대략 6시~잠들기 전까지, night 는 그보다 늦은 시간·잠자는 시간. 인사도 Good evening(저녁 인사) 과 Good night(헤어질 때·자러 갈 때) 으로 구별. '오늘 저녁' 은 this evening / tonight.

senses.meaningEn: in the central part of a place or thing

examples.en: There's a big tree in the middle of the park.
Don't stop in the middle of the road!

senses.note: in the middle of nowhere = 외딴 곳에(아무것도 없는 곳).

senses.meaningEn: busy doing something, or while something is happening

examples.en: Can I call you back? I'm in the middle of dinner.
examples.ko: 다시 전화해도 될까? 지금 저녁 먹는 중이야.

examples.en: He fell asleep in the middle of the movie.

senses.note: in the middle of + 명사/동명사: I'm in the middle of cooking. 전화 끊어야 할 때 쓰기 좋은 표현. in the middle of the night = 한밤중에.

senses.meaningEn: during the early part of the day, before noon

examples.en: I always drink coffee in the morning.
The shop opens at nine in the morning.

senses.note: 시간 뒤에 붙여 오전/오후를 표시: 9 in the morning = 9 a.m. 특정 요일의 아침은 on Monday morning(in 아님). '내일 아침' 은 tomorrow morning(전치사 없음).

senses.meaningEn: tomorrow morning, after you have slept

examples.en: Go to bed. We'll talk in the morning.
I'll call you in the morning, okay?

senses.note: 밤에 하는 대화에서 in the morning 은 보통 '다음 날 아침' 을 뜻함.

senses.meaningEn: early enough so that you are not late for something

examples.en: We got to the station just in time.
Will you be home in time for dinner?
examples.ko: 저녁 시간 맞춰서 집에 올 수 있어?

senses.note: in time = 늦지 않게(여유 있게 또는 간신히). on time = 정각에. "just in time" 은 아슬아슬하게 맞췄다는 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: after a period of time has passed; eventually

examples.en: Don't worry, you'll feel better in time.
examples.ko: 걱정 마, 시간이 지나면 괜찮아질 거야.

examples.en: In time, she learned to love the city.
examples.ko: 시간이 흐르면서 그녀는 그 도시를 사랑하게 됐어.

senses.meaningEn: a small animal with six legs and usually wings, such as a bee or an ant

examples.en: Ants and bees are insects.
Some insects can bite you.

senses.note: 일상 회화에서는 bug 를 더 자주 씀(insect 은 약간 교과서적). 거미는 다리가 여덟 개여서 insect 이 아님.

senses.meaningEn: in or into the inner part of something

examples.en: Your keys are inside the bag.
Please wait inside the house, it's cold.

senses.meaningEn: in or into a building or room

examples.en: It's raining. Let's go inside.
Is anyone inside? The door is open.
examples.ko: 안에 누구 있어요? 문이 열려 있는데.

senses.note: go inside 뒤에 to 를 쓰지 않음. inside of 는 구어에서만.

senses.meaningEn: wanting to know more about something or to do it

examples.en: I'm interested in learning Spanish.
Are you interested in going to the concert?

senses.note: interested in + 명사/동명사(to 부정사 아님). 사람은 interested, 흥미로운 것은 interesting. 권유에 Are you interested? 라고 물으면 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: holding your attention because it is unusual or exciting to think about

examples.en: This book is really interesting.
That's an interesting idea. Tell me more.

senses.note: interesting(사물이 흥미롭다) vs interested(사람이 흥미를 느끼다): I'm interesting. 은 '내가 흥미로운 사람' 이란 뜻이 됨 → I'm interested in it. 로. 웃긴 건 funny.

senses.meaningEn: moving to the inside of a place or thing

examples.en: Put the milk back into the fridge.
The kids ran into the house.

senses.note: in 은 '안에 있는 상태', into 는 '안으로 움직임'. go into, get into, jump into.

senses.meaningEn: used to show a change from one thing to another

examples.en: The water turned into ice overnight.
Can you translate this into Korean?
examples.ko: 이걸 한국어로 번역해 줄 수 있어?

senses.note: turn into(~로 변하다), change into, translate into, cut into pieces(조각으로 자르다).

senses.meaningEn: very interested in something

examples.en: I'm really into K-pop these days.
My dad is into fishing.

senses.note: be into + 명사/동명사. 구어체. 격식 글에서는 be interested in.

senses.meaningEn: to tell someone another person's name when they meet for the first time

examples.en: Let me introduce my friend Minho.
Can you introduce yourself to the class?
examples.ko: 반 친구들에게 자기소개 좀 해 줄래?

senses.note: introduce A to B(A 를 B 에게 소개). 자기소개 = introduce myself. 명사는 introduction. 발음 /ɪntrəˈduːs/ — 끝은 s 소리.

senses.meaningEn: to make or think of something completely new for the first time

examples.en: Who invented the telephone?
The light bulb was invented over 100 years ago.

senses.note: invent(없던 것을 만들다) vs discover(이미 있던 것을 찾아내다). 발명품 = invention, 발명가 = inventor.

senses.meaningEn: to make up a story or excuse that is not true

examples.en: He invented an excuse for being late.
Kids often invent stories about monsters.

senses.note: 회화에서는 make up an excuse 가 더 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: to ask someone to come to a party, meal, or event

examples.en: She invited me to her birthday party.
Let's invite the neighbors for dinner.

senses.note: invite 사람 to 장소/행사. 명사는 invitation(초대장). 'You're invited!' = 초대합니다. 구어에서 명사형 invite(/ˈɪnvaɪt/, 초대)도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: a piece of land with water all around it

examples.en: Jeju is the biggest island in Korea.
We took a boat to a small island.
examples.ko: 우리는 배를 타고 작은 섬에 갔어.

senses.note: s 는 발음하지 않음: /ˈaɪlənd/. 섬에 있다는 on the island (in ✗).

senses.meaningEn: a thing, animal, or idea that has already been mentioned

examples.en: Where is my phone? It was on the table.
examples.ko: 내 폰 어디 있지? 식탁 위에 있었는데.

examples.en: I like this bag. Can I try it?
examples.ko: 이 가방 마음에 들어요. 한번 들어 봐도 돼요?

senses.note: 주어·목적어 모두 it. 한국어로는 보통 번역하지 않고 생략하는 게 자연스러움. 아기·동물도 성별 모르면 it.

senses.meaningEn: used as the subject when talking about weather, time, or distance

examples.en: It is raining outside.
It is almost ten o'clock.

senses.note: 뜻은 없고 자리만 채우는 it. 한국어엔 없는 구조라 "Is raining" 처럼 주어를 빠뜨리기 쉬움. It is far / It is Monday 도 같은 패턴.

senses.meaningEn: said when you unexpectedly meet someone you know or find a surprising connection

examples.en: You know my cousin? Wow, it's a small world!
examples.ko: 내 사촌을 안다고? 와, 세상 참 좁네!

examples.en: We met in Paris by chance. It's a small world.
examples.ko: 우린 파리에서 우연히 만났어. 세상 정말 좁지.

senses.note: 뜻밖의 인연·우연한 만남에 감탄할 때. "What a small world!" 도 같은 뜻.

senses.meaningKo: 오늘은 되는 일이 없네, 운이 안 좋은 날이야
senses.meaningEn: said when several things go wrong for you on the same day

examples.en: I missed the bus and lost my keys. It's not my day.
examples.ko: 버스도 놓치고 열쇠도 잃어버렸어. 오늘 진짜 안 풀리네.

examples.en: Spilled coffee again? It's just not your day, huh?
examples.ko: 커피 또 쏟았어? 오늘 영 안 되는 날이구나?

senses.note: 주어에 맞춰 my/your/his 를 바꿈. 가볍게 투덜대는 말. 반대로 운 좋은 날은 "It's my lucky day."

senses.meaningEn: belonging to a thing, animal, or place already mentioned

examples.en: The dog wagged its tail.
The city is famous for its night markets.

senses.note: 아포스트로피 없는 its 가 소유. it's 는 it is / it has 의 줄임. 원어민도 자주 틀리는 철자: It's cold. / The cat licked its paw.

senses.meaningEn: a short coat worn over other clothes

examples.en: Take a jacket; it's cold outside.
He left his jacket on the chair.

senses.note: 무릎 아래까지 오는 긴 외투는 coat. 정장 상의도 jacket(suit jacket). 한국어 '점퍼'는 영어로 jacket 이 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: a sweet, soft food made by cooking fruit with sugar, spread on bread

examples.en: I like strawberry jam on my toast.
examples.ko: 나는 토스트에 딸기 잼 발라 먹는 걸 좋아해.

examples.en: We made apple jam at home last weekend.
examples.ko: 지난 주말에 집에서 사과 잼을 만들었어.

senses.note: 셀 수 없는 명사: a jar of jam(잼 한 병). 미국에서는 jelly 라고도 함(과육 없이 맑은 것). 오렌지 등 감귤류 잼은 marmalade.

senses.meaningEn: a situation where cars cannot move because the road is too full

examples.en: Sorry I'm late, there was a huge traffic jam.
We got stuck in a jam for an hour.
examples.ko: 한 시간 동안 차 막히는 데 갇혀 있었어.

senses.note: 거의 항상 traffic jam 으로 씀. be stuck in a traffic jam = 교통 체증에 갇히다. 기계가 걸려서 안 움직일 때도 jam(the printer is jammed).

senses.meaningEn: the first month of the year

examples.en: My birthday is in January.
It snows a lot here in January.

senses.note: 월 이름 앞에는 in 을 쓰고(in January), 날짜까지 말하면 on 을 쓴다(on January 5th). 줄여서 Jan. 로 쓴다. 월 이름은 항상 대문자.

senses.meaningEn: unhappy because someone has something you want

examples.en: I'm so jealous of your vacation photos!
examples.ko: 네 휴가 사진 보니까 진짜 부럽다!

examples.en: Don't be jealous. You'll get your turn.
examples.ko: 질투하지 마. 네 차례도 올 거야.

senses.note: be jealous of + 사람/것. 구어에서 "부럽다"는 뜻으로 가볍게 많이 씀(envious 보다 흔함). 한국어 "부럽다"에는 jealous 가 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: angry or upset because someone you love seems interested in another person

examples.en: He gets jealous when I talk to other guys.
examples.ko: 내가 다른 남자들과 얘기하면 그는 질투해.

examples.en: My girlfriend is a very jealous person.

senses.note: 연애의 질투는 jealous 만 가능(envious ✗). 명사는 jealousy.

senses.meaningEn: pants made of strong blue cotton cloth called denim

examples.en: She wears jeans almost every day.
I bought a new pair of jeans on sale.
examples.ko: 세일할 때 청바지 하나 새로 샀어.

senses.note: 항상 복수형. 한 벌은 a pair of jeans. 소재는 denim, 색이 아니어도 jeans 라고 부름(black jeans).

senses.meaningEn: the work you do regularly to earn money

examples.en: I got a new job at a bank.
What's your job? I'm a nurse.

senses.note: job 은 셀 수 있음(a job, two jobs), work 는 셀 수 없음. '구직 중'은 looking for a job. part-time job(아르바이트).

senses.meaningEn: a task or duty that someone has to do

examples.en: It's your job to feed the cat.
examples.ko: 고양이 밥 주는 건 네 담당이야.

examples.en: Painting the fence was a big job.

senses.note: 집안일을 나눌 때 It's your job to ~ 라고 자주 말함. '임무'라는 뜻에서는 task 와 비슷.

senses.meaningEn: used in phrases like good job to praise someone

examples.en: Good job! You finished all your homework.
Nice job on the test, Mia.

senses.note: Good job! / Nice job! / Great job! 은 아이·동료를 칭찬하는 가장 흔한 표현. Well done! 과 같은 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: the activity of running slowly for exercise

examples.en: I go jogging before breakfast.
examples.ko: 나는 아침 식사 전에 조깅을 해.

examples.en: Jogging is good for your heart.

senses.note: go jogging / go for a jog. 좀 더 빠르게 달리는 운동은 running 이라고 함. 미국 일상에서는 run 을 더 자주 씀(go for a run).

senses.meaningEn: to become a member of a group, club, or company

examples.en: I joined a tennis club last month.
When did you join the company?

senses.note: join 뒤에 바로 목적어(join the club). 'join in the club' 은 틀림. join the army = 입대하다.

senses.meaningEn: to come and do something together with someone

examples.en: Do you want to join us for dinner?
Can I join you? I'm alone today.

senses.note: '같이 할래?' = Want to join us? 혼자 앉은 사람 옆에 'Mind if I join you?' 도 자주 쓰는 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to take part in an activity that other people are already doing

examples.en: We're playing soccer. Do you want to join in?
Everyone joined in and sang the song together.

senses.note: join 은 '단체·모임에 가입하다'(join a club), join in 은 '이미 진행 중인 활동에 끼다'. 목적어 없이도 씀: Come and join in! join in the game / join in the fun.

senses.meaningEn: something you say or do to make people laugh

examples.en: Do you know any good jokes?
Relax, it was just a joke.

senses.note: tell a joke(농담하다) — say a joke 는 어색. make a joke 도 가능. 'I'm just kidding.' 도 같은 상황에서 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to say funny things that are not serious

examples.en: Don't worry, I'm only joking.
He likes to joke about his cooking.
examples.ko: 그는 자기 요리에 대해 농담하기를 좋아해.

senses.note: You must be joking! / You're joking! = '말도 안 돼, 진심이야?' 라는 놀람 표현.

senses.meaningEn: the act of traveling from one place to another, especially a long way

examples.en: It was a long journey from Seoul to Paris.
How long is the train journey?

senses.note: trip 보다 길고 힘든 이동이라는 느낌. 영국식에선 통근 같은 짧은 이동에도 journey 를 쓰지만 미국식은 trip 선호. 'Have a safe journey!' = 조심히 가. 인생 여정처럼 비유로도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: a feeling of great happiness

examples.en: The kids jumped for joy when they saw the snow.
examples.ko: 아이들은 눈을 보고 기뻐서 펄쩍 뛰었어.

examples.en: Her face was full of joy at the wedding.

senses.note: happiness 보다 강하고 조금 문어적인 느낌. jump for joy(기뻐 날뛰다), tears of joy(기쁨의 눈물). 사람이나 일을 가리켜 '즐거움의 원천'으로도 씀: She's a joy to teach.

senses.meaningEn: a drink made from the liquid of fruit or vegetables

examples.en: Can I get an orange juice, please?
The kids drink juice with breakfast.

senses.note: 주스 종류는 과일 이름을 앞에 붙임: orange juice, apple juice, grape juice. 음식점에서 한 잔을 셀 때는 an orange juice 처럼 셀 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: the liquid that comes out of fruit or meat

examples.en: Squeeze the juice out of the lemon.
This steak has so much juice in it.

senses.note: 형용사는 juicy(즙이 많은): a juicy peach, a juicy burger.

senses.meaningEn: the seventh month of the year

examples.en: It's really hot in July.
We're flying to Jeju in July.

senses.note: 강세가 두 번째 음절에 있다(ju-LY). 미국 독립기념일은 the Fourth of July. 줄임말 Jul.

senses.meaningEn: to push yourself up into the air using your legs

examples.en: The kids are jumping on the bed again.
Can you jump over that puddle?

senses.note: jump over(뛰어넘다), jump up(벌떡 일어나다), jump into the pool(풀에 뛰어들다). 한국어 '달리다'의 '뛰다'는 run — 혼동 주의.

senses.meaningEn: the act of pushing yourself into the air

examples.en: That was a really high jump!
He won the long jump at school.

senses.note: high jump(높이뛰기), long jump(멀리뛰기), ski jump(스키 점프) 처럼 종목명에 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: to enter water or a vehicle quickly by jumping

examples.en: The water looks great, jump in!
Jump in the car, we're late.

senses.note: jump in the car / the pool. get in 보다 더 급하고 활기찬 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: to start taking part in a conversation or activity quickly

examples.en: Feel free to jump in if you have a question.
Sorry to jump in, but I have an idea.

senses.note: jump in = 중간에 끼어들어 말하다/바로 시작하다. 회의에서도 자주 쓰임. jump right in = 바로 시작하자.

senses.meaningEn: to jump from one side of something to the other

examples.en: The horse jumped over the fence easily.
Can you jump over this puddle?

senses.note: jump over a fence / a wall / a puddle. 비슷한 jump across 는 "폭을 건너는" 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: a rope that you swing over your head and jump over as a game or exercise

examples.en: I got a new jump rope for gym class.
The girls are playing with a jump rope outside.

senses.note: 미국식 jump rope, 영국식 skipping rope. 운동으로서의 '줄넘기'도 jump rope: Jump rope is good exercise.

senses.meaningEn: to exercise or play by jumping over a rope you swing

examples.en: I jump rope for ten minutes every morning.
Can you jump rope a hundred times without stopping?
examples.ko: 안 멈추고 줄넘기 100번 할 수 있어?

senses.note: 동사로 쓸 때는 jump rope 그대로(He jumps rope). 영국식은 skip. '줄넘기 몇 번'은 ~ times 로 셈.

senses.meaningEn: to stand up very quickly and suddenly

examples.en: He jumped up when the phone rang.
She jumped up and hugged her friend.

senses.note: jump up from your seat / the sofa. 놀라거나 반가울 때 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to push yourself up into the air with your legs

examples.en: The dog jumped up to catch the ball.
Jump up and touch the ceiling if you can!
examples.ko: 할 수 있으면 뛰어서 천장을 만져 봐!

senses.note: jump up and down = 폴짝폴짝 뛰다(기뻐서). 개가 사람에게 뛰어오르는 것도 jump up (on someone).

senses.meaningEn: the sixth month of the year

examples.en: Summer vacation starts in June.
My parents' wedding was in June.

senses.note: 줄임말은 Jun. 미국 학교는 보통 6월에 학년이 끝나고 여름 방학이 시작된다. 발음은 '준'에 가깝게.

senses.meaningEn: a very short time ago

examples.en: I just got home.
She has just left the office.

senses.note: 미국식은 과거형(I just ate), 영국식은 현재완료(I've just eaten)를 선호. 둘 다 맞음.

senses.meaningEn: only; nothing more than

examples.en: I'm just looking, thanks.
It's just a small gift.

senses.note: 쇼핑할 때 점원에게 I'm just looking. 은 필수 표현. Just a moment. = 잠시만요. just kidding = 농담이야.

senses.meaningEn: exactly

examples.en: This shirt is just my size.
That's just what I wanted.

senses.note: just right = 딱 좋다, just in time = 딱 맞춰서. just like = ~와 똑같이.

senses.meaningEn: a large Australian animal that jumps on its strong back legs and carries its baby in a pocket on its front

examples.en: We saw kangaroos jumping in a field in Australia.
The baby kangaroo is sleeping in its mother's pouch.
examples.ko: 새끼 캥거루가 엄마 주머니 안에서 자고 있어.

senses.note: 강세는 마지막 음절(/-ˈruː/). 새끼 캥거루는 joey, 배 주머니는 pouch. 복수형은 kangaroos. 호주의 상징 동물.

senses.meaningEn: to continue to have something and not give it back or throw it away

examples.en: You can keep the change.
I keep my keys in this drawer.

senses.note: keep 은 '계속 가지고 있다'. 잠깐 쥐고 있는 건 hold.

senses.meaningEn: to continue doing something without stopping

examples.en: Keep going, you're almost there!
He kept talking during the whole movie.

senses.note: keep + -ing 형태. keep to do ✗. keep on -ing 도 같은 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: to make someone or something stay in a particular state or place

examples.en: Keep the door closed, please.
This jacket keeps me really warm.
examples.ko: 이 재킷은 정말 따뜻하게 해 줘.

senses.note: keep + 목적어 + 형용사: keep it clean, keep me warm. keep in touch = 연락하고 지내다.

senses.meaningEn: to write regularly in a diary about what happens in your life

examples.en: I've kept a diary since I was ten.
examples.ko: 열 살 때부터 일기를 써 왔어.

examples.en: Do you keep a diary in English?

senses.note: keep 은 '꾸준히 계속 쓴다'는 습관의 뜻. 오늘 하루 일기를 '쓴다'는 write in my diary. 미국에서는 diary 대신 journal 을 더 많이 쓴다(keep a journal).

senses.meaningEn: to not tell anyone about something secret

examples.en: Can you keep a secret? I'm moving to Seoul.
examples.ko: 비밀 지킬 수 있어? 나 서울로 이사 가.

examples.en: She kept my secret for years.
examples.ko: 그녀는 몇 년 동안 내 비밀을 지켜 줬어.

senses.note: 비밀을 '지키다'는 keep(protect 아님). 비밀을 '털어놓다'는 tell/share a secret. '비밀로 해 줘'는 Keep it a secret. / Keep it between us.

senses.meaningEn: to watch someone or something carefully so that nothing bad happens

examples.en: Can you keep an eye on the baby for a minute?
examples.ko: 잠깐 아기 좀 봐 줄 수 있어?

examples.en: Keep an eye on the soup so it doesn't boil over.

senses.note: keep an eye on + 사람/물건. 잠깐 맡기는 느낌이라 "봐 줘" 에 딱 맞음. 잘 지켜보는 것을 강조하면 keep a close eye on.

senses.meaningEn: to check something regularly to notice any changes

examples.en: I'm keeping an eye on the price of that laptop.
examples.ko: 그 노트북 가격을 계속 지켜보고 있어.

examples.en: Keep an eye on the weather before you leave.

senses.note: 사람뿐 아니라 가격·날씨·시간(keep an eye on the time) 에도 쓴다.

senses.meaningKo: 가까이 가지 않다, 멀리하다; 가까이 오지 못하게 하다
senses.meaningEn: to stay away from something or someone, or to stop them from coming near

examples.en: Keep away from the stove, it's hot!
Keep the kids away from the dog.

senses.note: keep away from + 대상 = 가까이 가지 않다. keep + 사람/물건 + away from = 가까이 못 오게 하다. 약 상자의 'Keep away from children' 이 대표 문구.

senses.meaningEn: to continue to talk to or write to someone you do not see often

examples.en: Let's keep in touch after you move.
I still keep in touch with my old teacher.
examples.ko: 나는 옛 선생님과 아직 연락하고 지내.

senses.note: 헤어질 때 인사로 "Keep in touch!" 하면 "연락해!". 연락이 끊기다 = lose touch. 연락하다(한 번) = get in touch with.

senses.meaningEn: to not walk or go on a particular area

examples.en: Keep off the grass, please.
Keep your feet off the sofa!

senses.note: 표지판 'Keep off the grass' 로 유명. keep + 물건 + off + 표면 = ~에 올리지 않다.

senses.meaningEn: to avoid eating, drinking, or talking about something

examples.en: The doctor told me to keep off sweets.
Let's keep off that topic tonight.

senses.note: keep off sugar / alcohol = 끊고 있다. 비슷한 give up 은 '완전히 끊다' 에 가까움.

senses.meaningEn: to continue doing something, often when it is difficult or annoying

examples.en: Keep on walking, the station is just ahead.
He kept on asking the same question.

senses.note: keep on + -ing. keep + -ing 와 뜻이 같고, on 이 붙으면 '꾸준히' 또는 '귀찮게 자꾸' 라는 느낌이 더해짐. keep on to do (X).

senses.meaningEn: to not enter a place, or to stop someone or something from entering

examples.en: The sign says 'Keep Out'.
Close the window to keep out the cold.
examples.ko: 찬 공기 못 들어오게 창문 닫아.

senses.note: Keep out! = 들어오지 마(출입 금지). keep + 대상 + out (of) = 못 들어오게 막다. keep out of trouble = 문제에 끼어들지 않다.

senses.meaningEn: to not make any noise or not speak

examples.en: Please keep quiet in the library.
The kids kept quiet during the movie.
examples.ko: 아이들이 영화 보는 동안 조용히 있었어.

senses.note: keep + 형용사 = 어떤 상태를 계속 유지하다(keep warm, keep calm). Be quiet! 는 '조용히 해!' 명령, keep quiet 은 '계속 조용히 있어'. keep quiet about ~ 는 '~에 대해 말하지 않다'.

senses.meaningEn: to not tell other people about something

examples.en: Keep quiet about the party. It's a surprise.
examples.ko: 파티 얘기는 하지 마. 깜짝 파티거든.

examples.en: He kept quiet about his new job.
examples.ko: 그는 새 직장에 대해 아무 말도 안 했어.

senses.note: keep quiet about + 명사. keep a secret 과 비슷하지만 '아무 말 하지 않는다'는 쪽에 초점.

senses.meaningEn: to move or progress at the same speed as someone else

examples.en: Slow down! I can't keep up.
He walks so fast that nobody can keep up.
examples.ko: 그는 너무 빨리 걸어서 아무도 못 따라가.

senses.note: keep up = 뒤처지지 않고 유지하다, catch up = 뒤처진 걸 따라잡다. 대상을 밝힐 땐 keep up with.

senses.meaningEn: to continue doing something at the same good level

examples.en: Keep up the good work!
If you keep up your practice, you'll get better.
examples.ko: 연습을 계속하면 더 잘하게 될 거야.

senses.note: Keep it up! / Keep up the good work! 는 칭찬·격려의 고정 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to stay at the same level or speed as someone or something

examples.en: I can't keep up with the other students in math.
It's hard to keep up with my little brother.

senses.note: keep up with + 사람/속도/수업. keep up with the Joneses = 남들 사는 것에 뒤지지 않으려 하다(관용구).

senses.meaningEn: to continue to learn about something that changes often

examples.en: I try to keep up with the news every morning.
examples.ko: 매일 아침 뉴스를 챙겨 보려고 해.

examples.en: It's hard to keep up with all the new apps.
examples.ko: 새로 나오는 앱을 다 따라가기 힘들어.

senses.note: keep up with the news / trends / fashion. 소식이 자주 바뀌는 대상에 씀.

senses.meaningEn: a small piece of metal that you use to open or lock a door

examples.en: I can't find my keys anywhere!
Here's the key to the front door.

senses.note: '~의 열쇠'는 the key to the door(of ✗). car keys, house keys 처럼 복수로 자주 말함.

senses.meaningEn: one of the buttons you press on a keyboard or a piano

examples.en: Press the Enter key to continue.
Some keys on my laptop don't work.
examples.ko: 내 노트북 키 몇 개가 안 먹어.

senses.note: 키보드 = keyboard. 피아노 건반도 key.

senses.meaningEn: very important

examples.en: Practice is the key to speaking English well.
Sleep is a key part of staying healthy.

senses.note: the key to success = 성공의 비결. 명사 앞에서 key point, key word 처럼 형용사로도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to hit something with your foot

examples.en: Kick the ball to me, please!
He kicked the door open with his foot.

senses.note: kick the ball(공을 차다), kick a goal(골을 넣다). '발로 차지 마'는 Don't kick! 한 단어로 충분.

senses.meaningEn: a hit made with the foot

examples.en: That was a great kick, Tom!
She gave the ball a hard kick.

senses.note: give something a kick = ~을 (한 번) 차다. 축구의 free kick(프리킥), penalty kick(페널티킥)으로도 익숙한 단어.

senses.meaningEn: to start a football or soccer game by kicking the ball

examples.en: The game kicks off at seven tonight.
Who kicked off in the second half?

senses.note: 축구에서 온 표현. 명사 kickoff(킥오프, 시작) 로도 씀: The kickoff is at 7.

senses.meaningEn: to begin an event, a meeting, or an activity

examples.en: Let's kick off the meeting with some good news.
The festival kicks off this Friday.

senses.note: start 보다 활기찬 느낌. 회의·행사·캠페인 등에 쓰고 격식 문서에서는 begin/launch.

senses.meaningEn: to take off your shoes quickly by moving your feet

examples.en: She kicked off her shoes and lay on the sofa.
examples.ko: 그녀는 신발을 벗어 던지고 소파에 누웠어.

examples.en: Kick off your boots before you come in.

senses.note: kick off one's shoes = 피곤해서 신발을 훌훌 벗는 그림. 반대로 '발로 차서 쫓아내다'는 kick out.

senses.meaningEn: to force someone to leave a place

examples.en: They kicked us out of the bar at midnight.
If you keep shouting, I'll kick you out.

senses.note: kick someone out of + 장소. 구어체. 격식은 remove / ask someone to leave.

senses.meaningEn: to make someone leave a school, a team, or a group because of bad behavior

examples.en: He got kicked out of school for fighting.
Two players were kicked out of the team.

senses.note: get kicked out of ~ = ~에서 쫓겨나다(수동). 학교라면 격식어 expel, 집이라면 evict.

senses.meaningEn: an informal word for a child or young person

examples.en: There are a lot of kids at the park today.
When I was a kid, I loved cartoons.
examples.ko: 어릴 때 나는 만화를 정말 좋아했어.

senses.note: 일상 대화에서 child 보다 훨씬 자주 씀. 글이나 격식 상황에서는 child.

senses.meaningEn: someone's son or daughter

examples.en: How are your kids doing?
My kids are both in high school.

senses.note: the kids = 우리 아이들. 어른이 된 자식에게도 쓸 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: to say something as a joke, not seriously

examples.en: I'm just kidding, don't be upset.
Are you kidding me? That's amazing!

senses.note: Just kidding! = 농담이야. You're kidding! / No kidding? = 설마! / 진짜?

senses.meaningEn: to make a person, animal, or plant die

examples.en: Don't kill the spider, just put it outside.
examples.ko: 거미 죽이지 말고 그냥 밖에 내보내.

examples.en: The cold killed all my tomato plants.

senses.note: be killed in an accident = 사고로 죽다(뉴스 표현). 명사 killer. 사람 외에 식물·시간·분위기(kill the mood)에도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to spend time doing something unimportant while you wait

examples.en: We killed time at a café before the movie.
examples.ko: 영화 보기 전에 카페에서 시간을 때웠어.

examples.en: I played games to kill an hour at the airport.

senses.note: kill time / kill an hour. 비슷한 표현 pass the time.

senses.meaningEn: to cause someone a lot of pain

examples.en: My feet are killing me after that long walk.
This headache is killing me.

senses.note: My back/feet/head is killing me. 진행형으로만 씀. '죽겠어' 과장 표현.

senses.meaningEn: friendly and caring about other people

examples.en: Thank you, that's very kind of you.
My teacher is kind to everyone.

senses.note: be kind to + 사람.

senses.meaningEn: a type or group of things

examples.en: What kind of music do you like?
They sell all kinds of cheese here.

senses.meaningEn: a little, somewhat

examples.en: I'm kind of tired today.
This soup is kind of salty.

senses.note: 구어에서 kinda 로 줄여 말함. 글에서는 피함.

senses.meaningEn: slightly; in some way, but not completely

examples.en: I'm kind of hungry. Let's eat.
The movie was kind of boring.

senses.note: 형용사·동사 앞에서 말을 부드럽게 하는 구어 표현. 말할 때 kinda 로 줄여 발음. 글에서는 피하고 a little / somewhat 을 쓸 것. "a kind of + 명사" 는 "일종의 ~" 라는 다른 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: used as an answer to say "yes, partly"

examples.en: Are you tired? Kind of.
Do you like him? Kind of, I guess.

senses.note: Yes 도 No 도 아닌 애매한 대답. 확답을 피할 때 유용.

senses.meaningEn: a man who rules a country, usually because his father or mother ruled before him

examples.en: The king lived in a big castle.
King Sejong made the Korean alphabet.

senses.note: 이름 앞에서는 King Sejong 처럼 대문자. 여왕은 queen, 왕국은 kingdom, '왕의'는 royal.

senses.meaningEn: the most important piece in chess, or the card with the letter K

examples.en: If you take my king, you win the game.
examples.ko: 내 킹을 잡으면 네가 이기는 거야.

examples.en: I have two kings and a queen.
examples.ko: 나한테 킹 두 장하고 퀸 한 장 있어.

senses.note: 체스에서는 king 을 잡히면 패배(checkmate). 카드에서 K 로 표시.

senses.meaningEn: to touch someone with your lips to show love

examples.en: He kissed the baby on the forehead.
They kissed goodbye at the door.
examples.ko: 둘은 문 앞에서 작별 키스를 했어.

senses.note: kiss someone on the + 신체 부위. 명사도 가능: give me a kiss / blow a kiss(손 키스를 보내다).

senses.meaningEn: the room in a house where you cook food

examples.en: Mom is in the kitchen making dinner.
Our kitchen is small but very clean.
examples.ko: 우리 집 부엌은 작지만 아주 깨끗해.

senses.note: in the kitchen (전치사 in). kitchen table, kitchen sink 처럼 명사 앞에도 자주 옴.

senses.meaningEn: a light frame covered with paper or cloth that you fly in the wind on a long string

examples.en: We flew a kite at the park on Sunday.
My kite got stuck in a tree.

senses.note: fly a kite = 연을 날리다. 동사는 fly(불규칙: flew). 한국의 연날리기 전통을 설명할 때 kite flying 이라고 함.

senses.meaningEn: a young cat

examples.en: Look at this tiny kitten!
examples.ko: 이 조그만 새끼 고양이 좀 봐!

examples.en: The kitten is playing with a ball of yarn.
examples.ko: 새끼 고양이가 털실 뭉치를 갖고 놀고 있어.

senses.note: 줄여서 kitty 라고도 하고, 아이들은 다 큰 고양이도 kitty 라고 부름. puppy(강아지)와 짝으로 익힐 것.

senses.meaningEn: a small fruit with brown fuzzy skin and green flesh

examples.en: I eat a kiwi every morning.
examples.ko: 나는 매일 아침 키위를 하나 먹어.

examples.en: Kiwis have a lot of vitamin C.

senses.note: kiwi fruit 라고도 함. 뉴질랜드 사람을 Kiwi 라고 부르기도 함.

senses.meaningEn: the joint in the middle of your leg where it bends

examples.en: I fell and hurt my knee.
Bend your knees a little when you lift it.

senses.note: k 는 발음하지 않음(/niː/). 무릎을 꿇다 = kneel.

senses.meaningEn: a tool with a sharp blade and a handle, used for cutting

examples.en: This knife is not sharp enough.
Please put the knives and forks on the table.

senses.note: k 는 묵음 /naɪf/. 복수는 knives(f→v). 요리용 큰 칼은 kitchen knife.

senses.meaningEn: to hit a door with your hand to get attention

examples.en: Someone is knocking on the door.
Please knock before you come in.

senses.note: knock on the door (at 도 가능). 한국어 "노크하다"는 knock 만 쓰면 됨 (do a knock X).

senses.meaningEn: to hit something so that it falls or moves

examples.en: I knocked the cup off the table.
The wind knocked over the chair.

senses.note: knock over(넘어뜨리다), knock off(쳐서 떨어뜨리다), knock down(쳐서 쓰러뜨리다/건물을 철거하다).

senses.meaningEn: the sound of someone hitting a door

examples.en: I heard a knock at the door.
There was a loud knock late at night.
examples.ko: 밤늦게 문을 크게 두드리는 소리가 났어.

senses.note: a knock at/on the door. Knock knock! = 똑똑!

senses.meaningEn: to hit a person so that they fall to the ground

examples.en: A cyclist knocked the old man down.
examples.ko: 자전거 탄 사람이 그 노인을 쳐서 넘어뜨렸어.

examples.en: She was knocked down by a car but she's okay.

senses.note: be knocked down by a car = 차에 치이다(주로 영국). 미국은 hit by a car 가 더 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: to destroy a building or wall so it falls down

examples.en: They knocked down the old school last year.
We want to knock this wall down to make the room bigger.
examples.ko: 방을 넓히려고 이 벽을 허물고 싶어.

senses.note: tear down 과 거의 같음. 목적어는 중간·뒤 모두 가능.

senses.meaningEn: to make a price lower

examples.en: They knocked the price down to fifty dollars.
Can you knock down the price a little?
examples.ko: 가격 조금만 깎아 줄 수 있어요?

senses.note: knock 10 dollars off 도 같은 뜻. 흥정할 때 쓰는 구어.

senses.meaningEn: to hit someone so hard that they become unconscious

examples.en: The boxer knocked out his opponent in round two.
examples.ko: 그 권투 선수는 2라운드에 상대를 KO 시켰어.

examples.en: The ball hit his head and knocked him out.

senses.note: 명사형 a knockout(KO). 약·피로가 사람을 '쓰러져 자게 만들다' 도 knock out: The medicine knocked me out.

senses.meaningEn: to defeat a team or player so that they leave a competition

examples.en: Our team was knocked out in the first round.
They knocked out the champions last night.

senses.note: get knocked out of the tournament. 토너먼트 방식 경기에서 특히.

senses.meaningEn: to make a machine or power supply stop working

examples.en: The storm knocked out the power all night.
Lightning knocked out our internet.

senses.note: 주어가 폭풍·사고 등 자연 현상인 경우가 많음.

senses.meaningEn: to hit something by accident so that it falls over

examples.en: Oops, I knocked over my coffee!
The cat knocked the vase over again.

senses.note: 실수로 치는 것이 핵심. knock down 은 사람·건물, knock over 는 컵·병·의자 같은 물건에 자주.

senses.meaningEn: to hit a person with a vehicle so that they fall

examples.en: He was almost knocked over by a bike.
Be careful, that truck nearly knocked you over!
examples.ko: 조심해, 저 트럭이 널 칠 뻔했어!

senses.note: 이 뜻은 knock down 과 거의 같음. 영국에서 더 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: to have information or facts in your mind

examples.en: Do you know what time it is?
I didn't know the store closed so early.
examples.ko: 가게가 그렇게 일찍 닫는 줄 몰랐어.

senses.note: I know. = 알아, 그렇지. I don't know. = 모르겠어. k 는 묵음, no 와 발음이 같음. 진행형(I'm knowing ✗)으로 쓰지 않음.

senses.meaningEn: to be familiar with a person or place

examples.en: I've known her since high school.
Do you know this neighborhood well?

senses.note: get to know someone = ~와 알게 되다. '처음 알게 되다'는 meet(I knew him yesterday ✗ → I met him yesterday).

senses.meaningEn: to have learned a skill, language, or how to do something

examples.en: Do you know how to swim?
She knows a little Spanish.

senses.note: know how to + 동사 = ~하는 법을 알다. know by heart = 외우고 있다.

senses.meaningEn: to have information about a subject or event

examples.en: Do you know about the party on Friday?
I didn't know about the test until today.

senses.note: know + 사람/사실 = 직접 알다(I know him). know about = 그에 관한 정보를 알다(I know about him = 그 사람 얘기는 들어서 알아). know of = 존재만 들어서 알다.

senses.meaningEn: to have knowledge about a subject

examples.en: My uncle knows a lot about cars.
examples.ko: 우리 삼촌은 자동차에 대해 아주 잘 알아.

examples.en: How much do you know about Korean food?

senses.note: know a lot / a little / nothing about ~ 으로 정도를 표현. 'I don't know about that.' = 글쎄, 그건 잘 모르겠네(가벼운 반대).

senses.meaningEn: a polite word for a woman

examples.en: The lady at the counter was very kind.
An old lady asked me for help.
examples.ko: 할머니 한 분이 나에게 도움을 청하셨어.

senses.note: 복수는 ladies. 아는 여성을 가리킬 때는 이름을, 모르면 that lady(그 여자분). that woman 은 조금 딱딱하게 들릴 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: used for things that are for women, or a women's restroom

examples.en: Where is the ladies' room, please?
The ladies' shoes are on the second floor.

senses.note: the ladies = 여자 화장실(the ladies' room). 남자 화장실은 the men's room.

senses.meaningEn: a large area of water with land all around it

examples.en: We went swimming in the lake.
The lake is frozen in winter.

senses.note: 호수 이름은 Lake Michigan 처럼 Lake 가 앞에 옴(강과 반대). 작은 연못은 pond.

senses.meaningEn: a light that you can move, usually with a shade over the bulb

examples.en: Turn on the lamp. It's getting dark.
There's a small lamp next to my bed.
examples.ko: 내 침대 옆에 작은 램프가 있어.

senses.note: 한국의 '스탠드'는 영어로 desk lamp / floor lamp(stand 라고 하지 않음). 천장 등은 ceiling light, 가로등은 street light/lamp.

senses.meaningEn: the part of the earth that is not covered by water, or an area of ground

examples.en: After two days at sea, we finally saw land.
examples.ko: 바다에서 이틀을 보낸 뒤 드디어 육지가 보였어.

examples.en: My uncle bought some land to build a house.
examples.ko: 우리 삼촌은 집을 지으려고 땅을 좀 샀어.

senses.note: 불가산명사(a land ✗, some land ○). by land = 육로로, on land = 육지에서.

senses.meaningEn: to come down onto the ground, especially from the air

examples.en: Our plane lands in Tokyo at noon.
The bird landed on my window.

senses.note: 이륙은 take off. 착륙 = landing.

senses.meaningEn: a small computer that you can carry and use on your lap

examples.en: I take my laptop to the café to work.
My laptop battery dies really fast.
examples.ko: 내 노트북 배터리가 너무 빨리 닳아.

senses.note: 한국어 '노트북'은 영어로 laptop. 영어의 notebook 은 필기용 노트를 뜻함.

senses.meaningEn: big in size or amount

examples.en: They have a large garden behind the house.
examples.ko: 그 집 뒤에는 넓은 정원이 있어.

examples.en: A large number of people came to the show.

senses.note: big 보다 약간 격식 있는 느낌. 사람 몸집에는 big 을 더 많이 쓰고, large 는 '뚱뚱하다'를 돌려 말하는 느낌이 날 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: the biggest of the standard sizes of clothes or drinks

examples.en: Can I get a large fries with that?
The large is a little too big for me.

senses.note: 음료·음식 사이즈는 small / medium / large. 옷은 L, 그 위는 XL(extra large).

senses.meaningEn: coming after all the others

examples.en: This is the last question on the test.
I was the last person to leave.

senses.meaningEn: the most recent one before now

examples.en: I saw that movie last week.
What did you do last weekend?

senses.note: last week / last night 앞에는 전치사를 쓰지 않음. in last week (X).

senses.meaningEn: to continue for a period of time

examples.en: The movie lasts about two hours.
examples.ko: 그 영화는 두 시간 정도 돼.

examples.en: How long does the battery last?

senses.meaningEn: the name you share with your family, which comes after your first name in English

examples.en: Please spell your last name for me.
Kim is the most common last name in Korea.

senses.note: last name = family name = surname(영국에서 많이 씀). 영어에선 성이 '마지막'에 오기 때문에 last name. 격식 호칭은 Mr./Ms. + last name(Mr. Kim), first name 과 섞어 Mr. Jiho 라고 하면 어색.

senses.meaningEn: arriving or happening after the expected time

examples.en: Sorry I'm late. The bus was slow.
Don't be late for school tomorrow.

senses.note: be late for + 행사/장소(late for class). 비교급 later(나중에)는 부사로 See you later. 와 같이 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: near the end of a day or a period of time

examples.en: It's late. Let's go home.
I went to bed late last night.

senses.note: late at night = 밤늦게, in the late afternoon = 오후 늦게. 여기서는 부사로도 쓰임(work late = 늦게까지 일하다). lately 는 '최근에'로 뜻이 전혀 다름.

senses.meaningEn: at a time after now or after the time you are talking about

examples.en: I'll call you back later.
See you later!

senses.note: later on = 나중에(조금 더 구어적). 시간 길이 뒤에 붙여 '~후에' 를 만든다: two hours later(두 시간 뒤), a week later. 과거 이야기에서는 after 가 아니라 later 를 쓴다는 점이 한국인에게 헷갈림.

senses.meaningEn: coming after something else in time

examples.en: Can we take a later bus?
examples.ko: 더 늦은 버스를 타면 안 될까?

examples.en: We'll talk about that in a later lesson.

senses.note: late 의 비교급. 반대는 earlier. latter(후자)와 철자 혼동 주의.

senses.meaningEn: to make sounds with your voice because something is funny

examples.en: We laughed so hard at his joke.
examples.ko: 그의 농담에 우리는 정말 많이 웃었어.

examples.en: Don't laugh at me, I'm serious.
examples.ko: 나 비웃지 마, 진지하게 말하는 거야.

senses.note: 발음은 [래프], gh 가 f 소리. laugh at someone 은 '비웃다'로 들릴 수 있으니 주의. 함께 웃는 것은 laugh with.

senses.meaningEn: the sound or act of laughing

examples.en: He has a really loud laugh.
We had a good laugh about it later.

senses.note: have a good laugh = 한바탕 웃다. for a laugh = 재미로.

senses.meaningEn: to laugh because something is funny

examples.en: Everyone laughed at his joke.
We laughed at the funny cat video.
examples.ko: 우리는 웃긴 고양이 영상을 보고 웃었어.

senses.note: laugh 는 자동사라서 목적어 앞에 at 이 꼭 필요함: laugh at the joke (not 'laugh the joke').

senses.meaningEn: to make fun of someone in an unkind way

examples.en: Don't laugh at me. I'm trying my best.
examples.ko: 나 비웃지 마. 최선을 다하고 있어.

examples.en: The kids laughed at his old shoes.
examples.ko: 아이들이 그의 낡은 신발을 보고 비웃었어.

senses.note: 사람이 목적어면 대개 부정적(비웃다). '함께 웃다' 는 laugh with: We laughed with him, not at him.

senses.meaningEn: a person whose job is to help people with the law

examples.en: You should talk to a lawyer about this.
My cousin is a lawyer in New York.

senses.note: law(법) + -yer. 미국에서는 attorney 도 흔함. 발음은 '로이어'에 가깝고 w 는 소리 나지 않음.

senses.meaningEn: not wanting to work or make an effort

examples.en: Don't be lazy. Clean your room!
examples.ko: 게으름 부리지 마. 방 좀 치워!

examples.en: My cat is so lazy. It sleeps all day.
examples.ko: 우리 고양이는 정말 게을러. 하루 종일 자.

senses.note: 사람을 직접 lazy 라고 하면 꽤 무례함. 자신에 대해 I'm feeling lazy today 는 가볍게 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: (of a time) relaxed, with nothing much to do

examples.en: We had a lazy Sunday at home.
I love lazy mornings with coffee.

senses.note: a lazy afternoon/weekend 는 긍정적인 뜻(여유로운). 사람에 대한 lazy 와 다르게 비난이 아님.

senses.meaningEn: to take someone somewhere by going in front of them

examples.en: The guide led us through the old town.
Lead the way, I'll follow you.

senses.note: lead the way = 앞장서다. 과거형 led(lead 라고 쓰면 금속 '납' /led/ 과 혼동).

senses.meaningEn: to be in charge of a group or activity

examples.en: She leads the school music club.
Who's going to lead the meeting today?

senses.note: leader = 리더, leadership = 지도력. lead a team / a class / a discussion.

senses.meaningEn: if a road or door leads somewhere, it goes there

examples.en: This road leads to the beach.
The stairs lead down to the basement.

senses.note: lead to + 장소. 중급에서는 lead to + 결과(~로 이어지다, 초래하다)로 확장.

senses.meaningEn: to be winning in a game or race

examples.en: Our team is leading by two goals.
examples.ko: 우리 팀이 두 골 차로 앞서고 있어.

examples.en: She led the race from start to finish.

senses.note: be in the lead / take the lead = 선두에 있다/선두로 나서다.

senses.meaningEn: one of the flat green parts that grow on a plant or tree

examples.en: A yellow leaf fell on my head.
examples.ko: 노란 나뭇잎 하나가 내 머리에 떨어졌어.

examples.en: The leaves turn red in October.

senses.note: 복수형은 leafs 가 아니라 leaves. 가을 단풍은 fall leaves / autumn leaves.

senses.meaningEn: to get knowledge or a skill by studying or practicing

examples.en: I'm learning English with an app.
My daughter learned to swim last summer.

senses.note: learn to + 동사 / learn how to + 동사. study 는 공부하는 과정, learn 은 익혀서 알게 되는 결과. 과거형은 learned(미) / learnt(영).

senses.meaningEn: to find out about something

examples.en: I just learned that she is moving away.
examples.ko: 그녀가 이사 간다는 걸 방금 알았어.

examples.en: We learned about the party from a friend.

senses.note: learn that... / learn about... = ~을 알게 되다.

senses.meaningEn: to memorize something so you can remember it

examples.en: We have to learn ten new words a day.
examples.ko: 하루에 새 단어 열 개를 외워야 해.

examples.en: Did you learn your lines for the play?

senses.note: learn something by heart = 완전히 외우다.

senses.meaningEn: to get knowledge or information about a subject

examples.en: We learned about dinosaurs in science class.
I want to learn about Korean history.

senses.note: learn + 기술/과목 = 익히다(learn English, learn to swim). learn about + 주제 = 그 주제에 관한 지식을 얻다. 소식을 '알게 되다' 뜻도: I learned about the accident on the news.

senses.meaningEn: to go away from a place

examples.en: What time does the train leave?
I'm leaving the office now. See you soon.

senses.note: leave for + 목적지: leave for Busan = 부산으로 떠나다.

senses.meaningEn: to let something stay in a place, or forget to take it

examples.en: Oh no, I think I'm leaving my keys at home again.
examples.ko: 이런, 또 열쇠를 집에 두고 가는 것 같아.

examples.en: Just leave the dishes. I'll do them later.
examples.ko: 설거지는 그냥 둬. 내가 나중에 할게.

senses.note: Leave me alone. = 나 좀 내버려 둬.

senses.meaningEn: to give a message for someone who is not there

examples.en: Would you like to leave a message?
Please leave your name and number.

senses.meaningEn: to forget or not take something with you when you go

examples.en: I left my umbrella behind on the bus.
Make sure you don't leave anything behind.
examples.ko: 두고 가는 물건 없는지 꼭 확인해.

senses.note: 목적어는 보통 leave 와 behind 사이: leave my bag behind. 한국어 '놓고 오다' 와 가장 가까운 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to go away and not take a person with you

examples.en: Don't leave me behind! Wait for me.
He left his family behind to work in the city.
examples.ko: 그는 가족을 두고 도시로 일하러 떠났어.

senses.note: get left behind 는 '뒤처지다'(공부·발전) 뜻으로도 씀: Some students get left behind.

senses.meaningEn: to not include something or someone

examples.en: You left out a word in this sentence.
Don't leave out the sugar, or it won't taste right.
examples.ko: 설탕 빼먹지 마, 안 그러면 맛이 안 나.

senses.note: 목적어는 중간이나 뒤 모두 가능: leave it out / leave out the sugar. 대명사는 반드시 중간.

senses.meaningEn: to not let someone join a group or activity

examples.en: I felt left out at the party.
Don't leave your little brother out of the game.

senses.note: feel left out = 소외감을 느끼다. 매우 자주 쓰는 표현. leave someone out of something.

senses.meaningEn: the plural form of leaf: the flat green parts of a plant

examples.en: The leaves are falling from the trees.
We raked the leaves in the yard.

senses.note: leaf → leaves 처럼 -f 로 끝나는 명사는 복수에서 -ves 가 됨(knife → knives, wolf → wolves).

senses.meaningEn: the he/she/it form of the verb leave: to go away from a place

examples.en: The bus leaves at eight.
She leaves for work very early.

senses.note: 철자가 똑같지만 뜻이 다름. 문장에서 주어 뒤 동사 자리에 오면 leave 의 변화형.

senses.meaningEn: on the side of your body where your heart is

examples.en: I hurt my left hand.
The bank is on the left side of the street.

senses.note: left-handed = 왼손잡이.

senses.meaningEn: toward the left side

examples.en: Turn left at the corner.
Go left and you'll see the bus stop.
examples.ko: 왼쪽으로 가면 버스 정류장이 보일 거야.

senses.note: turn left(좌회전하다). 명사로도 쓰임: on the left(왼쪽에), on your left(당신 왼편에). 'Take a left.' 도 가능.

senses.meaningEn: still there after everything else is used or gone

examples.en: There's only one cookie left.
How much time do we have left?

senses.note: leave(남기다)의 과거분사가 형용사처럼 쓰인 것. 항상 명사 뒤에 옴(one cookie left). leftovers = 남은 음식.

senses.meaningEn: one of the long parts of your body that you stand and walk on

examples.en: He broke his leg playing soccer.
My legs are tired after the long walk.

senses.note: 한국어 '다리'는 leg, 발은 foot. 다리 전체를 feet 라고 하지 않도록 주의. 가구의 다리도 leg(a table leg).

senses.meaningEn: a yellow fruit with a very sour taste

examples.en: Can I get some lemon with my tea?
examples.ko: 차에 레몬 좀 넣어 주실 수 있나요?

examples.en: Squeeze a lemon over the fish.

senses.note: lemonade(레모네이드)는 레몬으로 만든 음료. 발음은 '레몬'이 아니라 /ˈlemən/.

senses.meaningEn: to give something to someone for a short time, expecting it back

examples.en: Could you lend me ten dollars until Friday?
I lent him my umbrella and he never returned it.

senses.note: lend - lent - lent. lend 사람 물건 / lend 물건 to 사람. '빌려줄래?'를 borrow 로 말하는 실수가 많음 — 내가 내주는 쪽이면 lend. 'Lend me a hand.' = 도와줘.

senses.meaningEn: a period of teaching, or one part of a textbook

examples.en: Today's lesson is about the weather.
Open your book to Lesson Five.

senses.note: class 는 '수업 시간·학급', lesson 은 '수업 내용·단원'에 초점. 영국에서는 수업 자체도 lesson 이라 함.

senses.meaningEn: a time when someone teaches you a skill like music or sport

examples.en: I take piano lessons on Saturdays.
My dad is giving me driving lessons.
examples.ko: 아빠가 나한테 운전을 가르쳐 주고 있어.

senses.note: take lessons(받다) / give lessons(해 주다). 한국어 '레슨'과 쓰임이 거의 같음.

senses.meaningEn: to allow someone to do something

examples.en: My mom let me stay up late last night.
examples.ko: 어젯밤에 엄마가 늦게까지 안 자도 된다고 하셨어.

examples.en: Let me help you with those bags.

senses.note: let + 사람 + 동사원형. let me to go ✗. 과거형도 let. Let me know = 알려 줘(아주 자주 씀).

senses.meaningEn: used with 's to suggest doing something together

examples.en: Let's eat out tonight.
Let's not be late again, okay?

senses.note: Let's = Let us. 부정은 Let's not ~. 대답은 Sure. / Sounds good. / Okay, let's.

senses.meaningEn: to disappoint someone by not doing what they expected

examples.en: I promise I won't let you down.
He let his team down by coming late.

senses.note: 목적어는 let 과 down 사이: let me down (O), let down me (X). 명사형 a letdown = 실망스러운 일.

senses.meaningEn: to move something down to a lower position

examples.en: She let her hair down after work.
examples.ko: 그녀는 퇴근 후 머리를 풀어 내렸어.

examples.en: Let the blinds down, the sun is too bright.
examples.ko: 블라인드 내려 줘, 햇빛이 너무 세.

senses.note: let your hair down 은 '머리를 풀다' 외에 '긴장을 풀고 즐기다' 라는 관용 표현으로도 자주 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: to stop holding something or someone

examples.en: Don't let go of my hand in the crowd.
examples.ko: 사람 많은 데서 내 손 놓지 마.

examples.en: Hold on tight and don't let go!

senses.note: 목적어 없이 쓰면 let go, 목적어가 있으면 let go of + 명사. let it go = 그냥 잊어 버려/신경 쓰지 마.

senses.meaningEn: to make someone leave their job, said in a soft way

examples.en: The company let twenty workers go last month.
examples.ko: 회사는 지난달에 직원 스무 명을 해고했어.

examples.en: They had to let him go after the mistake.
examples.ko: 그 실수 뒤에 그를 내보내야 했어.

senses.note: fire 보다 부드러운 표현. 목적어는 let 과 go 사이: let him go.

senses.meaningEn: to stop worrying or thinking about something that upset you

examples.en: It happened years ago. Just let it go.
examples.ko: 몇 년 전 일이잖아. 그냥 잊어.

examples.en: I can't let go of what she said.
examples.ko: 그녀가 한 말을 떨쳐 낼 수가 없어.

senses.note: let it go 는 '그냥 넘어가' 라는 뜻으로 매우 자주 쓰는 구어 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to stop holding something with your hands

examples.en: Let go of the rope when I say so.
The baby wouldn't let go of my finger.
examples.ko: 아기가 내 손가락을 놓으려 하지 않았어.

senses.note: let go 와 달리 항상 of + 목적어 를 붙임. let go of my hand (O), let go my hand (X).

senses.meaningEn: to stop feeling angry or sad about something and move on

examples.en: You need to let go of the past.
It's hard to let go of old friends.

senses.note: 물건뿐 아니라 anger, fear, the past 같은 추상 명사와도 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to allow a person or animal to enter a place

examples.en: Can you let me in? I forgot my key.
examples.ko: 문 좀 열어 줄래? 열쇠를 깜빡했어.

examples.en: Don't let the dog in with wet feet.
examples.ko: 젖은 발로 개를 안에 들이지 마.

senses.note: 목적어는 보통 let 과 in 사이에: let me in, let the cat in. 소리·빛이 들어오는 것에도: let some light in.

senses.meaningKo: (let someone in on) ~에게 비밀을 알려 주다
senses.meaningEn: to tell someone a secret or something private

examples.en: I'll let you in on a secret.
Why didn't you let me in on the plan?
examples.ko: 왜 그 계획을 나한테 안 알려 줬어?

senses.note: let someone in on something 형태로만 이 뜻. 구어체.

senses.meaningEn: to allow a person or animal to leave a place

examples.en: Please let the cat out before you go.
examples.ko: 가기 전에 고양이 좀 밖에 내보내 줘.

examples.en: Can you let me out at the next corner?
examples.ko: 다음 모퉁이에서 내려 줄 수 있어?

senses.note: 차에서 '내려 주다' 도 let me out. 학교가 끝나는 것: School lets out at three.(미국 구어)

senses.meaningEn: to make a sound or show a feeling suddenly

examples.en: She let out a big laugh.
He let out a long sigh and sat down.

senses.note: let out a scream / a cry / a sigh / a laugh 처럼 소리 명사와 같이 씀.

senses.meaningEn: used when you pause to think or remember something

examples.en: Let's see... I think it was Tuesday.
How much is it? Let's see, about ten dollars.

senses.note: 대답 전에 시간을 벌면서 생각할 때. Let me see 와 같음. 글자 그대로 '보자' 보다 '생각해 보자' 의 뜻이 더 흔함.

senses.meaningKo: (실제로 보여 달라며) 한번 봐 보자, 보여 줘
senses.meaningEn: used to ask someone to show you something

examples.en: You got a new phone? Let's see!
Let's see what's in the box.

senses.note: 뒤에 what/if/how 절을 붙여 '~인지 확인해 보자': Let's see if it works(되는지 보자).

senses.meaningEn: one of the signs used to write words, such as A or B

examples.en: The English alphabet has 26 letters.
Start the name with a capital letter.

senses.note: capital letter = 대문자, small/lowercase letter = 소문자. 한글의 '글자'도 letter 또는 character.

senses.meaningEn: a written message you send to someone, usually in an envelope

examples.en: I wrote a letter to my grandmother.
Did you get my letter?

senses.note: write/send/get a letter. 이메일은 e-mail, 문자는 text(message). cover letter = 자기소개서(입사 지원용).

senses.meaningEn: a place where you can read or borrow books

examples.en: Let's study at the library after school.
I need to return these books to the library.

senses.note: library 는 책을 빌리는 곳, bookstore 는 책을 사는 곳. 발음 /ˈlaɪbreri/ 에서 r 두 번 모두 발음.

senses.meaningEn: to say something that is not true

examples.en: Don't lie to me. Where were you?
He lied about his age to get in.

senses.note: '거짓말하다'의 과거는 lied(규칙). lie to 사람 / lie about 내용. 명사도 lie(tell a lie). 거짓말하는 사람은 liar.

senses.meaningEn: to be in a flat position on a bed, floor, or other surface

examples.en: I just want to lie on the sofa all day.
examples.ko: 그냥 하루 종일 소파에 누워 있고 싶어.

examples.en: The cat was lying in the sun.

senses.note: '눕다'의 과거는 lay, 과거분사 lain(불규칙). lay(놓다, 눕히다 — lay the book down)와 혼동 주의: lie 는 목적어가 없고 lay 는 목적어가 있음. lie down = 눕다.

senses.meaningEn: something you say that you know is not true

examples.en: That's a lie! I never said that.
examples.ko: 거짓말이야! 난 그런 말 한 적 없어.

examples.en: She told a little lie to avoid the party.
examples.ko: 그녀는 파티에 안 가려고 작은 거짓말을 했어.

senses.note: tell a lie(거짓말하다) — say a lie 는 안 씀. white lie = 선의의 거짓말.

senses.meaningEn: to put your body flat on a bed or the floor to rest

examples.en: I'm going to lie down for a bit.
She lay down on the sofa and fell asleep.
