senses.note: lie(눕다)의 과거형은 lay, 진행형은 lying. lay(놓다, 눕히다)는 다른 동사: lay the baby down = 아기를 눕히다. 한국 학습자가 가장 많이 헷갈리는 쌍.

senses.meaningEn: to move something up to a higher position

examples.en: Can you help me lift this table?
examples.ko: 이 테이블 들어 올리는 것 좀 도와줄래?

examples.en: He lifted the box onto the top shelf.
examples.ko: 그는 상자를 맨 위 칸에 올렸어.

senses.note: lift weights = 역기를 들다(운동). 작은 물건을 집어 드는 건 pick up.

senses.meaningEn: a free ride in someone's car

examples.en: Can you give me a lift to the station?
examples.ko: 역까지 차로 태워 줄 수 있어?

examples.en: I'll give you a lift home after the party.

senses.note: give sb a lift. 미국에서는 give sb a ride 가 더 흔함. 영국에서 lift 는 엘리베이터 뜻으로도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to raise something or someone to a higher position

examples.en: Can you lift up the box for me?
examples.ko: 이 상자 좀 들어 올려 줄 수 있어?

examples.en: Dad lifted me up so I could see.
examples.ko: 아빠가 나를 들어 올려 줘서 볼 수 있었어.

senses.note: lift 혼자 써도 뜻은 같음. up 을 붙이면 '위로' 가 강조됨. 목적어는 중간·뒤 모두 가능.

senses.meaningEn: to make someone feel happier or more confident

examples.en: Her kind words really lifted me up.
examples.ko: 그녀의 다정한 말이 정말 힘이 됐어.

examples.en: Good music can lift you up on a bad day.
examples.ko: 좋은 음악은 안 좋은 날에 기분을 북돋아 줘.

senses.note: 조금 감성적인 표현. 일상에서는 cheer up 이 더 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: brightness, or a lamp that produces it

examples.en: Please turn off the light when you leave.
There's not enough light to read here.

senses.note: traffic light = 신호등.

senses.meaningEn: not heavy

examples.en: This bag is really light and easy to carry.
examples.ko: 이 가방은 정말 가볍고 들고 다니기 편해.

examples.en: I only had a light lunch today.

senses.note: light meal = 가벼운 식사, light rain = 가랑비.

senses.meaningEn: pale in color

examples.en: Do you have this in light blue?
She painted the room a light green.

senses.meaningEn: the glass part of a lamp that gives light

examples.en: The light bulb in the kitchen burned out.
Can you change the light bulb for me?

senses.note: change a light bulb = 전구를 갈다. burn out = (전구가) 나가다. 그냥 bulb 라고도 함.

senses.meaningEn: to make a place bright with light, or to become bright

examples.en: The whole street lights up at Christmas.
examples.ko: 크리스마스엔 거리 전체가 환하게 불을 밝혀.

examples.en: The screen lit up when I touched it.

senses.note: light(불을 켜다, 과거 lit)에 up 이 붙어 '환하게'. 자동사(화면이 켜지다)·타동사(거리를 밝히다) 둘 다 가능.

senses.meaningEn: if your face or eyes light up, you suddenly look happy or excited

examples.en: Her face lit up when she saw the puppy.
The kids' eyes light up at the word 'pizza'.

senses.note: face / eyes light up = 기쁨·설렘으로 표정이 밝아지다. 아주 자주 쓰는 묘사.

senses.meaningEn: to start smoking a cigarette

examples.en: He lit up as soon as he got outside.
examples.ko: 그는 밖에 나가자마자 담배에 불을 붙였어.

examples.en: You can't light up in here. It's no smoking.
examples.ko: 여기서 담배 못 피워. 금연 구역이야.

senses.note: 목적어 없이 light up 만 쓰면 보통 '담배를 피우기 시작하다'.

senses.meaningEn: a bright flash of light in the sky during a storm

examples.en: Lightning hit the tree in our yard.
Stay inside when you see lightning.

senses.note: 셀 수 없는 명사: a lightning ✗ → a flash of lightning(번개 한 번). 철자 주의: lightning(번개)에는 e 가 없음. lightening = 밝아지는 것. 벼락 맞다 = be struck by lightning.

senses.meaningEn: to enjoy or find something pleasant

examples.en: I really like this song.
Do you like spicy food?

senses.note: I'd like... = ~을 원해요 (주문·요청할 때 정중한 표현).

senses.meaningEn: similar to something or someone

examples.en: She looks like her mother.
It smells like fresh bread in here.
examples.ko: 여기 갓 구운 빵 냄새가 나.

senses.note: look like / sound like / feel like + 명사.

senses.meaningEn: used to ask for a description of something

examples.en: What's the weather like today?
What's your new teacher like?

senses.note: How is...? 와 비슷하지만 성격·특징을 물을 때 더 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: a long thin mark on a surface

examples.en: Draw a line under the title.
Write your name on the first line.

senses.note: straight line = 직선, dotted line = 점선. 글의 '한 줄'도 line (read line 5 = 5행을 읽어).

senses.meaningEn: a row of people waiting for something

examples.en: There was a long line at the bakery.
Are you in line for the ticket?

senses.note: 미국식 line, 영국식 queue. stand in line / wait in line = 줄 서다. cut in line = 새치기하다.

senses.meaningEn: a telephone connection, or a train or bus route

examples.en: Take Line 2 and get off at City Hall.
Hold the line, please.

senses.note: 지하철 2호선 = Line 2. 전화에서 Hold the line. / The line is busy.(통화 중). online 의 line 도 여기서 온 말.

senses.meaningEn: to stand in a line, or to make people stand in a line

examples.en: Please line up at the door.
People lined up for hours to buy tickets.
examples.ko: 사람들이 표를 사려고 몇 시간씩 줄을 섰어.

senses.note: 미국 영어 line up, 영국 영어 queue (up). 명사 line = 줄. 'Get in line!' = 줄 서!

senses.meaningEn: to put things in a straight row

examples.en: Line up the chairs along the wall.
She lined the bottles up on the shelf.
examples.ko: 그녀는 선반 위에 병들을 줄지어 놓았어.

senses.note: 목적어는 중간·뒤 모두 가능.

senses.meaningEn: to arrange or plan something for the future

examples.en: We have a lot of fun lined up for the weekend.
examples.ko: 주말에 재미있는 일을 많이 계획해 뒀어.

examples.en: I lined up a job interview for Monday.

senses.note: have something lined up = 미리 준비된 일정·계획이 있다(구어).

senses.meaningEn: a large wild cat with yellow-brown fur that lives in Africa

examples.en: The lion is called the king of the jungle.
We heard a lion roar at the safari park.
examples.ko: 사파리 공원에서 사자가 으르렁거리는 소리를 들었어.

senses.note: 암사자는 lioness, 새끼 사자는 cub. 사자는 roar(으르렁거리다). 두 음절(/ˈlaɪ-ən/)로 발음할 것.

senses.meaningEn: one of the two soft edges of your mouth

examples.en: My lips are dry in winter.
She bit her lip and said nothing.
examples.ko: 그녀는 입술을 깨물고 아무 말도 하지 않았어.

senses.note: 보통 복수 lips 로 씀. 립밤 = lip balm, 립스틱 = lipstick. 윗입술 upper lip, 아랫입술 lower lip.

senses.meaningEn: a set of names or things written one below the other

examples.en: Is my name on the list?
I made a list of things to pack.

senses.note: make/write a list, on the list(목록에 있음). to-do list(할 일 목록), waiting list(대기자 명단), shopping list(쇼핑 목록).

senses.meaningEn: to write things one after another in a list

examples.en: List three things you like about your city.
examples.ko: 네 도시에서 좋은 점 세 가지를 적어 봐.

examples.en: The ingredients are listed on the back of the box.

senses.note: 시험·수업 지시문에 자주 나옴: List the reasons... 부동산 '매물로 내놓다'도 list.

senses.meaningEn: to pay attention to a sound or to what someone says

examples.en: Listen carefully and repeat after me.
I listen to music on the bus.

senses.note: 목적어 앞에 to 필수: listen to music (listen music ✗). hear 는 저절로 들리는 것, listen 은 의식적으로 듣는 것. t 는 묵음.

senses.meaningEn: to accept someone's advice or do what they say

examples.en: You never listen to me!
examples.ko: 넌 내 말을 전혀 안 들어!

examples.en: Listen, we need to talk about this.
examples.ko: 들어 봐, 이 문제 얘기 좀 해야겠어.

senses.note: 문장 첫머리의 Listen, = '이봐, 들어 봐'로 주의를 끄는 표현. listen to one's parents = 부모 말을 잘 듣다.

senses.meaningEn: to pay attention to music or sounds with your ears

examples.en: I listen to music on my way to work.
We listened to the rain all night.

senses.note: hear 는 저절로 들리는 것, listen to 는 귀 기울여 듣는 것. listen 뒤에 목적어가 오면 to 가 반드시 필요(listen music ✗).

senses.meaningEn: to pay attention to what someone says and do what they say

examples.en: Listen to your mother and put on a coat.
He never listens to anyone's advice.

senses.note: '말을 듣다(순종하다)'도 listen to. Listen to me!(내 말 좀 들어!).

senses.meaningEn: used to tell a group of people to pay attention to what you are going to say

examples.en: Okay everyone, listen up! The bus leaves at nine.
examples.ko: 자 여러분, 잘 들어요! 버스는 9시에 떠납니다.

examples.en: Listen up, I'll only say this once.
examples.ko: 잘 들어, 한 번만 말할 거야.

senses.note: 명령형으로만 쓰임. 교사·코치가 무리를 향해 말할 때 전형적. 한 사람에게는 Listen. 또는 Listen to me.

senses.meaningEn: small in size, or young

examples.en: Look at that little kitten!
examples.ko: 저 작은 새끼 고양이 좀 봐!

examples.en: When I was little, I loved this song.
examples.ko: 어릴 때 이 노래 정말 좋아했어.

senses.note: small 은 크기만, little 은 '작고 귀여운/어린' 느낌. my little brother = 남동생(어린 쪽).

senses.meaningEn: not much; a small amount of something

examples.en: There's little milk left in the fridge.
We have very little time before the train.
examples.ko: 기차 타기 전까지 시간이 거의 없어.

senses.note: little + 셀 수 없는 명사 = '거의 없다'(부정적), a little = '조금 있다'(긍정적). 셀 수 있는 명사엔 few/a few.

senses.meaningEn: to a small degree; slightly

examples.en: I'm a little tired today.
Can you speak a little slower, please?

senses.note: a little = a bit. 'a little bit' 도 매우 흔함. 형용사·비교급 앞에서 정도를 낮춤.

senses.meaningEn: slowly, a small amount at a time

examples.en: Little by little, my English is getting better.
He saved money little by little for a year.

senses.note: 격식체는 gradually. bit by bit 도 같은 뜻. 문장 앞이나 끝에 자유롭게 놓을 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: to have your home in a particular place

examples.en: Where do you live?
I live with my parents in Busan.

senses.note: live in + 도시/나라, live with + 사람, live on + 층/거리 (live on the third floor). live in Seoul 에서 in 을 빠뜨리지 않기.

senses.meaningEn: to be alive or to stay alive

examples.en: My grandfather lived to be ninety.
You can't live without water.

senses.note: live a happy life = 행복하게 살다. live on + 음식 = ~만 먹고 살다.

senses.meaningEn: broadcast or performed at the same time as it happens

examples.en: The concert is live on TV tonight.
examples.ko: 그 콘서트는 오늘 밤 TV로 생중계돼.

examples.en: We watched a live baseball game.

senses.note: 발음이 다름: 동사 live /lɪv/, 형용사·부사 live /laɪv/. live music = 라이브 음악, go live = 생방송을 시작하다.

senses.meaningEn: the main room in a home where people sit, relax, and talk

examples.en: We watched a movie in the living room.
There's a big sofa in the living room.

senses.note: 영국식으로는 sitting room / lounge 도 씀. family room 은 TV 보는 편한 방.

senses.meaningEn: bread baked in one large piece that you cut into slices

examples.en: We need a loaf of bread for breakfast.
examples.ko: 아침 먹을 식빵 한 봉지가 필요해.

examples.en: I bought two loaves of bread at the bakery.

senses.note: bread 는 셀 수 없는 명사라서 한 덩이는 a loaf of bread, 한 장은 a slice of bread 로 센다. 복수는 loaves(/loʊvz/). 한국인이 자주 틀리는 것: a bread (X), two breads (X).

senses.meaningEn: relating to the particular area where you live or are staying

examples.en: Let's try some local food tonight.
examples.ko: 오늘 밤에는 현지 음식을 먹어 보자.

examples.en: The local market opens early on Saturdays.

senses.note: local time(현지 시간), local news(지역 뉴스). 여행 영어의 핵심 단어.

senses.meaningEn: a person who lives in the area you are talking about

examples.en: Ask the locals where to eat.
A local showed us a hidden beach.
examples.ko: 현지인 한 분이 숨겨진 해변을 알려 줬어.

senses.note: 명사로는 보통 복수 the locals 로 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to close something with a key so it cannot be opened

examples.en: Did you lock the door when you left?
Always lock your bike outside the school.
examples.ko: 학교 밖에서는 항상 자전거를 잠가 둬.

senses.note: lock the door / lock the car. 반대는 unlock. '나 자신이 밖에 갇혔다'는 I locked myself out.

senses.meaningEn: a device that keeps a door or box closed and is opened with a key

examples.en: The lock on the front door is broken.
Put a lock on your suitcase, just in case.

senses.meaningEn: to lock all the doors and windows of a building

examples.en: Don't forget to lock up when you leave.
Who's going to lock up the shop tonight?
examples.ko: 오늘 밤 가게 문은 누가 잠글 거야?

senses.note: 목적어 없이도 자주 씀. lock the door 는 문 하나, lock up 은 건물 전체를 '문단속' 하는 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: to put something or someone in a locked place

examples.en: Lock your bike up or it will get stolen.
examples.ko: 자전거 잠가 놔, 안 그러면 도둑맞아.

examples.en: The police locked him up for the night.

senses.note: lock someone up = 감옥·유치장에 넣다(구어). lock something up = 금고·창고에 넣고 잠그다.

senses.meaningEn: to enter your name and password to start using a computer or website

examples.en: Log in with your email and password.
I can't log in to my account.

senses.note: log in to + 사이트/계정. 동사는 두 단어 log in, 명사는 login(아이디·로그인 화면). 로그아웃은 log out.

senses.meaningEn: to end your session on a computer, website, or app

examples.en: Don't forget to log out when you finish.
I logged out of my email on the shared computer.

senses.note: log out of + 서비스(log out of Instagram). 한국어 '로그아웃'과 같지만 전치사 of 를 잊기 쉬움. 영국·구어에서는 log off 도 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: unhappy because you are alone or have no friends

examples.en: I felt lonely when I first moved here.
examples.ko: 여기 처음 이사 왔을 때 외로웠어.

examples.en: Call your grandma. She gets lonely sometimes.

senses.note: alone 은 '혼자 있는' 상태(중립), lonely 는 '외로운' 감정. I live alone but I'm not lonely. 처럼 구분.

senses.meaningEn: measuring a great distance from one end to the other

examples.en: She has long black hair.
The river is very long and wide.

senses.note: 길이를 물을 때 How long is it? 길이 명사는 length.

senses.meaningEn: lasting or taking a lot of time

examples.en: It was a long flight to New York.
We waited a long time for the bus.

senses.note: a long time(오랫동안), a long day(힘들고 긴 하루), long weekend(연휴 낀 주말).

senses.meaningEn: for a great amount of time

examples.en: How long have you lived here?
Don't stay out too long tonight.
examples.ko: 오늘 밤 너무 늦게까지 밖에 있지 마.

senses.note: How long ~? 는 기간을 묻는 필수 표현. 'long time no see' 는 '오랜만이야' 라는 인사.

senses.meaningEn: used to greet someone you have not seen for a long time

examples.en: Hey, Jina! Long time no see!
Long time no see. How have you been?

senses.note: 문법적으로 어색하지만 굳어진 인사. 친한 사이에서 씀. 조금 더 정중하게는 It's been a long time. / It's been a while. / It's good to see you again.

senses.meaningEn: to turn your eyes toward something so you can see it

examples.en: Look at that cute puppy over there!
examples.ko: 저기 저 귀여운 강아지 좀 봐!

examples.en: She looked out the window at the rain.

senses.note: look at + 대상(at 필수). see 는 '눈에 보이다', watch 는 '움직이는 것을 지켜보다', look 은 '시선을 돌려 보다'. 'Look!' = 저것 봐/잘 들어.

senses.meaningEn: to seem or appear a certain way

examples.en: You look tired. Did you sleep well?
That dress looks great on you.
examples.ko: 그 드레스 너한테 정말 잘 어울려.

senses.note: look + 형용사(look happy). 명사가 오면 look like(You look like your mom). 'It looks like rain.' = 비 올 것 같아.

senses.meaningEn: to try to find something (look for)

examples.en: I'm looking for my keys. Have you seen them?
What are you looking for in the fridge?

senses.note: look for = 찾다(과정), find = 찾아내다(결과). look after = 돌보다, look forward to = 기대하다, look up = (사전·인터넷에서) 찾아보다.

senses.meaningEn: to take care of a person or animal

examples.en: Can you look after the baby for an hour?
examples.ko: 한 시간만 아기 좀 봐 줄 수 있어?

examples.en: Who looks after your dog when you travel?
examples.ko: 여행 갈 때 강아지는 누가 돌봐?

senses.note: 미국에서는 take care of 를 더 많이 쓰고, look after 는 영국에서 더 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: to be responsible for something

examples.en: Could you look after my bag for a minute?
examples.ko: 잠깐 내 가방 좀 봐 줄래?

examples.en: She looks after the shop when the owner is away.
examples.ko: 사장님이 없을 때는 그녀가 가게를 맡아.

senses.meaningEn: to walk around a place and look at things in it

examples.en: I'm just looking around, thanks.
We looked around the market for an hour.
examples.ko: 우리는 시장을 한 시간 동안 둘러봤어.

senses.note: 가게에서 점원이 Can I help you? 라고 물으면 I'm just looking around. 가 정답. 영국식은 look round.

senses.meaningEn: to turn your head to see what is near you

examples.en: He looked around, but nobody was there.
Look around and find a seat anywhere.

senses.note: look around for + 찾는 것(look around for a bathroom).

senses.meaningEn: to turn your eyes toward something so you can see it

examples.en: Look at that cute dog over there!
examples.ko: 저기 저 귀여운 강아지 좀 봐!

examples.en: Why are you looking at me like that?

senses.note: see 는 눈에 들어오는 것, look at 은 의도적으로 보는 것, watch 는 움직이는 것을 지켜보는 것. look 뒤에 at 을 빼고 look the picture 라고 하는 실수가 많음.

senses.meaningEn: to examine something to find out what is wrong

examples.en: The doctor looked at my knee and said it's fine.
examples.ko: 의사가 내 무릎을 살펴보고 괜찮다고 했어.

examples.en: Can you look at my computer? It's really slow.
examples.ko: 내 컴퓨터 좀 봐 줄래? 너무 느려.

senses.note: '한번 봐 줘'라고 부탁할 때 Can you look at ~? 또는 have a look at ~.

senses.meaningEn: to think about a situation or possible plan

examples.en: Let's look at the price before we decide.
examples.ko: 결정하기 전에 가격을 한번 검토해 보자.

examples.en: We're looking at a few different hotels.
examples.ko: 우리는 호텔 몇 곳을 비교해 보고 있어.

senses.note: look at the options(선택지를 살펴보다). 좀 더 깊이 조사하는 것은 look into.

senses.meaningEn: to turn and look behind you

examples.en: She waved and didn't look back.
I looked back and saw my dog following me.
examples.ko: 뒤를 돌아보니 내 개가 따라오고 있었어.

senses.meaningEn: to think about something that happened in the past

examples.en: When I look back, high school was fun.
Looking back on last year, we did a lot.
examples.ko: 지난해를 되돌아보면 우리 많은 걸 했어.

senses.note: look back on + 시기/경험. 긍정·부정 모두 쓰임. never look back(후회 없이 나아가다).

senses.meaningEn: to lower your eyes and look at something below you

examples.en: Don't look down when you cross the bridge.
examples.ko: 다리를 건널 때 아래를 내려다보지 마.

examples.en: He looked down at his shoes and said sorry.
examples.ko: 그는 자기 신발을 내려다보며 미안하다고 했어.

senses.note: look down at + 대상.

senses.meaningEn: to think that you are better than someone else

examples.en: Don't look down on people with less money.
She felt that her boss looked down on her.

senses.note: look down on + 사람. 반대는 look up to(존경하다). on 을 빠뜨리면 '내려다보다'가 되므로 주의.

senses.meaningEn: to try to find something

examples.en: I'm looking for my keys. Have you seen them?
Are you looking for anything special today?

senses.note: '찾고 있다'(과정)는 look for, '찾았다'(결과)는 find.

senses.meaningEn: to try to get a job or find a person for a role

examples.en: My brother is looking for a new job.
examples.ko: 내 동생은 새 일자리를 구하고 있어.

examples.en: They're looking for a part-time cook.

senses.meaningEn: to feel happy and excited about something that is going to happen

examples.en: I'm looking forward to the weekend.
We look forward to seeing you soon.

senses.note: to 뒤에 동사원형이 아니라 -ing(look forward to seeing). 가장 많이 틀리는 부분. 이메일 끝인사 I look forward to hearing from you. 는 격식, I'm looking forward to ~ 는 친근함.

senses.meaningEn: to try to find out the facts about a problem or situation

examples.en: I'll look into the problem and call you back.
We're looking into cheaper flights to Jeju.
examples.ko: 제주행 더 싼 항공편을 알아보고 있어.

senses.note: 고객 응대에서 '확인해 보겠습니다'는 I'll look into it. 단순히 훑어보는 look over 보다 조사의 깊이가 있음.

senses.meaningEn: to have a similar appearance to someone or something

examples.en: You look like your mother.
That cloud looks like a rabbit.

senses.note: look like + 명사. 형용사가 오면 like 없이 look tired. What does he look like?(그는 어떻게 생겼어?) 는 외모 질문, What is he like? 는 성격 질문.

senses.meaningEn: to seem likely to happen

examples.en: It looks like it's going to rain.
Looks like we're the first ones here.
examples.ko: 우리가 여기 제일 먼저 온 것 같네.

senses.note: It looks like + 문장. 구어에서는 It 을 빼고 Looks like ~ 로 시작하기도 함.

senses.meaningEn: used to warn someone that something dangerous is near

examples.en: Look out! There's a car coming.
Look out, the floor is wet.

senses.note: 갑작스런 위험을 알리는 소리. watch out 과 같음. 명사 lookout(감시, 전망대)도 있음.

senses.meaningEn: to look at what is outside through a window or door

examples.en: She looked out the window at the snow.
Look out and tell me if it's still raining.
examples.ko: 밖을 보고 아직 비 오는지 알려 줘.

senses.note: look out (of) the window — 미국 영어는 of 를 자주 생략.

senses.meaningEn: to watch carefully so you notice something or someone

examples.en: Look out for a red sign on your left.
examples.ko: 왼쪽에 빨간 표지판이 있는지 잘 봐.

examples.en: I'm looking out for a cheap used bike.
examples.ko: 싼 중고 자전거가 나오나 눈여겨보고 있어.

senses.note: 위험을 조심하라는 뜻(look out for cars)과 좋은 것을 눈여겨본다는 뜻 둘 다 가능. 맥락으로 구별.

senses.meaningEn: to take care of someone and make sure they are safe

examples.en: Big brothers should look out for their little sisters.
Thanks for always looking out for me.

senses.note: look after 보다 가볍고 친근한 느낌. look out for yourself(네 몫은 네가 챙겨).

senses.meaningEn: to examine or check something quickly

examples.en: Could you look over my report before I send it?
examples.ko: 보내기 전에 내 보고서 좀 봐 줄 수 있어?

examples.en: I looked over the menu and chose the pasta.

senses.note: look over = 빠르게 훑어보며 확인. 꼼꼼히 조사하는 look into 와 구별. 목적어가 대명사면 look it over.

senses.meaningEn: to find information in a dictionary, book, or on the internet

examples.en: Look up the word in your dictionary.
I looked up the restaurant's opening hours.

senses.note: 목적어가 대명사면 look it up. 한국인이 search 를 과하게 쓰는데, 단어·번호·시간 등 작은 정보는 look up 이 가장 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: to raise your eyes and look at something above you

examples.en: Look up! There's a rainbow.
She looked up from her phone and smiled.
examples.ko: 그녀는 휴대폰에서 눈을 들어 미소 지었어.

senses.note: look up at + 대상(look up at the sky).

senses.meaningEn: to get better, especially after a bad time

examples.en: Things are finally looking up for us.
Business is looking up this year.

senses.note: 보통 진행형 be looking up 으로 쓰임. 주어는 things, business 같은 상황.

senses.meaningEn: to respect and admire someone

examples.en: I really look up to my grandmother.
Kids look up to their favorite players.

senses.note: look up to + 사람. '사전에서 찾다'의 look up 과 다름 — to 가 있으면 존경. 반대는 look down on.

senses.meaningEn: to not win a game, race, or competition

examples.en: We lost the match by one point.
I hate losing at card games.
examples.ko: 카드 게임에서 지는 게 정말 싫어.

senses.note: lose to + 상대: We lost to Korea. 철자 주의 — lose(지다, 잃다) 와 loose(헐렁한) 를 헷갈리지 말 것.

senses.meaningEn: to no longer have something because you cannot find it

examples.en: I lost my keys again this morning.
Don't lose your ticket on the bus.

senses.note: '잃어버린 물건'은 lost + 명사 (lost phone). 'I lost.' 라고만 하면 경기에서 졌다는 뜻이 됨.

senses.meaningEn: to become lighter or have less of something than before

examples.en: He lost five kilos this summer.
I want to lose a little weight before the trip.
examples.ko: 여행 전에 살을 조금 빼고 싶어.

senses.note: lose weight(살 빼다) ↔ gain/put on weight(살 찌다). 그 외 lose time, lose money 등 '줄다·사라지다'에도 폭넓게 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: the person or team that does not win a game or competition

examples.en: The loser has to wash the dishes.
Be a good loser and shake hands.

senses.note: a good loser(패배를 인정하는 사람), a sore loser(패배를 못 받아들이는 사람). 경기에서 진 사람을 가리킬 때는 중립적인 표현.

senses.meaningEn: an insulting word for a person who is not successful or popular

examples.en: Don't call your brother a loser.
He felt like a loser after failing the test.
examples.ko: 그는 시험에 떨어지고 나서 자신이 한심하게 느껴졌어.

senses.note: 사람에게 직접 쓰면 심한 욕에 가까움. 농담으로도 조심할 것. 미드에서 자주 들리지만 실제 대화에서는 피하는 게 안전.

senses.meaningEn: making a lot of noise

examples.en: The music is too loud. Can you turn it down?
examples.ko: 음악이 너무 커. 좀 줄여 줄래?

examples.en: He has a very loud voice.

senses.note: 소리가 '크다'는 big 이 아니라 loud. 'The TV is too big' 은 크기 얘기가 됨. 반대로 소리가 '작다'는 quiet/soft/low.

senses.meaningEn: in a way that others can hear

examples.en: Please read the sentence out loud.
examples.ko: 그 문장을 소리 내어 읽어 주세요.

examples.en: She laughed out loud at the joke.

senses.note: out loud = aloud. 'LOL' 은 laughing out loud 의 약자. 더 크게 말해 달라는 Speak louder, please.

senses.meaningEn: in a way that makes a lot of noise

examples.en: The baby cried loudly all night.
Don't talk so loudly on the train.
examples.ko: 기차에서 그렇게 큰 소리로 말하지 마.

senses.note: loud 는 형용사(a loud voice), loudly 는 부사. 구어에서는 talk loud 처럼 loud 를 부사로도 씀. '소리를 크게 하다'는 turn up.

senses.meaningEn: to have very strong feelings of affection for someone

examples.en: I love you, Mom.
They have loved each other for twenty years.
examples.ko: 두 사람은 20년 동안 서로 사랑해 왔어.

senses.note: 가족·연인에게 I love you. 친구 사이에서도 가볍게 Love you! 라고 함.

senses.meaningEn: to like something very much

examples.en: I love pizza!
She loves reading before bed.
examples.ko: 그녀는 자기 전에 책 읽는 걸 아주 좋아해.

senses.note: love + -ing / to. I'd love to! = 정말 좋아요(초대 수락). I'd love to, but... = 거절할 때.

senses.meaningEn: a strong feeling of caring about someone

examples.en: Love is the most important thing in life.
He fell in love with her at first sight.

senses.note: fall in love with = 사랑에 빠지다, be in love = 사랑하고 있다. 편지 끝인사 Love, Jisoo.

senses.meaningEn: close to the ground or not high

examples.en: Watch your head. The ceiling is low.
The sun was low in the sky.

senses.meaningEn: small in amount, level, or price

examples.en: This store has really low prices.
My phone battery is low. Where's the charger?
examples.ko: 폰 배터리가 거의 없어. 충전기 어디 있어?

senses.note: low price(저렴한 가격), low fat(저지방), low battery. 재고가 떨어질 땐 We're running low on milk.

senses.meaningEn: quiet or deep in sound

examples.en: Please keep your voice low in the library.
He spoke in a low voice so the baby wouldn't wake up.
examples.ko: 그는 아기가 깨지 않게 낮은 목소리로 말했어.

senses.note: 볼륨을 낮춰 달라는 Turn it down 또는 Turn the volume low. 기분이 가라앉았을 때 I'm feeling low. 도 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: good or bad things that happen to you by chance, not because of what you do

examples.en: Good luck on your test tomorrow!
We found a parking spot right away. What luck!
examples.ko: 주차 자리를 바로 찾았어. 운이 좋았네!

senses.note: 불가산 명사(a luck 아님). Good luck! 은 시험·면접 전 응원 인사. bad luck(불운), Just my luck.(내 운이 늘 이렇지), 형용사는 lucky.

senses.meaningEn: having good things happen to you by chance

examples.en: You're so lucky! You won the prize!
examples.ko: 넌 정말 운이 좋아! 상을 탔잖아!

examples.en: We were lucky to get the last two tickets.
examples.ko: 마지막 표 두 장을 구해서 운이 좋았어.

senses.note: lucky to + 동사 / lucky that... 패턴. 부러움을 표현할 때 Lucky you! '행운' 명사는 luck(Good luck! = 행운을 빌어). lucky number(행운의 숫자) 같은 콜로케이션도.

senses.meaningEn: the bags and suitcases that you take with you when you travel

examples.en: How much luggage do you have?
You can leave your luggage at the hotel.

senses.note: 불가산명사: a luggage (X), luggages (X). 하나를 셀 때는 a piece of luggage 또는 a suitcase/a bag. 미국 공항에서는 baggage(baggage claim = 수하물 찾는 곳)를 더 자주 봄. carry-on = 기내 휴대 가방.

senses.meaningEn: a meal eaten in the middle of the day

examples.en: Let's have lunch together tomorrow.
I usually bring my lunch to work.
examples.ko: 나는 보통 회사에 점심 도시락을 가져가.

senses.note: have/eat lunch(관사 없음). lunch break = 점심시간. 도시락은 packed lunch / lunch box.

senses.meaningEn: a container you carry your lunch in, or the lunch inside it

examples.en: Don't forget your lunch box today.
Mom packed a sandwich in my lunch box.
examples.ko: 엄마가 내 도시락에 샌드위치를 넣어 주셨어.

senses.note: 한국식 '도시락'은 lunch box 또는 packed lunch. 통 자체와 내용물 둘 다 가리킬 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: angry

examples.en: Are you still mad at me?
Don't get mad, it was just a joke.

senses.note: 미국 일상 회화에서 angry 보다 훨씬 자주 씀. mad at + 사람. 영국에서는 mad 가 주로 '미친' 뜻이라 주의.

senses.meaningEn: crazy or not sensible

examples.en: You want to swim in winter? Are you mad?
It was a mad idea, but it worked.
examples.ko: 말도 안 되는 생각이었는데 효과가 있었어.

senses.note: go mad(미쳐 버리다). 미국에서는 crazy 가 더 일반적.

senses.meaningEn: liking something very much

examples.en: My brother is mad about baseball.
examples.ko: 내 남동생은 야구에 완전 빠져 있어.

examples.en: She's mad about K-pop these days.

senses.note: be mad about + 명사 = be crazy about.

senses.meaningEn: a polite way to speak to a woman whose name you do not know

examples.en: Good evening, madam. Table for two?
This way, please, madam.

senses.note: 실제 대화에서는 줄인 ma'am(맘)이 훨씬 흔함. 격식 있는 식당·호텔에서 madam.

senses.meaningEn: a word used at the start of a formal letter to a woman

examples.en: Dear Madam, thank you for your email.
Dear Sir or Madam, I need some help.

senses.note: Dear Sir or Madam 은 받는 사람을 전혀 모를 때만.

senses.meaningEn: tricks that seem impossible, done to entertain people; also special powers in stories

examples.en: My uncle can do magic with cards.
examples.ko: 삼촌은 카드로 마술을 할 수 있어.

examples.en: Kids love stories about magic and dragons.

senses.note: do magic / do a magic trick = 마술을 하다. 마술사는 magician. 마술 쇼는 magic show.

senses.meaningEn: having or using special powers, or very special and wonderful

examples.en: He waved his magic wand.
That night in Paris was magic.
examples.ko: 파리에서의 그날 밤은 정말 마법 같았어.

senses.note: 형용사 magical 도 비슷하지만 '마법 같은, 황홀한' 느낌(a magical evening). magic words = '부탁해요(please)' 같은 마법의 말.

senses.meaningEn: a person whose job is to bring letters and packages to houses

examples.en: The mail carrier comes around noon every day.
Our mail carrier knows every dog on the street.
examples.ko: 우리 집배원 아저씨는 이 동네 개를 다 알아.

senses.note: mailman/postman 보다 성 중립적인 표현. 영국은 postman/postwoman 또는 postal worker. 택배 기사는 delivery driver.

senses.meaningEn: most important or largest

examples.en: What is the main problem here?
The main entrance is on the left.

senses.note: main 은 항상 명사 앞에만 씀(The problem is main ✗). main street(큰길), main point(요점), mainly(주로).

senses.meaningEn: the biggest part of a meal

examples.en: For the main course, I'll have the steak.
Rice is the main food in Korea.

senses.note: 식당에서 main 만 써도 통함(What's your main?). 전채는 starter/appetizer, 후식은 dessert.

senses.meaningEn: to create or prepare something

examples.en: My mom makes the best kimchi stew.
examples.ko: 우리 엄마가 김치찌개를 제일 잘 하셔.

examples.en: Can you make me a cup of coffee?
examples.ko: 커피 한 잔 타 줄 수 있어?

senses.note: make breakfast / make dinner / make a sandwich.

senses.meaningEn: to cause someone to feel or do something

examples.en: This song always makes me happy.
examples.ko: 이 노래는 항상 나를 행복하게 해.

examples.en: Don't make me laugh, I'm trying to study!

senses.note: make + 사람 + 형용사/동사원형. make me to laugh (X).

senses.meaningEn: to earn money

examples.en: How much do you make a month?
She makes good money as a nurse.
examples.ko: 그녀는 간호사로 돈을 꽤 잘 벌어.

senses.meaningEn: to choose what to do after thinking about it

examples.en: You need to make a decision by Friday.
We made a decision to move to Busan.

senses.note: 결정을 "내리다" 는 make. take a decision 은 영국식. 동사 decide 와 같은 뜻: decide = make a decision. 어려운 결정은 a hard/tough decision.

senses.meaningEn: to do something wrong by accident

examples.en: Don't worry, everyone makes mistakes.
I always make mistakes when I rush.

senses.note: 동사는 do 가 아니라 make: do a mistake (X). 실수를 '하다'라고 해서 do 로 쓰는 흔한 오류.

senses.meaningEn: to call someone on the phone

examples.en: Excuse me, I need to make a phone call.
examples.ko: 잠시만요, 전화 한 통 해야 해요.

examples.en: She made a quick phone call to her mom.

senses.note: 전화를 "하다" 는 make a (phone) call. do a call 은 틀림. 더 짧게는 call someone / give someone a call. 전화 받다 = answer / get a call.

senses.meaningEn: to decide what you are going to do and how

examples.en: Let's make a plan for the weekend.
We made a plan to meet at six.

senses.note: make a plan = 계획을 세우다. "약속이 있다" 는 복수로 have plans: Do you have plans tonight? plan 단독 동사도 자주: I plan to go.

senses.meaningEn: to silently hope for something you want, often at a special moment

examples.en: Close your eyes and make a wish before you blow out the candles.
examples.ko: 눈 감고 소원 빌고 촛불 불어.

examples.en: I made a wish when I saw a shooting star.

senses.note: 생일 케이크·별똥별·분수에 동전 던질 때. "소원을 빌다" 는 make 를 쓰고 do/pray 는 안 씀. 소원이 이루어지다 = a wish comes true.

senses.meaningEn: to cook and prepare the evening meal

examples.en: Whose turn is it to make dinner tonight?
Dad made dinner while I set the table.
examples.ko: 아빠가 저녁을 만들고 나는 식탁을 차렸어.

senses.note: make/cook dinner 둘 다 OK. breakfast, lunch 도 같은 패턴. dinner 앞에 a/the 를 붙이지 않는 게 보통. 저녁 먹다 = have dinner.

senses.meaningEn: to become friends with new people

examples.en: Did you make friends at your new school?
She makes friends easily wherever she goes.

senses.note: 친구를 사귀다 = make friends (with 사람). 항상 복수 friends. "get friends" 는 쓰지 않음. 화해하다 = make up.

senses.meaningEn: to arrive somewhere in time, or to be able to go to an event

examples.en: Hurry, or we won't make it to the train.
examples.ko: 서둘러, 안 그러면 기차 못 타.

examples.en: Sorry, I can't make it to the party tonight.
examples.ko: 미안, 오늘 밤 파티에 못 가겠어.

senses.note: can't make it = (약속에) 못 가다 — 초대를 거절할 때 가장 흔한 표현. make it to + 장소/행사. 'You made it!' = 왔구나!/해냈구나!

senses.meaningEn: to be successful in your job or in life

examples.en: She worked hard and finally made it as a singer.
examples.ko: 그녀는 열심히 노력해서 결국 가수로 성공했어.

examples.en: If you believe in yourself, you can make it.

senses.note: make it as a + 직업 = ~로 성공하다. make it big = 크게 성공하다.

senses.meaningEn: to survive a serious illness, accident, or difficult time

examples.en: The doctors say he's going to make it.
It was a hard year, but we made it through.
examples.ko: 힘든 한 해였지만 우리는 잘 견뎌 냈어.

senses.note: make it through + 기간/시련 = ~을 견뎌 내다. 병원 드라마에서 'He didn't make it.'(그는 결국 숨졌다) 자주 들림.

senses.meaningEn: to earn or get money, especially from work or business

examples.en: He makes money by selling old books online.
examples.ko: 그는 온라인에서 중고 책을 팔아서 돈을 벌어.

examples.en: I want to make more money this year.
examples.ko: 올해는 돈을 더 많이 벌고 싶어.

senses.note: 돈을 "벌다" 는 make 또는 earn. get money 는 "받다" 느낌이라 다름. make a lot of money / make good money(괜찮게 벌다). 돈을 쓰다 = spend money.

senses.meaningEn: to produce sounds that are loud or annoying

examples.en: Don't make noise. The baby is sleeping.
examples.ko: 시끄럽게 하지 마. 아기 자고 있어.

examples.en: The kids upstairs make so much noise at night.
examples.ko: 위층 아이들이 밤에 너무 시끄럽게 해.

senses.note: 소리를 "내다" 는 make. noise 는 셀 수 없는 명사라 a lot of / too much noise. 특정한 소리 하나는 a noise(a strange noise). 비슷한 말: be noisy / be loud.

senses.meaningKo: (잘 안 보이는·안 들리는 것을) 알아보다, 알아듣다
senses.meaningEn: to see, hear, or read something with difficulty

examples.en: I can't make out the sign from here.
Could you make out what she said?
examples.ko: 그 사람이 무슨 말 했는지 알아들었어?

senses.note: 거의 항상 can't / could hardly 와 함께 씀. 글씨·소리·멀리 있는 것을 겨우 알아보는 상황.

senses.meaningEn: to write a check or an official document

examples.en: Who should I make the check out to?
Please make out a receipt for me.

senses.note: make a check out to + 사람/회사 이름 = 수표의 받는 사람을 쓰다. 미국 생활 영어.

senses.meaningEn: to manage or succeed in a situation

examples.en: How did you make out at the interview?
We made out okay on our first day.

senses.note: How did you make out? = 어떻게 됐어? 또 미국 속어로 make out = 진하게 키스하다 라는 뜻이 흔하니, 'make out with someone' 은 그 뜻으로 들릴 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: to arrange the sheets and blankets neatly on a bed after sleeping

examples.en: Make your bed before you leave for school.
I made the bed and opened the window.

senses.note: make the/your bed = 자고 난 침대를 정돈하다. 침대를 "만드는" 게 아니다. clean the bed 라고 하지 않음.

senses.meaningEn: to invent a story, an excuse, or an explanation that is not true

examples.en: Don't make up excuses. Just say sorry.
examples.ko: 변명 꾸며내지 말고 그냥 미안하다고 해.

examples.en: Grandpa makes up funny stories for the kids.
examples.ko: 할아버지는 아이들에게 재미있는 이야기를 지어내 주셔.

senses.note: made-up story = 꾸며낸 이야기. 'You're making it up!' = 거짓말이지!

senses.meaningEn: to become friends again after an argument

examples.en: They had a fight but made up the next day.
Come on, let's kiss and make up.

senses.note: make up with someone = ~와 화해하다. kiss and make up 은 관용적 표현. 명사 makeup(화장)과 구별.

senses.meaningEn: to do something you missed, or to replace something that was lost

examples.en: Can I make up the test I missed yesterday?
examples.ko: 어제 못 본 시험 다시 볼 수 있을까요?

examples.en: I'll make up the hours on Saturday.

senses.note: make up a test/class = 보충 시험·수업을 치르다/듣다. make up for ~ = ~을 보상하다(I'll make up for it).

senses.meaningEn: to form something as its parts

examples.en: Women make up half of the class.
Six small teams make up the whole club.
examples.ko: 작은 팀 여섯 개가 동호회 전체를 이루고 있어.

senses.note: be made up of = ~로 구성되다(The team is made up of ten people). 비율·구성 설명에 자주 나옴.

senses.meaningKo: (손님에게) 편하게 계세요, 내 집처럼 편하게 하세요
senses.meaningEn: used to tell a guest to relax and behave as if they were in their own home

examples.en: Come in and make yourself at home.
Make yourself at home. I'll get some tea.

senses.note: 손님이 집에 들어왔을 때 하는 전형적인 인사. 여럿에게는 Make yourselves at home. 답은 Thank you / Thanks, I will. 손님이 자기 자신에게 쓰는 표현은 아님(I feel at home = 편하다).

senses.meaningEn: a large building with many stores, restaurants, and sometimes a cinema inside

examples.en: Let's meet at the mall after school.
There's a new mall opening downtown next month.
examples.ko: 다음 달에 시내에 새 쇼핑몰이 열려.

senses.note: shopping mall 의 줄임말. 미국에서는 그냥 the mall 이라고 많이 함. 온라인 쇼핑몰은 online store/shop 이라고 해야 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: an adult male person

examples.en: A tall man is waiting at the door.
examples.ko: 키 큰 남자가 문 앞에서 기다리고 있어.

examples.en: There were two men and one woman in the car.
examples.ko: 차 안에 남자 둘, 여자 하나가 있었어.

senses.note: 복수형은 mans 가 아니라 men. 발음 구분: man /mæn/ vs men /men/.

senses.meaningEn: used to show strong feeling or to speak to a friend

examples.en: Man, I'm so tired today.
Hey man, how's it going?

senses.note: 친구(주로 남성) 사이의 매우 캐주얼한 표현. 격식 상황에서는 피할 것.

senses.meaningEn: a sweet tropical fruit with orange flesh and a large flat seed

examples.en: Mango is my favorite fruit.
I'd like a mango smoothie, please.

senses.note: 복수형은 mangoes 와 mangos 둘 다 가능.

senses.meaningEn: a large number of people or things

examples.en: There are many people at the station.
I don't have many friends here yet.

senses.note: many + 셀 수 있는 복수 명사(many books). 셀 수 없는 것은 much. 긍정문 구어에서는 a lot of 를 더 많이 씀.

senses.meaningKo: how many: 몇 개, 몇 명
senses.meaningEn: used to ask about a number

examples.en: How many brothers do you have?
How many times have you been to Busan?

senses.note: How many + 복수 명사. 양을 물을 때는 How much.

senses.meaningEn: a drawing of an area that shows roads, rivers, towns, and so on

examples.en: Can you show me on the map?
I used a map app to find the hotel.

senses.note: look at a map, read a map(지도를 보다). a map of Seoul(서울 지도). subway map = 지하철 노선도. 동사 map 은 '지도를 만들다, 계획을 짜다(map out)'.

senses.meaningEn: the third month of the year

examples.en: School starts in March in Korea.
The flowers come out in late March.

senses.note: 소문자 march 는 '행진하다'라는 전혀 다른 단어. 월 이름은 대문자 March 로 구분. 줄임말은 Mar.

senses.meaningEn: a thick pen with a soft tip, used for writing or drawing

examples.en: Use a black marker so everyone can see.
examples.ko: 다들 볼 수 있게 검은 마커로 써.

examples.en: This marker is dry. Do you have another one?
examples.ko: 이 마커 안 나와. 다른 거 있어?

senses.note: 한국어 '매직'은 영어로 통하지 않음 → marker. 형광펜은 highlighter.

senses.meaningEn: a place, often outside, where people sell food and other things from tables or stalls

examples.en: We buy fresh fish at the market every Sunday.
examples.ko: 우리는 매주 일요일 시장에서 신선한 생선을 사.

examples.en: The fruit at the market is cheaper than at the store.

senses.note: 한국의 '마트'는 market 이 아니라 supermarket 또는 grocery store. market 은 재래시장·벼룩시장(flea market)·농산물 시장(farmers' market) 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: to become someone's husband or wife

examples.en: Will you marry me?
She married her best friend last year.
examples.ko: 그녀는 작년에 가장 친한 친구와 결혼했어.

senses.note: marry + 사람(with 없음!). marry with him 은 틀림. 상태를 말할 때는 be married to(~와 결혼한 상태다). get married = 결혼식을 하다.

senses.meaningEn: a sports game between two players or teams

examples.en: Did you watch the soccer match last night?
The tennis match lasted three hours.
examples.ko: 테니스 경기가 세 시간 동안 이어졌어.

senses.note: 영국식에서 흔히 match, 미국식은 game(baseball game, basketball game). 테니스·복싱·축구는 미국에서도 match 를 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to look good together or be the same in color or style

examples.en: Does this shirt match my pants?
Your socks don't match!

senses.note: match 는 색·무늬가 '맞다/일치하다'. 전체적으로 '어울리다'는 go with / suit 도 자주 씀. 한국어 '매치하다'와 비슷.

senses.meaningEn: a small stick that makes a flame when you rub it against something rough

examples.en: Do you have a match or a lighter?
Keep the matches away from the kids.
examples.ko: 성냥은 아이들 손에 닿지 않게 둬.

senses.note: a box of matches(성냥 한 통), light a match(성냥을 켜다).

senses.meaningEn: the study of numbers, shapes, and amounts

examples.en: I have math class right after lunch.
examples.ko: 점심 먹고 바로 수학 수업이 있어.

examples.en: Math is hard, but I like it.

senses.note: mathematics 의 줄임말. 미국식 math, 영국식 maths. 셀 수 없는 명사로 단수 취급(Math is...). 과목 이름은 보통 관사 없이 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to be important or to have an effect on something

examples.en: It doesn't matter what time you come.
Your opinion matters to me.

senses.note: It doesn't matter. = 괜찮아, 상관없어. 주어는 보통 사물·it. '사람이 중요하다'는 You matter. 도 가능.

senses.meaningEn: a subject or situation that you have to think about or deal with

examples.en: What's the matter? You look upset.
examples.ko: 무슨 일이야? 기분 안 좋아 보여.

examples.en: It's a private matter, so I can't tell you.
examples.ko: 개인적인 일이라서 말해 줄 수 없어.

senses.note: What's the matter (with you)? = 무슨 일이야? What's wrong? 과 같은 뜻. no matter what = 무슨 일이 있어도.

senses.meaningEn: the fifth month of the year

examples.en: We got married in May.
Children's Day is on May 5th in Korea.

senses.note: 줄임말 없이 항상 May 로 쓴다. 소문자 may(~해도 된다, ~일지도 모른다)는 조동사로 전혀 다른 단어. 문장 중간에 May 가 대문자면 월 이름.

senses.meaningEn: used to say that something is possible but not certain

examples.en: Maybe it will rain this afternoon.
Are you coming tonight? Maybe.

senses.note: 보통 문장 맨 앞. may be(일지도 모른다, 동사)와 띄어쓰기 구분: He may be late. / Maybe he is late. perhaps 보다 구어적. 제안할 때도: Maybe we should go.

senses.meaningEn: the speaker, used as the object of a verb or preposition

examples.en: Can you help me with this bag?
Please wait for me outside.

senses.note: 동사·전치사 뒤는 me(Give it to me). "Me too."(나도), "It's me."(저예요)처럼 짧은 대답에도 me 를 씀. "Tom and me went" 는 구어에서 들리지만 표준은 "Tom and I went".

senses.meaningEn: used to agree with a negative statement, meaning the same is true for you

examples.en: I don't like coffee. Me neither.
I didn't sleep well last night. Me neither.
examples.ko: 어젯밤에 잘 못 잤어. 나도 그래.

senses.note: 부정문에 동의할 때. 한국어는 '나도' 하나지만 영어는 긍정 → Me too, 부정 → Me neither 로 갈림. 'I don't like it' 에 'Me too' 라고 하면 틀림. 격식: Neither do I / Nor do I. neither 발음은 /ˈniːðər/ 와 /ˈnaɪðər/ 둘 다 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: used to say that you feel the same or have the same experience as someone, after a positive statement

examples.en: I'm so hungry. Me too!
I love this song. Me too, it's great.
examples.ko: 이 노래 정말 좋아. 나도, 진짜 좋아.

senses.note: 상대가 긍정문으로 말했을 때만 Me too. 부정문(I don't like it)에는 Me neither 로 답함. 'I love you' 에 'Me too' 는 '나도 나를 사랑해' 처럼 들릴 수 있어 'I love you too' 가 안전. 격식 있는 자리에서는 So do I / So am I.

senses.meaningEn: an occasion when you eat food, or the food eaten at that time

examples.en: I eat three meals a day.
That was a great meal, thank you.

senses.note: breakfast/lunch/dinner 를 모두 묶어 부르는 말. 약 복용 안내에서 after meals = 식후. 한국어 '식사하다'는 have a meal.

senses.meaningEn: to have a particular meaning

examples.en: What does this word mean?
A red light means you have to stop.

senses.note: What do you mean? = 무슨 말이야? 가장 많이 쓰는 되묻기 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to be serious about what you say, or to intend something

examples.en: I mean it. You did a great job.
Sorry, I didn't mean to hurt you.

senses.note: I didn't mean to... = 일부러 그런 게 아니야. 사과할 때 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: unkind or cruel

examples.en: Don't be mean to your little brother.
That was a really mean thing to say.

senses.meaningEn: to find the size, length, or amount of something

examples.en: Measure the table before you buy a cloth.
examples.ko: 식탁보 사기 전에 식탁 길이를 재 봐.

examples.en: The nurse measured my height.

senses.note: 길이·높이·양을 '재다'. 무게는 weigh 를 더 많이 씀. 명사 measurement = 치수.

senses.meaningEn: to be a particular size or length

examples.en: The room measures four by five meters.
This screen measures ten inches.

senses.note: 주어가 물건이고 뒤에 치수가 바로 옴. '4 by 5' 는 '4 곱하기 5' 크기.

senses.meaningEn: the flesh of animals, eaten as food

examples.en: I don't eat meat, I'm a vegetarian.
How long should I cook the meat?

senses.note: 셀 수 없는 명사: meats (×), a meat (×). 영어 meat 는 보통 소·돼지·닭고기를 뜻하고 생선은 fish 로 따로 말함. 발음이 같은 meet(만나다)와 혼동 주의.

senses.meaningEn: a flat piece of metal given to someone who wins a race or does something special

examples.en: She won a gold medal in swimming.
Everyone who finished the race got a medal.
examples.ko: 경주를 완주한 사람은 모두 메달을 받았어.

senses.note: gold/silver/bronze medal(금/은/동메달), win a medal(메달을 따다). 메달리스트는 medalist. 발음은 '메달'에 가깝지만 끝은 /dl/.

senses.meaningEn: something you drink or swallow to treat an illness

examples.en: Take this medicine three times a day after meals.
examples.ko: 이 약을 식후에 하루 세 번 먹어요.

examples.en: Did you take your medicine this morning?

senses.note: 약을 '먹다'는 eat 가 아니라 take medicine. 셀 수 없는 명사(a medicine 보다 some medicine). 약국 = pharmacy / drugstore.

senses.meaningEn: the study and practice of treating illness

examples.en: She studies medicine at university.
My brother wants to study medicine and become a doctor.
examples.ko: 내 형은 의학을 공부해서 의사가 되고 싶어 해.

senses.note: study medicine = 의대에서 공부하다. medical school(의대).

senses.meaningEn: between small and large in size or amount

examples.en: Do you have this jacket in a medium?
A medium latte, please.

senses.note: 형용사이지만 사이즈를 말할 때는 명사처럼 a medium 으로도 씀. 머리 길이는 medium-length hair.

senses.meaningEn: cooked so that the inside of the meat is pink but not red

examples.en: How would you like your steak? Medium, please.
I ordered my steak medium rare.

senses.note: 익힘 정도: rare → medium rare → medium → medium well → well done.

senses.meaningEn: to see and talk to someone for the first time

examples.en: Nice to meet you, I'm Jisoo.
We met at a friend's birthday party.
examples.ko: 우리는 친구 생일 파티에서 처음 만났어.

senses.note: 처음 만날 때 Nice to meet you, 헤어질 때 Nice meeting you. 이미 아는 사람과 만나는 건 see 도 많이 씀: I saw Tom yesterday.

senses.meaningEn: to come together with someone at a planned time and place

examples.en: Let's meet at the café at six.
I'm meeting my friends after work today.

senses.note: meet up (with) 도 캐주얼하게 자주 씀. meet with 는 주로 업무상 만남.

senses.meaningEn: a large round fruit with sweet juicy flesh and a thick skin

examples.en: This melon is really sweet and juicy.
examples.ko: 이 멜론 정말 달고 물이 많네.

examples.en: Can you cut the melon into small pieces?

senses.note: watermelon(수박)은 한 단어로 붙여 씀. 한국어 '메론'과 달리 발음은 /ˈmelən/.

senses.meaningEn: to change from solid to liquid because of heat

examples.en: The ice cream melted in the sun.
Melt the butter in a small pan.

senses.note: melt 는 열로 녹는 것. 설탕·소금이 물에 녹는 건 dissolve. 눈이 녹다 = The snow is melting.

senses.meaningEn: to suddenly feel love or kindness

examples.en: My heart melted when the puppy looked at me.
examples.ko: 강아지가 날 쳐다보는데 마음이 녹아 버렸어.

examples.en: Her smile melts everyone around her.
examples.ko: 그녀의 미소는 주변 사람 마음을 다 녹여.

senses.note: My heart melted. = 심쿵했다, 마음이 녹았다. SNS 에서 아주 흔한 표현.

senses.meaningEn: a list of the food and drinks you can order in a restaurant

examples.en: Can we see the menu, please?
Everything on the menu looks good.
examples.ko: 메뉴에 있는 게 다 맛있어 보여.

senses.note: 한국어 '메뉴'는 음식 하나를 가리키기도 하지만, 영어 menu 는 '목록(메뉴판)'. 음식 하나는 dish. '추천 메뉴 뭐예요?'는 What do you recommend?

senses.meaningEn: a list of choices shown on a computer or phone screen

examples.en: Click the menu in the top corner.
Open the settings menu and turn off the sound.

senses.note: drop-down menu = 드롭다운 메뉴. menu bar = 메뉴 바.

senses.meaningEn: to do something badly or make a mistake that spoils something

examples.en: I really messed up on the test today.
Don't worry, everyone messes up sometimes.

senses.note: mess up (on) something = ~을 망치다. 목적어 없이 I messed up. = 내가 실수했어. 더 거친 표현은 screw up.

senses.meaningEn: to make a place or thing dirty or untidy

examples.en: The kids messed up the living room again.
The wind messed up my hair.

senses.note: 명사 mess(엉망인 상태): What a mess! / My room is a mess.

senses.meaningEn: untidy, with things lying around everywhere

examples.en: My room is so messy right now.
Eating ribs is always messy.

senses.note: 사람에게도 씀: a messy person(정리 안 하는 사람). 명사는 mess (What a mess! = 엉망이네!).

senses.meaningEn: a small oven that heats food very quickly using waves of energy

examples.en: Put the soup in the microwave for two minutes.
Our microwave stopped working yesterday.

senses.note: 한국어 '전자레인지'를 electric range 라고 하면 안 됨. microwave 가 맞음.

senses.meaningEn: to heat food in a microwave

examples.en: Just microwave the leftovers for lunch.
examples.ko: 점심은 남은 음식 그냥 전자레인지에 돌려 먹어.

examples.en: Can you microwave this for thirty seconds?

senses.note: 구어에서는 nuke, zap 도 쓰지만 microwave 가 가장 무난함.

senses.meaningEn: twelve o'clock at night

examples.en: I went to bed after midnight last night.
The party ended at midnight.

senses.note: at midnight(자정에). 12 a.m. 과 같은 뜻이지만 noon 처럼 midnight 이라고 말하는 게 명확하다. midnight snack = 야식. 한국어 '새벽 2시'는 two in the morning 또는 2 a.m.

senses.meaningEn: used to say that something is possible but not certain

examples.en: I might be late, so start without me.
examples.ko: 늦을지도 모르니까 나 빼고 먼저 시작해.

examples.en: It might snow tonight.

senses.note: may 보다 조금 더 불확실·구어적. 한국어 '~할지도' 는 대부분 might 로 번역됨. 뒤에 동사 원형(might go, might to go ✗).

senses.meaningEn: used to make a gentle suggestion

examples.en: You might want to bring an umbrella.
examples.ko: 우산을 가져가는 게 좋을 것 같아.

examples.en: We might as well wait here.

senses.note: You might want to ~ = 부드러운 조언. might as well = 달리 할 일도 없으니 ~하자.

senses.meaningEn: the white drink that comes from cows and that people often drink or pour on cereal

examples.en: Do you want milk in your coffee?
We're out of milk again.

senses.note: 셀 수 없는 명사: a milk (×) → a glass of milk / a carton of milk. soy milk(두유), almond milk 등 식물성 음료에도 milk 를 씀.

senses.meaningEn: the number 1,000,000

examples.en: About ten million people live in Seoul.
The house sold for two million dollars.

senses.note: 한국어 '백만' = one million, '천만' = ten million, '1억' = one hundred million. 단위 바꾸는 연습이 필요함.

senses.meaningEn: a very large number or amount

examples.en: Thanks a million for your help!
I've seen that video a million times.

senses.note: Thanks a million = 정말 고마워(구어). one in a million = 아주 특별한 사람.

senses.meaningEn: to be bothered or annoyed by something

examples.en: Do you mind if I open the window?
I don't mind waiting a few minutes.

senses.note: Do you mind ~? 에 '괜찮아요'라고 답할 땐 No, not at all.(Yes 라고 하면 '싫다'는 뜻). Never mind. = 신경 쓰지 마, 됐어. mind + -ing.

senses.meaningEn: the part of you that thinks and remembers

examples.en: I changed my mind about the red dress.
What's on your mind? You look worried.

senses.note: change my mind(마음을 바꾸다), make up my mind(결정하다), keep in mind(기억해 두다). 감정의 '마음'은 heart 쪽.

senses.meaningEn: the thing or things that belong to the person speaking

examples.en: That red umbrella is mine.
Your phone is newer than mine.
examples.ko: 네 폰이 내 것보다 새 거네.

senses.note: 뒤에 명사를 붙이지 않음(mine bag ✗ → my bag). a friend of mine(내 친구 중 한 명)은 자주 쓰는 표현.

senses.meaningEn: a deep hole in the ground where coal, gold, or other things are dug out

examples.en: His grandfather worked in a coal mine.
The old gold mine is now a museum.

senses.note: gold mine, coal mine. 전혀 다른 뜻이지만 철자·발음이 같음.

senses.meaningEn: a period of sixty seconds

examples.en: The train leaves in ten minutes.
It's a five-minute walk from here.

senses.note: 형용사처럼 쓸 때는 단수: a five-minute walk, a ten-minute break. 한국인이 자주 틀리는 것: a five minutes walk (X).

senses.meaningEn: a very short time

examples.en: Wait a minute, I'm almost ready.
Do you have a minute to talk?

senses.note: Just a minute. / Hold on a minute. = 잠시만요. 실제로 1분을 뜻하는 게 아니라 '잠깐'. 형용사 minute(/maɪˈnuːt/, 아주 작은)는 발음이 다르다.

senses.meaningEn: a piece of glass that you can see yourself in

examples.en: She looked at herself in the mirror.
There's a big mirror in the bathroom.

senses.note: 거울'을' 보다는 look in the mirror(at ✗). 자동차 뒷거울은 rearview mirror, 사이드미러는 side mirror.

senses.meaningEn: to fail to catch a bus, train, or chance

examples.en: Hurry, or we'll miss the bus!
I missed the last train and took a taxi.

senses.meaningEn: to feel sad because someone or something is not with you

examples.en: I miss you so much. Come visit soon.
examples.ko: 너무 보고 싶어. 빨리 놀러 와.

examples.en: Do you miss Korean food when you travel?
examples.ko: 여행 가면 한국 음식 그립지 않아?

senses.note: '보고 싶다'를 want to see 로 직역하지 말고 miss 를 쓰면 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: to not go to a class, meeting, or event

examples.en: I missed class yesterday because I was sick.
Don't miss the meeting at three.

senses.meaningEn: something you do wrong by accident

examples.en: I made a few mistakes on the test.
Don't worry. Everyone makes mistakes.

senses.note: make a mistake(do a mistake 는 틀림!). by mistake = 실수로(I took your bag by mistake). spelling mistake = 철자 실수.

senses.meaningEn: to think wrongly that one person or thing is another

examples.en: Sorry, I mistook you for my friend.
People often mistake me for my sister.

senses.note: mistake A for B = A 를 B 로 착각하다. 과거형 mistook, 과거분사 mistaken. You're mistaken. = 네가 잘못 알고 있어.

senses.meaningEn: to combine two or more things so they become one

examples.en: Mix the eggs and sugar in a bowl.
Mix the rice well with the sauce.

senses.note: mix A with B / mix A and B. 비빔밥은 mixed rice 로 설명 가능. 재료를 저어 섞으면 stir.

senses.meaningEn: a powder you add water or milk to in order to make food

examples.en: I bought a pancake mix at the store.
Just add water to the cake mix.

senses.meaningEn: to think that one person or thing is another

examples.en: I always mix up the twins. They look the same.
examples.ko: 나는 그 쌍둥이를 늘 헷갈려. 똑같이 생겼거든.

examples.en: Sorry, I mixed up the dates of the meeting.

senses.note: mix A up with B = A 를 B 와 혼동하다. 'I got mixed up.' = 내가 헷갈렸어. 명사 mix-up(착오): There was a mix-up with the order.

senses.meaningEn: to put things together so they are no longer in order

examples.en: Someone mixed up all the papers on my desk.
examples.ko: 누가 내 책상 위 서류를 다 뒤섞어 놨어.

examples.en: Don't mix up the clean socks with the dirty ones.
examples.ko: 깨끗한 양말을 더러운 양말과 섞지 마.

senses.note: mix(섞다)와 달리 mix up 은 '섞여서 엉망·순서가 틀어진' 부정적 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: using the newest ideas, designs, or technology

examples.en: They live in a modern apartment downtown.
This kitchen looks very modern and clean.
examples.ko: 이 주방은 아주 현대적이고 깔끔해 보여.

senses.note: 건물·디자인·생활 방식에 자주 씀: modern art, modern life. '최신형 기기'는 the latest phone 이 더 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: belonging to the present time or the recent past, not ancient

examples.en: We're studying modern history this year.
Modern English is very different from old English.
examples.ko: 현대 영어는 고대 영어와 많이 달라.

senses.meaningEn: an informal word for mother

examples.en: Mom, can I go out and play?
My mom makes the best pancakes.
examples.ko: 우리 엄마는 팬케이크를 제일 잘 만들어.

senses.note: 미국식 mom, 영국식 mum. 직접 부를 때는 대문자 Mom. 어린아이는 mommy.

senses.meaningEn: the day of the week after Sunday and before Tuesday

examples.en: I have an English class on Monday.
Monday is the busiest day at work.

senses.note: 요일은 항상 대문자로 쓰고 전치사는 on 을 쓴다(on Monday). on Mondays = 월요일마다. this/next/last Monday 앞에는 전치사 없음. Monday blues = 월요병.

senses.meaningEn: coins and bills that you use to buy things

examples.en: I don't have enough money for a new phone.
examples.ko: 새 휴대폰 살 돈이 충분하지 않아.

examples.en: How much money did you spend today?

senses.note: 불가산 명사: a money, moneys 는 틀림. much money / a lot of money. 돈을 '벌다'는 make/earn money, '쓰다'는 spend money, '모으다'는 save money.

senses.meaningEn: an animal with a long tail that climbs trees and is similar to humans

examples.en: The monkeys at the zoo were eating bananas.
A monkey took my hat on the mountain!

senses.note: 복수형은 monkeys(monkies 아님). 꼬리 없는 큰 유인원(고릴라·침팬지)은 ape. monkey around = 장난치다(비격식). 장난꾸러기 아이를 little monkey 라고 부름.

senses.meaningEn: one of the twelve parts of a year, about four weeks

examples.en: My birthday is next month.
We pay rent at the beginning of each month.

senses.note: 복수 months 의 발음(/mʌnθs/)이 어렵다면 th 를 가볍게 발음해도 통함. 한국인이 자주 틀리는 것: '한 달에 두 번'은 twice a month, '다음 달에'는 next month(in 없이). 월 이름(January 등)은 대문자로 쓴다.

senses.meaningEn: happening or done once every month

examples.en: How much is your monthly rent?
I pay my phone bill monthly.

senses.note: monthly rent(월세), monthly salary(월급), monthly pass(한 달 정기권). 형용사·부사 모두 같은 형태.

senses.meaningEn: the way you feel at a particular time

examples.en: Dad is in a good mood today.
Don't talk to her now. She's in a bad mood.
examples.ko: 지금 그녀한테 말 걸지 마. 기분이 안 좋아.

senses.note: be in a good/bad mood 가 핵심 표현. be in the mood for + 명사 = ~가 당기다: I'm in the mood for pizza. / I'm not in the mood.(그럴 기분 아니야).

senses.meaningEn: the round object that shines in the sky at night

examples.en: Look, the moon is so bright tonight!
examples.ko: 봐, 오늘 밤 달이 정말 밝다!

examples.en: There's a full moon on Chuseok.

senses.note: full moon(보름달), new moon(초승달/삭), half moon(반달). once in a blue moon = 아주 드물게. over the moon = 너무 기뻐서(영국식 구어).

senses.meaningEn: almost, or mostly

examples.en: The homework is more or less finished.
We more or less agree on the plan.

senses.note: '완전히는 아니지만 거의' 라는 뜻. 대답으로 More or less. 하면 '대체로 그래' 라는 애매한 긍정.

senses.meaningEn: approximately; used with numbers and amounts

examples.en: It costs fifty dollars, more or less.
The trip takes two hours, more or less.
examples.ko: 가는 데 대략 두 시간쯤 걸려.

senses.note: 숫자 뒤에 콤마를 찍고 붙이는 형태가 자연스러움. about/around 와 같은 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: the early part of the day, from when you wake up until noon

examples.en: I drink coffee every morning.
The meeting is at ten in the morning.

senses.note: in the morning(아침에) 이지만 this/tomorrow/yesterday morning 앞에는 전치사 없음. on Monday morning(요일과 함께는 on). Good morning! 은 정오 전까지 쓰는 인사. 발음은 mourning(애도)과 같다.

senses.meaningEn: a small flying insect that bites people and drinks blood

examples.en: A mosquito bit me on the leg last night.
Close the window or the mosquitoes will come in.
examples.ko: 창문 닫아, 안 그러면 모기 들어와.

senses.note: 복수형은 mosquitoes. 모기에 물린 자국은 a mosquito bite, 모기약은 mosquito spray/repellent.

senses.meaningEn: almost all of a group

examples.en: Most people here speak English.
I spend most of my time at home.

senses.note: most people(대부분의 사람) 에는 the 를 붙이지 않음. most of + the/my + 명사(most of my friends). almost people ✗ → most people.

senses.meaningEn: used to make the superlative of longer adjectives and adverbs

examples.en: This is the most interesting book I've read.
examples.ko: 이건 내가 읽은 책 중에 가장 재미있어.

examples.en: What do you like most about your job?

senses.note: 2음절 이상 형용사 앞에 the most(the most beautiful). 짧은 형용사는 -est(the biggest). the most biggest ✗.

senses.meaningEn: a female parent

examples.en: My mother works at a hospital.
Her mother is a wonderful cook.

senses.note: 격식적·중립적 표현. 직접 부를 때는 보통 Mom 을 씀. Mother's Day = 어머니의 날.

senses.meaningEn: a road vehicle with two wheels and an engine

examples.en: My brother rides a motorcycle to work.
You must wear a helmet on a motorcycle.
examples.ko: 오토바이 탈 때는 꼭 헬멧을 써야 해.

senses.note: 한국어 '오토바이(autobike)'는 영어에 없는 말. 미국식 motorcycle, 영국·구어 motorbike. 배달용 소형 스쿠터는 scooter. 오토바이를 '타다'는 ride a motorcycle.

senses.meaningEn: a very high hill

examples.en: We climbed the mountain last weekend.
There is snow on top of the mountain.

senses.note: '등산하다'는 climb a mountain 또는 go hiking. 산 이름 앞에는 Mount(Mt.)를 붙임: Mt. Halla. mountain 은 hill 보다 훨씬 높음.

senses.meaningEn: a small animal with a pointed nose, a long thin tail, and gray or brown fur

examples.en: There's a mouse in the kitchen!
Our cat caught two mice last night.
examples.ko: 우리 고양이가 어젯밤에 쥐 두 마리를 잡았어.

senses.note: 복수형은 mice(mouses 는 틀림). mouse 는 작은 생쥐, rat 은 더 큰 시궁쥐. 쥐 소리는 squeak.

senses.meaningEn: a small device you move with your hand to control a computer

examples.en: My mouse isn't working. Can I borrow yours?
examples.ko: 내 마우스가 안 돼. 네 거 좀 빌려줄래?

examples.en: Click the right button on the mouse.

senses.note: 컴퓨터 마우스의 복수형은 mice 와 mouses 둘 다 쓰지만 보통 mice. wireless mouse(무선 마우스), mouse pad(마우스 패드).

senses.meaningEn: the part of your face that you eat and speak with

examples.en: Open your mouth and say 'ah'.
Don't talk with your mouth full.

senses.note: 입을 다물다 = close your mouth, 입이 마르다 = my mouth is dry. 복수 mouths 는 발음이 /maʊðz/.

senses.meaningEn: to change position, or to put something in a different place

examples.en: Can you move your car, please?
Don't move, there's a bee on your arm.

senses.note: move over = 옆으로 좀 가다 (자리 비켜 줄 때). move the chair = 의자를 옮기다.

senses.meaningEn: to go to live in a different house or city

examples.en: We moved to Seoul last year.
She's moving to a new apartment next month.
examples.ko: 그녀는 다음 달에 새 아파트로 이사해.

senses.note: move to + 장소. move in(입주하다), move out(이사 나가다). "이사하다"를 move house 라고도 함(영국).

senses.meaningEn: to make someone feel strong emotions, especially sadness or sympathy

examples.en: The movie really moved me.
I was moved by her kind words.

senses.note: be moved by ~ = ~에 감동하다. 형용사 moving = 감동적인 (a moving story).

senses.meaningEn: to start living in a new home

examples.en: We moved in last Saturday.
When can I move in to the new apartment?
examples.ko: 새 아파트에 언제 들어갈 수 있어요?

senses.note: move in = 들어가 살기 시작하다. '이사하다' 전체는 move: We're moving next month. 입주 날은 move-in date.

senses.meaningKo: (move in with) ~와 같이 살기 시작하다, 동거하다
senses.meaningEn: to start living together with someone

examples.en: She moved in with her boyfriend in May.
My brother moved in with me for a while.
examples.ko: 형이 한동안 우리 집에 들어와 살았어.

senses.note: move in with + 사람. 연인끼리 '동거하다'는 이 표현이 가장 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: to stop talking about or doing one thing and start another

examples.en: OK, let's move on to the next question.
We're out of time, so let's move on.

senses.note: move on to + 다음 항목. 회의·수업에서 아주 자주 쓰는 표현.

senses.meaningKo: (안 좋은 일을) 잊고 앞으로 나아가다, 털어내다
senses.meaningEn: to accept that a bad experience is over and start living normally again

examples.en: It's been a year. You need to move on.
examples.ko: 1년이나 지났어. 이제 잊고 앞으로 나아가야 해.

examples.en: After the breakup, it took him months to move on.
examples.ko: 헤어진 뒤 그가 털어내는 데 몇 달이 걸렸어.

senses.note: 이별·실패 뒤 '이제 그만 잊어'라고 할 때 가장 흔한 표현. move on from + 일.

senses.meaningEn: to leave a place or job and go somewhere else

examples.en: We stayed two nights and then moved on to Busan.
examples.ko: 우리는 이틀 밤 자고 부산으로 이동했어.

examples.en: He moved on to a new company last year.

senses.note: 여행 중 다음 도시로 이동하거나, 이직할 때. 'time to move on' = 떠날 때가 됐다.

senses.meaningEn: to stop living in a home and leave it

examples.en: I moved out of my parents' house at twenty.
examples.ko: 나는 스무 살에 부모님 집에서 나왔어.

examples.en: The tenants are moving out at the end of the month.

senses.note: move out of + 집. 부모 집에서 독립하는 것도 move out. '이사 나가는 날'은 move-out date.

senses.meaningKo: (자리를 내주려고) 옆으로 비키다, 좀 당겨 앉다
senses.meaningEn: to change your position so that there is space for someone else

examples.en: Move over a little so I can sit down.
examples.ko: 내가 앉을 수 있게 옆으로 좀 가 줘.

examples.en: Can you move over? There's room for three.
examples.ko: 좀 비켜 줄래? 세 명 앉을 수 있어.

senses.note: 앉은 자리에서 옆으로 당겨 앉을 때. 미국 구어는 scoot over 도 흔함. 비켜서 지나가게 할 때는 move aside / excuse me.

senses.meaningEn: to drive to a different lane, usually to let someone pass

examples.en: Move over and let the ambulance pass.
The truck moved over to the right lane.

senses.note: move over to the left/right lane. 운전 중 뒤차가 재촉하면 'Just move over.'

senses.meaningEn: a story shown in moving pictures that you watch at a cinema or at home

examples.en: Do you want to watch a movie tonight?
That movie was so funny!

senses.note: 미국식은 movie, 영국식은 film. 영화관은 미국 movie theater, 영국 cinema. '영화 보러 가다' = go to the movies(복수형).

senses.meaningEn: a place where people pay to watch movies on a big screen

examples.en: The movie theater is on the top floor of the mall.
Popcorn at the movie theater is so expensive!

senses.note: 미국식 표현. 영국은 cinema. 'go to the movies' 라고 하면 영화관에 간다는 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: a title used before a man's family name

examples.en: Good morning, Mr. Kim.
Mr. Brown is our new teacher.

senses.note: 반드시 성(family name) 앞에 붙임. Mr. Minsu(이름)는 틀림. 미국식은 마침표를 찍고(Mr.), 영국식은 생략(Mr). 한국의 '선생님'처럼 상대 직업과 상관없이 쓸 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: a title used before a married woman's family name

examples.en: Mrs. Lee lives next door to us.
Thank you for the cookies, Mrs. Park.

senses.note: 결혼 여부를 모르면 Ms. 를 쓰는 것이 안전함. 발음은 '미시즈'.

senses.meaningKo: ~씨 (결혼 여부와 상관없이 여성 성 앞에 붙이는 호칭)
senses.meaningEn: a title used before a woman's family name, whether she is married or not

examples.en: Ms. Choi is my English teacher.
Can I speak to Ms. Johnson, please?

senses.note: 발음은 '미즈'. 직장·이메일에서 여성에게 가장 무난한 호칭. Miss(미혼)·Mrs.(기혼)와 구별.

senses.meaningEn: a large amount of something that cannot be counted

examples.en: I don't have much time today.
There isn't much milk left.

senses.note: much + 셀 수 없는 명사(time, money, water). 주로 부정문·의문문에 쓰고, 긍정문에는 a lot of 가 자연스러움(I have much money ✗).

senses.meaningEn: used to ask about a price or an amount

examples.en: How much is this bag?
How much sugar do you want?

senses.note: 가격은 항상 How much (How many ✗). 셀 수 있는 수는 How many.

senses.meaningEn: to a great degree, often used with comparatives

examples.en: Thank you so much for your help.
I feel much better today.

senses.note: 비교급 강조는 much(much better). very better ✗. very much 는 동사 뒤(I like it very much).

senses.meaningEn: soft wet earth

examples.en: My shoes are covered in mud.
The kids love playing in the mud.

senses.note: 불가산. 진흙투성이의 = muddy(muddy shoes). 머드 축제 = mud festival.

senses.meaningEn: to add a number to itself a certain number of times

examples.en: Multiply four by six to get twenty-four.
I can multiply, but dividing is harder.
examples.ko: 곱셈은 할 수 있는데 나눗셈은 더 어려워.

senses.note: multiply A by B = A 에 B 를 곱하다. 식은 four times six 로 읽음. 명사 multiplication(곱셈), 구구단은 times table.

senses.meaningEn: a building where old, interesting, or beautiful things are shown to people

examples.en: The museum is free on Sundays.
We saw dinosaur bones at the museum.

senses.note: 강세는 두 번째 음절 /mjuˈziːəm/. 미술관은 art museum 또는 gallery. 복수형은 museums.

senses.meaningEn: a soft plant with a round top and a stem, often used in cooking

examples.en: I'd like a mushroom pizza, please.
Don't eat wild mushrooms you don't know.

senses.note: 버섯은 셀 수 있는 명사(mushrooms). 송이·표고 등은 pine mushroom, shiitake.

senses.meaningEn: the school subject where you sing and learn about sounds and songs

examples.en: We sang a new song in music class.
Our music teacher plays the guitar.

senses.meaningEn: sounds made by instruments or voices that people enjoy listening to

examples.en: I listen to music on the bus.
What kind of music do you like?

senses.note: listen to music(to 필수). 셀 수 없는 명사: a music ✗, musics ✗. 노래 한 곡은 a song. musician = 음악가.

senses.meaningEn: a person who plays an instrument or writes music, especially as a job

examples.en: The musicians played all night at the party.
He is a jazz musician from New Orleans.

senses.note: music 은 /ˈmjuːzɪk/, musician 은 강세가 둘째 음절 /mjuˈzɪʃən/ 으로 옮겨감. 가수는 singer, 악기 연주자는 player(guitar player).

senses.meaningEn: used to say that something is necessary or required

examples.en: You must wear a seat belt in the car.
Students must finish the test by noon.

senses.note: 과거형이 없어서 '해야 했다' 는 had to. mustn't = 하면 안 된다(금지), don't have to = 할 필요 없다 — 뜻이 전혀 다름!

senses.meaningEn: used to say that you are sure something is true

examples.en: You must be tired after that long flight.
That must be Jake at the door.

senses.note: You must be ~ = ~하시겠네요(공감). 반대 추측(~일 리가 없다)은 mustn't 가 아니라 can't be.

senses.meaningEn: something you really need to do, see, or have

examples.en: This beach is a must when you visit Busan.
examples.ko: 부산에 가면 이 해변은 꼭 가 봐야 해.

examples.en: A warm coat is a must in winter here.

senses.note: a must = 필수 항목(명사처럼). must-see(꼭 봐야 할 것), must-have(필수품).

senses.meaningEn: belonging to the person speaking

examples.en: This is my sister, Jiho.
I left my keys at home again.

senses.note: 항상 뒤에 명사가 옴(my bag). 명사 없이 쓰려면 mine. 한국어 "우리 엄마"는 영어로 my mom(our mom 아님).

senses.meaningEn: a casual way to say that something was your fault and you are sorry

examples.en: Oh, that was your seat? My bad.
My bad, I forgot to text you back.

senses.note: 아주 가벼운 사과. 작은 실수에만 쓰고 진지한 사과에는 I'm sorry / I apologize. 어른·상사에게는 쓰지 않는다.

senses.meaningEn: the hard part at the end of your finger or toe

examples.en: I need to cut my nails.
Stop biting your nails!

senses.note: 손톱 fingernail, 발톱 toenail. 네일숍 = nail salon, 매니큐어 = nail polish(manicure 는 손톱 관리 서비스).

senses.meaningEn: a thin pointed piece of metal that you hit into wood

examples.en: Hang the picture on that nail.
Be careful, there's a nail on the floor.

senses.note: 못을 박다 = hammer a nail / nail something to the wall(동사로도 씀). 나사는 screw.

senses.meaningEn: the word that someone or something is called by

examples.en: What's your name?
My name is Minsu, nice to meet you.

senses.note: first name(이름) / last name, family name(성). full name = 성명. 영어는 이름을 먼저 말함.

senses.meaningEn: to give a name to a person, animal, or thing

examples.en: They named their baby Emma.
We named the dog Max.

senses.note: name A B = A 를 B 라고 이름 짓다. be named after = ~의 이름을 따서 짓다.

senses.meaningEn: to say the names of people or things

examples.en: Can you name three colors?
examples.ko: 색깔 세 가지 말해 볼 수 있어?

examples.en: Name a country that starts with K.
examples.ko: K 로 시작하는 나라 하나 말해 봐.

senses.note: 퀴즈·수업에서 자주 쓰는 표현. Name it! = 뭐든 말만 해!

senses.meaningEn: a piece of paper or cloth used at meals to clean your mouth and hands

examples.en: Could I have some more napkins?
He wiped his mouth with a napkin.

senses.note: 미국에서는 식탁용 휴지가 napkin. 휴지(화장지)는 tissue / toilet paper 로 구분. 영국에서는 serviette 도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: measuring a small distance from one side to the other

examples.en: The streets in the old town are very narrow.
Be careful. The bridge is narrow.

senses.note: narrow 는 폭이 좁은 것(길·복도·침대). 방이 좁다(면적)는 small, 사람이 꽉 찬 좁음은 crowded/tight. 한국어 '좁다'를 다 narrow 로 옮기면 어색함.

senses.meaningEn: relating to a whole country, not just one part of it

examples.en: Tomorrow is a national holiday, so school is closed.
The story was on the national news last night.
examples.ko: 그 이야기는 어젯밤 전국 뉴스에 나왔어.

senses.note: national team(국가 대표팀), national park(국립공원), national anthem(국가). nation(국가) + -al.

senses.meaningEn: coming from nature, not made by people

examples.en: This juice has only natural ingredients.
examples.ko: 이 주스는 천연 재료만 들어 있어.

examples.en: I love her natural hair color.

senses.note: natural food, natural light(자연광). nature(자연) + -al.

senses.meaningEn: normal and expected in a situation

examples.en: It's natural to feel nervous before a test.
Just act natural and smile.

senses.note: It's natural to + 동사 = ~하는 게 당연하다. 위로할 때 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: everything in the world not made by people, such as plants, animals, and weather

examples.en: I love walking in nature on weekends.
examples.ko: 주말에 자연 속을 걷는 게 좋아.

examples.en: We should protect nature for our children.

senses.note: 셀 수 없고 the 를 붙이지 않음: the nature ✗ → nature ✓. in nature = 자연 속에서. nature documentary(자연 다큐). 자연재해 = natural disaster(형용사 natural).

senses.meaningEn: the way a person or thing really is

examples.en: It's not in his nature to be rude.
examples.ko: 무례한 건 그 사람 천성이 아니야.

examples.en: She's kind by nature.

senses.note: by nature = 천성적으로. human nature = 인간 본성. good-natured = 성격이 온화한.

senses.meaningEn: a short distance from a place or person

examples.en: Is there a bank near here?
I live near the subway station.

senses.note: near + 명사(전치사 to 불필요: near to 도 가능하지만 near 만 쓰는 게 더 흔함). close to 와 거의 같은 뜻. nearby = 근처의/근처에(부사·형용사).

senses.meaningEn: close in distance or time

examples.en: The nearest hospital is ten minutes away.
I'll see you in the near future.

senses.note: 비교급 nearer, 최상급 nearest. 'the nearest station' 처럼 최상급으로 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: the part of your body that joins your head to your shoulders

examples.en: I have a stiff neck from sleeping badly.
She wore a scarf around her neck.

senses.note: 한국어 '목'은 두 가지: 바깥쪽 목은 neck, 목구멍(안쪽)은 throat. '목이 아파'가 감기면 I have a sore throat, 뻐근하면 My neck hurts.

senses.meaningEn: a piece of jewelry that you wear around your neck

examples.en: She wore a gold necklace with her dress.
He gave her a necklace for her birthday.

senses.note: neck(목)+lace. 목걸이를 '하다/차다'도 wear/put on. 발음은 /ˈnekləs/ 로 'lace'를 길게 읽지 않음.

senses.meaningEn: to have to have something or do something because it is important

examples.en: I need a new umbrella; mine broke.
examples.ko: 새 우산이 필요해. 내 건 망가졌어.

examples.en: You need to drink more water.

senses.note: need + 명사 / need to + 동사. want(원하다)보다 강한 '꼭 필요함'. 부정 don't need to = ~할 필요 없다(You don't need to come).

senses.meaningEn: something that you must have or do

examples.en: There's no need to hurry; we have time.
Kids have a need for love and sleep.

senses.note: There's no need to + 동사(~할 필요 없다) 는 회화 필수 표현. in need(어려운 처지에 있는): help people in need.

senses.meaningEn: a person who lives near you

examples.en: Our neighbors are very friendly.
My next-door neighbor has a cute dog.

senses.note: 영국식 철자는 neighbour. next-door neighbor = 바로 옆집 사람. gh 는 묵음.

senses.meaningEn: a person or thing that is next to another

examples.en: Please share the book with your neighbor.
Turn to your neighbor and say hello.

senses.note: 교실·행사에서 '옆자리 사람'을 가리킬 때 자주 씀. 나라끼리도 neighboring countries(이웃 나라).

senses.meaningEn: the area of a town where you live and the people who live there

examples.en: We live in a quiet neighborhood.
There's a new café in my neighborhood.

senses.note: 영국식 철자는 neighbourhood. '이웃 사람'은 neighbor. in the neighborhood = 근처에.

senses.meaningEn: worried and a little afraid about something that is going to happen

examples.en: I always get nervous before a test.
Don't be nervous. You'll do great.

senses.note: nervous about + 명사. 발표·면접·시험 앞의 '떨림'에 딱 맞는 단어. 한국어 '신경질적인'과는 다름(그건 irritable).

senses.meaningEn: a home that a bird builds for its eggs and babies

examples.en: There's a bird's nest in that tree.
The baby birds are waiting in the nest.

senses.note: build a nest = 둥지를 틀다. 다 큰 자식이 독립해 집이 빈 상태를 empty nest 라고 함.

senses.meaningEn: not at any time; not ever

examples.en: I never drink coffee at night.
examples.ko: 나는 밤에 커피를 절대 안 마셔.

examples.en: Never give up on your dream.

senses.note: never 자체가 부정이라 not을 같이 쓰지 않음(I don't never go ✗ → I never go). Never mind. = 신경 쓰지 마, 괜찮아.

senses.meaningEn: not even once in your life up to now

examples.en: I have never been to Japan.
examples.ko: 나는 일본에 한 번도 가 본 적이 없어.

examples.en: He has never eaten sushi before.
examples.ko: 그는 전에 초밥을 한 번도 먹어 본 적이 없어.

senses.note: 경험을 말할 때는 have/has + never + 과거분사 형태로 씀. 질문은 Have you ever...? 로 묻고 부정 답은 never 로 함.

senses.meaningEn: used to tell someone that something is not important or to forget what you just said

examples.en: Never mind, I found my keys.
Oh, never mind. It doesn't matter.
examples.ko: 아, 신경 쓰지 마. 중요한 거 아니야.

senses.note: 방금 한 말·질문을 취소할 때(됐어, 아니야) 와 상대를 안심시킬 때(걱정 마) 모두 씀. 짜증 섞인 말투로 하면 '됐어, 말 안 할래' 처럼 들릴 수 있으니 주의.

senses.meaningEn: used to comfort someone when something has gone wrong

examples.en: You missed the bus? Never mind, there's another one soon.
examples.ko: 버스 놓쳤어? 괜찮아, 곧 다른 거 와.

examples.en: Never mind about the broken plate. I have more.
examples.ko: 접시 깨진 건 신경 쓰지 마. 더 있어.

senses.note: never mind about + 명사 로 대상을 밝힐 수 있음. 영국식에서 특히 많이 쓰는 위로 표현.

senses.meaningEn: recently made or bought, not used before

examples.en: I got a new phone last week.
Are these shoes new? They look great.

senses.note: brand new = 완전히 새것. '중고'는 used 또는 second-hand. 영국식 발음은 /njuː/.

senses.meaningEn: recently arrived at a place or recently started doing something

examples.en: I'm new here. Could you help me?
examples.ko: 제가 여기 처음이라서요. 도와주실 수 있어요?

examples.en: We have a new teacher this year.

senses.note: be new to + 장소/일 = ~에 익숙하지 않다(I'm new to this job). What's new? = 별일 없어? (안부 인사).

senses.meaningEn: coming right after this one in time or order

examples.en: See you next week!
Who's next, please?

senses.note: next week / next Monday 앞에는 전치사를 쓰지 않음(on next Monday ✗). the next day = 그 다음 날(과거 이야기).

senses.meaningEn: after this or that, in order

examples.en: What should we do next?
Next, add the eggs and mix well.

senses.meaningEn: beside; very close to something

examples.en: The bank is next to the post office.
Can I sit next to you?

senses.note: '옆에'는 꼭 next to 로 to 를 붙임. next the door ✗ → next to the door ✓.

senses.meaningEn: very close to something or someone, with nothing in between

examples.en: Can I sit next to you?
The bank is next to the post office.

senses.note: next to = beside(조금 더 격식). near 는 '가까이' 로 거리가 더 멀 수 있음. '옆 사람' 은 the person next to me.

senses.meaningEn: almost; used before words like nothing or impossible

examples.en: I got this bag for next to nothing.
Getting tickets now is next to impossible.
examples.ko: 지금 표를 구하는 건 거의 불가능해.

senses.note: next to nothing(거의 없음·공짜), next to impossible(거의 불가능) 두 표현으로 외워 두면 됨.

senses.meaningEn: pleasant, enjoyable, or good

examples.en: What a nice day! Let's go outside.
We had a nice dinner at a small restaurant.

senses.note: 거의 모든 좋은 것에 쓸 수 있는 만능 형용사. 다만 너무 자주 쓰면 밋밋하게 들리니 great, lovely, delicious 등으로 바꿔 보자.

senses.meaningEn: kind and friendly to other people

examples.en: Thank you, that's very nice of you.
Be nice to your little brother.

senses.note: It's nice of you to + 동사 = ~해 줘서 고마워요. Nice to meet you. 는 첫 만남 인사. 한국인이 자주 틀리는 것: 사람에 대해 쓰면 '외모가 멋지다'가 아니라 '성격이 좋다'는 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: a polite greeting you say when you meet someone for the first time

examples.en: Hi, I'm Mina. Nice to meet you.
Nice to meet you, Mr. Lee. Nice to meet you too.
examples.ko: 만나서 반갑습니다, 이 선생님. 저도 반갑습니다.

senses.note: 첫 만남에서만 씀. 두 번째 만남부터는 Nice to see you(again). 답은 Nice to meet you too / You too. 헤어질 때는 It was nice meeting you. 격식: Pleased to meet you / How do you do?

senses.meaningEn: the time when it is dark and most people sleep

examples.en: I couldn't sleep last night.
The stars are bright at night in the countryside.

senses.note: at night(밤에)는 at 을 쓰고 in the night 은 '한밤중에 (무슨 일이 일어남)'의 느낌. last night = 어젯밤(yesterday night X). Good night! 은 잘 자라는 인사. 발음은 knight(기사)와 같다.

senses.meaningEn: one stay of a night at a hotel or someone's home

examples.en: We stayed in Busan for three nights.
The hotel costs 100 dollars a night.

senses.note: 호텔 요금은 per night / a night(1박당). 2박 3일 = three days and two nights, 혹은 간단히 two nights. 친구 집에 하루 자고 가는 것은 stay the night / stay over.

senses.meaningEn: the number 9

examples.en: The store opens at nine in the morning.
examples.ko: 그 가게는 아침 아홉 시에 열어.

examples.en: Nine people came to the party.

senses.note: 서수는 ninth(9th, e 가 빠짐). nineteen(19), ninety(90)는 e 를 그대로 둠. 미국 긴급 전화 911은 nine one one 으로 읽음.

senses.meaningEn: the number 19

examples.en: My sister is nineteen and goes to college.
examples.ko: 우리 누나는 열아홉 살이고 대학에 다녀.

examples.en: I was born in nineteen ninety-nine.

senses.note: 연도는 두 자리씩 끊어 읽음: 1999 = nineteen ninety-nine, 1980 = nineteen eighty. 2000년대 이후는 two thousand (and) five 또는 twenty twenty-five.

senses.meaningEn: the number 90

examples.en: My grandfather is ninety years old.
The bus takes about ninety minutes.

senses.note: ninety(90)와 nineteen(19)은 강세로 구별: NINE-ty / nine-TEEN. 90년대 = the nineties.

senses.meaningEn: used to give a negative answer or to refuse

examples.en: Do you want more rice? No, thanks. I'm full.
examples.ko: 밥 더 먹을래? 아니, 괜찮아. 배불러.

examples.en: No, I didn't see him today.
examples.ko: 아니, 오늘 그 사람 못 봤어.

senses.note: 거절은 No, thank you. 가 정중함. 부정 의문문 Don't you like it? 에 싫으면 No, I don't. — 한국어 '네, 안 좋아해요'와 반대이니 주의.

senses.meaningEn: not any; not one

examples.en: There's no milk left in the fridge.
I have no time to play today.

senses.note: no + 명사 = not any + 명사: There's no milk = There isn't any milk. 표지판: No parking(주차 금지), No smoking(금연).

senses.meaningEn: used to say that something will happen or stay true whatever happens

examples.en: I'll always love you, no matter what.
examples.ko: 무슨 일이 있어도 난 항상 널 사랑해.

examples.en: No matter what happens, don't give up.
