examples.en: They want to settle down and have kids.
examples.ko: 그들은 정착해서 아이를 갖고 싶어 해.

examples.en: After years of travel, he settled down in Jeju.
examples.ko: 몇 년을 떠돌다가 그는 제주에 정착했어.

senses.note: settle down with someone = ~와 가정을 꾸리다. 어른이 되어 한곳에 자리 잡는 그림.

senses.meaningEn: to become calm and quiet after being excited or noisy

examples.en: Settle down, kids! The movie is starting.
It took a while for the class to settle down.
examples.ko: 반 아이들이 조용해지기까지 시간이 좀 걸렸어.

senses.note: calm down 과 비슷하지만 settle down 은 '소란·흥분이 가라앉아 자리에 앉는' 느낌. 선생님·부모가 자주 쓰는 말.

senses.meaningEn: to start to feel comfortable in a new home, school, or job

examples.en: Have you settled down in your new school?
It took me a month to settle down at work.
examples.ko: 회사에 자리 잡는 데 한 달 걸렸어.

senses.note: 이 뜻은 settle in 이 더 흔함. settle down to work = (딴짓 멈추고) 일에 집중하기 시작하다.

senses.meaningEn: the number 7

examples.en: There are seven days in a week.
Dinner is at seven, so don't be late.

senses.note: 서수는 seventh(7th). seventeen(17), seventy(70). 서양에서 7은 행운의 숫자(lucky seven). 편의점 이름 7-Eleven 도 seven.

senses.meaningEn: the number 17

examples.en: My cousin is seventeen and in high school.
Our flight leaves from gate seventeen.

senses.note: sevenTEEN(17) vs SEVenty(70). 서수는 seventeenth(17th).

senses.meaningEn: the number 70

examples.en: My grandmother is seventy, but she still works.
The speed limit here is seventy.

senses.note: SEVenty(70) vs sevenTEEN(17). 미국 고속도로 제한 속도는 보통 마일 단위로 65~70. the seventies = 1970년대.

senses.meaningEn: more than two but not many

examples.en: I called you several times yesterday.
There are several good cafes near here.
examples.ko: 이 근처에 좋은 카페가 여러 곳 있어.

senses.note: a few(2~3개) 보다 조금 많은 느낌(3~7개 정도). 항상 복수 명사와 씀. several of us = 우리 중 몇 명.

senses.meaningEn: the dark shape made when something blocks the light

examples.en: My shadow is very long in the evening.
The cat was scared of its own shadow.

senses.note: shadow 는 물체 모양의 '그림자', shade 는 그늘(시원한 곳). sit in the shade = 그늘에 앉다.

senses.meaningEn: to move quickly up and down or from side to side

examples.en: Shake the bottle well before you open it.
The whole house shook during the earthquake.

senses.note: milkshake 의 shake. 자동사·타동사 모두 가능.

senses.meaningEn: to hold someone's hand and move it up and down as a greeting

examples.en: We shook hands and introduced ourselves.
He shook my hand firmly.
examples.ko: 그는 내 손을 꽉 잡고 악수했어.

senses.note: shake hands with 사람 / shake sb's hand. hands 는 항상 복수.

senses.meaningEn: to move your head from side to side to mean no

examples.en: She shook her head and said no.
Dad just shook his head at my joke.

senses.note: 고개를 끄덕이는 건 nod. shake your head = 부정·실망.

senses.meaningEn: to tremble because you are cold, afraid, or nervous

examples.en: I was shaking with cold at the bus stop.
Her voice shook when she started to speak.
examples.ko: 말을 시작할 때 그녀의 목소리가 떨렸어.

senses.note: be shaking with cold/fear. 추워서 떠는 건 shiver 도 많이 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to get rid of an illness, a feeling, or a bad habit

examples.en: I can't shake off this cold.
She shook off her nerves and walked on stage.
examples.ko: 그녀는 긴장을 털어 내고 무대로 걸어 나갔어.

senses.note: shake off a cold / a feeling / a bad habit. 몸을 흔들어 떨어내는 그림. shake(흔들다)의 과거 shook, 과거분사 shaken.

senses.meaningEn: to escape from someone who is following or chasing you

examples.en: The runner shook off the others in the last lap.
examples.ko: 그 선수는 마지막 바퀴에서 다른 선수들을 따돌렸어.

examples.en: He shook off the defender and scored.

senses.note: 경기·추격 상황에서 자주 쓰임. 명사 shake 와 혼동 주의.

senses.meaningEn: used in questions to make a suggestion or offer

examples.en: Shall we go for a walk?
Shall I open the window?

senses.note: 미국 영어에서는 Shall we/I ~? 로 제안할 때만 거의 쓰임. 다른 자리에서는 Should I ~? / Let's ~ 가 더 자연스러움. 대답은 Yes, let's. / Sure.

senses.meaningEn: used in formal or legal writing to say what will or must happen

examples.en: Each member shall pay a yearly fee.
I shall return before dark.

senses.note: 계약서·규정의 shall = must. 일상 대화에서 I shall ~ 은 매우 격식적이거나 옛스러운 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: the outer form of something, such as a circle or square

examples.en: What shape is the box? It is a square.
The cloud had the shape of a heart.

senses.note: in the shape of ~ (~ 모양의). 색은 color, 모양은 shape, 크기는 size.

senses.meaningEn: the physical condition of a person or thing

examples.en: He runs every day to stay in shape.
I am out of shape after the holidays.
examples.ko: 연휴 지나고 나니 몸이 다 망가졌어.

senses.note: in shape(건강한, 몸이 좋은) / out of shape(운동 부족인). get in shape = 몸을 만들다.

senses.meaningEn: to have or use something together with other people

examples.en: Let's share this pizza; it's too big.
examples.ko: 이 피자 너무 커서 같이 나눠 먹자.

examples.en: I share a room with my sister.

senses.note: share A with B. 식당에서 'Do you want to share?' = 나눠 먹을래? 한국어 '쉐어하다'와 같은 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: to tell others about something or post it so they can see it

examples.en: She shared the photos in our group chat.
Thank you for sharing your story with us.

senses.note: SNS 의 '공유'도 share. share your thoughts = 생각을 말해 주다.

senses.meaningEn: a large sea fish with sharp teeth that can be dangerous

examples.en: Are there sharks in this water?
The shark swam right under our boat.
examples.ko: 상어가 우리 배 바로 밑으로 지나갔어.

senses.note: shark fin(상어 지느러미), shark attack(상어 공격). 비격식으로 '남을 속여 돈을 뜯는 사람'(loan shark = 고리대금업자)을 뜻하기도 함. 발음 주의: shark /ʃɑːrk/ 와 shock /ʃɑːk/.

senses.meaningEn: having a thin edge or point that can cut

examples.en: Be careful. This knife is very sharp.
examples.ko: 조심해. 이 칼 아주 잘 들어.

examples.en: I need a sharp pencil for the test.
examples.ko: 시험 볼 때 쓸 잘 깎은 연필이 필요해.

senses.note: 칼이 '잘 든다'는 sharp, 안 든다는 dull/blunt. 연필을 깎는 기구는 sharpener.

senses.meaningEn: sudden and strong (used about pain)

examples.en: I felt a sharp pain in my chest.
There's a sharp pain when I bend my knee.

senses.note: a sharp pain(찌르는 통증) ↔ a dull pain(둔한 통증). 병원에서 통증을 설명할 때 유용.

senses.meaningEn: exactly at the time stated

examples.en: The meeting starts at nine sharp.
Be here at six sharp. Don't be late.

senses.note: 숫자 시각 뒤에 sharp 를 붙이면 '정각, 딱 그 시간에'. 비슷한 표현은 on the dot. 머리가 '좋다, 예리하다' 는 a sharp mind.

senses.meaningEn: a female person or animal that has already been mentioned, as the subject

examples.en: She works at the hospital.
This is my mom. She loves cooking.

senses.note: 목적어 her, 소유 her/hers. 한국인은 말할 때 he/she 를 자주 섞어 쓰니 의식적으로 연습할 것.

senses.meaningEn: a farm animal with a thick woolly coat, kept for its wool and meat

examples.en: There are hundreds of sheep on that hill.
examples.ko: 저 언덕에 양이 수백 마리 있어.

examples.en: I can't sleep, so I'm counting sheep.
examples.ko: 잠이 안 와서 양을 세고 있어.

senses.note: 단수·복수 모두 sheep(sheeps 는 틀림). 새끼 양은 lamb, 양고기도 lamb, 양털은 wool. count sheep = 잠들려고 양을 세다.

senses.meaningEn: a flat board on a wall or in a cupboard where you put things

examples.en: Put the books back on the shelf, please.
examples.ko: 책들을 다시 선반에 올려 놔 줘.

examples.en: The cups are on the top shelf.

senses.note: 복수형 shelves. 책장 전체는 bookshelf / bookcase. 가게 진열대도 shelf: on the shelves = 진열 중.

senses.meaningEn: to give out or reflect bright light

examples.en: The sun is shining, so let's go outside.
The stars shone brightly over the lake.

senses.note: 과거형 shone(/ʃoʊn/). 날씨 표현 The sun is shining. 명사 sunshine(햇빛).

senses.meaningEn: to point a light at something, or to polish something until it is bright

examples.en: Shine the flashlight over here, please.
He shined his shoes before the interview.
examples.ko: 그는 면접 전에 신발을 닦아 광을 냈어.

senses.note: "닦아서 빛내다" 뜻일 때는 과거형이 shined. shiny = 반짝이는(형용사).

senses.meaningEn: a large boat that carries people or goods across the sea

examples.en: The ship leaves the port at nine.
My grandfather worked on a big ship.

senses.note: 바다를 건너는 큰 배. cruise ship(크루즈), cargo ship(화물선). 작은 배는 boat.

senses.meaningEn: to send goods to a customer or another place

examples.en: Your order will ship tomorrow.
They shipped the package to my office.
examples.ko: 그 사람들이 소포를 내 사무실로 보냈어.

senses.note: 배가 아니라 트럭·비행기로 보내도 ship 이라고 함. 온라인 쇼핑에서 shipping = 배송(비), free shipping = 무료 배송.

senses.meaningEn: a piece of clothing with sleeves and buttons worn on the top half of the body

examples.en: He wore a white shirt and a blue tie.
examples.ko: 그는 흰 셔츠에 파란 넥타이를 했어.

examples.en: This shirt is too big for me.

senses.note: 한국어 '와이셔츠'는 dress shirt. 단추 없는 상의는 top 이라고 두루 부름.

senses.meaningEn: things you wear on your feet, usually made of leather or cloth

examples.en: Please take off your shoes at the door.
I need new shoes for school.
examples.ko: 학교 갈 때 신을 새 신발이 필요해.

senses.note: 보통 복수형, a pair of shoes. 신다/벗다 = put on / take off. 신발 가게는 shoe store(단수형으로 수식).

senses.meaningEn: a small building or room where you can buy things

examples.en: There's a little coffee shop on the corner.
The shop closes at nine tonight.

senses.note: 영국에서는 shop, 미국에서는 store 를 더 많이 씀. 미국에서 shop 은 coffee shop, gift shop 처럼 작은 전문점에 주로 붙음.

senses.meaningEn: to go to shops and buy things

examples.en: I usually shop for food on Saturdays.
We went shopping at the mall yesterday.

senses.note: '쇼핑하러 가다'는 go shopping. shop for + 물건(식료품 등을 사다). 온라인은 shop online.

senses.meaningEn: to compare prices or quality in different shops before buying something

examples.en: Shop around before you buy a new phone.
examples.ko: 새 폰 사기 전에 여러 곳 비교해 봐.

examples.en: We shopped around and found a cheaper flight.
examples.ko: 여기저기 알아보다가 더 싼 항공편을 찾았어.

senses.note: 물건뿐 아니라 보험·대출·직장(shop around for a job)에도 씀. shop around for + 사고 싶은 것.

senses.meaningEn: a list of the things you need to buy at a store

examples.en: Did you bring the shopping list?
Add milk and eggs to the shopping list.

senses.note: 식료품만 살 때는 grocery list 라고도 함. '쇼핑 목록에 올리다'는 put/add ~ on the list.

senses.meaningEn: having less than average height

examples.en: I'm a little short, so I can't reach the top shelf.
examples.ko: 내가 키가 좀 작아서 맨 위 칸에 손이 안 닿아.

examples.en: My sister is shorter than me.

senses.note: 키가 작다는 short, small 이 아니다. small 은 몸집이 작다는 뜻에 가깝다.

senses.meaningEn: small in length or lasting only a little time

examples.en: She has short hair now.
It's just a short walk to the station.

senses.note: short break(짧은 휴식), short answer(짧은 대답), for short(줄여서) 등으로 자주 쓴다.

senses.meaningEn: short pants that end above the knee

examples.en: It's hot, so I'm wearing shorts today.
He plays basketball in shorts and a t-shirt.
examples.ko: 그는 반바지에 티셔츠 입고 농구를 해.

senses.note: 항상 복수형, a pair of shorts. 미국에서는 남성용 사각 속옷도 (boxer) shorts 라고 함.

senses.meaningEn: used to say what is the right or best thing to do

examples.en: You should see a doctor about that cough.
examples.ko: 그 기침은 병원에 가 보는 게 좋겠어.

examples.en: We shouldn't eat so late at night.
examples.ko: 우리 밤에 그렇게 늦게 먹으면 안 돼.

senses.note: must 보다 약한 '권유·조언'. 한국어 '~해야 해' 를 번역할 때 강한 의무가 아니면 should 가 자연스러움. Should I ~? = ~할까요?(조언 구하기).

senses.meaningEn: used to say that something is likely or expected

examples.en: The bus should arrive in five minutes.
It shouldn't take long to get there.
examples.ko: 거기 가는 데 오래 걸리지 않을 거야.

senses.note: '정상적이라면 ~일 것' 이라는 기대. will 보다 조금 자신 없는 예측.

senses.meaningEn: one of the two parts of your body between your neck and your arms

examples.en: My shoulders are sore from carrying the bag.
He tapped me on the shoulder.

senses.note: 보통 복수 shoulders. 어깨를 으쓱하다 = shrug your shoulders. 발음은 '쇼울더'(l 소리 약함).

senses.meaningEn: to say something very loudly

examples.en: Don't shout; I can hear you fine.
He shouted my name across the street.
examples.ko: 그가 길 건너편에서 내 이름을 크게 불렀어.

senses.note: shout at 사람 = 화나서 소리치다(부정적), shout to 사람 = 멀어서 크게 부르다. 미국 구어는 yell 을 더 많이 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to say something in a very loud voice

examples.en: Shout out the answer when you know it.
Someone shouted out my name in the street.
examples.ko: 길에서 누가 내 이름을 크게 불렀어.

senses.note: shout out + 내용(답·이름). shout at 사람 = ~에게 소리치다(화내서), shout to 사람 = 멀리 있어서 크게 부르다.

senses.meaningEn: a public message of thanks or greeting, especially on TV, radio, or social media

examples.en: I want to give a shout-out to my mom.
examples.ko: 엄마한테 공개적으로 감사 인사를 전하고 싶어요.

examples.en: The DJ gave a shout-out to all the fans.
examples.ko: DJ 가 모든 팬들에게 인사를 전했어.

senses.note: 명사는 하이픈 shout-out. give a shout-out to 사람. 유튜브·라디오에서 "shout-out to ~!" 로 매우 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: a program on television or radio

examples.en: What's your favorite TV show?
The show starts at eight tonight.

senses.note: 한국어 'TV 프로그램'은 보통 TV show 또는 program. 시리즈물은 series, 한 회는 episode.

senses.meaningEn: a performance for people to watch, such as a play or a concert

examples.en: We saw a magic show at the mall.
The show was sold out.

senses.note: fashion show, talent show, magic show 등. 연극은 play, 뮤지컬은 musical 이라고 더 구체적으로 말함.

senses.meaningEn: to let someone see something

examples.en: Show me your new phone!
She showed us pictures of her trip.

senses.note: show + 사람 + 물건(Show me the photo.) 또는 show + 물건 + to + 사람. 과거분사 shown 은 불규칙.

senses.meaningEn: to teach someone how to do something by doing it in front of them

examples.en: Can you show me how to use this app?
examples.ko: 이 앱 어떻게 쓰는지 알려 줄래?

examples.en: My dad showed me how to ride a bike.
examples.ko: 아빠가 자전거 타는 법을 가르쳐 주셨어.

senses.note: show someone how to ~ 는 직접 시범을 보이며 알려 주는 것. 말로만 설명하면 tell/explain.

senses.meaningEn: to take someone to all the parts of a place so they can see it

examples.en: Let me show you around the office.
My friend showed me around Seoul last weekend.
examples.ko: 지난 주말에 친구가 서울을 구경시켜 줬어.

senses.note: 반드시 show + 사람 + around (+ 장소) 순서. 'show around me' ✗. 새 직원·손님에게 자주 쓰는 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to try to make people notice and admire you or your things, often in an annoying way

examples.en: Stop showing off in front of the girls.
He only bought that car to show off.
examples.ko: 그는 그냥 자랑하려고 그 차를 산 거야.

senses.note: 자동사(show off)로도, 타동사(show off his new watch)로도 씀. 명사 show-off = 잘난 척하는 사람. 한국어 '플렉스하다'에 가까운 뉘앙스.

senses.meaningEn: to make something look especially good by showing it clearly

examples.en: That dress really shows off your figure.
examples.ko: 그 드레스는 네 몸매를 정말 돋보이게 해.

examples.en: The white frame shows off the photo nicely.
examples.ko: 흰 액자가 사진을 멋지게 살려 줘.

senses.note: 이 뜻은 부정적이지 않음. show off + 물건/장점.

senses.meaningEn: to arrive at a place where people are expecting you

examples.en: He showed up twenty minutes late.
Only five people showed up to the party.

senses.note: '안 오다'는 didn't show up / was a no-show. turn up 과 거의 같고, 미국에서는 show up 이 더 흔함. 구어에서 그냥 show 라고도 함(He didn't show).

senses.meaningEn: to become easy to see or notice

examples.en: The problem didn't show up on the X-ray.
Dirt really shows up on a white shirt.
examples.ko: 흰 셔츠에는 얼룩이 정말 잘 보여.

senses.note: show up on a test / a screen. 타동사로 show someone up = 남을 창피하게 만들다.

senses.meaningEn: washing your body under running water

examples.en: I take a shower every morning.
Can I have a quick shower first?

senses.note: 샤워하다 take a shower(미국) / have a shower(영국). do a shower 는 틀림. 샤워기 자체도 shower.

senses.meaningEn: a short period of rain

examples.en: There will be showers this afternoon.
Take an umbrella, we might get a shower.
examples.ko: 우산 가져가, 소나기 올 수도 있어.

senses.note: 날씨 예보에서 showers(복수)로 자주 쓴다.

senses.meaningEn: to close something

examples.en: Shut the door, please. It's noisy outside.
examples.ko: 문 좀 닫아 줘. 밖이 시끄러워.

examples.en: He shut his book and stood up.

senses.note: close 와 거의 같지만 조금 더 세고 직접적인 느낌. 과거형·과거분사 모두 shut. 가게가 문을 닫다에도 씀: The shop is shut.

senses.meaningEn: to stop talking (rude)

examples.en: Shut up, I'm trying to listen!
Oh, shut up, you're making me blush.

senses.note: 매우 무례한 표현. 정중하게는 Please be quiet. 친한 사이에서는 '에이, 그만해' 정도의 장난으로도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to turn off a computer or machine completely

examples.en: Shut down your computer before you leave.
My laptop shut down by itself.

senses.note: 컴퓨터 메뉴의 Shut Down. 잠시 끄는 건 turn off, 완전 종료는 shut down. 명사 shutdown.

senses.meaningEn: to close a business or place, often for a long time

examples.en: The factory shut down last year.
They shut down the road for repairs.

senses.meaningEn: to stop the flow of water, gas, or electricity, or stop a machine

examples.en: Shut off the water before you fix the tap.
He shut the engine off and got out.

senses.note: 수도·가스·엔진·알람에 자주. turn off 와 거의 같지만 '흐름을 차단하다' 느낌. The heat shuts off at night(자동으로 꺼진다).

senses.meaningEn: to stop talking, or to make someone stop talking

examples.en: Shut up! I'm trying to hear the TV.
examples.ko: 조용히 해! TV 소리 들으려고 하잖아.

examples.en: He just wouldn't shut up about his new car.
examples.ko: 그는 새 차 얘기를 도통 그치지 않았어.

senses.note: 매우 무례한 표현. 친한 친구 사이의 농담이 아니면 쓰지 말 것. 공손하게는 Could you please be quiet? / Please keep it down. 참고로 놀라서 'Shut up!'(말도 안 돼!) 라고 쓰는 구어 용법도 있음.

senses.meaningEn: to close a place completely, or to keep someone or something inside a closed place

examples.en: They shut up the shop for the holidays.
examples.ko: 그들은 연휴 동안 가게 문을 닫았어.

examples.en: Don't keep the dog shut up in the car.
examples.ko: 개를 차 안에 가둬 두지 마.

senses.note: shut up shop = 가게를 닫다(영업 종료·폐업). 이 뜻은 무례하지 않음.

senses.meaningEn: nervous and quiet around other people

examples.en: My daughter is shy around new people.
examples.ko: 우리 딸은 낯선 사람 앞에서 수줍어해.

examples.en: Don't be shy. Come and say hello!

senses.note: shy 는 성격(수줍음), embarrassed 는 특정 상황에서 '창피한' 느낌 — '부끄럽다' 를 둘 다 shy 로 옮기지 말 것. 명사 shyness.

senses.meaningEn: not well; having an illness

examples.en: I can't come to work today. I'm sick.
She was sick for a whole week.

senses.note: 미국에서 '아프다'의 가장 일반적인 말. get sick(병나다), call in sick(아파서 못 간다고 연락하다), sick day(병가).

senses.meaningKo: 속이 안 좋은, 토할 것 같은
senses.meaningEn: feeling like you are going to vomit

examples.en: I feel sick on long bus rides.
examples.ko: 버스 오래 타면 속이 안 좋아.

examples.en: He got sick after eating the old fish.

senses.note: feel sick = 토할 것 같다, be sick(영국) = 토하다. carsick(차멀미), seasick(배멀미).

senses.meaningEn: bored with or annoyed by something because it has happened too much

examples.en: I'm sick of this rainy weather.
examples.ko: 이 비 오는 날씨 정말 지겨워.

examples.en: We're sick of eating the same lunch.

senses.note: be sick of + 명사/-ing. 강조하면 sick and tired of.

senses.meaningEn: next to each other, facing the same way

examples.en: We walked side by side along the beach.
The two cars were parked side by side.

senses.note: 걷기·앉기·세우기 등 위치가 '옆으로 나란함' 을 말할 때. 비유적으로 work side by side = 함께 협력하여 일하다. 형용사는 하이픈: a side-by-side comparison.

senses.meaningEn: a path next to a road for people to walk on

examples.en: Please ride your bike on the road, not the sidewalk.
The sidewalk was icy, so I walked slowly.

senses.note: 미국식 sidewalk, 영국식 pavement(미국에서 pavement 는 도로 포장면을 뜻함). 인도 '위에서'는 on the sidewalk.

senses.meaningEn: a board or notice with words or pictures that gives information or a warning

examples.en: The sign says you can't park here.
examples.ko: 표지판에 여기 주차하면 안 된다고 써 있어.

examples.en: Follow the signs to the exit.

senses.note: road sign(도로 표지판), stop sign(정지 표지판), a sign on the door. 표지판에 '~라고 쓰여 있다'는 The sign says ~ 로 says 를 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to write your name on a document to show you agree or it is yours

examples.en: Please sign your name at the bottom.
I signed the form and handed it back.

senses.note: '사인(서명)'은 명사로 signature 임. sign 은 동사. 유명인의 '사인'은 autograph. 한국어 '싸인해 주세요'를 Give me your sign 이라고 하면 틀림 → Can I have your autograph? / Please sign here.

senses.meaningEn: something that shows that something exists or is happening

examples.en: Dark clouds are a sign of rain.
She gave me a sign to be quiet.

senses.note: a sign of ~ (~의 징후). 손짓으로 신호를 보내다 = give a sign / make a sign. 수화는 sign language.

senses.meaningEn: to enter your name and password to start using a website or app

examples.en: Please sign in with your email address.
I can't sign in. Did I forget my password?

senses.note: log in 과 거의 같은 뜻. 요즘 앱·웹사이트 버튼에는 Sign in 이 더 많이 보임. sign in to + 서비스.

senses.meaningEn: to write your name on a list when you arrive at a place

examples.en: Visitors must sign in at the front desk.
examples.ko: 방문객은 안내 데스크에서 방문 등록을 해야 합니다.

examples.en: Did you sign in when you got to the gym?

senses.note: 병원·학원·회사 로비 등에서 이름을 적는 것. sign-in sheet(출석 명단).

senses.meaningEn: to end your session on a website or app

examples.en: Sign out before you close the browser.
I signed out of all my accounts on the old phone.

senses.note: sign out of + 서비스. log out 과 같은 뜻이며 둘 다 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to write your name on a list when you leave a place

examples.en: Please sign out when you leave the building.
examples.ko: 건물에서 나갈 때 퇴실 서명을 해 주세요.

examples.en: She signed out at five and went home.
examples.ko: 그녀는 5시에 퇴실 등록을 하고 집에 갔어.

senses.meaningEn: to create an account or join a service

examples.en: You can sign up for free in a minute.
I signed up for a new music app yesterday.

senses.note: sign up for + 서비스/강좌. 한국어 '회원가입'에 해당. '로그인'은 sign in 이므로 혼동 주의.

senses.meaningEn: to put your name on a list to join a class or activity

examples.en: I want to sign up for the cooking class.
Twenty people signed up for the soccer team.

senses.note: sign up to do something(~하기로 신청하다)도 가능. 자원봉사·마라톤·뉴스레터 등에 널리 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: not sensible; showing a lack of good judgment

examples.en: Don't be silly. Of course you can come.
examples.ko: 바보 같은 소리 하지 마. 당연히 와도 돼.

examples.en: That was a silly mistake.

senses.note: stupid 보다 훨씬 부드럽고 애정이 담김. Don't be silly! 는 상대가 사과하거나 지나치게 걱정할 때 '그런 소리 마' 의 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: funny in a childish or playful way

examples.en: He made a silly face and we all laughed.
examples.ko: 그가 우스꽝스러운 표정을 지어서 우리 모두 웃었어.

examples.en: The kids are being silly again.

senses.note: a silly hat / silly song 처럼 '귀엽게 우스운' 느낌. 아이들에 대해 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: a shiny white metal used for jewelry, coins, and spoons

examples.en: These earrings are made of silver.
Silver is cheaper than gold.

senses.note: silverware(식기류)는 은이 아니어도 포크·나이프를 통칭.

senses.meaningEn: having a shiny gray-white color

examples.en: My dad drives a silver car.
I like the silver watch better.

senses.meaningEn: a silver medal, given for second place

examples.en: He took silver in the 100 meters.
Our team got silver this year.

senses.meaningEn: easy to understand or do, without many parts

examples.en: The rules of the game are simple.
Let me explain it in simple words.

senses.note: easy 는 '힘이 안 든다', simple 은 '복잡하지 않다'에 초점. It's simple. = 간단해. keep it simple = 단순하게 해.

senses.meaningEn: plain, without extra decoration or anything special

examples.en: She wore a simple black dress.
We had a simple dinner of rice and soup.
examples.ko: 우리는 밥과 국으로 소박한 저녁을 먹었어.

senses.note: simple life = 소박한 삶. 사람에게 simple 을 쓰면 '단순한, 머리가 좋지 않은'으로 들릴 수 있어 주의.

senses.meaningEn: from a time in the past until now

examples.en: I've lived here since 2020.
She has been sick since Monday.

senses.note: since + 시작 시점(since Monday), for + 기간(for three days). 보통 현재완료(have + p.p.)와 함께 쓴다. '언제부터' 를 from 으로 쓰면 '지금까지' 의 뜻이 약해지니 since 가 자연스러움. ever since = 그때부터 줄곧.

senses.meaningEn: because; as

examples.en: Since it's raining, let's stay home.
I'll drive, since you're tired.

senses.note: because 보다 가볍고 '상대도 이미 아는 이유' 를 댈 때 쓴다. 문장 앞에 자주 온다. 시간의 since 와 헷갈리지 않도록 문맥을 본다.

senses.meaningEn: to make music with your voice

examples.en: My sister sings in the school choir.
We sang happy birthday to Grandma.
examples.ko: 우리는 할머니께 생일 축하 노래를 불러 드렸어.

senses.note: sing-sang-sung. sing a song(노래를 부르다), sing along(따라 부르다). 노래하는 사람 singer, 노래 song — 한국어 '노래방 가자'는 Let's go to karaoke.

senses.meaningEn: when a bird makes musical sounds

examples.en: I love hearing the birds sing in the morning.
examples.ko: 아침에 새들이 노래하는 소리가 참 좋아.

examples.en: A little bird was singing outside my window.
examples.ko: 작은 새 한 마리가 창밖에서 노래하고 있었어.

senses.note: 새는 sing, 개는 bark, 고양이는 meow. 한국어로는 모두 '울다'지만 영어는 동물마다 동사가 다름.

senses.meaningEn: a person who sings, especially as a job

examples.en: She is a famous singer in Korea.
My brother is a good singer.

senses.note: a good singer = 노래 잘하는 사람(직업 아니어도 됨). sing(동사)의 g 는 묵음에 가깝게 /ŋ/ 로 발음.

senses.meaningEn: a large bowl fixed to a wall or counter with taps for washing

examples.en: Put the dirty dishes in the sink.
The bathroom sink is leaking again.

senses.note: kitchen sink(싱크대), bathroom sink(세면대). 둘 다 sink 로 부름.

senses.meaningEn: to go down below the surface of water

examples.en: The boat started to sink in the storm.
Heavy things sink to the bottom.

senses.note: sink - sank - sunk. 반대말 float(떠 있다).

senses.meaningEn: a polite way to speak to a man whose name you do not know

examples.en: Can I help you, sir?
Excuse me, sir, you dropped your wallet.

senses.note: 가게·식당·공항 직원이 남성 고객에게 쓰는 말. 친구나 아는 사람에게는 쓰지 않음. 여성에게는 ma'am.

senses.meaningEn: a word used at the start of a formal letter to a man

examples.en: Dear Sir, I am writing about my order.
examples.ko: 귀하, 제 주문 건으로 글을 드립니다.

examples.en: Dear Sir or Madam, I have a question.

senses.note: 받는 사람 이름을 모를 때 Dear Sir or Madam. 이름을 알면 Dear Mr. Kim 이 더 좋음.

senses.meaningEn: a girl or woman who has the same parents as you

examples.en: My sister is two years older than me.
examples.ko: 우리 언니는 나보다 두 살 많아.

examples.en: I share a room with my little sister.

senses.note: 영어는 언니/누나/여동생을 구분하지 않음. 필요하면 older sister / younger (little) sister.

senses.meaningEn: to rest with your weight on your bottom, as on a chair

examples.en: Please sit down and relax.
We sat by the window and talked.

senses.note: sit down = (동작) 앉다, be sitting = (상태) 앉아 있다. Have a seat. / Take a seat. 가 Sit down. 보다 부드러운 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to take an exam

examples.en: I'm sitting a math test tomorrow.
She sat the exam last week.

senses.note: sit an exam 은 주로 영국식. 미국에서는 take a test / take an exam 이 일반적.

senses.meaningKo: 빈둥거리다, 하는 일 없이 앉아 있다
senses.meaningEn: to spend time sitting and doing nothing useful

examples.en: Don't just sit around all day. Go outside!
examples.ko: 하루 종일 빈둥거리지만 말고 밖에 나가!

examples.en: We sat around chatting and drinking coffee.
examples.ko: 우리는 앉아서 수다 떨며 커피를 마셨어.

senses.note: 보통 약간 비난하는 느낌(게으르다). 뒤에 -ing 를 붙여 sit around doing nothing / watching TV.

senses.meaningEn: to lean back in a chair and relax

examples.en: Sit back, relax, and enjoy the show.
He sat back in his chair and closed his eyes.
examples.ko: 그는 의자에 등을 기대고 눈을 감았어.

senses.note: 'Sit back and relax.' 는 비행기·공연 안내 멘트에서 거의 고정 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to do nothing and let things happen without trying to change them

examples.en: We can't just sit back and wait for help.
examples.ko: 가만히 앉아서 도움만 기다릴 수는 없어.

examples.en: Don't sit back and let others do all the work.
examples.ko: 뒷짐 지고 다른 사람들이 다 하게 두지 마.

senses.note: 보통 비판적인 뉘앙스: sit back and do nothing / sit back and watch.

senses.meaningEn: to move your body so that you are sitting

examples.en: Please sit down and make yourself comfortable.
We sat down at a table by the window.

senses.note: sit 은 '앉아 있는 상태', sit down 은 '앉는 동작'. 손님에게는 Sit down 보다 Have a seat / Take a seat 이 부드러움. 과거형 sat down.

senses.meaningEn: to take time to talk about or deal with something carefully

examples.en: Let's sit down and talk about this.
examples.ko: 우리 앉아서 이 얘기 좀 하자.

examples.en: I need to sit down with my teacher after class.
examples.ko: 수업 후에 선생님과 따로 앉아 이야기해야 해.

senses.note: sit down with + 사람 = ~와 진지하게 이야기하다. 실제 앉는 동작보다 '시간 내서 다루다'는 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: to move from lying down into a sitting position

examples.en: The patient can sit up in bed now.
examples.ko: 환자가 이제 침대에서 일어나 앉을 수 있어요.

examples.en: I sat up quickly when I heard the noise.

senses.note: '허리를 펴고 똑바로 앉다'도 sit up: Sit up straight!(똑바로 앉아!). 운동 '윗몸 일으키기'는 sit-ups.

senses.meaningEn: to stay awake and not go to bed until late

examples.en: We sat up talking until midnight.
She sat up all night waiting for the call.
examples.ko: 그녀는 전화를 기다리며 밤새 깨어 있었어.

senses.note: sit up late / sit up all night. 요즘 구어는 stay up 이 더 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: the number 6

examples.en: I usually wake up at six.
A pack of six eggs, please.
examples.ko: 달걀 여섯 개짜리 한 팩 주세요.

senses.note: 서수는 sixth(6th). sixteen(16), sixty(60). sex 와 발음이 비슷해지지 않도록 /ɪ/를 짧고 또렷하게.

senses.meaningEn: the number 16

examples.en: You can drive at sixteen in some states.
examples.ko: 미국 일부 주에서는 열여섯 살에 운전할 수 있어.

examples.en: There are sixteen students in my class.
examples.ko: 우리 반에는 학생이 열여섯 명 있어.

senses.note: sixTEEN(16) vs SIXty(60). 미국에서 16세 생일(sweet sixteen)은 특별히 크게 축하하는 문화가 있음.

senses.meaningEn: the number 60

examples.en: An hour has sixty minutes.
My grandfather is sixty years old.

senses.note: SIXty(60) vs sixTEEN(16). 1분 = sixty seconds, 1시간 = sixty minutes. 서수는 sixtieth(60th).

senses.meaningEn: one of the standard measurements that clothes or shoes are made in

examples.en: What size do you wear?
Do you have this shirt in a bigger size?
examples.ko: 이 셔츠 더 큰 사이즈 있어요?

senses.note: 사이즈를 물을 때 What size are you? 도 자연스러움. 신발은 shoe size, 옷은 그냥 size. try on(입어 보다)과 같이 자주 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: how big or small something is

examples.en: The two rooms are about the same size.
Look at the size of that dog!

senses.note: the size of ~ = ~의 크기. '크기가 어느 정도예요?'는 How big is it? 이 더 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: to move on ice or the ground wearing special shoes with blades or wheels

examples.en: We skated on the frozen lake all afternoon.
examples.ko: 우리는 오후 내내 얼어붙은 호수에서 스케이트를 탔어.

examples.en: Can you skate backwards?

senses.note: go skating(스케이트 타러 가다). ice skating(아이스스케이팅), roller skating(롤러스케이팅), skateboarding(스케이트보드). 피겨 스케이팅은 figure skating.

senses.meaningEn: a boot with a blade or wheels on the bottom for moving on ice or the ground

examples.en: I got new skates for my birthday.
Put your skates on and let's go!

senses.note: 신발이므로 보통 복수형 skates. 한 켤레는 a pair of skates. 스케이트 '보드'는 skateboard 로 다른 단어.

senses.meaningEn: the activity of moving on ice or on wheels wearing skates

examples.en: We went skating on the frozen lake.
Skating looks easy, but it's hard at first.

senses.note: ice skating(얼음), roller skating(바퀴). go skating(스케이트 타러 가다). 보드는 skateboarding. '스케이트장'은 skating rink / ice rink.

senses.meaningEn: to move over snow on two long narrow boards

examples.en: I learned to ski when I was six.
examples.ko: 여섯 살 때 스키 타는 걸 배웠어.

examples.en: We go skiing every winter in Gangwon.
examples.ko: 우리는 겨울마다 강원도에 스키를 타러 가.

senses.note: go skiing(스키 타러 가다). 과거형은 skied, 진행형은 skiing(i 두 개). 스키장은 ski resort, 스키 리프트는 ski lift.

senses.meaningEn: one of two long narrow boards you wear on your feet to move over snow

examples.en: These skis are too long for me.
You can rent skis at the resort.

senses.note: 장비는 복수형 skis 로 말함(a pair of skis). 스키복은 ski suit/ski jacket, 스키 여행은 ski trip.

senses.meaningEn: the sport of moving over snow on long narrow boards fixed to your boots

examples.en: We go skiing every winter.
examples.ko: 우리는 매년 겨울 스키를 타러 가.

examples.en: Skiing is expensive but a lot of fun.

senses.note: go skiing(스키 타러 가다). 스키장은 ski resort, 스키 리프트는 ski lift. 발음은 두 음절 /ˈskiː-ɪŋ/.

senses.meaningEn: the outer layer that covers your body

examples.en: My skin gets very dry in winter.
This cream is good for sensitive skin.

senses.note: dry skin(건성), oily skin(지성), sensitive skin(민감성). skin care(피부 관리).

senses.meaningEn: the outer layer of a fruit, vegetable, or animal

examples.en: You can eat the skin of an apple.
I don't like chicken skin.

senses.note: 바나나·오렌지처럼 두꺼운 껍질은 peel, 견과류·달걀 껍질은 shell.

senses.meaningEn: to not do or not go to something you should do

examples.en: I skipped breakfast this morning.
He skipped class to play games.

senses.note: skip breakfast/class/a meeting. 책에서 몇 페이지 건너뛰는 것도 skip. 과거형 skipped.

senses.meaningEn: to move with small jumps, or to jump over a rope

examples.en: The little girl skipped down the street.
We skipped rope at recess.

senses.note: 줄넘기: 미국식 jump rope, 영국식 skip/skipping rope.

senses.meaningEn: a piece of clothing for women and girls that hangs from the waist

examples.en: She wore a long skirt to the party.
examples.ko: 그녀는 파티에 긴 치마를 입고 갔어.

examples.en: This skirt goes well with your boots.
examples.ko: 이 치마는 네 부츠랑 잘 어울려.

senses.note: shirt(셔츠)와 발음이 비슷하니 /skɜːrt/ 의 k 를 분명히. mini skirt, long skirt.

senses.meaningEn: the space above the earth where you see clouds, the sun, and stars

examples.en: The sky is really blue today.
There's not a cloud in the sky.

senses.note: 보통 the sky. 복수 skies 는 날씨 표현에서: clear skies(맑은 하늘), sunny skies. sky blue = 하늘색. The sky's the limit. = 한계가 없다.

senses.meaningEn: to rest with your eyes closed and your mind not awake

examples.en: I slept for nine hours last night.
Did you sleep well?

senses.note: go to bed(자러 가다)와 fall asleep(잠들다), sleep(자는 상태)을 구분. 과거형 slept.

senses.meaningEn: the state of resting with your eyes closed

examples.en: I didn't get enough sleep this week.
examples.ko: 이번 주에 잠을 충분히 못 잤어.

examples.en: A good night's sleep will help.
examples.ko: 밤에 푹 자면 도움이 될 거야.

senses.note: get enough sleep = 충분히 자다. go to sleep = 잠들다.

senses.meaningEn: to sleep later than usual in the morning, often on purpose

examples.en: I love sleeping in on Sundays.
examples.ko: 일요일에 늦잠 자는 게 정말 좋아.

examples.en: We slept in and skipped breakfast.

senses.note: sleep in 은 보통 '쉬는 날 느긋하게 늦게까지 자다'(좋은 뜻). 실수로 늦잠 자서 지각한 경우는 oversleep(I overslept).

senses.meaningEn: to sleep at someone else's house for a night

examples.en: Can I sleep over at Jimin's house tonight?
examples.ko: 오늘 밤 지민이 집에서 자고 와도 돼요?

examples.en: My cousins slept over last weekend.
examples.ko: 지난 주말에 사촌들이 우리 집에서 자고 갔어.

senses.note: sleep over at + 사람's house. 명사 sleepover(친구 집에서 자는 파티): have a sleepover. 어른은 stay over / stay the night 를 더 많이 씀.

senses.meaningEn: feeling that you want to sleep

examples.en: I always get sleepy after lunch.
The baby is sleepy, so let's put her to bed.

senses.note: tired(피곤한)와 구분: sleepy 는 잠이 오는 상태. feel / get sleepy. 졸음운전 = drowsy driving.

senses.meaningEn: one thin, triangle-shaped piece cut from a pizza

examples.en: Can I have one more slice of pizza?
examples.ko: 피자 한 조각 더 먹어도 돼?

examples.en: A slice of pizza costs three dollars here.

senses.note: slice 는 얇게 '썬' 조각: a slice of pizza/bread/cheese/cake. 미국에서는 피자를 조각 단위(by the slice)로도 판다. 피자 한 판은 a whole pizza 또는 a pie(뉴욕식).

senses.meaningEn: thin in an attractive way

examples.en: You look so slim in that dress.
examples.ko: 그 드레스 입으니까 정말 날씬해 보여.

examples.en: She stays slim by walking every day.

senses.note: thin 보다 긍정적인 칭찬 표현. 한국어 '슬림하다'와 뜻이 거의 같다.

senses.meaningEn: to slide by accident and fall or almost fall

examples.en: I slipped on the ice and fell.
Careful, the floor is wet and you might slip.
examples.ko: 조심해, 바닥이 젖어서 미끄러질 수 있어.

senses.note: slip(발이 미끄러짐) vs trip(발이 걸려 넘어짐) vs fall(넘어지다). slippery = 미끄러운.

senses.meaningEn: to put something somewhere, or go somewhere, quickly and quietly

examples.en: He slipped a note into my bag.
examples.ko: 그가 내 가방에 메모를 슬쩍 넣었어.

examples.en: She slipped out of the room during the movie.
examples.ko: 그녀는 영화 도중에 슬쩍 방에서 나갔어.

senses.note: It slipped my mind. = 깜빡 잊었어. 아주 흔한 표현.

senses.meaningEn: a small piece of paper

examples.en: Keep the slip in case you want to return it.
Write your name on this slip of paper.

senses.note: a slip of paper = 작은 종이 한 장. permission slip = (학교) 동의서.

senses.meaningEn: moving or happening without much speed

examples.en: The bus is so slow in the morning.
My internet is slow today.

senses.note: 부사는 slowly(Speak slowly, please). 다만 구어에서 Drive slow. 처럼 slow 를 부사로도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to go or make something go less fast

examples.en: Slow down! You're driving too fast.
examples.ko: 속도 줄여! 너무 빨리 몰고 있어.

examples.en: The car slowed down at the corner.

senses.note: slow down 은 운전뿐 아니라 '말을 천천히 해', '일을 좀 쉬어 가며 해' 에도 씀. 반대는 speed up.

senses.meaningEn: to move or drive more slowly

examples.en: Slow down! There's a school ahead.
The train slowed down as it came into the station.

senses.note: 운전·걷기·말하기 모두에 씀: Could you slow down? I can't follow.(천천히 말해 주세요). 자동사·타동사 둘 다 가능.

senses.meaningEn: to be less active or work less hard, often because of your health

examples.en: The doctor told Dad to slow down a bit.
examples.ko: 의사가 아빠한테 조금 쉬어 가며 일하라고 했어.

examples.en: Things are slowing down at work this month.
examples.ko: 이번 달엔 회사 일이 좀 한가해지고 있어.

senses.note: business / sales / things slow down = 경기·일이 둔해지다. 사람에게 쓰면 '무리하지 말고 쉬어 가라'.

senses.meaningEn: at a slow speed; not quickly

examples.en: Could you speak more slowly, please?
The old man walked slowly up the stairs.

senses.note: 영어 학습자에게 가장 유용한 문장 중 하나: Please speak slowly. 구어에서 Drive slow. 처럼 slow 를 부사로 쓰기도 함.

senses.meaningEn: not large in size, amount, or number

examples.en: We live in a small apartment near the station.
examples.ko: 우리는 역 근처 작은 아파트에 살아.

examples.en: Can I have a small coffee, please?

senses.note: small 은 크기·양을 객관적으로 말할 때, little 은 '작고 귀여운' 느낌이 들어감(a little boy). 식당·카페 사이즈는 small / medium / large.

senses.meaningEn: the smallest standard size of clothes or drinks

examples.en: These shoes are too small for me.
I'll take the small, please.

senses.note: 옷 라벨의 S 는 small, M 은 medium, L 은 large. '작다'를 tight(꽉 낀다)로 말하기도 함.

senses.meaningEn: able to learn and understand things quickly

examples.en: My little sister is really smart.
That was a smart answer.

senses.note: 미국 구어에서 '똑똑하다'는 smart 가 가장 흔함. 영국에서는 clever 를 더 씀. smart phone/smart TV 의 smart 도 '똑똑한'.

senses.meaningEn: clean, neat, and stylish in appearance

examples.en: You look smart in that suit.
Wear something smart for the interview.

senses.note: 주로 영국식 용법. smart casual = 단정한 캐주얼(드레스 코드). 미국에서는 sharp 나 nice 를 더 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to have a particular smell

examples.en: Something smells good in the kitchen!
These socks smell terrible.

senses.note: smell + 형용사: smell good/bad. smell like + 명사: It smells like coffee. 목적어 없이 It smells. 라고만 하면 '냄새 난다(악취)'.

senses.meaningEn: to notice or sense a smell with your nose

examples.en: Smell this flower, it's lovely.
examples.ko: 이 꽃 냄새 맡아 봐, 정말 좋아.

examples.en: I can smell smoke. Is something burning?
examples.ko: 연기 냄새가 나. 뭐 타는 거 아니야?

senses.note: 지각동사라 보통 can smell 로 씀(I'm smelling ✗).

senses.meaningEn: the quality of something that you notice with your nose

examples.en: I love the smell of fresh bread.
examples.ko: 갓 구운 빵 냄새 정말 좋아.

examples.en: What's that strange smell?

senses.note: 좋은 향은 scent/fragrance, 나쁜 냄새는 odor/stink. smell 은 중립.

senses.meaningEn: to make a happy expression with your mouth, without sound

examples.en: She smiled at me and said hello.
Smile for the camera!

senses.note: smile 은 소리 없이 웃는 것, laugh 는 소리 내어 웃는 것. smile at someone.

senses.meaningEn: a happy expression on your face

examples.en: He has a warm smile.
She said goodbye with a big smile.
examples.ko: 그녀는 환하게 웃으며 작별 인사를 했어.

senses.note: with a smile = 웃으며. a big smile, a warm smile.

senses.meaningEn: to look at someone with a smile

examples.en: The baby smiled at me on the bus.
She smiled at the camera and waved.
examples.ko: 그녀는 카메라를 보고 웃으며 손을 흔들었어.

senses.note: smile 도 자동사라서 대상 앞에 at 이 필요함(smile at him). laugh at 과 달리 smile at 은 거의 항상 호의적인 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: the gray or black gas that comes from something burning

examples.en: I can smell smoke. Is something burning?
examples.ko: 연기 냄새가 나. 뭐 타는 거 아니야?

examples.en: Black smoke came out of the chimney.

senses.note: 불가산. 연기 감지기 = smoke detector/alarm.

senses.meaningEn: to breathe in and out the smoke from a cigarette

examples.en: You can't smoke in here.
My dad stopped smoking last year.

senses.note: 금연 구역 = no smoking area. 담배를 끊다 = quit/stop smoking. 흡연자 = smoker.

senses.meaningEn: having an even surface with no bumps or rough parts

examples.en: The table has a smooth, shiny surface.
This cream makes your skin feel smooth.
examples.ko: 이 크림은 피부를 매끄럽게 해 줘.

senses.note: 끝 th 는 /ð/ 로 유성음. 음식에선 smooth sauce(덩어리 없는 소스), smoothie 가 여기서 나온 말.

senses.meaningEn: happening without problems or sudden movements

examples.en: We had a smooth flight with no turbulence.
Everything went smoothly on the first day.

senses.note: a smooth flight/ride(편안한 비행/운전), go smoothly(순조롭게 진행되다). 사람에게 smooth 는 '말솜씨가 번드르르한' 뉘앙스가 있을 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: a small amount of food eaten between meals

examples.en: I need a snack before the meeting.
Fruit is a healthy snack for kids.

senses.note: have/grab a snack = 간식을 먹다. 한국어 '스낵(과자)'보다 뜻이 넓어 과일·샌드위치도 snack.

senses.meaningEn: to eat a small amount of food between meals

examples.en: I snack on nuts while I work.
Stop snacking, dinner is almost ready.
examples.ko: 그만 주워 먹어, 저녁 거의 다 됐어.

senses.note: snack on + 음식. 동사로 쓰면 '주워 먹다'는 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: a small, slow animal with a soft body and a round shell

examples.en: A snail is slowly climbing up the wall.
My son keeps a snail in a small box.

senses.note: 'at a snail's pace' = 아주 느리게. 종이 편지를 이메일과 대비해 snail mail 이라고 부름.

senses.meaningEn: a long thin animal with no legs that moves by sliding along the ground

examples.en: Watch out! There's a snake on the path.
Are the snakes in this area dangerous?

senses.note: 독사는 poisonous/venomous snake. 뱀은 slide/slither(미끄러지듯 기어가다), 소리는 hiss. 사람을 snake 라고 하면 '믿을 수 없는 사람'.

senses.meaningEn: soft comfortable shoes with rubber bottoms, worn for sports or everyday

examples.en: I wear sneakers when I walk to work.
Her new sneakers are white and pink.

senses.note: 미국식. 영국식은 trainers. 달리기 전용은 running shoes. a pair of sneakers.

senses.meaningEn: to suddenly push air out through your nose and mouth, for example when you have a cold

examples.en: I always sneeze when I'm near cats.
examples.ko: 고양이 근처에 가면 항상 재채기가 나.

examples.en: He sneezed three times in a row.

senses.note: 누가 재채기하면 Bless you! 라고 말해 줌. 명사로도 씀(a loud sneeze).

senses.meaningEn: soft white pieces of frozen water that fall from the sky

examples.en: The kids are playing in the snow.
We had the first snow of the year today.

senses.note: 셀 수 없는 명사: a snow ✗, snows ✗ → heavy snow(폭설). 첫눈 = the first snow. 눈사람 = snowman, 눈싸움 = snowball fight.

senses.meaningEn: to fall from the sky as snow

examples.en: It snowed all night.
It's snowing! Let's go outside.

senses.note: rain 처럼 주어는 it: It snows / It's snowing / It snowed. Snow is falling 도 가능하지만 더 문학적.

senses.meaningEn: with snow falling or covering the ground

examples.en: It was a cold, snowy night.
The roads are snowy, so drive slowly.

senses.note: It's snowing(지금 눈이 온다) 과 구별. 눈이 많은 겨울 = a snowy winter. snowy white = 눈처럼 하얀.

senses.meaningEn: to a great degree; very

examples.en: I'm so happy to see you!
The test was so hard.

senses.note: so + 형용사/부사 (so hot), such + 명사 (such a hot day). 'so beautiful girl' 은 틀림 → such a beautiful girl.

senses.meaningEn: used to show the result of what was said before

examples.en: It was raining, so we stayed home.
I was hungry, so I made a sandwich.

senses.note: because(이유)와 순서가 반대: Because it rained, we stayed home = It rained, so we stayed home. 둘을 한 문장에 같이 쓰지 않음.

senses.meaningKo: (I think so / I hope so) 그렇게
senses.meaningEn: used instead of repeating something that was just said

examples.en: Is she coming? I think so.
Will it be sunny tomorrow? I hope so.

senses.note: I think so / I hope so / I guess so / I'm afraid so. 부정은 I don't think so / I hope not.

senses.meaningEn: until now; up to this point in time

examples.en: So far, I like my new job.
How's the trip going? So far, so good!

senses.note: "So far, so good." = 지금까지는 순조로워(정해진 표현). 현재완료와 잘 어울림: So far we have visited three cities.

senses.meaningEn: not very good but not very bad; average

examples.en: How was the test? It was so-so.
I'm feeling so-so today.

senses.note: 하이픈 포함 so-so. 대답할 때 쓰는 구어체. 음식·영화·기분 모두 가능. 비슷한 표현: not bad, it was okay.

senses.meaningEn: a substance you use with water to wash your body or things

examples.en: Wash your hands with soap and water.
We're out of soap. Can you buy some?
examples.ko: 비누가 다 떨어졌어. 좀 사다 줄래?

senses.note: soap 은 보통 셀 수 없는 명사. '비누 한 개'는 a bar of soap. 세제는 detergent, 주방 세제는 dish soap.

senses.meaningEn: a game in which two teams of eleven players kick a ball and try to score goals

examples.en: We play soccer after school.
My son is on the school soccer team.

senses.note: 미국·캐나다에서는 soccer, 영국·대부분의 나라에서는 football. 미국에서 football 은 미식축구이므로 주의. 축구 선수는 soccer player.

senses.meaningEn: soft pieces of clothing that cover your feet inside your shoes

examples.en: Put on clean socks every day.
These socks have a hole in them.

senses.note: 보통 복수형, a pair of socks. 한 짝은 a sock. 양말을 '신다'도 wear/put on. 스타킹은 tights/pantyhose.

senses.meaningEn: a sweet drink with bubbles in it, such as cola

examples.en: Can I have a soda with my burger?
I'm trying to drink less soda.

senses.note: 미국에서는 지역에 따라 soda / pop / soft drink / coke 라고 부름. 한국어 '사이다'는 영어로 lemon-lime soda 나 Sprite 이고, 영어 cider 는 사과술·사과주스를 뜻함.

senses.meaningEn: a white powder used in baking or cleaning (baking soda)

examples.en: Add a little baking soda to the dough.
Baking soda cleans the sink really well.
examples.ko: 베이킹 소다는 싱크대를 정말 잘 닦아 줘.

senses.meaningEn: a long, soft seat for two or more people

examples.en: Sit on the sofa and make yourself comfortable.
I fell asleep on the sofa last night.

senses.note: 미국에서는 couch 를 더 자주 씀. 소파'에' 앉다는 on the sofa.

senses.meaningEn: not hard; easy to press or pleasant to touch

examples.en: This pillow is really soft.
The baby's skin is so soft.

senses.note: soft 는 촉감(만져서 부드러움). 사람 성격이 부드럽다는 gentle. 피부 결이 매끄럽다는 smooth.

senses.meaningEn: quiet or gentle, not loud or bright

examples.en: She spoke in a soft voice.
I like soft music when I read.
examples.ko: 나는 책 읽을 때 잔잔한 음악이 좋아.

senses.note: soft voice(작고 부드러운 목소리), soft light(은은한 조명). 음료의 soft drink 는 '탄산음료·무알코올 음료'.

senses.meaningEn: a person who is a member of an army

examples.en: My brother is a soldier in the army.
The soldiers marched through the town.

senses.note: soldier 는 주로 육군 병사. 전체 '군대'는 the military/the army, '군 복무 중'은 be in the army. 발음에서 d 는 /dʒ/ 로 소리 남.

senses.meaningEn: to find the correct answer to a problem or puzzle

examples.en: Can you solve this math problem?
examples.ko: 이 수학 문제 풀 수 있어?

examples.en: He solved the puzzle in two minutes.

senses.note: solve a problem/puzzle/mystery. 답을 "풀다"에 answer 를 쓰지 말고 solve. 명사는 solution.

senses.meaningEn: to find a way to deal with a difficult situation

examples.en: Talking about it will help solve the problem.
examples.ko: 그 얘기를 하면 문제 해결에 도움이 될 거야.

examples.en: Money alone cannot solve everything.
examples.ko: 돈만으로 모든 걸 해결할 수는 없어.

senses.meaningEn: an amount or number of something that is not stated

examples.en: Would you like some water?
I bought some apples at the market.

senses.note: 긍정문에는 some, 부정문·의문문에는 any. 단, 권하거나 부탁할 때(Would you like some...? / Can I have some...?)는 의문문에도 some.

senses.meaningEn: a part of a group, but not all of them

examples.en: Some people don't like spicy food.
examples.ko: 어떤 사람들은 매운 음식을 안 좋아해.

examples.en: Some days I just want to stay home.
examples.ko: 어떤 날은 그냥 집에만 있고 싶어.

senses.note: some ... others ... (어떤 것은 ~, 다른 것은 ~) 패턴. 강세를 두고 /sʌm/ 로 읽으면 "일부" 뜻이 강조됨.

senses.meaningEn: a person, when you do not know or say who

examples.en: Somebody is knocking on the door.
Ask somebody for directions.

senses.note: someone 과 같은 뜻, 더 구어적. 단수 동사와 함께: Somebody is(○).

senses.meaningEn: a person, when you do not know or say who

examples.en: Someone left a bag on the bus.
I need someone to help me move.

senses.note: 긍정문에 someone, 의문·부정문에는 보통 anyone. 단, 부탁·제안할 때는 질문에도 someone: Can someone open the door?

senses.meaningEn: a thing that you do not know or do not say the name of

examples.en: I want something to drink.
examples.ko: 뭔가 마실 것 좀 먹고 싶어.

examples.en: There's something in my eye.

senses.note: 긍정문에서 something, 의문·부정문에서 anything. 형용사는 뒤에: something cold(O), cold something(X). 권유 의문문에서는 something: Would you like something to eat?

senses.meaningEn: used after a number or word to mean 'about' or 'or so'

examples.en: He's thirty-something, I think.
Let's get pizza or something tonight.
examples.ko: 오늘 밤엔 피자나 뭐 그런 거 먹자.

senses.note: 구어 표현: or something(~나 뭐 그런 거), twenty-something(20대), something like that(그런 것).

senses.meaningEn: on some occasions but not always

examples.en: Sometimes I walk to work instead of driving.
She sometimes forgets to lock the door.
examples.ko: 그녀는 가끔 문 잠그는 걸 잊어.

senses.note: 문장 맨 앞·중간·끝 어디에나 올 수 있어 자유로운 편. sometime(어느 때, 언젠가)과 some time(얼마간의 시간)과 혼동 주의: Let's meet sometime. / I need some time.

senses.meaningEn: in or to a place that you do not know or do not say

examples.en: I left my phone somewhere in the house.
Let's go somewhere warm this winter.

senses.note: 긍정문에서 somewhere, 의문·부정문에서는 anywhere. somewhere + 형용사(somewhere quiet). 미국 구어 someplace 도 같은 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: a person's male child

examples.en: They have a son and a daughter.
examples.ko: 그들은 아들 하나 딸 하나가 있어.

examples.en: My son just started elementary school.

senses.note: sun(태양)과 발음이 같음 /sʌn/. only son = 외아들.

senses.meaningEn: a short piece of music with words that you sing

examples.en: This is my favorite song!
Let's sing a song together.

senses.note: sing a song(노래를 부르다), a love song(사랑 노래). 노래방은 karaoke. 가수는 singer, 가사는 lyrics.

senses.meaningEn: in a short time from now

examples.en: Dinner will be ready soon.
I hope you feel better soon.

senses.note: See you soon!(곧 보자), as soon as possible(가능한 한 빨리, ASAP), sooner or later(언젠가는). 비교급 sooner, 최상급 soonest. 한국어 '빨리'를 fast 로 옮기지 말고 아플 때는 get well soon 처럼 soon 을 쓴다.

senses.meaningEn: at some time in the future, even if you do not know exactly when

examples.en: Sooner or later, she'll find out the truth.
examples.ko: 언젠가는 그녀도 진실을 알게 될 거야.

examples.en: You'll have to tell him sooner or later.

senses.note: '피할 수 없이 언젠가는' 이라는 뉘앙스. 격식체는 eventually. 순서를 바꿔 later or sooner 라고 하지 않음.

senses.meaningEn: painful, especially when touched or used

examples.en: I have a sore throat and a cough.
My legs are sore from running yesterday.

senses.note: sore throat(목 아픔), sore muscles(근육통). 운동 후 '알이 배다'도 sore. 날카롭게 '아프다'는 hurt, 통증은 pain.

senses.meaningEn: feeling bad because you did something wrong

examples.en: I'm sorry I'm late.
Sorry for the mess in the kitchen.

senses.note: sorry for + 명사/-ing, sorry (that) + 문장, sorry to + 동사. 모르고 부딪혔을 때는 Sorry!, 못 들었을 때는 Sorry? (뭐라고요?).

senses.meaningEn: feeling sad about something bad that happened to someone

examples.en: I'm sorry to hear that your dog is sick.
I'm so sorry for your loss.

senses.note: 내 잘못이 아니어도 I'm sorry 를 씀 — "유감이다, 마음이 아프다"는 뜻. 한국인은 사과로만 오해하기 쉬움. I'm sorry for your loss 는 조문 인사.

senses.meaningEn: to feel pity for someone

examples.en: I feel sorry for the kids who lost the game.
Don't feel sorry for me. I'm fine.
examples.ko: 나 불쌍하게 보지 마. 난 괜찮아.

senses.note: feel sorry for + 사람 = 안쓰럽게 여기다. 상대에게 직접 I feel sorry for you 라고 하면 무시하는 느낌이 들 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: slightly; in some way, but not exactly

examples.en: It's sort of cold in here.
I sort of understand what you mean.

senses.note: kind of 와 뜻·용법이 같음. 미국에서는 kind of 가 더 흔하고 sort of 는 영국에서 더 자주. 발음 sorta.

senses.meaningEn: used as an answer meaning "yes, but not completely"

examples.en: Did you finish your homework? Sort of.
Is she your friend? Sort of, we work together.
examples.ko: 그 사람 친구야? 뭐 그런 셈이지, 같이 일해.

senses.meaningEn: to deal with a problem or a difficult situation successfully

examples.en: Don't worry, we'll sort it out together.
examples.ko: 걱정 마, 우리가 같이 해결할 거야.

examples.en: I need to sort out my visa before the trip.
examples.ko: 여행 전에 비자 문제를 처리해야 해.

senses.note: 영국식에서 매우 흔함. sort it out = 해결하다. get something sorted (out) = 처리해 놓다. 미국식은 figure out / take care of 가 더 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: to arrange things into groups or to tidy them

examples.en: I spent the morning sorting out my closet.
Let's sort out the clothes to give away.

senses.note: sort(분류하다)에 out 이 붙어 '쓸 것과 버릴 것을 가려 정리하다'. sort out A from B = A 를 B 에서 가려내다.

senses.meaningEn: something that you can hear

examples.en: I heard a strange sound outside.
Can you turn the sound down a little?

senses.note: noise 는 시끄럽거나 거슬리는 소리, sound 는 중립적인 소리. TV·스피커 음량도 sound.

senses.meaningEn: to seem a particular way from what you hear or read

examples.en: That sounds like a great idea.
examples.ko: 그거 정말 좋은 생각인 것 같아.

examples.en: You sound tired. Are you okay?

senses.note: Sounds good! / Sounds like a plan! = 좋아, 그렇게 하자. sound + 형용사, sound like + 명사/절.

senses.meaningEn: a hot liquid food made by cooking vegetables, meat, or fish in water

examples.en: I'd like the chicken soup to start.
Mom makes soup when I have a cold.
examples.ko: 내가 감기 걸리면 엄마가 국을 끓여 주셔.

senses.note: 보통 셀 수 없음: a bowl of soup(한 그릇). 영어에서는 수프를 '마신다(drink)'가 아니라 eat soup / have soup 라고 함. 한국 음식의 국·찌개를 설명할 때도 soup 또는 stew 를 씀.

senses.meaningEn: having a sharp taste like a lemon

examples.en: This lemon is really sour!
I don't like sour candy.

senses.note: 신 김치처럼 발효로 신맛은 sour, 레몬의 상큼한 신맛은 tart / tangy 라고도 함.

senses.meaningEn: having a bad taste because it is no longer fresh

examples.en: The milk smells sour. Don't drink it.
examples.ko: 우유가 쉰 냄새 나. 마시지 마.

examples.en: This milk went sour in the heat.

senses.note: go sour / turn sour = 쉬다, 상하다. 주로 우유·크림에 씀.

senses.meaningEn: the direction that is opposite north

examples.en: Busan is in the south of Korea.
Birds fly south in the winter.

senses.note: South Korea(남한), the South(미국 남부). 형용사·부사로도 쓰임(south side, drive south). southern = 남부의, 발음 /ˈsʌðərn/ 으로 모음이 바뀜에 주의.

senses.meaningEn: time when you are not busy and can do what you like

examples.en: I read comics in my spare time.
Do you have any spare time this weekend?

senses.note: free time 과 거의 같은 뜻. spare 는 '남는, 여분의' 라는 뜻으로 spare key(여분 열쇠), spare room(남는 방) 에도 쓴다. 영국에서 조금 더 자주 쓰는 편. in my spare time.

senses.meaningEn: to be able to talk in a particular language

examples.en: Do you speak English?
She speaks three languages.

senses.note: 언어 이름 앞에는 전치사 없음: speak Korean (speak in Korean 은 '한국어로 말하다' 뉘앙스). Can you speak English? 보다 Do you speak English? 가 더 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: to talk to someone about something

examples.en: Can I speak to the manager, please?
I spoke with my teacher after class.

senses.note: speak to/with someone. talk 보다 조금 더 격식적. 전화에서 'This is Minho speaking.' = 저 민호인데요.

senses.meaningEn: to use your voice to say words

examples.en: Please speak more slowly.
Speak up! I can't hear you.

senses.note: speak up = 더 크게 말하다 / 의견을 당당히 말하다. speak loudly = 큰 소리로 말하다.

senses.meaningEn: to say publicly what you think, especially against something wrong

examples.en: Many people spoke out against the new law.
examples.ko: 많은 사람이 새 법에 반대하는 목소리를 냈어.

examples.en: Don't be afraid to speak out when something is wrong.
examples.ko: 뭔가 잘못됐을 때는 겁내지 말고 말해.

senses.note: speak out against ~(~에 반대 발언하다). speak up 보다 더 공개적·사회적인 발언. 뉴스에서 자주 보임.

senses.meaningEn: to speak more loudly so that people can hear you

examples.en: Could you speak up? I can't hear you.
examples.ko: 좀 더 크게 말해 줄래? 안 들려.

examples.en: Speak up, please. The room is noisy.

senses.note: "Speak up!" 은 "크게 말해!" 전화나 시끄러운 곳에서 자주 씀. 반대는 keep your voice down.

senses.meaningEn: to say what you think clearly instead of staying quiet

examples.en: If you don't like the plan, speak up now.
She always speaks up in meetings.
examples.ko: 그녀는 회의에서 늘 자기 의견을 말해.

senses.note: 소리 크기가 아니라 "침묵하지 않고 의견을 내다" 의 뜻. speak up for 사람 = ~를 위해 목소리를 내다.

senses.meaningEn: better or more important than usual

examples.en: Today is a special day. It's my birthday!
You are very special to me.

senses.note: something special = 뭔가 특별한 것. Is there anything special you want? 처럼 형용사가 뒤에 옴.

senses.meaningEn: made or used for one particular purpose

examples.en: Do you have a special menu for kids?
What's today's special?

senses.note: today's special(명사) = 식당의 '오늘의 요리'. 쇼핑에서 on special = 세일 중(주로 영국·호주).

senses.meaningEn: to move or drive faster

examples.en: The car sped up and passed us.
examples.ko: 그 차가 속도를 올려서 우리를 앞질렀어.

examples.en: Speed up a little, or we'll be late.
examples.ko: 조금만 더 빨리 가, 안 그러면 늦어.

senses.note: speed 의 과거는 sped(또는 speeded). 명사 speed(속도): at full speed.

senses.meaningEn: to make something happen more quickly

examples.en: Can we speed up the order? I need it today.
examples.ko: 주문 처리를 좀 빨리 해 줄 수 있나요? 오늘 필요해요.

examples.en: The new app speeds up the check-in process.
examples.ko: 새 앱이 체크인 과정을 빨라지게 해 줘.

senses.note: speed up the process / delivery / work. 사람에게 '서둘러' 는 Hurry up! 이 더 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: to say or write the letters of a word in the right order

examples.en: How do you spell your last name?
I always spell 'Wednesday' wrong.

senses.note: How do you spell it? = 철자가 어떻게 돼요? 철자(명사)는 spelling. 과거형 spelled(미)/spelt(영).

senses.meaningEn: magic words that make something happen

examples.en: The witch put a spell on the prince.
Say the magic spell and the door will open.

senses.note: put a spell on / cast a spell = 마법을 걸다. 동화·영화에서 자주 나옴.

senses.meaningEn: to use money to buy or pay for things

examples.en: I spent too much money on clothes this month.
examples.ko: 이번 달에 옷에 돈을 너무 많이 썼어.

examples.en: How much do you spend on food each week?

senses.note: spend money on + 대상. 'spend money for' 는 틀림. 과거형 spent /spent/.

senses.meaningEn: to use time doing something or being somewhere

examples.en: We spent the weekend at my parents' house.
I spend an hour a day studying English.
examples.ko: 나는 하루에 한 시간 영어 공부에 써.

senses.note: spend time (in) -ing = ~하면서 시간을 보내다. spend time with + 사람. 한국어 '시간을 때우다'는 kill time.

senses.meaningEn: having a strong hot flavor from spices like chili or pepper

examples.en: Korean food is often very spicy.
Can you make it less spicy, please?
examples.ko: 덜 맵게 해 주실 수 있어요?

senses.note: '맵다'는 spicy 또는 hot. spicy 는 향신료의 맛, hot 은 혀가 타는 느낌이 강조됨. 안 매운 것은 mild.

senses.meaningEn: a small animal with eight legs that makes webs

examples.en: There's a big spider in the bathroom.
Are you afraid of spiders?

senses.note: 거미줄은 spider web(또는 cobweb). 거미는 다리가 여덟 개라 과학적으로 insect(곤충)가 아님.

senses.meaningEn: to accidentally pour liquid out of a container

examples.en: Oops, I spilled coffee on my shirt.
Be careful, don't spill the juice.

senses.note: spill 은 실수로 쏟는 것. 의도적으로 붓는 건 pour. 과거형 spilled(미국식)/spilt(영국식).

senses.meaningEn: to tell a secret

examples.en: Come on, spill it! What did he say?
examples.ko: 얼른 말해 봐! 그가 뭐라고 했어?

examples.en: She spilled the whole story to her mom.

senses.note: spill the beans = 비밀을 말해 버리다. Spill it! = 빨리 말해!(친한 사이)

senses.meaningEn: to make water fly into the air and hit someone or something

examples.en: The kids splashed each other in the pool.
A car drove by and splashed water on me.

senses.note: splash water on/over 사람. splash your face with cold water = 찬물로 얼굴을 적시다.

senses.meaningEn: the sound or mark made when something hits water

examples.en: He jumped in with a big splash.
examples.ko: 그가 첨벙 소리를 내며 물에 뛰어들었어.

examples.en: There are splashes of paint on the floor.

senses.note: make a splash = 큰 화제를 모으다(관용 표현).

senses.meaningEn: to end a romantic relationship or a marriage

examples.en: Did you hear? Tom and Sara split up.
My parents split up when I was ten.
examples.ko: 내가 열 살 때 부모님이 헤어지셨어.

senses.note: split up with someone = ~와 헤어지다. break up 과 같은 뜻. split 은 현재·과거·과거분사 모두 split.

senses.meaningEn: to divide into smaller groups or parts

examples.en: Let's split up into teams of four.
We split up the work so it would go faster.
examples.ko: 일을 나눠서 더 빨리 끝나게 했어.

senses.note: split up into + 수/그룹. 'Let's split up and look for it.'(흩어져서 찾자). 계산을 나눌 때는 split the bill.

senses.meaningEn: a tool with a small bowl and a handle, used for eating or stirring

examples.en: I need a spoon for my soup.
Koreans eat rice with a spoon.

senses.note: 작은 숟가락은 teaspoon, 큰 숟가락은 tablespoon(레시피 계량 단위로도 씀).

senses.meaningEn: the amount a spoon holds

examples.en: Add a spoon of sugar to the tea.
Just try one spoon of this.

senses.note: 정확히는 a spoonful of sugar 가 표준이지만 구어에서는 a spoon of 도 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: a game or physical activity that people do for exercise or fun, often in a competition

examples.en: What sports do you like?
Soccer is the most popular sport in my country.
examples.ko: 우리 나라에서 가장 인기 있는 스포츠는 축구야.

senses.note: play sports(운동하다). 헬스장에서 하는 운동은 sport 가 아니라 exercise / work out. 미국식은 흔히 복수 sports(sports fan, sports car).

senses.meaningEn: the season between winter and summer when plants start to grow

examples.en: Spring is my favorite season.
Cherry blossoms bloom in early spring.

senses.note: 계절 앞에는 in 을 쓰고(in spring / in the spring), 관사는 있어도 없어도 된다. 계절 이름은 보통 소문자.

senses.meaningEn: a curled piece of metal that goes back to its shape after you press it

examples.en: The old bed has a broken spring.
examples.ko: 그 낡은 침대는 스프링이 하나 부러졌어.

examples.en: This toy jumps because of a spring inside.
examples.ko: 이 장난감은 안에 스프링이 있어서 뛰어올라.

senses.meaningEn: a place where water comes up naturally from the ground

examples.en: The water comes from a mountain spring.
examples.ko: 이 물은 산속 샘에서 나온 거야.

examples.en: We relaxed in a hot spring in Japan.

senses.note: hot spring = 온천. spring water = 샘물(생수 상표에도 자주 보임).

senses.meaningEn: a flat shape with four equal straight sides and four right angles

examples.en: Draw a square and color it blue.
Cut the paper into small squares.

senses.note: 직사각형은 rectangle, 삼각형은 triangle, 원은 circle.

senses.meaningEn: having the shape of a square

examples.en: We need a square table for the kitchen.
The room is about four square meters.

senses.note: square meter(제곱미터, m²)는 면적 단위. 평수 대신 영어로 면적을 말할 때 자주 필요.

senses.meaningEn: an open area in a town, often with buildings around it

examples.en: Let's meet at the main square at noon.
There's a market in the town square every Sunday.
examples.ko: 매주 일요일에 마을 광장에서 장이 열려.

senses.note: Times Square, Gwanghwamun Square 처럼 지명에 자주 등장. 관광 안내에서 '광장' = square.

senses.meaningEn: a large building with seats around a field where people watch sports or concerts

examples.en: The stadium was full of fans.
We watched the game at the stadium last night.

senses.note: 야구장은 baseball stadium/ballpark, 축구장은 soccer stadium. 실내 체육관은 gym / arena. 경기장 '에서'는 at the stadium.

senses.meaningEn: the raised area in a theater or hall where people perform

examples.en: The singer walked onto the stage and smiled.
examples.ko: 가수가 무대로 걸어 나와 미소 지었어.

examples.en: I was so nervous on stage!

senses.note: on stage(무대 위에서) — 관사 없이 씀. go on stage(무대에 오르다), backstage(무대 뒤). 무대 공포증은 stage fright.

senses.meaningEn: one part of a process or a period in someone's life

examples.en: We're at the first stage of the project.
At this stage, the baby can't walk yet.
examples.ko: 이 시기에는 아기가 아직 걷지 못해.

senses.note: at this stage(현 단계에서), the early/final stage(초기/마지막 단계). 게임의 '스테이지'도 같은 단어(level 이 더 흔함).

senses.meaningEn: a set of steps that you walk up or down to go to another floor

examples.en: Let's take the stairs instead of the elevator.
Be careful, the stairs are wet.

senses.note: 보통 복수형으로 씀. 계단 한 칸은 a step/stair. 위층으로 = upstairs, 아래층으로 = downstairs(둘 다 to 없이 씀).

senses.meaningEn: to be on your feet in an upright position

examples.en: Please stand up when the teacher comes in.
We stood in line for twenty minutes.

senses.note: stand up = (동작) 일어서다, be standing = (상태) 서 있다. stand in line = 줄을 서다(미국식).

senses.meaningEn: to accept or bear something unpleasant

examples.en: I can't stand this hot weather.
examples.ko: 이 더운 날씨 정말 못 참겠어.

examples.en: She can't stand waiting in long lines.
examples.ko: 그녀는 긴 줄 서서 기다리는 걸 못 견뎌.

senses.note: 거의 항상 can't stand 형태로 쓰임. I can't stand him. = 그 사람 정말 싫어. hate 보다 구어적이고 감정이 강함.

senses.meaningEn: to be ready to do something or help if needed

examples.en: Please stand by. Your call is important to us.
examples.ko: 잠시만 기다려 주세요. 고객님의 전화는 소중합니다.

examples.en: The doctors are standing by in case we need them.
examples.ko: 필요할 경우를 대비해 의사들이 대기하고 있어요.

senses.note: 방송·공항·전화 안내에서 'Please stand by.' 명사형 standby: on standby(대기 중), standby ticket(대기 항공권).

senses.meaningEn: to continue to support someone in a difficult time

examples.en: My friends stood by me when I lost my job.
examples.ko: 직장을 잃었을 때 친구들이 내 곁을 지켜 줬어.

examples.en: She stood by her husband through everything.
examples.ko: 그녀는 모든 일을 겪으면서도 남편 곁을 지켰어.

senses.note: stand by + 사람 = 어려울 때 떠나지 않다. stand by a decision = 결정을 고수하다. 그냥 '옆에 서서 보고만 있다' 뜻도 있음(stood by and did nothing).

senses.meaningEn: to be easy to see or notice because of being different

examples.en: Her red coat really stands out in the crowd.
examples.ko: 그녀의 빨간 코트는 사람들 속에서 정말 눈에 띄어.

examples.en: The white letters stand out against the black wall.
examples.ko: 검은 벽에 흰 글자가 또렷하게 보여.

senses.note: stand out against + 배경. 외모·색이 눈에 띌 때.

senses.meaningEn: to be much better than others

examples.en: One student stood out from the rest of the class.
What makes your resume stand out?

senses.note: stand out from the crowd(남들 사이에서 돋보이다). 형용사 outstanding(뛰어난) 과 함께 기억.

senses.meaningEn: to get up onto your feet from sitting or lying

examples.en: Everyone, please stand up for the song.
He stood up when the teacher came in.

senses.note: stand 는 '서 있는 상태', stand up 은 '일어서는 동작'. 과거형 stood up.

senses.meaningEn: to not come to meet someone when you promised to

examples.en: She stood me up last night.
I can't believe he stood you up again.
examples.ko: 그가 또 너를 바람맞혔다니 믿기지 않아.

senses.note: stand + 사람 + up 순서. 데이트 상황에서 흔히 쓰는 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to defend or support someone or something

examples.en: Always stand up for your friends.
You should stand up for yourself.
examples.ko: 너 자신을 위해 당당히 말해야 해.

senses.note: stand up for yourself = 자기 의견을 당당히 말하다, 자신을 지키다.

senses.meaningEn: to defend or support someone or something that is being attacked or criticized

examples.en: You should stand up for your little brother.
She always stands up for what she believes in.
examples.ko: 그녀는 항상 자기가 믿는 것을 지켜 내.

senses.note: stand up for yourself = 자기 입장을 당당히 밝히다. stand up to + 사람 = ~에게 맞서다(의미가 다름).

senses.meaningEn: a small bright point of light in the night sky

examples.en: You can see so many stars from here.
Can you find the brightest star in the sky?
examples.ko: 하늘에서 가장 밝은 별 찾을 수 있어?

senses.note: a shooting star = 별똥별. 밤하늘에 별이 많다 = The sky is full of stars.

senses.meaningEn: a famous and popular actor, singer, or player

examples.en: She wants to be a movie star.
He's the star of the team.

senses.note: K-pop star, movie star, soccer star 처럼 뒤에 붙여 씀.

senses.meaningEn: a symbol used to show how good something is

examples.en: I gave the restaurant five stars.
This hotel only has three stars.

senses.note: a five-star hotel = 5성급 호텔. 리뷰 별점 = star rating.

senses.meaningEn: to look at someone or something for a long time without moving your eyes

examples.en: Why is that man staring at us?
examples.ko: 저 남자가 왜 우리를 빤히 쳐다보지?

examples.en: Don't stare; it's not polite.

senses.note: stare at + 대상. look 보다 오래, 눈을 떼지 않고 보는 것 — 무례하거나 놀란 느낌. 'stare into space' = 멍하니 허공을 보다.

senses.meaningEn: to begin doing something, or to begin happening

examples.en: Let's start the meeting now.
School starts at eight thirty.

senses.note: start to do / start doing 둘 다 가능. begin 보다 구어적이고 훨씬 자주 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: to make a car or machine begin to work

examples.en: The car won't start this morning.
examples.ko: 오늘 아침에 차 시동이 안 걸려.

examples.en: Press this button to start the washing machine.

senses.note: 기계에는 begin 을 쓰지 않음. start the engine = 시동을 걸다.

senses.meaningEn: the beginning of something

examples.en: We were late from the start.
It's a good start. Keep going!

senses.note: at the start of = ~의 초반에. 명사로는 start 가 begin 보다 훨씬 흔함(beginning 과 비교).

senses.meaningEn: to begin doing something again from the beginning

examples.en: I made a mistake, so I had to start over.
Let's start over from the first line.

senses.note: 미국식. 영국식은 start again / start afresh. 틀린 것을 지우고 새로 하는 그림.

senses.meaningEn: to begin a new life or relationship after a bad experience

examples.en: She moved to a new city to start over.
examples.ko: 그녀는 새로 시작하려고 다른 도시로 이사했어.

examples.en: Can we forget the fight and start over?
examples.ko: 그 싸움은 잊고 다시 시작할 수 있을까?

senses.note: start over (again) = 새 출발하다. 이별·이사·실패 뒤 '새 출발'의 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: a place where trains or buses stop so people can get on or off

examples.en: The train leaves from Seoul Station at nine.
How do I get to the subway station?

senses.note: train station, subway station, bus station 처럼 앞에 교통수단을 붙여 말함. 한국어 '역'을 그대로 station 하나로 말해도 보통 기차역/지하철역으로 이해됨.

senses.meaningEn: a building where a particular service or type of work is done

examples.en: There's a police station across the street.
We stopped at a gas station to fill up.

senses.note: police station(경찰서), fire station(소방서), gas station(주유소), TV/radio station(방송국) 등 짝으로 외우기.

senses.meaningEn: to live or sleep somewhere for a short time

examples.en: We stayed at a small hotel near the beach.
examples.ko: 우리는 해변 근처 작은 호텔에 묵었어.

examples.en: Can I stay at your place tonight?
examples.ko: 오늘 밤 너희 집에서 자도 돼?

senses.note: stay at + 숙소, stay with + 사람, stay in + 도시. stay home = 집에 있다(at 없이도 됨). 짧은 체류는 stay, 거주는 live.

senses.meaningEn: to continue to be in a particular state

examples.en: Stay calm and don't worry.
It's cold outside, so stay warm!

senses.note: stay + 형용사: stay healthy, stay safe, stay awake(안 자고 있다). stay up late = 늦게까지 안 자다.

senses.meaningEn: a period of time that you spend in a place

examples.en: Enjoy your stay in Korea!
How long was your stay in Tokyo?

senses.note: Enjoy your stay. 는 호텔에서 자주 듣는 말. overnight stay = 1박.

senses.meaningEn: to not go near a person, place, or thing

examples.en: Stay away from the dog. It bites.
examples.ko: 그 개 가까이 가지 마. 물어.

examples.en: The doctor told me to stay away from sugar.

senses.note: stay away from + 사람/장소/음식. 'Stay away from me!'(저리 가!) 는 강한 경고.

senses.meaningEn: to not go to a place you normally go to

examples.en: Many students stayed away because of the flu.
examples.ko: 독감 때문에 많은 학생이 학교에 나오지 않았어.

examples.en: If you have a fever, stay away from work.

senses.note: 병이 전염될 때 쓰는 공지 표현. stay home 과 비슷.

senses.meaningEn: to stay at home instead of going out

examples.en: It's raining, so let's just stay in tonight.
examples.ko: 비 오니까 오늘 밤은 그냥 집에 있자.

examples.en: I stayed in all weekend and watched movies.

senses.note: stay in = stay (at) home. 'stay in bed'(침대에 계속 있다)처럼 stay in + 장소 로도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to not come home, especially until late at night

examples.en: Don't stay out too late. It's a school night.
examples.ko: 너무 늦게까지 밖에 있지 마. 내일 학교 가잖아.

examples.en: We stayed out until two in the morning.
examples.ko: 우리는 새벽 두 시까지 밖에 있었어.

senses.note: 부모가 아이에게 자주 하는 말. stay out all night = 밤새 안 들어오다.

senses.meaningEn: to not become involved in something

examples.en: Please stay out of this. It's not your problem.
examples.ko: 이 일에 끼어들지 마. 네 문제 아니야.

examples.en: Try to stay out of trouble this time.

senses.note: stay out of + 일/장소. stay out of trouble, stay out of my room(내 방에 들어오지 마).

senses.meaningEn: to sleep at someone's house for a night

examples.en: It's late. Why don't you stay over tonight?
examples.ko: 늦었네. 오늘 밤 자고 가는 게 어때?

examples.en: My cousin stayed over at our place last weekend.
examples.ko: 지난 주말에 사촌이 우리 집에서 자고 갔어.

senses.note: stay over at + 집. 아이들의 '파자마 파티'는 sleepover. stay overnight 도 같은 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: to not go to bed until later than usual

examples.en: I stayed up late watching a movie.
Don't stay up too late, you have school tomorrow.
examples.ko: 너무 늦게까지 안 자고 있지 마, 내일 학교 가야 해.

senses.note: stay up late / stay up all night(밤새다) / stay up until 2 처럼 시간 표현과 함께. '밤새다'는 stay up all night 또는 pull an all-nighter.

senses.meaningEn: to take something that belongs to someone else without permission

examples.en: Someone stole my bike from the station.
examples.ko: 누가 역에서 내 자전거를 훔쳐 갔어.

examples.en: My wallet was stolen on the subway.

senses.note: steal + 물건(steal a bike). 사람을 털 때는 rob + 사람/장소(rob a bank). 과거형 stole, 과거분사 stolen. steel(강철)과 발음이 같음.

senses.meaningEn: to suddenly get someone's love or attention

examples.en: The little puppy stole everyone's heart.
examples.ko: 그 작은 강아지가 모두의 마음을 사로잡았어.

examples.en: She stole the show with her dance.
examples.ko: 그녀의 춤이 그날 무대를 완전히 휘어잡았어.

senses.note: steal someone's heart = 마음을 훔치다. steal the show = 주목을 독차지하다.

senses.meaningEn: to move one step backwards

examples.en: Please step back from the edge of the platform.
He stepped back to let me through the door.
examples.ko: 그는 내가 문을 지나갈 수 있게 뒤로 물러섰어.

senses.note: step back from + 위험한 곳. 지하철·공연장 안내 방송에서 자주 들림.

senses.meaningKo: 한 발 물러서서 (큰 그림을) 보다, 거리를 두다
senses.meaningEn: to stop being closely involved for a while so you can think clearly

examples.en: Let's step back and look at the whole plan.
examples.ko: 한 발 물러서서 전체 계획을 살펴보자.

examples.en: Sometimes you need to step back and take a break.
examples.ko: 가끔은 한 발 물러나 쉬어야 해.

senses.note: step back from the project = 프로젝트에서 잠시 손을 떼다. 'take a step back' 도 같은 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: doing one part at a time, in order

examples.en: Let me explain it step by step.
Follow the recipe step by step.

senses.note: little by little 은 '양이 조금씩', step by step 은 '순서대로 한 단계씩'. 형용사로 쓸 때는 하이픈: a step-by-step guide(단계별 안내서).

senses.meaningEn: to become involved in a difficult situation in order to help or stop it

examples.en: The teacher stepped in to stop the fight.
If they can't agree, Mom will step in.
examples.ko: 그들이 합의하지 못하면 엄마가 개입하실 거야.

senses.note: 보통 도우려고 끼어드는 긍정적인 뉘앙스. 격식은 intervene.

senses.meaningEn: to do someone's job for a short time because they cannot do it

examples.en: Jane is sick, so I'll step in for her today.
Thanks for stepping in at the last minute.
examples.ko: 마지막 순간에 대신 들어와 줘서 고마워.

senses.note: step in for + 사람. fill in for 와 거의 같음.

senses.meaningEn: to leave a room or building for a short time

examples.en: Can I step out for a minute? I have a call.
She just stepped out. Can I take a message?
examples.ko: 지금 잠깐 자리를 비우셨어요. 메모 남겨 드릴까요?

senses.note: go out 보다 '잠깐' 나가는 느낌. 전화 응대에서 'He's stepped out.' = 잠시 자리에 없음. step out of the room / the car.

senses.meaningEn: to come out beyond a surface, or to push part of your body out

examples.en: Your shirt is sticking out of your bag.
The boy stuck out his tongue at me.

senses.note: stick out your tongue / hand / leg. stick out of + 장소 = ~에서 튀어나오다.

senses.meaningEn: to be easy to notice because of being different

examples.en: With that red hat, you really stick out.
examples.ko: 그 빨간 모자를 쓰니까 정말 눈에 띈다.

examples.en: Her name stuck out on the list.
examples.ko: 명단에서 그녀 이름이 눈에 확 들어왔어.

senses.note: stand out 은 좋은 뜻(돋보이다)으로 많이 쓰고, stick out 은 '어울리지 않아 튄다'는 느낌이 섞임. stick out like a sore thumb = 유난히 튀다.

senses.meaningEn: to continue doing something difficult until it is finished

examples.en: The class is hard, but I'll stick it out.
examples.ko: 수업이 어렵지만 끝까지 버텨 볼 거야.

examples.en: He stuck out the job for one more year.

senses.note: 보통 stick it out 의 형태로 씀. 포기하고 싶지만 끝까지 간다는 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: to continue doing or using something and not change it

examples.en: I'm trying to stick to my diet this month.
examples.ko: 이번 달엔 식단을 꾸준히 지키려고 노력 중이야.

examples.en: Stick to the plan and don't change anything.

senses.note: stick to the plan / rules / diet / schedule. 'Stick to it!' = 포기하지 말고 계속해! 과거 stuck.

senses.meaningEn: to limit yourself to one thing instead of trying others

examples.en: I'll stick to water, thanks.
Let's stick to the main road. It's safer.

senses.note: 음식·음료 주문 때 'I'll stick to ~' = 그냥 ~로 할게요. stick to the point = 요점만 말하다.

senses.meaningEn: continuing up to now, longer than expected

examples.en: Are you still at the office?
I still love this old song.
examples.ko: 나는 이 옛날 노래가 여전히 좋아.

senses.note: 계속되고 있는 상태를 말함. 끝나지 않은 일을 부정문에서 말할 때는 yet(not yet)을 더 자주 씀. 위치는 be동사 뒤, 일반동사 앞.

senses.meaningEn: despite that; even so

examples.en: It was cold, but we still had fun.
He is busy, but he still calls his mom.

senses.note: but 과 함께 "그래도"의 뜻을 강조할 때 자주 씀. 문장 맨 앞에 Still, ... 로 쓰면 "그렇기는 해도".

senses.meaningEn: not moving

examples.en: Stand still while I take the picture.
examples.ko: 사진 찍을 테니까 가만히 서 있어.

examples.en: The baby would not sit still.

senses.note: sit still, stand still, keep still, hold still 처럼 동사와 묶어서 씀. still water = (탄산 없는) 생수, sparkling water 의 반대.

senses.meaningEn: the organ inside your body where food goes after you eat, or the front part of your body below your chest

examples.en: My stomach hurts after eating too much.
Don't take this medicine on an empty stomach.

senses.note: 발음 주의: 끝의 ch 는 /k/ 소리. 아이들 말로는 tummy, 구어로 belly. 배가 꾸르륵 = My stomach is growling.

senses.meaningEn: a pain in your stomach

examples.en: I have a stomachache. I think I ate too much.
examples.ko: 배가 아파. 너무 많이 먹었나 봐.

examples.en: He stayed home from school with a stomachache.
examples.ko: 그는 배가 아파서 학교에 안 가고 집에 있었어.

senses.note: have a stomachache. stomach ache 로 띄어 쓰기도 함. 더 일반적인 구어: My stomach hurts.

senses.meaningEn: a small piece of rock, or the hard material it is made of

examples.en: He threw a stone into the water.
The old bridge is made of stone.

senses.note: 재료일 때는 불가산(made of stone). 미국 일상어에서는 작은 돌을 rock 이라고 더 많이 함. 보석은 precious stone / gemstone.

senses.meaningEn: to not continue doing something

examples.en: Stop talking and listen, please.
It stopped raining an hour ago.

senses.note: stop doing = ~하는 것을 멈추다. stop to do = ~하기 위해 멈추다(뜻이 다름!). Stop it! = 그만해!

senses.meaningEn: to not move any more, or to make something not move

examples.en: The bus stops right in front of my house.
examples.ko: 버스가 우리 집 바로 앞에 서.

examples.en: Please stop here. I'll get out.

senses.note: 택시에서 '여기 세워 주세요'는 Please stop here. / Right here is fine.

senses.meaningEn: a place where a bus or train stops for people to get on and off

examples.en: Get off at the next stop.
Where's the nearest bus stop?

senses.note: bus stop = 버스 정류장, 지하철역은 station. 'my stop' = 내가 내릴 역.

senses.meaningEn: to visit a place or person for a short time, often on the way somewhere

examples.en: Can I stop by your place after work?
examples.ko: 퇴근하고 너희 집에 잠깐 들러도 돼?

examples.en: I stopped by the store to get some milk.

senses.note: stop by + 장소(전치사 없이도 됨: Stop by anytime!). 짧고 가벼운 방문. visit 보다 훨씬 캐주얼.

senses.meaningEn: to stay somewhere for a short time during a long journey

examples.en: We stopped over in Tokyo for one night.
examples.ko: 우리는 도쿄에서 하루 밤 묵고 갔어.

examples.en: Does this flight stop over anywhere?

senses.note: 명사 stopover = 경유(지). 비행기 환승은 layover 도 많이 씀. stop by(잠깐 들르다)와 혼동 주의.

senses.meaningEn: a place where you can buy things

examples.en: I need to go to the store for some milk.
Is there a convenience store around here?

senses.note: 미국식에서 가장 일반적인 '가게'. grocery store(식료품점), department store(백화점), convenience store(편의점). the store 라고만 하면 흔히 마트를 뜻함.

senses.meaningEn: to keep things in a place until you need them

examples.en: Store the rice in a cool, dry place.
Where do you store your winter clothes?

senses.note: 컴퓨터·휴대폰의 저장도 store(저장 공간 = storage). '안전하게 보관하다'는 keep safe 로도 자주 말함.

senses.meaningEn: very bad weather with strong wind and heavy rain or snow

examples.en: A big storm is coming this weekend.
The storm knocked down a lot of trees.

senses.note: snowstorm(눈보라), thunderstorm(뇌우), typhoon(태풍: 한국·동아시아), hurricane(허리케인: 미국). a storm in a teacup = 사소한 일로 큰 소란.

senses.meaningEn: with strong wind, heavy rain, and sometimes thunder

examples.en: Don't go swimming in stormy weather.
It was a dark and stormy night.

senses.meaningEn: full of strong feelings and arguments

examples.en: They had a stormy relationship.
It was a stormy meeting with lots of shouting.

senses.note: a stormy relationship/meeting = 감정이 격하게 오가는 관계·회의.

senses.meaningEn: a description of real or imagined events, told for fun or to teach

examples.en: Grandma told us a story before bed.
examples.ko: 할머니가 자기 전에 이야기를 해 주셨어.
