examples.en: I like stories with a happy ending.

senses.note: tell a story(이야기를 해 주다), read a story. short story = 단편 소설. '사정/변명'의 뜻도: That's a long story.(얘기하면 길어).

senses.meaningEn: a report about something in the news

examples.en: Did you see the story about the storm?
It was the top story on the news tonight.
examples.ko: 오늘 밤 뉴스의 첫 번째 소식이었어.

senses.note: 뉴스의 꼭지 하나를 story 라고 함. cover story = 잡지 표지 기사. 거짓말을 가볍게 '꾸며낸 이야기'로 말할 때도 story.

senses.meaningEn: a level of a building

examples.en: We live in a two-story house.
The building is twenty stories tall.

senses.note: '몇 층짜리 건물'을 말할 때 story(미국식) / storey(영국식). '3층에 있다'는 on the third floor 로 floor 를 씀.

senses.meaningEn: a kitchen appliance with burners on top that you cook on

examples.en: Turn off the stove when the water boils.
Don't touch the stove, it's still hot.

senses.note: 한국어 '가스레인지'는 영어로 stove(또는 range). on the stove = 레인지 불 위에서. '전자레인지'는 microwave.

senses.meaningEn: a closed heater that burns wood or gas to warm a room

examples.en: We sat by the wood stove to stay warm.
examples.ko: 우리는 몸을 녹이려고 장작 난로 옆에 앉았어.

examples.en: The old cabin has a small stove for heat.
examples.ko: 그 오래된 오두막에는 난방용 작은 난로가 있어.

senses.note: wood stove(장작 난로). 전기 난방기는 보통 heater 라고 함.

senses.meaningEn: in a line that does not bend or turn

examples.en: Go straight for two blocks.
Keep going straight and you'll see it.

senses.note: go straight(직진하다), straight ahead(바로 앞에). 길 안내의 기본 표현.

senses.meaningEn: immediately, without stopping or doing anything else first

examples.en: I went straight home after work.
Go straight to bed, it's late.

senses.note: straight home/to bed/to the point. 미국 구어에서 right 도 같은 뜻(right after work).

senses.meaningEn: not bent or curved

examples.en: She has long straight hair.
Draw a straight line here.

senses.note: straight hair = 생머리(curly 의 반대). 발음이 같은 strait(해협)과 혼동 주의.

senses.meaningEn: unusual or surprising; difficult to understand

examples.en: I heard a strange noise last night.
It's strange that the shop is closed today.

senses.note: 구어에서는 weird 를 더 많이 씀. stranger(명사) = 낯선 사람. '이상하다(아프다)' 는 I feel strange.

senses.meaningEn: not known or seen before

examples.en: It's hard to sleep in a strange bed.
examples.ko: 낯선 침대에선 잠이 잘 안 와.

examples.en: I felt lost in the strange city.

senses.note: a strange city / strange place = 처음 가 본, 익숙하지 않은 곳. 이 뜻에서는 '이상하다' 는 뉘앙스가 약함.

senses.meaningEn: a person you do not know

examples.en: Don't talk to strangers, okay?
A stranger asked me for directions.

senses.note: strange(이상한)에서 왔지만 stranger 는 '이상한 사람'이 아니라 '모르는 사람'.

senses.meaningKo: 처음 온 사람, 그곳을 잘 모르는 사람
senses.meaningEn: a person who is new to a place and does not know it well

examples.en: Sorry, I'm a stranger here too.
He's a stranger in this town.
examples.ko: 그는 이 동네에 처음 온 사람이야.

senses.note: 길을 물어볼 때 I'm a stranger here. = 저도 여기 잘 몰라요.

senses.meaningEn: a small, soft red fruit with tiny seeds on the outside

examples.en: Strawberries are my favorite fruit in spring.
examples.ko: 딸기는 봄에 내가 제일 좋아하는 과일이야.

examples.en: I'd like a strawberry milkshake, please.

senses.note: 복수형은 strawberries(y → ies). strawberry jam, strawberry ice cream 처럼 맛을 나타낼 때는 단수형으로 앞에 붙임. 비슷한 과일: blueberry, raspberry.

senses.meaningEn: a road in a town or city with buildings on both sides

examples.en: I live on Main Street, near the park.
examples.ko: 나는 공원 근처 메인 스트리트에 살아.

examples.en: Be careful when you cross the street.

senses.note: on the street(거리에서), across the street(길 건너편에). 도시 안의 길은 street, 도시 밖 큰길은 road.

senses.meaningEn: a long narrow line of color on a surface

examples.en: The shirt has blue and white stripes.
examples.ko: 그 셔츠에는 파란색과 흰색 줄무늬가 있어.

examples.en: Zebras have black and white stripes.

senses.note: a striped shirt(줄무늬 셔츠, 형용사). 한국어 "스트라이프"와 같은 뜻. 점무늬는 dots.

senses.meaningEn: having a lot of physical power or good health

examples.en: My brother is strong enough to carry two boxes.
examples.ko: 우리 형은 상자 두 개를 들 만큼 힘이 세.

examples.en: Eat well and you'll grow strong.

senses.meaningEn: having a lot of flavor, smell, or alcohol

examples.en: I need a strong coffee this morning.
This cheese has a very strong smell.

senses.note: strong coffee / strong tea / strong smell. '진하다'를 thick 이나 deep 으로 옮기지 않도록 주의.

senses.meaningEn: having a lot of force or power

examples.en: There was a strong wind last night.
Hold on tight, the current is strong here.

senses.note: strong wind, strong rain 은 heavy rain 이 더 자연스럽다.

senses.meaningEn: wind that blows with a lot of force

examples.en: There was a strong wind, so my hat flew away.
Strong winds are expected tomorrow afternoon.

senses.note: 바람은 strong(heavy wind 는 어색, 비는 heavy rain). 동사로는 The wind is blowing hard. 날씨 설명은 It's windy today. 아주 강한 바람은 gale, 약한 바람은 breeze.

senses.meaningEn: a person who is studying at a school or university

examples.en: How many students are in your class?
I'm a student at Seoul National University.

senses.note: 미국에서는 초등학생도 student. 영국에서는 어린 학생을 pupil 이라고도 함. '대학생'은 college/university student.

senses.meaningEn: to spend time learning about a subject

examples.en: I have to study for my English test.
She studied all night for the exam.

senses.note: study for a test = 시험 공부를 하다. study English (전치사 없음). learn 은 결과(익히다), study 는 과정(공부하다)에 초점.

senses.meaningEn: to learn a subject at a university or college

examples.en: My sister studies medicine in Seoul.
What did you study in college?

senses.note: What's your major? 도 흔히 쓰지만 What do you study? 가 더 구어적.

senses.meaningEn: a room in a house used for reading and working

examples.en: Dad is working in his study.
We turned the small room into a study.

senses.note: study room 이라고 하면 도서관의 '열람실'처럼 들릴 수 있음. 집의 서재는 그냥 study.

senses.meaningEn: not smart; showing a lack of good thinking

examples.en: That was a stupid thing to say. Sorry.
examples.ko: 그렇게 말한 건 바보 같았어. 미안해.

examples.en: Don't call your brother stupid.

senses.note: 사람에게 직접 쓰면 매우 무례함. 자기 실수에는 I feel so stupid.(내가 너무 바보 같아) 로 자주 씀. 좀 더 부드러운 말은 silly.

senses.meaningEn: used to show you are annoyed about something

examples.en: This stupid phone won't turn on!
examples.ko: 이 바보 같은 전화기가 안 켜지네!

examples.en: I'm so tired of this stupid traffic.
examples.ko: 이 지겨운 교통 체증 정말 지쳤어.

senses.note: 물건·상황에 붙여 짜증을 표현하는 구어. 친한 사이에서만.

senses.meaningEn: a particular design or shape of clothes, hair, or things

examples.en: I like this style of jacket.
She changed her hair style last week.

senses.note: hairstyle 은 한 단어로도 씀. 한국어 '스타일 좋다'(몸매·옷차림)는 영어로 She has great style. 또는 She dresses well.

senses.meaningEn: the way someone does something

examples.en: Everyone has their own style of learning.
I don't like his style of talking.
examples.ko: 그의 말하는 방식이 마음에 안 들어.

senses.note: That's not my style. = 내 취향/방식이 아니야. in style = 유행하는(in fashion).

senses.meaningEn: an area of knowledge that you study at school, like math or history

examples.en: What's your favorite subject at school?
Math is my worst subject.

senses.note: favorite subject = 좋아하는 과목. 과목 이름(math, English)은 subject 뒤에 바로 붙이지 않고 단독으로 씀.

senses.meaningEn: the thing that people are talking or writing about

examples.en: Let's change the subject, okay?
The subject of her talk was healthy eating.

senses.note: change the subject = 화제를 바꾸다. 이메일 제목 줄도 subject (line).

senses.meaningEn: to take one number away from another

examples.en: Subtract three from ten, and you get seven.
The kids are learning to subtract.

senses.note: subtract A from B = B 에서 A 를 빼다(from 순서 주의). 식을 읽을 때는 ten minus three. 일상에서 '빼다'는 take away 도 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: an underground train system in a city

examples.en: The subway is the fastest way to get downtown.
I take the subway to work every day.

senses.note: 미국식 subway, 영국식 the underground / the tube, 유럽은 metro. 지하철을 '타다'는 take the subway, '지하철로'는 by subway. 지하철역은 subway station, 노선은 line(Line 2).

senses.meaningEn: quickly and without warning

examples.en: Suddenly, the lights went out.
The dog suddenly started to bark.

senses.note: 이야기할 때 문장 맨 앞에 두고 쉼표: Suddenly, ... 형용사 sudden(갑작스러운). all of a sudden 도 같은 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: a sweet white or brown substance used to make food and drinks sweet

examples.en: How many sugars do you take in your coffee?
examples.ko: 커피에 설탕 몇 개 넣어 드세요?

examples.en: This cake has too much sugar in it.
examples.ko: 이 케이크는 설탕이 너무 많이 들어갔어.

senses.note: 보통 셀 수 없음(a spoonful of sugar). 커피·차에 넣는 '설탕 한 개(한 스푼)' 를 말할 때만 one sugar, two sugars 처럼 셈. 발음은 [슈거].

senses.meaningEn: a jacket and trousers or skirt made of the same cloth

examples.en: He wears a suit to work every day.
I need a new suit for the wedding.
examples.ko: 결혼식 때 입을 새 정장이 필요해.

senses.note: swimsuit(수영복), spacesuit(우주복)처럼 "~복"에도 쓰임. 한 벌이 a suit(단수).

senses.meaningEn: to look good on someone

examples.en: That color really suits you.
examples.ko: 그 색깔 너한테 정말 잘 어울려.

examples.en: Short hair suits her face.
examples.ko: 짧은 머리가 그녀 얼굴에 잘 어울려.

senses.note: suit 은 색·스타일이 "사람에게" 어울릴 때. 옷과 옷이 어울리면 match, 사이즈가 맞으면 fit.

senses.meaningEn: to be convenient or acceptable for someone

examples.en: Does Friday suit you for lunch?
Any time after five suits me.

senses.note: Suit yourself. = 네 맘대로 해.(약간 퉁명스러움)

senses.meaningEn: a large bag with a handle that you carry clothes in when you travel

examples.en: I packed my suitcase the night before the trip.
examples.ko: 여행 전날 밤에 짐을 다 쌌어.

examples.en: Her suitcase was too heavy to lift.
examples.ko: 그녀의 여행 가방은 너무 무거워서 들 수 없었어.

senses.note: 한국어 '캐리어'는 영어로 suitcase(또는 carry-on = 기내용). carrier 는 통신사·항공사·운반 기구를 뜻함. pack/unpack a suitcase = 짐을 싸다/풀다. 짐 전체는 luggage/baggage.

senses.meaningEn: to say the main points of something in a short way

examples.en: Can you sum up the story in one sentence?
examples.ko: 그 이야기를 한 문장으로 요약해 줄래?

examples.en: To sum up, we need more time and money.
examples.ko: 요약하면, 우리는 시간과 돈이 더 필요해요.

senses.note: To sum up, ... = 결론적으로/요약하면(발표·글 마무리 표현). 명사 summary(요약). 수학의 sum(합)에서 온 말.

senses.meaningEn: to show or describe the most important qualities of something or someone very well

examples.en: That photo sums up our whole trip.
examples.ko: 그 사진이 우리 여행을 한마디로 보여 줘.

examples.en: 'Lazy but lovely' sums him up perfectly.

senses.note: That sums it up. = 바로 그거야(딱 그 말이야). 사람·상황의 특징을 한마디로 요약할 때.

senses.meaningEn: the warmest season of the year, between spring and fall

examples.en: What are you doing this summer?
Korean summers are hot and humid.

senses.note: summer vacation(여름 방학), summer camp, in the summer. 형용사처럼 명사 앞에 바로 쓴다(summer clothes). this summer 앞에는 in 을 쓰지 않는다.

senses.meaningEn: the big bright star in the sky that gives us light and heat

examples.en: The sun comes up at six in summer.
Don't look straight at the sun.

senses.note: 하나뿐이라 보통 the sun. 해가 뜨다 = the sun rises/comes up, 지다 = the sun sets/goes down. sun(해)과 son(아들)은 발음이 같음.

senses.meaningEn: the light and heat that come from the sun

examples.en: Let's sit in the sun for a while.
I got too much sun at the beach.

senses.note: in the sun = 햇볕 아래, in the shade = 그늘에. get some sun = 햇볕을 좀 쬐다.

senses.meaningEn: the day of the week after Saturday and before Monday

examples.en: We visit my grandparents every Sunday.
examples.ko: 우리는 일요일마다 할아버지 할머니 댁에 가.

examples.en: The store is closed on Sunday.

senses.note: 미국 달력은 일요일이 한 주의 첫 날. Sunday brunch, Sunday dinner 처럼 가족 식사와 자주 짝을 이룸. sundae(아이스크림)와 발음이 같아 혼동 주의.

senses.meaningEn: a tall plant with a very large yellow flower

examples.en: Sunflowers grow very tall in summer.
I like eating sunflower seeds.

senses.note: sun + flower 를 붙여 한 단어로. 해바라기씨 = sunflower seeds, 해바라기유 = sunflower oil.

senses.meaningEn: with bright light from the sun and few clouds

examples.en: It's sunny today, so let's go to the park.
Tomorrow will be sunny and warm.

senses.note: 날씨 표현은 It's + 형용사: It's sunny. 'sunny side up' = 한쪽만 익힌 달걀 프라이.

senses.meaningEn: cheerful and happy

examples.en: She has a sunny personality.
He gave me a big, sunny smile.

senses.meaningEn: the time in the morning when the sun first appears

examples.en: We got up early to watch the sunrise.
The sunrise over the sea was beautiful.

senses.note: at sunrise = 해 뜰 때. 새해 첫 일출 = the first sunrise of the year. 해가 뜨다(동사) = the sun rises.

senses.meaningEn: the time in the evening when the sun goes down

examples.en: Let's watch the sunset from the beach.
The sky turns orange at sunset.
examples.ko: 해 질 때 하늘이 주황색으로 변해.

senses.note: at sunset = 해 질 때. 해가 지다(동사) = the sun sets / goes down. '노을'을 말할 때도 sunset 을 쓰면 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: a large store that sells food, drinks, and things for the house

examples.en: I'm going to the supermarket. Do you need anything?
The supermarket is open twenty-four hours.

senses.note: 미국 일상 회화에서는 grocery store 를 더 자주 씀. 한국어 '마트'를 mart 라고 하면 통하지 않을 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: a light meal eaten in the evening, or the last meal of the day

examples.en: What's for supper tonight?
We had a late supper after the movie.
examples.ko: 영화 보고 나서 늦은 저녁을 먹었어.

senses.note: dinner 보다 가볍고 가정적인 느낌. 지역·가정에 따라 dinner 와 같은 뜻으로도 쓰임. 일상에서는 dinner 가 훨씬 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: to think that something is probably true

examples.en: I suppose he forgot about the meeting.
Do you suppose it will snow tonight?
examples.ko: 오늘 밤 눈이 올 것 같아?

senses.note: I suppose so. = 그런 것 같아.(약간 마음에 안 들지만 동의) I suppose 는 guess 보다 조금 격식.

senses.meaningEn: (be supposed to) to be expected or required to do something

examples.en: You're supposed to be in bed by nine.
We were supposed to meet at six.

senses.note: be supposed to 는 "약속·규칙상 그렇게 하기로 되어 있다". 실제로는 안 했을 때 자주 씀(were supposed to). 수동형 아님에 주의.

senses.meaningEn: certain that something is true

examples.en: Are you sure the store is open today?
examples.ko: 오늘 가게가 문 연 거 확실해?

examples.en: I'm not sure what time the bus comes.
examples.ko: 버스가 몇 시에 오는지 잘 모르겠어.

senses.note: I'm not sure. = '잘 모르겠어' 의 부드러운 표현(I don't know 보다 공손). sure about + 명사 / sure (that) 절. make sure = 확인하다, 꼭 ~하도록 하다.

senses.meaningEn: used to say yes or agree to a request

examples.en: Can I borrow your pen? — Sure, here you go.
examples.ko: 펜 좀 빌릴 수 있을까? — 물론이지, 여기.

examples.en: Sure, I'd love to come to your party.

senses.note: 요청에 대한 가벼운 승낙. 미국에서 Thank you. 에 대한 답으로 Sure. 도 흔함(= 별말씀을). 격식 자리에서는 Certainly.

senses.meaningEn: to make someone feel surprised, often with something they did not expect

examples.en: We surprised Dad with a birthday cake.
examples.ko: 우리는 생일 케이크로 아빠를 놀라게 했어.

examples.en: It surprised me that she came early.

senses.note: '내가 놀랐다'는 I was surprised(수동) — I surprised ✗. surprised at/by + 명사. 'Surprise!' 는 깜짝 파티 등장 때 외치는 말.

senses.meaningEn: something you did not expect, or the feeling it gives you

examples.en: I have a surprise for you. Close your eyes.
examples.ko: 너한테 깜짝 선물이 있어. 눈 감아.

examples.en: What a surprise to see you here!

senses.note: surprise party = 깜짝 파티. 'What a surprise!' = 이게 누구야/깜짝 놀랐네. 'No surprise there.' = 뭐 그럴 줄 알았어.

senses.meaningEn: feeling or showing surprise because something unexpected happened

examples.en: I was surprised to see him at the party.
She wasn't surprised by the news at all.
examples.ko: 그녀는 그 소식에 전혀 놀라지 않았어.

senses.note: surprised to + 동사 / surprised at/by + 명사. 놀라운 것은 surprising. 좋은 의미든 나쁜 의미든 '예상 밖'이면 모두 쓸 수 있음.

senses.meaningEn: to make food or drink go down your throat into your stomach

examples.en: Swallow the pill with a glass of water.
examples.ko: 약을 물 한 잔과 함께 삼켜.

examples.en: My throat hurts when I swallow.

senses.note: 병원에서 It hurts to swallow. 는 꼭 알아 둘 표현. 씹지 않고 통째로 삼키는 것은 swallow whole.

senses.meaningEn: a small bird with long pointed wings and a forked tail

examples.en: We saw swallows flying over the river.
A swallow built a nest under our roof.
examples.ko: 제비가 우리 집 지붕 밑에 둥지를 지었어.

senses.note: 동사 '삼키다'와 철자·발음이 같은 전혀 다른 뜻. 문맥으로 구분.

senses.meaningEn: a warm knitted piece of clothing for the top half of the body

examples.en: I wore a warm sweater under my coat.
My grandma made me this sweater.
examples.ko: 이 스웨터는 할머니가 짜 주신 거야.

senses.note: 영국식은 jumper. 한국어 '니트'는 영어로 sweater 또는 knit top. 발음은 sweat(땀)+er.

senses.meaningEn: to clean a floor with a broom

examples.en: I sweep the kitchen floor every morning.
examples.ko: 나는 매일 아침 주방 바닥을 쓸어.

examples.en: She swept the leaves off the steps.

senses.note: sweep - swept - swept. sweep the floor(바닥을 쓸다), sweep up(쓸어 모으다). 진공청소기로 청소하는 건 vacuum.

senses.meaningEn: tasting like sugar

examples.en: This cake is too sweet for me.
I like my coffee a little sweet.

senses.note: sweet and sour = 달고 신(탕수육 소스). 단 것을 좋아하면 have a sweet tooth.

senses.meaningEn: kind and gentle in a way that makes people like you

examples.en: That's so sweet of you, thank you.
My grandmother is a very sweet person.

senses.note: 칭찬할 때 You're so sweet. 자주 씀. 미국 구어로 'Sweet!'(좋다!) 감탄사로도 사용.

senses.meaningEn: to move through water by moving your arms and legs

examples.en: I can't swim, so I stay near the edge.
We swam in the sea every morning.

senses.note: swim-swam-swum. '수영하러 가다'는 go swimming, 수영장은 swimming pool, 수영복은 swimsuit. 물고기도 swim 한다.

senses.meaningEn: a time when you swim

examples.en: Let's go for a swim after lunch.
examples.ko: 점심 먹고 수영 한 번 하러 가자.

examples.en: A quick swim in the lake felt great.

senses.note: go for a swim / have a swim = 수영 한 번 하다. go for a walk, go for a run 과 같은 구조.

senses.meaningEn: the sport or activity of moving through water using your arms and legs

examples.en: Swimming is my favorite summer activity.
examples.ko: 수영은 내가 여름에 가장 좋아하는 활동이야.

examples.en: I go swimming twice a week.
examples.ko: 나는 일주일에 두 번 수영하러 가.

senses.note: go swimming(수영하러 가다). 수영장은 swimming pool, 수영복은 swimsuit. 동사 swim 은 불규칙(swam, swum).

senses.meaningEn: a large structure filled with water for people to swim in

examples.en: Is there a swimming pool in this building?
We go to the swimming pool every Saturday morning.

senses.note: 실내 수영장 indoor swimming pool, 야외 outdoor swimming pool. 대화에서는 그냥 pool 로 줄여 말함. 수영복은 swimsuit(여) / swim trunks(남).

senses.meaningEn: to stop a machine or light by pressing a switch

examples.en: Please switch off your phones now.
Did you switch the heater off?

senses.meaningEn: to stop paying attention or stop thinking about work

examples.en: I switch off when he talks about cars.
On vacation, I just want to switch off.
examples.ko: 휴가 때는 그냥 머리를 비우고 싶어.

senses.note: '집중을 끄다'. 지루해서 귀를 닫는 것, 혹은 일 생각을 멈추고 쉬는 것 둘 다.

senses.meaningEn: to start a machine or light by pressing a switch

examples.en: Switch on the light, it's dark in here.
She switched the TV on to watch the news.
examples.ko: 그녀는 뉴스 보려고 TV 를 켰어.

senses.note: turn on 과 같은 뜻. 영국에서 switch on/off 가 더 흔함. 명사 switch = 스위치.

senses.meaningEn: a soft shirt with short sleeves and no collar or buttons

examples.en: I usually wear a t-shirt and jeans on weekends.
Can I get this t-shirt in a medium?

senses.note: 글로는 T-shirt(대문자 T)가 표준 표기. 모양이 T 자여서 붙은 이름.

senses.meaningEn: a piece of furniture with a flat top and legs

examples.en: Could we get a table for two, please?
Put the plates on the table, please.

senses.note: 식탁을 차리다 = set the table, 치우다 = clear the table. 식당 예약: book a table.

senses.meaningEn: a list of facts or numbers arranged in rows and columns

examples.en: Look at the table on page twelve.
The table shows the prices for each month.
examples.ko: 이 표는 월별 가격을 보여 줘.

senses.note: 구구단은 times tables / multiplication table. 목차는 table of contents.

senses.meaningEn: the long part at the back of an animal's body

examples.en: The dog is wagging its tail. It's happy!
examples.ko: 개가 꼬리를 흔들고 있어. 좋아하나 봐!

examples.en: A monkey can hang by its tail.

senses.note: tale(이야기)과 발음이 같음(/teɪl/). 동전 던지기에서 'heads or tails?' 는 '앞면이야 뒷면이야?'. 비행기 뒷부분도 tail.

senses.meaningEn: to carry or move something or someone to another place

examples.en: Don't forget to take your umbrella today.
I'll take the kids to school this morning.
examples.ko: 오늘 아침은 내가 애들 학교에 데려다줄게.

senses.note: take 는 '여기서 저기로' 가져가다, bring 은 '이쪽으로' 가져오다.

senses.meaningEn: to travel using a bus, train, taxi, etc.

examples.en: Let's take a taxi. It's raining.
I take the subway to work every day.

senses.note: take a bus / take the train / take a taxi. ride 보다 take 가 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: to need a certain amount of time

examples.en: It takes about ten minutes to walk there.
How long does it take by bus?

senses.note: It takes + 시간 + to 동사. '걸리다'를 spend 로 쓰지 않도록 주의.

senses.meaningEn: to swallow medicine

examples.en: Take this medicine twice a day after meals.
examples.ko: 이 약은 하루 두 번 식후에 드세요.

examples.en: Did you take your pills this morning?

senses.note: 약은 eat 이 아니라 take.

senses.meaningEn: to wash yourself while sitting in a bathtub full of water

examples.en: I like to take a hot bath on cold nights.
examples.ko: 추운 밤엔 뜨거운 물에 목욕하는 게 좋아.

examples.en: The kids took a bath before bed.

senses.note: bath = 욕조에 몸을 담그는 것, shower = 서서 물 맞는 것. 영국식은 have a bath. 아기를 씻기다 = give the baby a bath.

senses.meaningEn: to stop working or studying for a short time to rest

examples.en: Let's take a break and get some coffee.
You've been studying for hours. Take a break.
examples.ko: 몇 시간 동안 공부했잖아. 좀 쉬어.

senses.note: take a rest 보다 take a break 가 훨씬 자연스러움. take a short break / take a coffee break.

senses.meaningEn: to travel somewhere by bus

examples.en: I take a bus to school every day.
examples.ko: 나는 매일 버스를 타고 학교에 가.

examples.en: We took a bus to the beach yesterday.
examples.ko: 우리는 어제 버스 타고 해변에 갔어.

senses.note: take a bus = '버스로 이동하다'. ride a bus 는 '버스에 타고 있는 행위' 느낌. 특정 노선이면 take the bus / take the number 5 bus. 한국어 '타다'를 보고 ride 를 쓰면 어색할 때가 많음.

senses.meaningEn: to sleep for a short time, usually during the day

examples.en: I'm tired. I'm going to take a nap.
The baby took a nap after lunch.

senses.note: '낮잠 자다'를 sleep a nap ✗ 으로 쓰지 않음. take a short nap / take a quick nap. 영국식은 have a nap.

senses.meaningEn: to photograph someone or something with a camera or phone

examples.en: Can you take a picture of us, please?
I took a lot of pictures on the trip.

senses.note: 사진을 "찍다" 는 take (a picture/photo). make a picture 는 그림을 만든다는 뜻이 되므로 틀림. take a picture of + 대상. 셀카 = take a selfie.

senses.meaningEn: a polite way to tell or ask someone to sit down

examples.en: Please take a seat, the doctor will see you soon.
examples.ko: 앉아서 기다리세요, 선생님이 곧 봐 주실 거예요.

examples.en: I took a seat near the back.

senses.note: 손님·방문자에게 Sit down 보다 공손. Have a seat 도 같은 뜻. 병원·사무실·면접에서 자주 들음. 과거형 took a seat.

senses.meaningEn: to wash yourself under running water from a shower

examples.en: I take a shower every morning before work.
examples.ko: 나는 매일 아침 출근 전에 샤워해.

examples.en: He took a quick shower after the game.

senses.note: 미국식 take a shower, 영국식 have a shower. "do a shower" 는 틀림. shower 는 동사로도 OK: I shower every day.

senses.meaningEn: to travel somewhere by taxi

examples.en: It's late. Let's take a taxi home.
I took a taxi to the airport this morning.
examples.ko: 오늘 아침에 택시 타고 공항에 갔어.

senses.note: 미국 구어에서는 take a cab 도 매우 흔함. '택시를 잡다'는 catch / get a taxi, '택시를 부르다'는 call a taxi.

senses.meaningEn: to do an exam or test to show what you know

examples.en: I have to take a math test tomorrow.
She took the test and passed easily.

senses.note: '시험을 보다'를 see a test ✗ 로 쓰지 않음. 미국식 take a test / take an exam, 영국식 sit an exam. 시험을 '내는' 쪽(선생님)은 give a test. pass(합격) / fail(불합격).

senses.meaningEn: to go for a short walk for pleasure or exercise

examples.en: Let's take a walk after dinner.
I took a walk along the river this morning.

senses.note: take a walk = go for a walk. 영국식은 have a walk 도 씀. 개를 산책시키다 = walk the dog / take the dog for a walk.

senses.meaningEn: to look or behave like an older member of your family

examples.en: She takes after her mother.
Who do you take after, Mom or Dad?

senses.note: 가족(윗사람)에게만 씀. 친구와 비슷하다는 look like / be similar to. 분리 불가: take after her(○) take her after(×).

senses.meaningEn: to separate something into its parts

examples.en: He took the old clock apart to fix it.
Don't take apart the remote again!

senses.note: take A apart / take apart A 둘 다 가능. 반대말은 put together(조립하다).

senses.meaningEn: to remove something from a place or from someone

examples.en: The waiter took our plates away.
Mom took my phone away for a week.
examples.ko: 엄마가 일주일 동안 내 휴대폰을 뺏어 가셨어.

senses.note: take something away from someone = 압수하다, 빼앗다. 영국에서 takeaway 는 '포장 음식'.

senses.meaningEn: to subtract one number from another

examples.en: Ten take away three is seven.
Take away five and what do you get?

senses.note: 초등 수학에서 minus 대신 자주 쓰는 말. 더하기는 plus / add.

senses.meaningEn: to return something to the shop or to its owner

examples.en: I took the shoes back to the store.
Can you take this book back to the library?
examples.ko: 이 책 도서관에 반납해 줄 수 있어?

senses.meaningEn: to say that something you said was wrong or you did not mean it

examples.en: I'm sorry, I take it back.
You can't take back what you said.
examples.ko: 네가 한 말은 되돌릴 수 없어.

senses.note: I take it back. = 방금 한 말 취소. 싸움 후 사과할 때 유용.

senses.meaningEn: to look after someone or something

examples.en: Who takes care of the baby at night?
I'll take care of your dog this weekend.
examples.ko: 이번 주말에 내가 네 강아지 봐 줄게.

senses.note: take care of + 사람/동물/식물. 헤어질 때 Take care! = 잘 지내.

senses.meaningEn: to deal with a task or problem

examples.en: Don't worry, I'll take care of the bill.
She took care of all the paperwork.

senses.note: I'll take care of it. = 내가 처리할게. 식당에서 계산을 맡겠다는 말로 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to remove something from a wall or high place, or to pull a structure apart

examples.en: Take down the old posters, please.
We took the tent down in the rain.

senses.meaningEn: to write down what someone says

examples.en: Take down this phone number.
She took down every word the teacher said.
examples.ko: 그녀는 선생님 말씀을 한 마디도 안 놓치고 적었어.

senses.meaningEn: to understand and remember something you hear or see

examples.en: It was too much to take in at once.
Give me a minute to take this in.

senses.meaningEn: to let a person or animal live in your home

examples.en: We took in a stray cat last winter.
Her family took me in for the summer.
examples.ko: 그녀 가족이 여름 동안 나를 받아 주셨어.

senses.meaningEn: to make a piece of clothing smaller

examples.en: Can you take in this skirt a little?
examples.ko: 이 스커트 조금 줄여 주실 수 있어요?

examples.en: I had the pants taken in at the waist.

senses.note: 옷 수선: take in(줄이다) / let out(늘리다) / shorten(기장 줄이다).

senses.meaningEn: to relax, calm down, or not work too hard

examples.en: Take it easy. Everything will be okay.
The doctor told me to take it easy this week.
examples.ko: 의사가 이번 주는 무리하지 말라고 했어.

senses.meaningEn: used as a casual way to say goodbye

examples.en: See you tomorrow. Take it easy!
Okay, take it easy, man.

senses.note: 미국 구어에서 친한 사이의 작별 인사. 격식 있는 자리에서는 피함.

senses.meaningEn: to swallow medicine such as pills or liquid in order to get better

examples.en: Take this medicine three times a day after meals.
examples.ko: 이 약은 하루 세 번 식후에 드세요.

examples.en: Did you take your medicine this morning?

senses.note: 한국어 '약을 먹다'를 eat medicine ✗ 으로 옮기면 틀림. 반드시 take. take a pill / take two tablets / take some medicine for a cold.

senses.meaningEn: to write down important points while you listen or read

examples.en: Please take notes during the lesson.
I took notes while the teacher was talking.

senses.note: '메모하다'를 memo ✗ 라고 쓰지 않음(영어 memo 는 사내 공문). take notes 가 가장 자연스럽고, '한 가지를 적어 두다'는 make a note of it. 수업 필기 노트 = notes(복수).

senses.meaningEn: to remove clothes or shoes

examples.en: Please take off your shoes at the door.
It's hot. Take your jacket off.

senses.meaningEn: to leave the ground and start flying

examples.en: The plane takes off at nine thirty.
We're taking off soon, so turn off your phone.

senses.meaningEn: to not go to work for a period of time

examples.en: I'm taking Friday off to see the doctor.
Why don't you take a few days off?

senses.note: take + 날 + off: take Monday off, take a week off.

senses.meaningEn: to remove something from a place, or carry it outside

examples.en: Take out your books, everyone.
It's your turn to take the trash out.

senses.meaningEn: to buy food at a restaurant and eat it somewhere else

examples.en: For here or to take out?
Let's take out some pizza tonight.

senses.note: 미국 영어 takeout(명사) = 포장 음식. 영국은 takeaway. 주문 시 To go, please. 도 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to go somewhere with someone and pay for them

examples.en: He took me out for dinner on Friday.
I'm taking the kids out to the zoo.

senses.meaningEn: to get money from a bank account

examples.en: I need to take out some cash.
She took out fifty dollars from the ATM.

senses.meaningEn: to start doing a job or duty that someone else was doing

examples.en: Can you take over the cooking for a minute?
examples.ko: 잠깐 요리 좀 대신 맡아 줄래?

examples.en: She took over as manager in May.

senses.note: take over from someone = ~의 뒤를 이어 맡다. 운전·요리 교대할 때도 Let me take over.

senses.meaningEn: to get control of a company or place

examples.en: A big company took over the little shop.
examples.ko: 큰 회사가 그 작은 가게를 인수했어.

examples.en: Weeds have taken over the garden.

senses.note: 명사 takeover = 인수. 비즈니스 뉴스에서 매우 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: to do something one after another, each person doing it in turn

examples.en: Let's take turns washing the dishes.
The kids took turns on the swing.

senses.note: take turns + -ing / take turns at(to) + 동사. '네 차례야'는 It's your turn. 반드시 복수 turns 로 쓰고(take turn ✗), 어떤 순서로 하는지는 in turn.

senses.meaningEn: to start doing a new hobby or activity

examples.en: I took up yoga last year.
He wants to take up the guitar.

senses.note: take up + 취미/운동/악기. '시작하다'를 start 만 쓰지 말고 take up 을 써 보기.

senses.meaningEn: to fill an amount of space or time

examples.en: This sofa takes up too much room.
examples.ko: 이 소파가 자리를 너무 많이 차지해.

examples.en: Homework takes up my whole evening.

senses.note: take up space / room / time. 공간은 room(불가산)으로 자주 표현.

senses.meaningEn: used to tell someone there is no need to hurry

examples.en: Take your time. We're not in a hurry.
Take your time and read it carefully.
examples.ko: 서두르지 말고 천천히 꼼꼼히 읽어 봐.

senses.note: 상대를 배려하는 표현. 주어를 바꿔 쓸 수 있음: He took his time getting ready.(그는 느긋하게 준비했다 — 약간 불평하는 뉘앙스).

senses.meaningEn: to say things to someone in a conversation

examples.en: We talked for hours on the phone.
examples.ko: 우리는 전화로 몇 시간 동안 이야기했어.

examples.en: Can we talk about this later?
examples.ko: 이 얘기는 나중에 하면 안 될까?

senses.note: talk to/with someone about something. speak 보다 가볍고 일상적. '우리 얘기 좀 하자' = We need to talk.

senses.meaningEn: a short speech or conversation about a subject

examples.en: She gave a talk about recycling.
I had a long talk with my dad last night.

senses.note: give a talk = 강연(발표)하다. have a talk with = ~와 이야기하다. 잡담은 small talk.

senses.meaningEn: to speak about a particular subject with someone

examples.en: Let's talk about your trip to Jeju.
examples.ko: 네 제주 여행 얘기 좀 해 보자.

examples.en: We talked about the movie for an hour.
examples.ko: 우리는 그 영화에 대해 한 시간 동안 이야기했어.

senses.note: talk about + 명사/-ing(talk about going). discuss 는 about 없이 바로 목적어(discuss the plan). "discuss about" 은 한국인이 자주 하는 실수.

senses.meaningEn: to speak about a problem or feeling so that you feel better or get help

examples.en: Do you want to talk about it?
It helps to talk about your worries.

senses.note: "Do you want to talk about it?" 은 힘들어하는 사람에게 건네는 대표적인 위로 표현.

senses.meaningEn: to answer someone rudely, especially a parent or teacher

examples.en: Don't talk back to your mother!
He got in trouble for talking back to the teacher.

senses.note: 주로 아이가 어른에게 버릇없이 대답하는 상황. talk back to 사람. 명사형 backtalk(말대꾸). "No backtalk!" = 말대꾸 금지.

senses.meaningEn: to speak with someone

examples.en: Can I talk to you for a minute?
examples.ko: 잠깐 얘기 좀 할 수 있을까?

examples.en: I talked to my mom on the phone last night.

senses.note: talk to = talk with(미국 구어에서는 둘 다 흔함). talk to 사람 about 주제 순서. "Don't talk to me like that." 처럼 말투를 말할 때도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: to speak to someone in order to get help or solve a problem

examples.en: You should talk to your teacher about it.
I'll talk to the manager and ask for a refund.

senses.note: 문제가 있을 때 "담당자에게 말하다" 의 뜻. "I'll talk to him." 은 "내가 그 사람한테 말해 볼게(해결해 볼게)".

senses.meaningEn: having a greater height than average

examples.en: My dad is very tall, almost two meters.
examples.ko: 우리 아빠는 키가 아주 커, 거의 2미터야.

examples.en: How tall are you?

senses.note: 사람·나무·건물의 키는 tall, 산·천장처럼 바닥에서 높이 있는 것은 high. 키를 물을 때는 How tall are you? 이고 How high 는 쓰지 않는다.

senses.meaningEn: a long thin strip of sticky material

examples.en: Can I borrow some tape?
Hold the poster while I put tape on it.
examples.ko: 내가 테이프 붙이는 동안 포스터 잡아 줘.

senses.note: 셀 수 없는 명사. 한국어 '스카치테이프'는 상표명이고, 영어는 tape 또는 Scotch tape(미).

senses.meaningEn: to fasten something with tape

examples.en: Tape the box shut before you mail it.
She taped the note to the door.

senses.note: tape A to B = A 를 B 에 붙이다.

senses.meaningEn: to have a particular flavor

examples.en: This soup tastes a little salty.
It tastes like chicken.

senses.note: taste + 형용사(tastes good / sweet), taste like + 명사(tastes like chicken). '맛있다'는 It tastes good. 이 가장 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: to put a small amount of food in your mouth to find out its flavor

examples.en: Taste the soup and tell me what you think.
examples.ko: 수프 맛 좀 보고 어떤지 말해 줘.

examples.en: Have you ever tasted Korean rice cake?
examples.ko: 한국 떡 먹어 본 적 있어?

senses.note: '한번 먹어 봐'는 Try it. 이 더 흔함. taste 는 조금 맛보는 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: the flavor of food or drink

examples.en: I love the taste of fresh strawberries.
examples.ko: 나는 신선한 딸기 맛을 정말 좋아해.

examples.en: This tea has a strong taste.

senses.note: '내 취향이다'는 It's my taste. 가 아니라 It's to my taste. / It's my style. 가 자연스러움. 명사 taste 에는 '취향·감각(good taste)' 뜻도 있음.

senses.meaningEn: having a good, strong flavor

examples.en: These noodles are really tasty.
Do you know any tasty and cheap restaurants?
examples.ko: 맛있고 싼 식당 아는 데 있어?

senses.note: delicious 보다 조금 가벼운 느낌. 짜고 매운 음식처럼 '맛이 진한' 음식에 잘 어울림. '맛있다'를 It tastes good. 로도 자주 표현.

senses.meaningEn: a car with a driver that you pay to take you somewhere

examples.en: Let's take a taxi, it's raining.
I called a taxi to the airport.

senses.note: take a taxi / get a taxi / call a taxi. 미국 구어로 cab 도 매우 흔함(grab a cab). 길에서 손 들어 잡는 건 hail a taxi. 택시 기사는 taxi driver / cab driver.

senses.meaningEn: a hot drink made by pouring water over dried leaves

examples.en: Would you like some tea?
I drink green tea every morning.

senses.note: 영어에서 tea 만 말하면 보통 홍차(black tea). 녹차는 green tea, 허브차는 herbal tea. 한 잔은 a cup of tea, 가게에서는 two teas 도 가능. 영국에서는 tea 가 '저녁 식사'를 뜻하기도 함.

senses.meaningEn: to give lessons to students in a school or class

examples.en: My mom teaches math at a high school.
Who taught you English?

senses.note: teach someone something(간접목적어 먼저). 과거·과거분사 모두 taught. 가르치는 사람은 teacher.

senses.meaningEn: to show someone how to do something

examples.en: Can you teach me how to ride a bike?
examples.ko: 자전거 타는 법 가르쳐 줄 수 있어?

examples.en: Grandpa taught us to fish last weekend.
examples.ko: 할아버지가 지난 주말에 우리한테 낚시를 가르쳐 주셨어.

senses.note: teach someone (how) to + 동사. 길을 '가르쳐 주다'는 teach ✗ → tell/show me the way.

senses.meaningEn: a person whose job is to teach in a school

examples.en: My English teacher is from Canada.
The teacher asked us to sit down.

senses.note: 호칭으로 Teacher! 라고 부르지 않음. Mr. Kim / Ms. Lee 처럼 성을 붙여 부름.

senses.meaningEn: a group of players who play a sport or game together against another group

examples.en: Our team won the game two to one.
Which team do you play for?

senses.meaningEn: a group of people who work together on a job

examples.en: I work on a small team of five people.
examples.ko: 나는 다섯 명짜리 작은 팀에서 일해.

examples.en: The whole team is meeting at three.

senses.note: 미국식은 on a team, 영국식은 in a team. team up (with) = 함께 팀을 이루다. 한국식 '팀장'은 team leader/manager.

senses.meaningEn: to join another person or group in order to do something together

examples.en: Let's team up for the science project.
The two shops teamed up to hold a sale.
examples.ko: 두 가게가 힘을 합쳐 세일을 열었어.

senses.note: team up with + 사람/회사 = ~와 팀을 이루다. 학교 과제·게임·회사 협업 모두 OK. 명사 team(팀), teammate(팀 동료).

senses.meaningEn: a drop of water that comes from your eye when you cry

examples.en: Tears ran down her face.
He wiped away a tear and smiled.

senses.note: '눈물'은 /tɪr/ [티어]. 보통 복수 tears 로 쓴다. in tears = 울면서.

senses.meaningEn: to pull something such as paper or cloth into pieces

examples.en: Be careful not to tear the map.
I tore my jeans on the fence.

senses.note: '찢다'는 /ter/ [테어]로 발음이 다르다. 과거형 tore, 과거분사 torn. tear up = 갈기갈기 찢다.

senses.meaningEn: to tear paper into small pieces

examples.en: She tore up the letter and threw it away.
Tear up the old bills before you recycle them.

senses.note: tear(찢다, /ter/) – tore – torn. tear up a contract = 계약을 파기하다. 발음 주의: 눈물 tear 는 /tɪr/.

senses.meaningEn: to start to have tears in your eyes because you are sad or moved

examples.en: I teared up at the end of the movie.
examples.ko: 영화 끝날 때 눈물이 핑 돌았어.

examples.en: Mom tears up every time she hears that song.
examples.ko: 엄마는 그 노래만 들으면 눈물이 글썽해져.

senses.note: 이 뜻은 tear 가 '눈물'(/tɪr/)이라 발음이 다르고, 과거형도 규칙형 teared up 임. 뜻과 발음이 완전히 다른 두 단어.

senses.meaningEn: a young person between 13 and 19 years old

examples.en: My son is a teenager now, so he sleeps a lot.
examples.ko: 우리 아들이 이제 십 대라서 잠을 많이 자.

examples.en: Many teenagers spend hours on their phones.
examples.ko: 많은 십 대들이 폰을 몇 시간씩 봐.

senses.note: thirteen~nineteen 처럼 -teen 으로 끝나는 나이라서 teenager. 구어로 짧게 teen. 형용사는 teenage (teenage boy).

senses.meaningEn: the plural of tooth

examples.en: Brush your teeth before bed.
He has very white teeth.

senses.note: tooth 의 불규칙 복수. 이를 닦다 = brush my teeth(wash ×). 이 사이에 뭐가 끼다 = something is stuck in my teeth.

senses.meaningEn: a device you use to talk to someone far away

examples.en: The telephone is ringing, can you get it?
May I use your telephone, please?

senses.note: 일상에서는 phone 이 훨씬 흔하고 telephone 은 약간 격식적. telephone number = phone number.

senses.meaningEn: to call someone on the phone

examples.en: Please telephone us if you have any questions.
She telephoned the office this morning.

senses.note: 동사로는 call 이 훨씬 자연스러움. telephone to us (X) → telephone us.

senses.meaningEn: a machine with a screen that shows programs

examples.en: We bought a new television for the living room.
Turn the television down, please.

senses.note: 일상 회화에서는 TV 가 훨씬 많이 쓰임. 격식 있는 글에서 television.

senses.meaningEn: the programs that are shown on a television

examples.en: I don't watch much television these days.
She works in television.

senses.note: watch television 에는 the 를 붙이지 않음 (watch the television X). on television = 텔레비전에(서).

senses.meaningEn: to give information to someone by speaking

examples.en: Tell me about your weekend.
He told me the store was closed.

senses.note: tell + 사람 + 내용(tell me the truth). say 와 달리 듣는 사람이 바로 뒤에 옴: tell me (tell to me ✗). tell a story / tell a lie / tell the truth.

senses.meaningEn: to order or advise someone to do something

examples.en: Mom told me to clean my room.
I told you not to touch that!

senses.note: tell someone to + 동사 / tell someone not to + 동사. ask 보다 강한 지시.

senses.meaningEn: to know or recognize the difference between things

examples.en: Can you tell the twins apart?
I can't tell if he's joking or not.

senses.note: can/can't tell = 알아보다/못 알아보다. tell A from B = A 와 B 를 구별하다. You can never tell. = 알 수 없는 일이야.

senses.meaningEn: to say something that is not true on purpose

examples.en: Don't tell a lie to your mom.
He told a lie about where he was last night.
examples.ko: 그는 어젯밤 어디 있었는지 거짓말을 했어.

senses.note: '거짓말하다'는 tell a lie 또는 동사 lie(say a lie 아님). 'lie to + 사람': Don't lie to me. 가벼운 거짓말은 white lie.

senses.meaningEn: to describe events to someone, either real or made up

examples.en: Grandma told us a story before bed.
examples.ko: 할머니가 자기 전에 이야기를 해 주셨어.

examples.en: Can you tell me a story about your trip?

senses.note: '이야기하다'는 tell a story(say/speak a story 아님). tell + 사람 + a story: tell me a story. 책을 읽어 주는 건 read a story. 농담은 tell a joke.

senses.meaningEn: to be able to read a clock and know what time it is

examples.en: My son is learning to tell the time.
examples.ko: 우리 아들이 시계 보는 법을 배우고 있어.

examples.en: Can you tell the time on this old clock?
examples.ko: 이 오래된 시계로 시간 읽을 수 있어?

senses.note: tell 이 '말하다'가 아니라 '알아보다, 구별하다'의 뜻. 상대에게 '지금 몇 시예요?'는 Can you tell me the time? / What time is it? (me 가 들어가면 묻는 말이 됨).

senses.meaningEn: to say what really happened or what is really true

examples.en: Just tell the truth. I won't be angry.
examples.ko: 그냥 사실대로 말해. 화 안 낼게.

examples.en: She told the truth about the broken window.
examples.ko: 그녀는 깨진 창문에 대해 사실대로 말했어.

senses.note: truth 앞에는 항상 the(tell a truth 아님). To tell the truth, ... = '사실은, 솔직히 말하면'(문장 앞 표현): To tell the truth, I don't like coffee.

senses.meaningEn: how hot or cold something is

examples.en: What's the temperature outside?
The temperature will drop tonight.

senses.note: 기온이 오르다/내리다 = the temperature rises/goes up / drops/falls. 미국은 화씨(Fahrenheit) 사용: 섭씨 20도 ≈ 화씨 68도. room temperature = 상온.

senses.meaningEn: the heat of a person's body; a fever

examples.en: Let me take your temperature.
She has a temperature, so she's staying home.

senses.note: 체온을 재다 = take someone's temperature. have/run a temperature = 열이 있다(= have a fever). 정상 체온 = normal temperature.

senses.meaningEn: a building where people of some religions, such as Buddhists, go to pray

examples.en: We visited a beautiful temple in the mountains.
Take off your shoes before you enter the temple.

senses.note: 불교 사원은 Buddhist temple, 템플스테이는 temple stay 로 그대로 통함. 교회는 church, 이슬람 사원은 mosque.

senses.meaningEn: the flat part on each side of your head, next to your eye

examples.en: I have a headache right here, in my temples.
He rubbed his temples and closed his eyes.

senses.note: 보통 복수 temples 로 씀. 안경다리가 닿는 부분.

senses.meaningEn: the number 10

examples.en: Can you count to ten in English?
I'll be back in ten minutes.

senses.note: 서수는 tenth(10th). ten out of ten = 10점 만점에 10점(아주 좋다). 달러를 말할 때 ten bucks = 10달러.

senses.meaningEn: a game in which two or four players hit a small ball over a net with rackets

examples.en: Do you want to play tennis this afternoon?
I take tennis lessons on Saturdays.

senses.note: play tennis(테니스를 치다). 라켓은 racket, 코트는 court. 탁구는 table tennis 또는 ping-pong.

senses.meaningEn: coming after the ninth one

examples.en: Today is our tenth wedding anniversary.
My daughter's tenth birthday is next week.
examples.ko: 딸의 열 번째 생일이 다음 주야.

senses.note: 10th. 서수는 날짜·층·생일·기념일에 자주 쓰임: on the tenth(10일에).

senses.meaningEn: one of ten equal parts of something

examples.en: A tenth of the students got full marks.
He finished in less than a tenth of a second.

senses.note: 소수 0.1 = one tenth(또는 point one).

senses.meaningEn: very bad or unpleasant

examples.en: The weather was terrible all week.
I'm terrible at singing.

senses.note: terrible at + 활동 = ~을 아주 못하다. 부사 terribly 는 '몹시'(terribly sorry = 정말 죄송)로 좋은 뜻에도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: feeling very ill or very unhappy

examples.en: I feel terrible. I think I have a fever.
examples.ko: 몸이 아주 안 좋아. 열이 있는 것 같아.

examples.en: You look terrible. Go home and rest.
examples.ko: 안색이 아주 안 좋아. 집에 가서 쉬어.

senses.note: feel terrible 은 몸이 아픈 것 외에 '미안해서 마음이 안 좋다' 로도 씀(I feel terrible about yesterday).

senses.meaningEn: a set of questions to check what someone knows

examples.en: We have a spelling test on Friday.
I got a good grade on the test.

senses.note: take a test(시험을 보다) — see a test ✗. pass/fail a test = 합격/불합격하다. exam 보다 작고 자주 보는 시험.

senses.meaningEn: a medical check to find out about your health

examples.en: The doctor did a blood test.
I need an eye test for new glasses.
examples.ko: 새 안경 때문에 시력 검사를 받아야 해.

senses.note: blood test(혈액 검사), eye test(시력 검사). 검사를 받다 = have/get a test.

senses.meaningEn: to try something to see if it works

examples.en: Let me test the microphone first.
They tested the new phone for a week.
examples.ko: 그들은 새 폰을 일주일 동안 테스트했어.

senses.meaningEn: to send someone a short written message on a phone

examples.en: Text me when you get home.
He texted me back right away.

senses.note: text + 사람 = 문자하다(동사로 아주 흔함). text back = 답장하다. 한국의 '카톡하다'도 영어로는 text/message 로 말함.

senses.meaningEn: the written words in a book, article, or on a screen

examples.en: Read the text and answer the questions.
The text on this page is too small.

senses.note: a text 는 '문자 메시지'(= a text message), 셀 수 없는 text 는 '글/본문'. 교과서는 textbook.

senses.meaningEn: a book used for studying a subject at school

examples.en: Please open your textbook to page 20.
I left my math textbook at home.

senses.note: 한 단어로 붙여 씀(text book ✗). 참고서는 study guide, 문제집은 workbook.

senses.meaningEn: used after a comparative to introduce the second thing being compared

examples.en: This one is cheaper than that one.
My brother is taller than me.

senses.note: 비교급(-er / more) 뒤에는 꼭 than. then(그 다음에)과 철자·발음이 비슷해 글로 쓸 때 자주 틀림. 구어에서는 than me, 격식에서는 than I (am).

senses.meaningEn: used with 'more' or 'less' before a number or amount

examples.en: It costs less than ten dollars.
I waited more than an hour.

senses.note: more than 10 = 10 초과(10 포함 아님). '10 이상' 을 정확히 말하려면 10 or more.

senses.meaningEn: to tell someone you are grateful for something they did

examples.en: Thank you so much for your help.
I thanked her for the lovely gift.
examples.ko: 멋진 선물을 줘서 고맙다고 그녀에게 말했어.

senses.note: thank 사람 for 명사/-ing. Thank you 뒤에 for 를 쓰는 것에 주의(Thank you for coming). 'Thanks' 는 더 가벼운 표현. 명사 thanks 는 항상 -s.

senses.meaningEn: happy and grateful that something good happened or something bad did not

examples.en: I'm thankful for my family and friends.
We were thankful that nobody got hurt.

senses.note: thankful for + 명사 / thankful that + 문장. grateful 과 거의 같음. 미국 Thanksgiving(추수감사절)에 많이 듣는 단어.

senses.meaningEn: a friendly, informal way to say thank you

examples.en: Thanks for the ride home!
Thanks a lot, that really helped.

senses.note: thank you 보다 가벼운 말. thanks for + 명사/동명사(Thanks for coming). 격식 있는 자리나 윗사람에게는 Thank you 가 더 안전. 대답은 You're welcome / No problem / Sure.

senses.meaningEn: used with no to politely refuse something offered

examples.en: No thanks, I'm full.
Would you like a bag? — No, thanks.

senses.note: No, thanks. 는 '싫어요'가 아니라 공손한 거절. 받아들일 때는 Yes, please.

senses.meaningEn: words or actions that show you are grateful

examples.en: He left without a word of thanks.
examples.ko: 그는 고맙다는 말 한마디 없이 떠났어.

examples.en: Thanks to you, we got there on time.
examples.ko: 네 덕분에 우리 시간 맞춰 도착했어.

senses.note: thanks to + 사람/사물 = '~덕분에'(좋은 결과). 나쁜 결과에 쓰면 비꼬는 느낌. 복수형처럼 보여도 항상 s 를 붙임.

senses.meaningEn: used for a person or thing that is farther away or already mentioned

examples.en: Who is that man by the door?
examples.ko: 문 옆에 있는 저 남자 누구야?

examples.en: I did not know that. Thanks for telling me.

senses.note: 멀리 있거나 이미 언급된 것. 복수는 those. That's right / That's okay 처럼 앞 말 전체를 받을 때도 that.

senses.meaningEn: used to join a sentence to verbs like think, say, or know

examples.en: I think that she is right.
He said that he was tired.

senses.note: 말할 때는 that 을 자주 생략함: I think she is right. 이 that 은 약하게 /ðət/ 로 발음.

senses.meaningEn: to the degree shown or mentioned

examples.en: The test was not that hard.
I did not know he was that tall.

senses.note: not that + 형용사 = 그렇게 ~하지는 않다. so 보다 가벼운 구어 표현.

senses.meaningEn: used before a noun when the listener already knows which one you mean

examples.en: Can you close the door, please?
The movie we saw last night was great.

senses.note: 처음 언급하면 a, 다시 말하면 the: I saw a dog. The dog was big. 모음 앞에서는 /ði/ 로 발음(the apple).

senses.meaningEn: used before things that there is only one of, or places everyone knows

examples.en: The sun is very strong today.
I'm going to the bank after lunch.

senses.note: the sun, the moon, the sky, the internet. 일상 장소(the bank, the station, the doctor)는 어느 곳인지 서로 알기 때문에 the 를 씀.

senses.meaningEn: used before a superlative, an instrument, or an adjective used as a noun

examples.en: She is the tallest girl in our class.
examples.ko: 그 애가 우리 반에서 키가 가장 커.

examples.en: My son plays the piano every evening.

senses.note: 악기 앞엔 the(play the guitar), 운동 앞엔 없음(play soccer). 식사·나라·언어(have lunch, Korea, English) 앞에도 the 를 안 붙임.

senses.meaningKo: 눈에 넣어도 아프지 않을 사람, 가장 소중한 사람
senses.meaningEn: the person you love most and are very proud of

examples.en: Her little daughter is the apple of her eye.
examples.ko: 그녀의 어린 딸은 눈에 넣어도 아프지 않을 아이야.

examples.en: You're the apple of my eye, Grandpa said.

senses.note: 주로 부모·조부모가 자식·손주를, 또는 연인을 가리킬 때. be the apple of + 소유격 + eye. 사과와는 무관한 아주 오래된 표현.

headword: the early bird catches the worm

senses.meaningKo: 일찍 일어나는 새가 벌레를 잡는다, 부지런해야 얻는다
senses.meaningEn: people who get up or act early have the best chance of success

examples.en: I got to the sale at 7. The early bird catches the worm!
examples.ko: 세일에 7시에 도착했지. 부지런한 사람이 얻는 거야!

examples.en: Wake up early. The early bird catches the worm.
examples.ko: 일찍 일어나. 일찍 일어나는 새가 벌레를 잡는다잖아.

senses.note: 줄여서 "the early bird" 라고도 한다. 식당·행사의 early bird discount(조기 할인) 도 여기서 온 말.

senses.meaningEn: used to reply to a good wish by wishing the other person the same thing

examples.en: Have a nice weekend! The same to you.
Merry Christmas! And the same to you!

senses.note: Happy New Year, Good luck, Enjoy your meal 같은 덕담에 답할 때. 구어에서는 Same to you! / You too! 로 줄임. 가게 점원이 'Have a good day' 하면 'You too' 가 가장 자연스러움. 단, 'Nice to meet you' 에는 'You too' 가 맞고 'The same to you' 는 어색.

senses.meaningEn: a building where plays and shows are performed on a stage

examples.en: We're going to the theater to see a musical.
The theater was full on opening night.
examples.ko: 첫 공연 날 극장이 꽉 찼어.

senses.note: 영국식 철자는 theatre. 연극·뮤지컬 '분야' 자체도 theater 라고 함(She studies theater).

senses.meaningEn: a place where you watch movies on a big screen

examples.en: Is the new movie still in theaters?
examples.ko: 그 새 영화 아직 극장에서 하고 있어?

examples.en: Let's watch it at the theater, not at home.

senses.note: 미국에서는 영화관을 movie theater 또는 그냥 theater 라고 함. 영국은 cinema. in theaters = 극장 상영 중.

senses.meaningEn: belonging to two or more people or things already mentioned

examples.en: The kids are doing their homework.
My neighbors painted their door red.

senses.note: their(그들의) / there(거기) / they're(they are) 는 발음이 모두 같음. 성별 모르는 한 사람에게도 씀: Everyone brought their lunch.

senses.meaningEn: two or more people or things already mentioned, used as the object

examples.en: I bought apples and put them in the fridge.
My friends are here. Do you want to meet them?

senses.note: they(주어) → them(목적어) → their(소유). 빠르게 말할 때 'em 으로 줄어듦(Get 'em!). 성별 모르는 한 사람에게도 씀: Someone called; call them back.

senses.meaningEn: at that time in the past or future

examples.en: I was only five years old then.
Call me at six. I'll be home by then.
examples.ko: 6시에 전화해. 그때까지는 집에 가 있을 거야.

senses.note: by then = 그때까지, since then = 그때 이후로, until then = 그때까지(계속). back then = 그 당시에는.

senses.meaningEn: after that; next

examples.en: Boil the water, then add the noodles.
We had dinner and then watched a movie.
examples.ko: 우리는 저녁을 먹고 나서 영화를 봤어.

senses.note: 순서를 말할 때 first, then, finally 로 이어진다. than(~보다)과 철자 혼동 주의: then 은 시간·순서, than 은 비교.

senses.meaningEn: in that case; as a result

examples.en: If you're tired, then go to bed early.
You don't like it? Then don't eat it.

senses.note: If ... then ... 구조에서 then 은 생략해도 된다. 대화 끝에 OK then / See you then 처럼 마무리 말로도 자주 쓴다.

senses.meaningEn: in, at, or to that place

examples.en: Put the bag over there, please.
How do I get there from here?

senses.note: go there (to 없음). 'go to there' 는 흔한 실수. their(그들의)·they're 와 발음이 같으니 글로 쓸 때 주의.

senses.meaningEn: used with 'be' to say that something exists or is in a place

examples.en: There is a cat under the car.
examples.ko: 차 밑에 고양이가 한 마리 있어.

examples.en: Are there any good restaurants near here?

senses.note: 뒤에 오는 명사가 복수면 There are. 한국인은 'It has a cat' 처럼 have 를 쓰기 쉬운데, 존재는 There is/are 로 말함.

senses.meaningEn: used to comfort someone or to get their attention

examples.en: There, there. Don't cry.
There! I told you it would work.

senses.meaningEn: used when you give something to someone

examples.en: There you go, your change is two dollars.
There you go. Enjoy your meal!

senses.note: Here you go 와 거의 같음. 점원·종업원이 물건을 내놓으면서 매우 자주 씀.

senses.meaningEn: used to tell someone they have done something correctly or well

examples.en: Like this? Yes, there you go!
There you go, you did it by yourself.

senses.note: 아이가 처음 자전거를 타거나 문제를 풀었을 때 격려. 'There you go, I told you.' 는 '봐, 내가 말했잖아' 로 약간 으스대는 느낌도 됨.

senses.meaningKo: (체념) 뭐, 그런 거지, 어쩔 수 없지
senses.meaningEn: used to accept a situation that you cannot change

examples.en: We lost again, but there you go.
It's expensive, but there you go, it's Seoul.

senses.note: 문장 끝에 붙여 '그게 현실이야' 라는 체념. 억양을 내려서 말함.

senses.meaningEn: used to point to more than one thing that is near you

examples.en: How much are these?
These are my favorite shoes.

senses.note: this 의 복수형. 가까운 것 여러 개를 가리킬 때. 발음은 /ðiːz/ 로 길게, this(/ðɪs/) 와 구별.

senses.meaningEn: used before a plural noun to show which things you mean

examples.en: These cookies are still warm.
I've been so busy these days.

senses.note: these days = 요즘(현재 시제와 함께). 'this days' 는 틀림.

senses.meaningEn: at the present time, compared with the past

examples.en: I'm really busy these days.
Kids spend a lot of time on phones these days.

senses.note: 현재시제와 씀. 한국인이 자주 쓰는 recently 는 과거·완료시제와 어울리므로(I recently moved.) '요즘 ~하다(현재 상태)' 에는 these days / nowadays 가 맞음. in these days 라고 하지 않음.

senses.meaningEn: two or more people, animals, or things already mentioned, as the subject

examples.en: My parents are nice. They help everyone.
These shoes are nice, but they are too small.

senses.note: 사람·사물 모두 복수면 they. 목적어 them, 소유 their. there(거기)와 발음·철자 혼동 주의.

senses.meaningEn: one person whose gender is not known or not important

examples.en: Someone called, but they did not leave a name.
If a friend is late, they should text you.

senses.note: he or she 대신 자연스럽게 쓰는 단수 they. 동사는 복수형(they are)을 그대로 씀.

senses.meaningEn: having a large distance between two opposite sides

examples.en: I need a thick coat for winter.
The book is really thick, about 800 pages.

senses.note: th 발음 /θ/ 에 주의(sick 처럼 들리지 않게). 명사는 thickness.

senses.meaningEn: not flowing easily, or growing closely together

examples.en: The soup is too thick. Add some water.
examples.ko: 수프가 너무 걸쭉해. 물 좀 넣어.

examples.en: He has thick, curly hair.

senses.note: thick soup(걸쭉한), thick hair(숱 많은), thick fog(짙은 안개). 반대로 묽은 수프는 thin soup.

senses.meaningEn: having little fat on the body

examples.en: He got very thin when he was sick.
You look thinner. Are you eating well?
examples.ko: 살이 빠진 것 같네. 밥은 잘 먹고 있어?

senses.note: thin 은 중립적이거나 약간 부정적(너무 마른). 칭찬할 때는 slim 이 좋다.

senses.meaningEn: having a small distance between two sides

examples.en: This paper is too thin to write on.
examples.ko: 이 종이는 너무 얇아서 글씨를 쓸 수 없어.

examples.en: Wear a thin jacket, it's not that cold.
examples.ko: 얇은 재킷 입어, 그렇게 춥지 않아.

senses.note: 두께가 얇으면 thin, 두꺼우면 thick. 소리가 작으면 thin 이 아니라 quiet.

senses.meaningEn: to have an opinion or believe something is true

examples.en: I think it's going to rain today.
What do you think of my new hat?

senses.note: I think so. = 그런 것 같아 / I don't think so. = 아닐 것 같아. 부정은 I think it's not 보다 I don't think it is 가 자연스러움.

senses.meaningEn: to use your mind to solve a problem or decide something

examples.en: Let me think for a minute.
Think before you answer.

senses.note: think about = ~에 대해 생각하다, think of = ~을 떠올리다/생각해 내다. 쉽게 혼동됨.

senses.meaningEn: to have someone or something in your mind

examples.en: I think about my family every day.
What are you thinking about?

senses.note: think about = 머릿속에 떠올리다, think of = 의견이 어떤지/생각해 내다(What do you think of it?). 과거형 thought.

senses.meaningEn: to consider something carefully before deciding

examples.en: I'm thinking about moving to Busan.
Let me think about it and tell you tomorrow.

senses.note: think about + -ing(think about moving). Let me think about it. 은 즉답을 피할 때 가장 유용한 문장.

senses.meaningEn: to remember something or produce an idea in your mind

examples.en: I can't think of his name right now.
examples.ko: 지금 그 사람 이름이 생각이 안 나.

examples.en: Can you think of a good restaurant near here?
examples.ko: 이 근처 괜찮은 식당 생각나는 데 있어?

senses.note: think of + 명사. 이름·답·아이디어가 "떠오르다" 는 뜻. "I can't think of it." = 생각이 안 나.

senses.meaningEn: to have a particular opinion about someone or something

examples.en: What do you think of my new haircut?
I always think of you as my best friend.
examples.ko: 나는 늘 너를 가장 친한 친구로 생각해.

senses.note: What do you think of ~? 는 의견을 묻는 가장 흔한 표현. think of A as B = A 를 B 로 여기다.

senses.meaningEn: to consider doing something

examples.en: We're thinking of moving to Busan.
I'm thinking of buying a new phone.

senses.note: be thinking of + -ing 로 "~할까 하다". think about 과 바꿔 쓸 수 있지만, think about 은 시간을 들여 곰곰이 생각하는 느낌이 더 강함.

senses.meaningEn: to consider something carefully before you make a decision

examples.en: Let me think it over and call you tomorrow.
Think over the offer before you say yes.
examples.ko: 수락하기 전에 그 제안을 잘 생각해 봐.

senses.note: 분리 가능 구동사: 대명사는 반드시 중간에(think it over ✓, think over it ✗). 결정 전에 시간을 두고 고민할 때 씀.

senses.meaningEn: coming after the second one

examples.en: Our room is on the third floor.
This is the third time I've called you.
examples.ko: 너한테 전화하는 게 벌써 세 번째야.

senses.note: 3rd 로 줄여 씀. 날짜: March third(3월 3일). th 발음은 혀를 윗니에 살짝 대고 냄.

senses.meaningEn: one of three equal parts of something

examples.en: Cut the cake into thirds.
I ate a third of the pizza.

senses.note: 분수: one third(1/3), two thirds(2/3). 분자가 2 이상이면 -s.

senses.meaningEn: wanting or needing to drink something

examples.en: I'm really thirsty. Can I have some water?
examples.ko: 목이 너무 말라. 물 좀 마셔도 될까?

examples.en: Running makes me thirsty.

senses.note: '목마르다'는 I'm thirsty. I'm thirst 는 틀림(thirst 는 명사). 발음은 [써스티]에 가깝다.

senses.meaningEn: the number 13

examples.en: My nephew just turned thirteen.
examples.ko: 우리 조카가 막 열세 살이 됐어.

examples.en: Room thirteen is at the end of the hall.

senses.note: -teen 은 끝음절에 강세, -ty 는 첫음절에 강세: thirTEEN(13) vs THIRty(30). 서양에서 13은 불길한 숫자로 여겨져 13층이 없는 건물도 있음. teenager 는 13~19세.

senses.meaningEn: the number 30

examples.en: It's half past six, so six thirty.
About thirty people came to the wedding.

senses.note: THIRty(30) vs thirTEEN(13), 강세 위치로 구별. 시간 표현 "~시 30분"은 six thirty 처럼 숫자 뒤에 바로 붙임. 서수는 thirtieth(30th).

senses.meaningEn: used for a person or thing that is near you or that you are showing

examples.en: This soup is really good.
Is this seat taken?

senses.note: 가까우면 this, 멀면 that. 복수는 these. 전화에서 자기소개는 This is Mina.(I am Mina 보다 자연스러움).

senses.meaningEn: used for the current or coming period of time

examples.en: What are you doing this weekend?
It is very cold this winter.

senses.note: this morning / this week / this year 앞에 전치사를 붙이지 않음(on this weekend ✗).

senses.meaningEn: used to point to more than one thing that is farther away from you

examples.en: Are those your keys on the table?
examples.ko: 테이블 위에 있는 저거 네 열쇠야?

examples.en: Those look nicer than these.

senses.note: that 의 복수형. 전화로 상대방 쪽 물건을 말할 때도 those 를 씀.

senses.meaningEn: used before a plural noun for things that are not near you or were mentioned before

examples.en: Who are those people over there?
Do you remember those days in school?
examples.ko: 학교 다닐 때 그 시절 기억나?

senses.note: in those days = 그 당시에(과거). these days(요즘)와 대비해서 기억하면 좋음.

senses.meaningEn: the number 1,000

examples.en: The laptop costs about a thousand dollars.
Five thousand people live in this town.

senses.note: 영어는 세 자리마다 쉼표: 10,000 = ten thousand. 한국어 '만(10,000)'에 해당하는 단어가 없어서 ten thousand 로 말함.

senses.meaningEn: a very large number of people or things

examples.en: Thousands of fans came to the concert.
I have a thousand things to do today.

senses.note: a thousand things to do = 할 일이 엄청 많다(과장 표현).

senses.meaningEn: the number 3

examples.en: My son is three years old.
I'll be there in three minutes.

senses.note: th 는 혀를 윗니 뒤에 대고 내는 /θ/ 소리. tree(/triː/)와 구별할 것. 서수는 third(3rd). three times = 세 번.

senses.meaningEn: from one side or end of something to the other, going inside it

examples.en: The train goes through a long tunnel.
We walked through the park to school.

senses.note: across(표면 위를 가로질러)와 달리 through 는 '안을 지나서'. 창문 '너머로' 보다 = look through the window.

senses.meaningEn: from the beginning to the end of a time or activity

examples.en: She slept through the whole movie.
We're open Monday through Friday.

senses.note: 미국식 Monday through Friday = 월~금(금요일 포함). be through with(끝내다): Are you through with the book?

senses.meaningEn: to send something through the air using your hand and arm

examples.en: Throw the ball to your brother.
He threw the stone into the lake.

senses.note: throw A to B(B에게 던지다) 와 throw A at B(B를 맞히려고 던지다)는 뜻이 다름. 발음은 /θr/ — '스로우'가 아니라 번데기 발음으로 시작.

senses.meaningEn: to put something in the trash because you do not want it

examples.en: Can you throw away these old newspapers?
examples.ko: 이 낡은 신문들 좀 버려 줄래?

examples.en: Don't throw the box out yet, I need it.
examples.ko: 그 상자 아직 버리지 마, 필요해.

senses.note: '버리다'는 throw 혼자가 아니라 throw away / throw out 으로 씀. 그냥 throw the box 라고 하면 '상자를 던진다'는 뜻.

senses.meaningEn: to organize a party for people

examples.en: We're throwing a party for Dad's birthday.
They threw a big party after the game.
examples.ko: 그들은 경기 후에 큰 파티를 열었어.

senses.note: throw a party = have a party. 구어체에서 아주 흔한 표현이지만 격식 자리에서는 hold a party 가 더 어울림.

senses.meaningEn: to get rid of something you do not want, by putting it in the trash

examples.en: Don't throw away those boxes yet.
I threw the old magazines away.

senses.note: 물건을 버리다 = throw away / throw out. 쓰레기통에 '넣다'는 put it in the trash.

senses.meaningEn: to waste a chance, money, or something valuable

examples.en: Don't throw away this chance.
He threw away all his money on games.

senses.meaningEn: to get rid of something you no longer want

examples.en: Let's throw out this broken chair.
She threw out all the old food.

senses.note: throw away 와 거의 같음. 미국 구어에서 throw out 이 더 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: to force someone to leave a place

examples.en: They threw him out of the club.
The teacher threw me out of class.

senses.meaningEn: to bring food up from your stomach through your mouth

examples.en: I feel like I'm going to throw up.
The baby threw up on my shirt.

senses.note: vomit 은 의학적·격식, throw up 이 일상에서 가장 흔함. 속이 안 좋다 = I feel sick / nauseous.

senses.meaningEn: the short thick finger on the side of your hand

examples.en: The baby is sucking her thumb.
He gave me a thumbs up.

senses.note: 끝의 b 는 소리 내지 않음(/θʌm/). thumbs up = 좋아요, 찬성. 엄지발가락은 big toe.

senses.meaningEn: a sign of approval or agreement, made by raising your thumb

examples.en: She gave me a thumbs up from across the room.
examples.ko: 그녀는 방 건너편에서 나한테 엄지를 세워 보였어.

examples.en: Mom gave the plan a thumbs up.

senses.note: give (something) a thumbs up = 승인하다. 몸짓이면서 "좋아, 통과" 라는 뜻. 반대는 thumbs down(반대·거절).

senses.meaningEn: the loud sound you hear in the sky during a storm

examples.en: Did you hear that thunder?
My dog is scared of thunder.

senses.note: 셀 수 없는 명사: a thunder ✗ → a clap of thunder(천둥 한 번). 천둥은 소리(thunder), 번개는 빛(lightning): thunder and lightning 순서로 묶어 말함. thunderstorm = 뇌우.

senses.meaningEn: the day of the week after Wednesday and before Friday

examples.en: I'll send you the report by Thursday.
We usually have pizza night on Thursday.
examples.ko: 우리는 보통 목요일에 피자 먹는 날을 해.

senses.note: 철자에 주의: Thursday(Tuesday 와 혼동). 첫소리 th 는 /θ/ 로 혀를 윗니에 대고 발음한다. by Thursday = 목요일까지(기한). 줄임말은 Thu. 또는 Thurs.

senses.meaningEn: a piece of paper or a code that shows you have paid to travel or enter a place

examples.en: I bought two tickets to Busan.
examples.ko: 부산 가는 표 두 장 샀어.

examples.en: Can I see your ticket, please?

senses.note: 기차표·영화표·콘서트표 모두 ticket. a ticket to/for + 목적지/공연. 왕복표 = round-trip ticket(미), 편도 = one-way ticket.

senses.meaningEn: an official notice that you must pay money for breaking a traffic rule

examples.en: I got a parking ticket this morning.
He got a ticket for driving too fast.

senses.note: get a ticket = 딱지를 끊기다(받는 사람 입장). 경찰이 끊어 주는 쪽은 give someone a ticket. speeding ticket(과속), parking ticket(주차 위반).

senses.meaningEn: with everything in its place and nothing lying around

examples.en: Her desk is always neat and tidy.
examples.ko: 그녀의 책상은 항상 깔끔하게 정돈돼 있어.

examples.en: Keep your room tidy, please.

senses.note: neat and tidy 로 자주 붙여 씀. clean(더럽지 않은)과 tidy(물건이 정리된)는 다름.

senses.meaningEn: to put things in their right place so a room looks neat

examples.en: Let's tidy the living room before Mom comes.
examples.ko: 엄마 오시기 전에 거실 좀 치우자.

examples.en: I need to tidy my desk.

senses.note: tidy up = 정리하다. 미국에서는 clean up 이 더 흔하고 tidy 는 영국식 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: to put things back in their places so a room looks neat

examples.en: Please tidy up your room before Grandma comes.
examples.ko: 할머니 오시기 전에 네 방 정리해.

examples.en: I tidied up my desk and felt much better.

senses.note: clean up 은 '더러운 것을 닦아내는' 쪽, tidy up 은 '흩어진 것을 제자리에 두는' 쪽. 미국보다 영국에서 더 자주 쓰고, 미국은 clean up/straighten up 선호.

senses.meaningEn: a long narrow piece of cloth worn around the neck under a shirt collar

examples.en: He wore a blue tie to the interview.
examples.ko: 그는 면접에 파란 넥타이를 하고 갔어.

examples.en: Can you help me with my tie?

senses.note: necktie 라고도 함. 넥타이를 '매다' = put on/tie a tie, '풀다' = take off/loosen.

senses.meaningEn: to fasten something with a string, rope, or knot

examples.en: Tie your shoes before you run.
She tied her hair back with a ribbon.

senses.note: tie - tied - tied, 현재분사는 tying. 풀다 = untie.

senses.meaningEn: a result in a game where both sides have the same score

examples.en: The game ended in a tie, two to two.
It was a tie, so nobody won.

senses.note: 영국식은 draw. 동사로도 쓰임: The two teams tied.

senses.meaningEn: to fasten something with string or rope so it stays closed or in place

examples.en: Tie up the bag so the trash doesn't fall out.
He tied up the boat at the dock.

senses.note: tie(묶다) – tied – tying. tie up your hair = 머리를 묶다. tie up the dog = 개를 묶어 두다.

senses.meaningEn: to be very busy so that you cannot do anything else

examples.en: Sorry, I'm tied up all morning. Can we talk at two?
examples.ko: 미안, 오전 내내 바빠. 2시에 얘기할 수 있을까?

examples.en: He got tied up in traffic and missed the start.
examples.ko: 그는 차가 막혀 꼼짝 못해서 시작을 놓쳤어.

senses.note: 거의 항상 수동 be tied up (with/in ~). 전화나 약속을 미룰 때 정중한 핑계로 자주 씀. 물건에 쓰면 tie up money = 돈을 묶어 두다(못 쓰게 되다).

senses.meaningEn: a large wild cat with orange fur and black stripes that lives in Asia

examples.en: The tiger is the biggest cat in the world.
examples.ko: 호랑이는 세계에서 가장 큰 고양잇과 동물이야.

examples.en: My son's favorite animal is the tiger.
examples.ko: 우리 아들이 가장 좋아하는 동물은 호랑이야.

senses.note: 호랑이 무늬는 stripes(줄무늬). 호랑이는 한국의 상징 동물. 새끼는 cub. 발음은 '타이거'(/ˈtaɪɡər/).

senses.meaningEn: what we measure in hours and minutes, or a point on the clock

examples.en: What time is it now?
Sorry, I don't have time today.

senses.note: '시간이 있다/없다'는 have time(셀 수 없는 명사, a 없이). on time = 정각에, in time = 시간 안에(늦지 않게). 시각을 묻는 가장 자연스러운 말은 What time is it? 또는 Do you have the time?

senses.meaningEn: a particular moment or period when something happens

examples.en: This is not a good time to call.
I had a great time at your party.

senses.note: have a good/great/hard time = 좋은/힘든 시간을 보내다. at the same time = 동시에. for the time being = 당분간.

senses.meaningEn: one occasion when something happens

examples.en: I've seen this movie three times.
Next time, let's try the other restaurant.

senses.note: once(한 번), twice(두 번), three times(세 번)… 한국인이 자주 틀리는 것: one time 보다 once, two times 보다 twice 가 자연스럽다. every time = 매번, this time = 이번에.

senses.meaningEn: time seems to pass very quickly

examples.en: Is it already June? Time flies!
Time flies when you're having fun.

senses.note: Time flies when you're having fun. 이 통째로 자주 쓰이는 문장. "How time flies!" 도 흔함. fly 의 3인칭 flies 로 고정.

senses.meaningEn: extremely small

examples.en: Look at the tiny kitten!
examples.ko: 저 조그만 아기 고양이 좀 봐!

examples.en: My first apartment was tiny but cozy.
examples.ko: 내 첫 아파트는 아주 작았지만 아늑했어.

senses.note: small 보다 강한 말로, 귀엽거나 정겹게 들리기도 함. tiny little(아주 조그만)처럼 겹쳐 쓰는 구어 표현도 흔함.

senses.meaningEn: very small in amount

examples.en: Just a tiny bit of salt, please.
There's only a tiny piece of cake left.
examples.ko: 케이크가 아주 작은 조각 하나밖에 안 남았어.

senses.note: a tiny bit = 아주 조금. a little bit 보다 더 적은 느낌.

senses.meaningEn: to fall onto its side, or to make something fall onto its side

examples.en: The vase tipped over and water spilled everywhere.
Careful! Don't tip over your glass.

senses.note: tip(기울이다)에서 온 말: 기울어져서 넘어지는 그림. 사람이 넘어지는 건 fall over, 손으로 쳐서 넘어뜨리는 건 knock over.

senses.meaningEn: feeling that you need to rest or sleep

examples.en: I'm so tired. I didn't sleep well last night.
examples.ko: 너무 피곤해. 어젯밤에 잠을 잘 못 잤어.

examples.en: You look tired. Why don't you go to bed early?
examples.ko: 피곤해 보여. 일찍 자는 게 어때?

senses.note: be/feel/get/look tired. 매우 피곤하면 exhausted. 피곤하게 만드는 것은 tiring(a tiring day).

senses.meaningEn: bored with something because it has happened too often

examples.en: I'm tired of eating the same thing every day.
examples.ko: 매일 같은 것 먹는 게 지겨워.

examples.en: She is tired of waiting for his call.
examples.ko: 그녀는 그의 전화를 기다리는 데 지쳤어.

senses.note: be tired of + 명사/-ing. sick of 와 비슷하며 sick and tired of 로 강조.

senses.meaningEn: in the direction of a place; used to show where someone goes

examples.en: I go to school by bus.
Welcome to Seoul!

senses.note: go to + 장소. 단, home·here·there 앞에는 to 를 안 씀(go home). from A to B = A에서 B까지.

senses.meaningEn: used to show the end of a period of time, or minutes before the hour

examples.en: The shop is open from nine to six.
It's ten to five.

senses.note: ten to five = 4:50. 반대는 past(ten past five = 5:10). 기한 '~까지' 는 by/until 을 씀.

senses.meaningEn: used to show the person who receives something or is affected

examples.en: Give this letter to your teacher.
Be nice to your little sister.

senses.note: give/send/show/say + 물건 + to + 사람. talk to, listen to, belong to 처럼 to 가 붙는 동사도 세트로 암기.

senses.meaningEn: used before a verb to make the infinitive, often to show purpose

examples.en: I want to learn English.
She went out to buy some milk.

senses.note: want/need/hope/plan + to + 동사. 조동사(can, will, must) 뒤에는 to 없음: I can swim (not 'can to swim').

senses.meaningEn: on this day

examples.en: I'm not going to school today.
What did you do today?

senses.note: today 앞에 전치사를 쓰지 않는다: on today (X). 명사로도 씀: Today is Friday. / today's news(오늘의 뉴스).

senses.meaningEn: in the present time, these days

examples.en: Today, most people have a smartphone.
examples.ko: 오늘날 대부분의 사람들이 스마트폰을 가지고 있어.

examples.en: Kids today spend a lot of time online.
examples.ko: 요즘 아이들은 온라인에서 시간을 많이 보내.

senses.note: 이 뜻으로는 문장 앞에 Today, 로 시작하거나 명사 뒤에 붙인다(young people today). 글에서는 nowadays 보다 today 가 더 자연스럽다.

senses.meaningEn: one of the five parts at the end of your foot

examples.en: Ouch, I hit my toe on the door.
Wiggle your toes to warm them up.

senses.note: 손가락은 finger, 발가락은 toe. big toe(엄지발가락), little toe(새끼발가락).

senses.meaningEn: with each other

examples.en: We had dinner together last night.
Let's go to the park together.

senses.note: together with = ~와 함께. "함께 하다"를 together 로 끝내는 패턴(work together, live together). 동사 뒤에 둠.

senses.meaningEn: so that things are joined or combined

examples.en: Put the two pieces together.
Mix the eggs and sugar together.

senses.note: put together(조립하다), get together(모이다), all together(모두 함께) vs altogether(총, 완전히) 구별.

senses.meaningEn: the bowl with a seat that you sit on to use the bathroom

examples.en: The toilet is clogged again.
Please flush the toilet after you use it.
examples.ko: 사용한 뒤에는 변기 물을 내려 주세요.

senses.note: flush the toilet = 변기 물을 내리다. toilet paper = 휴지.

senses.meaningEn: a room with a toilet in it

examples.en: Excuse me, where's the toilet?
I need to go to the toilet.

senses.note: 미국에서는 toilet 이 변기 자체를 뜻해서 '화장실 어디예요?'는 Where's the bathroom/restroom? 이 자연스러움. 영국·호주에서는 toilet 으로 화장실을 말함.

senses.meaningEn: a soft red fruit eaten as a vegetable, often in salads and sauces

examples.en: Add two tomatoes to the salad.
I don't like raw tomato.

senses.note: 복수형은 tomatoes(-es). 미국식 발음은 /təˈmeɪtoʊ/, 영국식은 /təˈmɑːtəʊ/.

senses.meaningEn: on the day after today

examples.en: See you tomorrow!
I have a big test tomorrow morning.

senses.note: tomorrow morning/afternoon/night 처럼 바로 이어 쓴다(전치사 없음). the day after tomorrow = 내후일. 명사로도 씀: Tomorrow is a holiday. 철자에 주의: m 하나, r 두 개.

senses.meaningEn: the soft part inside your mouth that you taste and speak with

examples.en: I burned my tongue on the hot soup.
Stick out your tongue, please.

senses.note: 발음은 '텅'(/tʌŋ/), 끝의 ue 는 소리 나지 않음. 혀를 깨물다 = bite my tongue.

senses.meaningEn: a language, especially the one you learned as a child

examples.en: Korean is my mother tongue.
English is not her native tongue.

senses.note: mother tongue = native language(모국어). 보통 이 표현 안에서만 쓰고, 일반적인 '언어'는 language.

senses.meaningEn: on the evening or night of today

examples.en: Are you free tonight?
Let's order pizza for dinner tonight.

senses.note: 오늘 저녁 식사 시간대까지 포함해서 넓게 '오늘 밤'을 가리킨다. '어젯밤'은 last night, '내일 밤'은 tomorrow night. this night (X) 라고 하지 않는다.

senses.meaningEn: more than is good or needed

examples.en: This soup is too hot to eat.
examples.ko: 이 수프는 너무 뜨거워서 못 먹겠어.

examples.en: You're walking too fast for me.

senses.note: too 는 부정적 '지나침'. 긍정 강조에는 very: very good(O), too good(X, '지나치게 좋다'로 이상함). too ... to 동사 = 너무 ~해서 ...할 수 없다.

senses.meaningEn: also; as well

examples.en: I like pizza. Me too!
Can I come too?

senses.note: 문장 끝에 둠. 부정문의 '~도 (아니다)'는 too 대신 either: I don't like it either. 'Me too' 는 긍정에만.

senses.meaningEn: one of the hard white things in your mouth that you bite with

examples.en: I have a loose tooth.
The dentist pulled out my bad tooth.

senses.note: 한 개는 tooth, 두 개 이상은 teeth(tooths ×). 이가 아프다 = have a toothache. 치과 = the dentist's.

senses.meaningEn: a pain in one of your teeth

examples.en: I have a toothache, so I'm going to the dentist.
A bad toothache kept me awake all night.
examples.ko: 심한 치통 때문에 밤새 잠을 못 잤어.

senses.note: tooth(이 하나) + ache. 치과 = the dentist / dentist's office. 이가 아프다 = My tooth hurts.

senses.meaningEn: a small brush used for cleaning your teeth

examples.en: I need a new toothbrush. This one is old.
Don't forget to pack your toothbrush.

senses.note: tooth(단수)+brush. teethbrush 라고 하지 않는다. 전동 칫솔은 electric toothbrush.

senses.meaningEn: a soft substance you put on a toothbrush to clean your teeth

examples.en: Put a little toothpaste on the brush.
Which toothpaste do you use?

senses.note: 셀 수 없는 명사. '치약 하나'는 a tube of toothpaste.

senses.meaningEn: to put your hand or fingers on something

examples.en: Please don't touch the paintings.
He touched my arm to get my attention.
examples.ko: 그는 내 주의를 끌려고 팔을 살짝 건드렸어.

senses.note: 박물관 표지 Do not touch. 음식에 손도 안 댔다 = didn't touch the food.

senses.meaningEn: communication with someone, especially by phone or message

examples.en: Let's keep in touch after you move.
I've lost touch with my old classmates.

senses.note: keep/stay in touch = 연락하다, get in touch = 연락을 취하다, lose touch = 연락이 끊기다.

senses.meaningEn: to make someone feel strong emotion, especially sympathy or gratitude

examples.en: Her kind words really touched me.
I was touched by the surprise party.

senses.note: be touched by = ~에 감동하다. touching = 감동적인.

senses.meaningEn: a visit to a place during which you look at its interesting parts, often with a guide

examples.en: We took a bus tour of the city.
Let me give you a tour of the house.

senses.note: take/go on a tour(투어하다), give someone a tour(안내해 주다). tour guide(가이드), package tour(패키지 여행). 가수 공연 투어도 tour(on tour).

senses.meaningEn: to travel around a place to see it

examples.en: We toured Italy for two weeks.
You can tour the museum for free today.
examples.ko: 오늘은 박물관을 무료로 둘러볼 수 있어.

senses.note: tour + 장소(전치사 없음). 동사보다 명사 take a tour 가 훨씬 많이 쓰임.

senses.meaningEn: a person who is visiting a place for pleasure

examples.en: The beach is full of tourists in summer.
Many tourists visit this old palace.
examples.ko: 관광객이 이 오래된 궁궐을 많이 찾아.

senses.note: tourist attraction(관광 명소), tourist information center(관광 안내소). 약간 '단체 관광객' 느낌이 있어서, 자기 소개엔 traveler 를 선호하는 사람도 있음.

senses.meaningEn: a piece of soft cloth used for drying yourself or things

examples.en: Can you hand me a towel, please?
The hotel gives you fresh towels every day.
examples.ko: 그 호텔은 매일 새 수건을 줘.

senses.note: 목욕 수건 bath towel, 손 수건 hand towel, 종이 타월 paper towel. 발음은 [타월]에 가깝다.

senses.meaningEn: a tall, narrow building or part of a building

examples.en: You can see the whole city from the top of the tower.
The Eiffel Tower is the most famous tower in Paris.

senses.note: N Seoul Tower, Tokyo Tower 처럼 고유명사에 많이 쓰임. 교회의 종탑은 bell tower, 시계탑은 clock tower. 아파트 '~타워'처럼 고층 건물 이름에도 씀.

senses.meaningEn: a place with houses and shops that is bigger than a village but smaller than a city

examples.en: We live in a small town by the sea.
examples.ko: 우리는 바다 옆 작은 마을에 살아.

examples.en: This town has only one school.

senses.note: village < town < city 순서로 커짐. 한국의 '읍·소도시' 느낌. 고향은 hometown.

senses.meaningEn: the center of the place where you live, or that place itself

examples.en: I'm going into town to buy some shoes.
My parents are out of town this week.
examples.ko: 부모님이 이번 주에 다른 지역에 가 계셔.

senses.note: 이 뜻에서는 보통 관사 없이 in town / into town / out of town 으로 씀. out of town = 출장·여행 등으로 동네를 떠나 있다.

senses.meaningEn: a thing for children to play with

examples.en: Please put your toys back in the box.
The baby got a new toy for her birthday.
examples.ko: 아기가 생일 선물로 새 장난감을 받았어.

senses.note: toy store(장난감 가게), toy car(장난감 자동차). 강아지 장난감도 dog toy.

senses.meaningEn: a shop that sells toys for children

examples.en: The kids want to go to the toy store after lunch.
examples.ko: 아이들이 점심 먹고 장난감 가게에 가고 싶어 해.

examples.en: We bought a puzzle at the toy store.

senses.note: 미국식은 store, 영국식은 toy shop. 장난감은 toy(셀 수 있는 명사) → toys.

senses.meaningEn: all the cars and other vehicles moving on the roads

examples.en: There was a lot of traffic this morning.
Sorry, I'm late because of the traffic.

senses.note: 불가산명사: a traffic (X), traffics (X). heavy traffic = 교통 혼잡, traffic jam = 교통 체증, traffic light = 신호등. '차가 막힌다' = There's a lot of traffic / I'm stuck in traffic.

senses.meaningEn: a set of red, yellow, and green lights that controls traffic on a road

examples.en: Turn right at the second traffic light.
The traffic light turned red, so we stopped.

senses.note: 보통 복수 traffic lights 로도 많이 씀(신호등 한 세트). 미국 구어로는 stoplight. '빨간불에 걸렸다'는 We got stuck at a red light. 신호등 색이 '바뀌다'는 turn green/red.

senses.meaningEn: a long vehicle with many connected cars that runs on rails

examples.en: The train to Busan leaves at eight.
I read a book on the train.

senses.note: 기차를 '타다'는 take the train / get on the train, 기차 '안에서'는 on the train(in 아님). '기차로'는 by train. 고속열차는 high-speed train(KTX).

senses.meaningEn: to practice a sport or skill regularly to get better at it

examples.en: She trains for the marathon every morning.
examples.ko: 그녀는 마라톤을 위해 매일 아침 훈련해.

examples.en: The team trains hard before every game.
examples.ko: 그 팀은 매 경기 전에 열심히 훈련해.

senses.note: train for + 대회/목표, train to be a nurse(간호사가 되기 위해 교육받다). 코치가 선수를 훈련시키다도 train(train the players). 명사 '훈련'은 training.

senses.meaningEn: things you throw away because you do not want them
